17.en: **Love one another.** See on ch. 13:34; cf. ch. 15:12.
17.zh:
我這樣吩咐你們，是要叫你們彼此相愛。

**彼此相愛。**見約13:34註釋；參約15:12。
[關於逼迫的警告：約15:18至16:4]。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第382頁；《歷代願望》第504頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–20節）**。《證言》卷二第492頁。

12.en: **My commandments.** See on ch. 13:34.
12.zh:
你們要彼此相愛，像我愛你們一樣；這就是我的命令。

**我的命令。**見約13:34註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第32頁；《歷代願望》第641，677頁；《基督教育原理》第210頁；《今日的生活》第187頁；《給傳道人的證言》第158，192頁；《證言》卷一第150，166，371頁；《證言》卷五第35，360，604頁；《證言》卷六第455頁；《論福利工作》第83頁；見約13：34懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《證言》卷二第169頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–14節）**。《證言》卷一第690頁。

4.en: **Abide in me.** A continuous abiding in a living connection with Christ is essential for growth and fruitfulness. Occasional attention to matters of religion is not sufficient. Riding high on a wave of religious fervor one day, only to fall low into a period of neglect the next, does not promote spiritual strength. To abide in Christ means that the soul must be in daily, constant communion with Jesus Christ and must live His life (Gal. 2:20). It is not possible for one branch to depend upon another for its vitality; each must maintain its own personal relationship to the vine. Each member must bear its own fruits.
4.zh:
你們要常在我裡面，我也常在你們裡面。枝子若不常在葡萄樹上，自己就不能結果子；你們若不常在我裡面，也是這樣。

**你們要常在我裡面。**持續恆久的與基督保持活潑的聯繫對於成長和結果子是非常重要的。偶爾光顧一下宗教事務是不夠的。一會兒馳騁於宗教熱忱的浪尖，一會兒又跌入疏忽怠惰的低谷，這樣是不能增進人屬靈力量的。在基督裡面意味著我們的心靈必須天天不斷地與耶穌基督保持聯絡並且要過祂的生活（加2:20）。一根枝子再不能依靠其他什麼來獲得它的生命力；每根枝子都必須保持它自己與葡萄樹的關係。每根枝子都必須結出它自己的果子。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷四第355頁；《證言》卷五第232頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《使徒行述》第284頁；《安息日學訓言》第30頁；《基督教育之研究》第329頁；《拾級就主》第68頁；《成聖的人生》第80頁；《給傳道人的證言》第151，324頁；《證言》卷一第289，340頁；《證言》卷五第47，228，254頁；見太11:29懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–6節）**。《歷代願望》第676頁；《證言》卷一第300頁；《證言》卷二第263，441，454頁；《證言》卷四第542頁；《證言》卷五第49頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–16節）**。《服務真詮》第514頁。

5.en: **Without me.** “The carnal mind … is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be” (Rom. 8:7). It is impossible for man in his own strength to escape from the pit of sin into which he has fallen and to bring forth fruits unto holiness (see SC 18). Wherever men hold to the principle that they can save themselves by their own works they have no barrier against sin (see DA 35, 36).
5.zh:
我是葡萄樹，你們是枝子。常在我裡面的，我也常在他裡面，這人就多結果子；因為離了我，你們就不能做什麼。

**離了我。**“原來體貼肉體的，就是與上帝為仇；因為不服上帝的律法，也是不能服”（羅8:7）。一個人靠自己的力量決不能逃出他所跌落之罪惡的深坑並結出向善的果實來（《拾級就主》18頁）。人何時認為能夠靠自己的力量得救，他就再沒有抵禦罪惡的屏障了（見《歷代願望》35，36頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《兒童教育指南》第232頁；《基督比喻實訓》第52，332頁；《安息日學訓言》第94，158，165，168頁；《基督教育之研究》第231，412頁；《歷代願望》第675頁；《佈道論》第343，643頁；《早期著作》第73頁；《基督教育原理》第110，178，196，200，225，249，284，292，349，476頁；《善惡之爭》第73頁；《傳道良助》第392頁；《服務真詮》第513頁；《今日的生活》第11，15，74頁；《醫療佈道論》第41，99，150頁；《成聖的人生》第55頁；《給傳道人的證言》第142，154，339，381頁；《證言》卷三第387，522頁；《證言》卷四第320，354，560頁；《證言》卷五第229，230，306，344，425，583，586，591頁；《證言》卷六第45，247，438頁；《證言》卷七第39，152，194，298頁；《證言》卷九第152，203頁。

2.en:
**Every branch.** The disciples are represented as the branches of the vine. As the branches are dependent upon their connection with the stock for life and productiveness, so the Christian is dependent upon union with Christ for spiritual life and fruitfulness.
**Beareth not fruit.** He who professes to be in Christ is expected to bring forth fruits appropriate to his profession. These fruits are elsewhere termed “the fruit of the Spirit” ( Gal. 5:22; Eph. 5:9), or “fruits of righteousness” Phil. 1:11; cf. Heb. 12:11), that is, fruits which are righteousness. These fruits are evident in the character and the life. When these “good fruits” (James 3:17) are absent it becomes necessary to sever the fruitless branch.
**Taketh away.** Gr. airō (see below under “Purgeth”).
**Purgeth.** Gr. kathairō, “to cleanse,” in this case, by removing superfluous growth. There is a word play in the Greek in the words for “taketh away” (airō) and “purgeth” (kathairō) that cannot be reproduced in English. The character is “purged” by the tests and trials of life. The Father, the heavenly Husbandman, oversees the process. And though the “chastening” may seem to be grievous, “nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby” (Heb. 12:11).
**More fruit.** There can be no life without growth. As long as there is life there is need of continual development. Character development is the work of a lifetime (see COL 65, 66). See on Matt. 5:48.
2.zh:
凡屬我不結果子的枝子，他就剪去；凡結果子的，他就修理乾淨，使枝子結果子更多。

**凡……的枝子。**門徒們被比作葡萄樹上的枝子。就像枝子為了生命和結果子依靠樹幹一樣，基督徒為了他們屬靈的生命和多結果實也要依靠與基督的聯絡。
**不結果子。**那些承認自己在基督裡面的人要結出果子來與他們的表白相稱。這些果實被稱為“聖靈的果子”（加5:22；弗5:9）或“仁義的果子”（腓1:11；參來12:11），即這果子是義的。這些果子在生活和品格中是明顯的。若沒有這些“善果”（雅3:17），就必須將不結果子的枝子剪掉。
**剪去。**airō（見下面“修理乾淨”註釋）。
**修理乾淨。**kathairō，“潔淨，”這裡指除掉多餘生長的東西。它由airo（“除去”）和kathairo“淨化”組成。品格經過生活的試煉和磨難得以淨化。天父，天上栽培的人，監察著整個過程。“管教”似乎難以忍受，“後來卻為那經練過的人結出平安的果子，就是義。”（來12:11）
**果子更多。**不成長就沒有生命。只要有生命就必須不斷地生長。品格的發展是一生的工作（見《基督比喻實訓》65頁）。見太5:48註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第676頁；《成聖的人生》第82頁；《證言》卷三第387頁；《證言》卷四第354頁；《證言》卷五第18，344頁。

6.en:
**If a man abide not.** The delusion, “once in grace always in grace,” is denied by this condition. It is possible for those who have been in Christ to sever their connection with Him and be lost (see on Heb. 6:4–6. Salvation is conditional upon abiding in Christ until the end.
**Is withered.** The Christian represented by the severed branch may carry on a form of religion, but the vital power is lacking (2 Tim. 3:5). Under test and trial the shallowness of his profession is seen. As the severed branches are eventually gathered and burned, so the unfruitful Christian, along with the nonprofessor, will suffer ultimate extinction (Matt. 10:28; 13:38–40; 25:41, 46). No overt act of disobedience is mentioned, simply the sin of neglect. Compare the parable of the Sheep and the Goats (Matt. 25:31–46). Those to the left of the King were excluded from the kingdom for neglect of practical Christian duty.
6.zh:
人若不常在我裡面，就像枝子丟在外面枯乾，人拾起來，扔在火裡燒了。

**人若不常在我裡面。**這節經文否定了“一日得救，永遠得救”的謬論。那些在基督裡面的人是有可能斷絕與祂的聯絡而失喪的（見來6:4-6節註釋）。得救是有條件的，人必須住在基督裡面，直到末時。
**枯乾。**那些被比作剪下來枝子的基督徒或許會繼續實行一種形式上的宗教，但他們卻缺乏生命的力量（提後3:5）。他信仰的膚淺在考驗和試煉之下就會暴露出來。就像剪下來的枝子最終會收聚並焚燒一樣，那些不結果子的基督徒，和無信仰者，也將最終被根除（太10:28；13:38-40；25:41,46）。這裡沒有提到公然悖逆的行為，只是在說疏忽的罪。參綿羊和山羊的比喻（太25:31-46）。那些被留在王左邊的被排除在天國之外，因為他們忽略了基督徒實際的責任。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第739頁；《今日的生活》第93頁；《證言》卷五第229頁。

9.en:
**Father hath loved me.** Compare chs. 3:35; 5:20; 10:17; 17:24.
**In my love.** To abide in Christ means to abide in the shelter of His love. It is comforting to know Christ’s love for us is as abiding as the Father’s love for the Son. More than that, “the Father himself loveth you” (ch. 16:27) with the same love with which He loves the Son (EGW RH Nov. 4, 1890).
9.zh:
我愛你們，正如父愛我一樣；你們要常在我的愛裡。

**父愛我。**將這裡與約3:35；5:20；10:17；17:24進行比較。
**在我的愛裡。**住在基督裡面就意味著住在祂的保護裡。知道基督愛我們，就像聖父愛聖子一樣，這一點是很安慰人的的。此外，“父自己愛你們”（約16:27），祂對我們的愛與祂對祂自己兒子的愛是一樣的（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1890年11月4日）。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–10節）**。《基督教育原理》第399頁。

10.en:
**My commandments.** See on ch. 14:15.
**Father’s commandments.** Looking back Jesus could say with perfect confidence, “I have kept my Father’s commandments.” He did always those things that pleased His Father (ch. 8:29). He “did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth” (1 Peter 2:22). His sinless life proved that it was possible for men with divine help to keep the commandments (see DA 24).
10.zh:
你們若遵守我的命令，就常在我的愛裡，正如我遵守了我父的命令，常在他的愛裡。

**我的命令。**見約14:15註釋。
**父的命令。**耶穌回顧以往，可以滿懷信心地說：“我遵守了我父的命令”。祂常做祂父喜悅的事（約8:29）。祂“並沒有犯罪，口裡也沒有詭詐”（彼前2:22）。祂無罪的生活證明人靠著上帝的幫助是可以遵守誡命的（見《歷代願望》24頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第283，312頁；《歷代願望》第287頁；《教育論》第78頁；《基督教育原理》第135，402頁；《善惡之爭》第469頁；《服務真詮》第426，451頁；《今日的生活》第311頁；《拾級就主》第61頁；《成聖的人生》第67，80頁；《給傳道人的證言》第138頁；《證言》卷七第141頁；《證言》卷八第289，312頁；見太24:23.24懷愛倫註釋。

18.en:
**If the world hate you.** [A Warning of Persecution, John 15:18 to 16:4.] There would be hatred from the world, but among the inner group there ought to be love (v. 17). They would have sufficient to endure from the bitter conflict with the world, without adding to the antagonism from without (Luke 22:24). The world hates those whose sympathies and interests are at variance with it (see on ch. 7:7).
**It hated me.** The full fury of the world’s hatred the disciples were yet to see.
18.zh:
世人若恨你們，你們知道（或作：該知道），恨你們以先已經恨我了。

**世人若恨你們。**世人會恨你們，但你們內部要彼此相愛（第17節）。你們要充分忍受與世界的劇烈鬥爭，所以不要再雪上加霜（路22:24）。世人恨那些與他們情感和利益不同的人（見約7:7註釋）。
**已經恨我了。**門徒將要領教世人刻骨的仇恨。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第559頁；《證言》卷一第418頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–21節）**。《歷代願望》第678頁；《證言》卷五第433頁。

19.en:
**If ye were.** The condition is unfulfilled according to the construction in the Greek. They had been of the world but had heeded the call of Jesus to come out of the world. Of His brothers, the sons of Joseph (see on Matt. 12:46), Jesus said, “The world cannot hate you” (John 7:7). See on ch. 15:18.
**Hateth you.** The reason for the hatred is indicated in the preceding verses: Abiding in Christ (v. 4), bringing forth the fruits of righteousness (v. 5), and demonstrating them (v. 16). The deeds of the world are reproved by the righteous life and the open testimony of the Christian (John 7:7; 1 John 3:13). Robertson asks the significant question: “Does the world hate us? If not, why not? Has the world become more Christian or Christians more worldly?”
19.zh:
你們若屬世界，世界必愛屬自己的；只因你們不屬世界，乃是我從世界中揀選了你們，所以世界就恨你們。

**你們若屬。**希臘文的結構是一個未完成的條件句。他們過去曾屬這世界，但他們聽從耶穌的呼召從這世界出來。耶穌論到祂的弟兄──約瑟的兒子們（見太12:46註釋）說，“世人不能恨你們”（約7:7）。見18節註釋。
**恨你們。**仇恨的原因在前面幾節中已經說明了：在基督裡面（第4節），結出義的果子來（第5節），將它們表現出來（第16節）。世人的行為受到了基督徒公義生活和公開見證的譴責（約7:7；約一3:13）。羅伯遜提過一個很重要的問題：“這世界恨我們嗎？如果不，為什麼？是世界變得更基督化了，還是基督徒變得世俗化了？”
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷二第690頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《善惡之爭》第144頁。

8.en:
**Bear much fruit.** It is glory to a vinedresser when his plants bear well. Thus glory comes to God when His image is reflected in the lives of His followers. Satan claims that the requirements of God are too severe and that men cannot attain to the ideal of Christian perfection. Thus the character of God is vindicated when men, through divine grace, become partakers of the divine nature.
**Be my disciples.** The reflection of the Christian graces is evidence of discipleship. Without a vital connection with Christ it impossible to bring forth the fruits of righteousness (v. 5; ch. 13:35).
8.zh:
你們多結果子，我父就因此得榮耀，你們也就是我的門徒了。

**多結果子。**樹木果實累累，這是栽培之人的榮耀。同樣，當上帝的形象在信祂之人的生活中反照出來時，祂也就得了榮耀。撒但宣稱上帝的要求過於嚴格，人是不可能達到一個基督徒完美之標準的。這樣，當人靠著上帝的恩典而與祂的性情有份時，上帝的品德就得到了維護。
**也就是我的門徒了。**反映基督徒的美德，是門徒身份的證據。不與基督有生命的聯繫就不可能結出仁義的果實（第5節；約13:35）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第301頁；《給管家的勉言》第302頁；《安息日學訓言》第181頁；《歷代願望》第251頁；《傳道良助》第287頁；《給青年人的信息》第314頁；《成聖的人生》第84頁；《證言》卷三第523頁；《證言》卷五第239，349，348頁；《證言》卷六第42頁；《證言》卷八第243，246頁。

11.en:
**My joy.** The joy of Christ lay in the consciousness of a successfully accomplished mission. The Saviour had joy in carrying out the divine purpose in man’s redemption and in enduring that men might be saved. His purpose in life was to glorify His Father.
**Your joy.** Joy is the second of the graces of the Spirit listed by Paul (Gal. 5:22). True joy is not found in noisy laughter or in giddy excitement caused by the world’s shallow pleasures. The Christian finds his joy in resting in the love of Christ, in victories won, and in unselfish service for humanity. Joy will reach its highest realization in the world to come, but a high degree of joy may be experienced here and now by those who abide in Christ.
11.zh:
這些事我已經對你們說了，是要叫我的喜樂存在你們心裡，並叫你們的喜樂可以滿足。

**我的喜樂。**基督的喜樂在於祂意識到自己的使命勝利地完成了。基督的喜樂在於祂實現了救贖人類的神聖計劃，人類可以永遠得救了。祂生活中的目的就是要榮耀祂的父。
**你們的喜樂。**喜樂是保羅所列之第二顆聖靈的果實（加5:22）。這個世界膚淺的娛樂中嘈雜的笑談和輕浮的興奮不能給人帶來真正的喜樂的。基督徒的喜樂在主的愛裡，在救靈工作的勝利中，在為人類的無私的服務上樂。最大的喜樂在未來的世界，但是如今住在基督裡面的人也可以體驗一種極大的喜樂。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第504頁；《拾級就主》第124頁；《證言》卷七第273頁。

16.en:
**Ye have not chosen me.** The disciples had chosen to be followers of Christ, but it was Jesus who from His many followers had selected twelve to be apostles (Luke 6:13; see on Mark 3:14). All may choose to follow Christ, but it is He who chooses and qualifies men to occupy positions of responsibility and leadership in His cause (1 Cor. 12:7–11, 28).
**Bring forth fruit.** That is, be successful in their mission.
**Your fruit should remain.** Compare ch. 4:36.
**Whatsoever ye shall ask.** Compare ch. 14:13. The condition for answered prayer is to abide in Christ.
**In my name.** See on ch. 14:13.
16.zh:
不是你們揀選了我，是我揀選了你們，並且分派你們去結果子，叫你們的果子常存，使你們奉我的名，無論向父求什麼，他就賜給你們。

**不是你們揀選了我。**門徒選擇跟從耶穌，但是耶穌從許多跟從者中揀選了十二使徒（路6:13；見可3:14註釋）。所有的人都有可能選擇跟從基督，然而是祂挑選並使人有資格承擔祂聖工中領導和負責的職務（林前12:7-11,28）。
**結果子。**就是在他們的使命中獲得成功。
**你們的果子常存。**將這裡與約4:36進行比較。
**無論向父求什麼。**將這裡與約14:13進行比較。禱告蒙垂聽的條件是人必須住在基督裡面。
**奉我的名。**見約14:13註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第509頁；《拾級就主》第100頁；《給傳道人的證言》第212，217頁；《證言》卷二第426，431頁；《證言》卷七第259頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–19節）**。《證言》卷一第285頁。

13.en:
**Greater love.** The “new commandment” (ch. 13:34; cf. ch. 15:12) enjoined the disciples to exercise the same love toward one another that Jesus had manifested toward them. The extent of that love Jesus now revealed. That love led Him to lay down His life for them. However, His love exceeded that which He now commends: “While we were yet sinners” He died for us (see Rom. 5:6–8).
**Friends.** See on v. 14.
13.zh:
人為朋友捨命，人的愛心沒有比這個大的。

**朋友。**見第14節註釋。
**愛心沒有比這個大的。**“新命令”（約13:34；參約15:12）吩咐門徒要彼此相愛，就像耶穌為他們做出的榜樣。耶穌現在解釋了這種愛的廣度。這種愛使祂為他們捨棄生命。然而，基督的愛超過了現在祂所吩咐的愛：“我們還作罪人的時候” 祂就為我們死（見羅5:6-8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷三第529頁。

20.en:
**Remember the word.** See John 13:16; cf. Matt. 10:24; Luke 6:40.
**Persecute you.** Of this, Jesus had warned earlier (see Matt. 10:17–23). He did not want the disciples to become discouraged when the full force of persecution should break loose upon them. How effectively this lesson was learned was later to be seen in the undaunted courage with which the disciples faced imprisonment, beating, torture, and death (Acts 5:41; 16:22–25; etc.). In the face of unparalleled persecution (2 Cor. 4:8–12; 1 Cor. 11:23–28) Paul could say, “For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory” (2 Cor. 4:17). Fearful that afflictions would overwhelm the infant church at Thessalonica, Paul wrote to the believers, “That no man should be moved by these afflictions: for yourselves know that we are appointed thereunto” (1 Thess. 3:3; cf. Phil. 1:29; 2 Tim. 3:12; 8T 127–129).
**Kept my saying.** Despite rejection by the majority, some believed the word of Christ. Thus it would be with the disciples. Some would receive their word and be saved. Their work would be rewarded.
20.zh:
你們要記念我從前對你們所說的話：僕人不能大於主人。他們若逼迫了我，也要逼迫你們；若遵守了我的話，也要遵守你們的話。

**記念……話。**見約13:16；參太10:24；路6:40。
**逼迫你們。**對此，耶穌早就警告過了（見太10:17-23）。當逼迫的勢力完全臨到門徒的時候，祂不希望他們灰心喪氣。這一課門徒們是如何有效學習的，在後來我們會看到。當他們面臨監禁，擊打，折磨和死亡時（徒5:41；16:22-25等），表現出堅強無畏的勇氣。保羅在面對空前的逼迫時（林前4:8-12；林後11:23-28）曾說，“我們這至暫至輕的苦楚，要為我們成就極重無比永遠的榮耀”（林後4:17）。對這種患難的懼怕曾經要壓倒帖撒羅尼迦幼小的教會。保羅寫信給他們，“免得有人被諸般患難搖動。因為你們自己知道，我們受患難原是命定的”（帖前3:3；參腓1:29；提後3:12；《教誨證言》卷八第127-129頁）。
**遵守了我的話。**儘管大多數人要拒絕，還是有一部分人會相信基督的話。基督的話就這樣與門徒們同在。一些人接受了基督的話以致拯救。他們的工作會得到報償。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第47頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（20–21節）**。《使徒行述》第79頁。

26.en:
**Comforter.** See on ch. 14:16.
**I will send.** Again in ch. 16:7 Jesus is presented as the one who sends the Spirit, whereas in ch. 14:26; cf. v. 16, the Father sends the Spirit. There is no contradiction here. The Father and Son work in unison (see on ch. 10:30).
26.zh:
但我要從父那裡差保惠師來，就是從父出來真理的聖靈；他來了，就要為我作見證。

**保惠師。**見約14:16註釋。
**我要……差。**約16:7又說是耶穌差遣聖靈，而約14:26說聖靈是天父派來的；參約14:16，父差遣聖靈。其實這裡並沒有矛盾。父與子的工作是一致的（見約10:30註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第51頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–27節）**。《使徒行述》第22頁；《給傳道人的證言》第69，285頁；見徒1:8懷愛倫註釋。

1.zh:
我是真葡萄樹，我父是栽培的人。

**我是。**又一個耶穌說“我是”的著名事例（見約6:20註釋；參約8:12；10:7,11；11:25；14:6節）。關於“我是”不加代詞“他”的意義，見約8:24註釋。
**真。**alēthinos。聖經常把以色列比作葡萄樹（詩80:8-16；賽5:1-7；27:2,3；耶2:21；12:10）。希律聖殿的入口處裝飾有一棵金制的葡萄樹（見《密西拿》Middoth 3. 8，《塔木德》松奇諾版第15頁），常有錢幣和建築物呈現葡萄樹葉子和果實累累的枝條的圖形。猶太人依靠他們與以色列葡萄樹的聯繫得救。但以色列辜負了自己屬靈的優勢，拒絕了她真正的君王──耶穌。現在耶穌將自己比作真葡萄樹。人只有通過與祂建立生命的連接才能得救。
**栽培的人。**geōrgos，“農民，這裡指栽培葡萄園的人。參gēorgos在路20:9；提後2:6；雅5:7中的用法。早先上帝“從埃及挪出一棵葡萄樹”（詩80:8）並把它栽種在迦南地。現在祂又培植了一棵葡萄樹，就是祂自己的兒子，祂栽種在以色列的土地上（見《歷代願望》675頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第674，675，676頁；《證言》卷五第230頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《佈道論》第361頁；《證言》卷一第300頁；《證言》卷四第353頁；《證言》卷六第133頁；《證言》卷八第186頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–8節）**。《證言》卷七第171頁；見約13:2懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–27節）**。《歷代願望》第674-678頁；《給傳道人的證言》第271頁。
1.en:
**I am.** [The True Vine, John 15:1–17.] Another of the famous ‘I am’ sayings of Jesus (see on ch. 6:20; cf. chs. 8:12; 10:7, 11; 11:25; 14:6). For the meaning of “I am” without the pronoun “he” see on ch. 8:24.
**True.** Gr. alēthinos, “genuine.” In Bible imagery Israel had been likened to a vine (Ps. 80:8–16; Isa. 5:1–7; 27:2, 3; Jer. 2:21; 12:10). A golden vine decorated the entrance to Herod’s Temple (see Mishnah Middoth 3. 8, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 15), and figures of the leaves of the vine or of clusters of grapes were displayed on coins and architecture. The Jews depended upon their connection with the vine of Israel for their salvation. But Israel had proved unfaithful to its spiritual advantages and had rejected its true king, Jesus. Now Jesus presented Himself as the genuine vine. Only through vital connection with Him could men be saved.
**Husbandman.** Gr. geōrgos, “a worker of the soil,” here, a vinedresser. Compare the use of gēorgos in Luke 20:9; 2 Tim. 2:6; James 5:7. Earlier God had taken “a vine out of Egypt” (Ps. 80:8) and had planted it in the land of Canaan. Now He took another vine, His own Son, and planted Him in the land of Israel (see DA 675).

3.zh:
現在你們因我講給你們的道，已經乾淨了。

**現在。**ēdē，“已經”，“如今”。
**已經乾淨了。**見約13:10註釋。
因……道。門徒們對耶穌傳給他們的道有了回應（參約12:48註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第 339頁。
3.en:
**Now.** Gr. ēdē, “already,” “now.”
**Ye are clean.** See on ch. 13:10.
**Through the word.** Rather, “on account of the word.” The disciples had responded to the word of salvation brought to them by Jesus (cf. on ch. 12:48).

7.zh:
你們若常在我裡面，我的話也常在你們裡面，凡你們所願意的，祈求，就給你們成就。

**你們若常在我裡面。**就像第4節所表達的，居住是相互性的。人住在基督裡面，基督也住在他們裡面，並使他們與上帝的性情有份（彼後1:4）。他們的思想與上帝的旨意一致，只求符合祂旨意的東西（見約壹5:14；《歷代願望》668頁）。此外，沒有罪惡的干預能阻礙有利的回答。
**我的話也常在你們裡面。**這句話表明，基督住在我們裡面完全不是一種神秘的、不可理解的經驗。人接受了基督的話，就是接受了祂。他們領受了這話，這話就照亮他們的思想。當他們做出明智的選擇聽從祂的話並靠著從天而來的力量徹底地順從祂時，基督就在他們裡面成了有榮耀的盼望（西1:27）。此外，他們因著這種恆久的經驗就不斷地從基督的話中得到供養。見約6:53註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《兒童教育指南》第499頁；《基督比喻實訓》第144頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第80，207頁；《今日的生活》第20頁；《證言》卷三第209頁；《證言》卷四第259，355頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《歷代願望》第677頁；《早期著作》第29，73頁。
7.en:
**If ye abide in me.** The abiding is mutual as expressed in v. 4. As men abide in Christ, Christ dwells in them and they become partakers of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). Their thoughts become so identified with the divine will that only such requests are made as are in harmony with that will (see 1 John 5:14; DA 668). Furthermore, no sin intervenes to prevent a favorable answer.
**My words abide.** These words show that the indwelling of Christ is not wholly a mystical, inexplicable experience. Men receive Christ by receiving His word. As they feed upon that word it enlightens the mind. And as they make an intelligent choice to follow that word and obey it implicitly through the enabling power of Heaven, Christ, the hope of glory, is formed within (Col. 1:27). Furthermore, for this experience to be constant they feed daily upon the word. See on John 6:53.

14.zh:
你們若遵行我所吩咐的，就是我的朋友了。

**朋友。**philoi，它的單數形式為philos，與動詞phileō，“去愛”（見太5:43,44註釋）同源。Philos的意思是，一個被愛的人，一個可愛的人，或者是一個親愛、友善的人。在真正的友誼中有互相的愛。門徒們藉著謙卑的順從顯出他們的愛（約14:15）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《醫療佈道論》第43頁；《證言》卷四第188頁；《證言》卷五第553頁。
14.en: **Friends.** Gr. philoi, singular philos, related to the verb phileō, “to love” (see on Matt. 5:43, 44). Philos means one beloved or dear, or one who is loving or friendly. In true friendship there is reciprocal love. The disciples would show their love by humble obedience (John 14:15).

15.zh:
以後我不再稱你們為僕人，因僕人不知道主人所做的事。我乃稱你們為朋友；因我從我父所聽見的，已經都告訴你們了。

**僕人。**douloi，單數形式為doulos，經常指“奴隸”，這裡可能指社會地位受到限制的僕人（見約8:34註釋）。這類僕人只能一味地順從主人而不能參與主人的謀劃。耶穌信任祂的門徒並將許多的事啟示他們。聖靈還要進一步教導他們（約14:26）。耶穌很快就會離開門徒，他們要在祂不在他們中間的情況下自己作工。他們的肩上會承擔相當重的責任。耶穌希望他們想到他們與祂之間是朋友的關係。祂按時說他們本是僕人（見約13:16），現在他們是祂的朋友。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《教育論》第94頁；《基督教育原理》第303頁；《傳道良助》第267頁；《證言》卷二第510頁。
15.en: **Servants.** Gr. douloi, singular doulos, often designating “slave,” here, perhaps, a servant with restricted status (see on ch. 8:34). A servant of this rank would be expected to obey blindly without being taken into the master’s counsels. Jesus had taken the disciples into His confidence and had revealed many things to them. The Holy Spirit would further enlighten them (ch. 14:26). Jesus was soon to leave them, and they were to labor on without His bodily presence. A weighty responsibility would be theirs. He wanted them to think of their relationship with Him as that of friends. Before, He had implied that they were servants (see ch. 13:16); now they were His friends.

21.zh:
但他們因我的名要向你們行這一切的事，因為他們不認識那差我來的。

**因我的名。**即，為了我的緣故或因為我。“名”經常代表一個人或他的品格（見太10:22；12:21）。
**不認識那差我來的。**他們自稱認識並敬拜上帝，但他們對祂的品格一無所知並且誤解祂的話。將這裡與約14:7；16:3；17:3進行比較。
21.en:
**For my name’s sake.** That is, for my sake, or, on my account. “Name” often stands for person or character (see Matt. 10:22; 12:21).
**Know not him.** They professed to know and worship God, but they were ignorant of His character and misconstrued His word. Compare chs. 14:7; 16:3; 17:3.

22.zh:
我若沒有來教訓他們，他們就沒有罪；但如今他們的罪無可推諉了。

**沒有罪。**見約9:41註釋。“世人矇昧無知的時候，上帝並不監察”（徒17:30）。但耶穌既然來了並將得救的道路顯示給他們，他們就沒有什麼藉口了。上帝還能給他們什麼更大的啟示呢？世人的罪在於不接受耶穌，“道路、真理、生命”（約14:6）。“人若知道行善，卻不去行，這就是他的罪了”（雅4:17）。世人在審判中被定罪不是因為他們曾經在錯誤中，而是他們“疏忽了天賜的機會，不去明白什麼是真理”（《歷代願望》490頁）。
**推諉。**prophasis，“藉口，託詞”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第164頁。
22.en:
**Not had sin.** See on ch. 9:41. “The times of this ignorance God winked at” (Acts 17:30). Now that Jesus had come and revealed to them the way of salvation, they were without excuse. What greater revelation of Himself could God have given? Their sin lay in not accepting Jesus, “the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14:6). “To him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin” (James 4:17). In the judgment men will be condemned not because they have been in error but because they “have neglected heaven-sent opportunities for learning what is truth” (DA 490).
**Cloke.** Gr. prophasis, “a pretext.”

23.zh:
恨我的，也恨我的父。

**也恨我的父。**將這裡與約13:20；14:7,9-11進行比較。
23.en: **Hateth my Father also.** Compare chs. 13:20; 14:7, 9–11.

24.zh:
我若沒有在他們中間行過別人未曾行的事，他們就沒有罪；但如今連我與我的父，他們也看見也恨惡了。

**事。**第22節是呼籲人們注意耶穌說過的話。這裡是呼籲他們注意祂做過的事。這兩方面都有充分的證據，可以讓人們建立信心，相信祂是世界的救贖主。
**沒有罪。**見第22節註釋。
24.en:
**The works.** In v. 22 the appeal was to the words that Jesus had spoken. Here the appeal is to the works. Either was sufficient evidence on which to base faith in Him as the Saviour of the world.
**Had not had sin.** See on v. 22.

25.zh:
這要應驗他們律法上所寫的話，說：他們無故的恨我。

……話。這句話在希臘原文中表示結果，而不是目的（見約9:3註釋；參太1:22註釋）。
**他們律法上。**見約10:34註釋。
**他們……恨我。**這裡可能引用詩69:4。將這裡與詩35:19進行比較。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》第32頁。
25.en:
**That the word.** The Greek of this clause may be interpreted as expressing result rather than purpose (see on John 9:3; cf. on Matt. 1:22).
**In their law.** See on ch. 10:34.
**They hated me.** The quotation is probably from Ps. 69:4. However, compare Ps. 35:19.

27.zh:
你們也要作見證，因為你們從起頭就與我同在。

**你們也要。**見徒5:32。
**從起頭。**他們就是這樣獲得作見證的資格（見徒1:21,22）。參“從起頭”（“從起初”）在約壹2:7,24；3:11；約貳5,6中的用法。
27.en:
**Ye also.** See Acts 5:32.
**From the beginning.** They were thus qualified to be witnesses (see Acts 1:21, 22). Compare the use of the phrase “from the beginning” in 1 John 2:7, 24; 3:11; 2 John 1:5, 6.

16.en:
**Another.** Gr. allos, “another of the same kind.” Jesus Himself was a Comforter (see 1 John 2:1, where “advocate” is the translation of the word here rendered “Comforter”; see below under “Comforter”). He would leave His disciples (John 13:33), but He would petition the Father to send One who was like Him to remain with the disciples, not temporarily, as He had remained, but “for ever.”
**Comforter.** Gr. paraklētos, a word used in the NT only by John (here; John 14:26; 15:26; 16:7; 1 John 2:1). It is made up of the preposition para, meaning, “beside,” and the adjective klētos, “called,” or “one called.” Hence the literal meaning is “one called to the side of.” However, in Scripture usage the word seems to reflect more of an active sense such as is found in the corresponding verb parakaleō, “to exhort,” “to comfort,” hence, “one who exhorts” (see John 16:8). The Latin Fathers translated paraklētos by advocatus, but the technical meaning, “advocate,” or “lawyer,” applies to only a few of the rare occurrences of the word in pre-Christian and non-Christian literature. The word “advocate” is not entirely appropriate to describe the work of either the Holy Spirit or Christ. The Father and Son work in the fullest cooperation for the salvation of man (ch. 10:30). It is Satan’s work to present the Father as stern and harsh and unwilling to forgive the sinner, and as willing to forgive only upon the intercession of the Son. It is true that the incarnation, death, and resurrection of Christ made forgiveness possible. But both the Father and the Son love the sinner and work in unison for his salvation. An advocate in the human sense of the term is not needed to induce the Father to have mercy on the sinner. He who desires to learn of the love and compassion of the Father need but look at the Son (see on ch. 1:18). Elsewhere in pre-Christian and non-Christian literature paraklētos retains the more general meaning of “one who stands up in behalf of another,” “a mediator,” “an intercessor,” “a helper.” See on Matt. 5:4.
The verb parakaleō, though translated “to comfort” 23 times in the NT, is also rendered “exhort” 19 times. To call the Holy Spirit a “Comforter” is to emphasize but one feature of His work. He is also an “Exhorter.” In fact, this latter meaning is the prominent feature of the work of the Spirit as outlined by John. He will “teach” and “bring all things to … remembrance” (ch. 14:26). He will testify of Christ (ch. 15:26). He will “reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment” (ch. 16:8). He will guide into all truth and show things to come (ch. 16:13). He will glorify Christ and receive from Him and impart to the disciples (ch. 16:14).
**For ever.** Not temporarily, like Christ during His earthly ministry.
16.zh:
我要求父，父就另外賜給你們一位保惠師（或作：訓慰師；下同），叫他永遠與你們同在，

**另外……一位。**allos，“另外相同的一位”。耶穌自己就是一位安慰者（見約壹2:1，譯成“中保””；見下面“保惠師”註釋）。耶穌將要離開祂的門徒（約13:33），但祂會求父差遣一位像祂的來與門徒們同在。祂來了，不像耶穌是暫時的。祂“永遠”與他們同在。
**保惠師（或作“訓慰師”；下同）。**paraklētos，該詞在《新約》中只有約翰使用過（本節；約14:26；15:26；16:7；約壹2:1）。它是由介詞para（“在……旁邊”）和形容詞klētos（“被呼叫的”或“被呼叫的一位”）組成的。因此paraklētos字面上的意思就是“能叫到身邊的一位”。然而，該詞在聖經中的用法似乎更多帶有主動意義，比如它相應的動詞parakaleō（“勸勉，”“安慰”，“安慰者”，見約16:8）所表達的。拉丁教父們將paraklētos譯成advocatus，但是其學術含義“辯護人”或“律師”只適合在基督教以前的文學或非基督教文學中的少數情況。“中保”不能充分描述聖靈或基督的工作。父與子在拯救人類的工作上完全合作（約10:30）。撒但的工作就是要將天父刻畫成嚴厲、苛暴、不肯饒恕人的，並且說天父只肯原諒那些有子從中代為求情的人。基督的道成肉身、受死以及復活使赦免成為可能，這是真理。但是，父與子都愛罪人，並且為他們的得救通力合作。天父並不需要人觀念中的辯護者來引發對罪人的憐憫。那些想要了解天父慈愛與憐憫的人只需要看看子就可以了（見約1:18註釋）。在基督教以前的文學和非基督教文學中的其他地方，paraklētos更多的是泛指“一個為另一人站起來的人”，“一位調停者”，“一位幫助者”。見太5:4註釋。
動詞parakaleō在《新約》中儘管有23次譯為“安慰”但是還有19次譯成“勸勉”。將聖靈稱為“安慰者”只是強調了祂工作的一方面性質。祂也是“勸勉者”。實際上後一種意思才是約翰所描述聖靈工作的主要特色。聖靈要“指教”並“叫你們想起……一切話”（約14:26）。祂要為基督作見證（約15:26）。祂“要叫世人為罪、為義、為審判，自己責備自己”（約16:8）。祂要引導你們進入一切的真理並要把將來的事告訴你們（約16:13）。祂要榮耀基督，並要將受於基督的告訴門徒（約16:14）。
**永遠。**不像基督在世的服務是暫時的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第249頁；《給傳道人的證言》第218，517頁；《證言》卷八第19頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–17節）**。《使徒行述》第47頁；《今日的生活》第36頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–18節）**。《歷代願望》第669頁。

15.en:
**If ye love me.** Love is the motive power of obedience. For a definition of “love” see on Matt. 5:43, 44; 1 Cor. 13:1. Obedience that springs from compulsion or from fear is not the ideal form of obedience. There may be times, of course, where the motive power of love is lacking or weak. It is necessary under those circumstances to render obedience from principle alone. In the meantime love should be cultivated. A lack of the requisite love should never be made an excuse for disobedience. One of the best human illustrations of obedience that springs from love is that of children to their parents.
**Keep my commandments.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between this and the reading “you will keep my commandments.” In the latter reading the Greek verb is in the future tense, which may also be translated as an imperative, as in Matt. 22:37, 39. If translated thus, there is little difference between the readings. However, the indicative “you will keep” brings out the significant thought that obedience is the natural result of love. The parallel statement in John 14:23 is clearly in the indicative mood, and hence supports this thought.
The commandments of Jesus were also the commandments of the Father, for Jesus spake not of Himself (chs. 12:49; 14:10). He endorsed the moral commands given to ancient Israel (see on Matt. 5:17–19) and magnified them (see on Isa. 42:21). He gave commands of His own, such as the new commandment (John 13:34), not to replace any of the moral precepts, which reflected the character of the unchangeable God, but to set forth their true meaning and to show how their principles should be applied to various life situations.
15.zh:
你們若愛我，就必遵守我的命令。

**你們若愛我。**愛是順從的原動力。關於“愛”的定義，見太5:43,44；林前13:1註釋。出自勉強或懼怕的順從不是真正的順從。當然，有的時候，愛這種原動力也會缺乏或軟弱。在這些情況下我們就必須使順從成為一種原則，而同時，也應該積極地培養我們的愛。我們缺乏應有的愛，這決不能成為我們悖逆的藉口。人世間出於愛的順從最好的說明就是孩童對他們父母親的順從。
**就必遵守我的命令。**有文本為“應當遵守我的命令”。參太22:37,39。前者表達了一個重要的概念，即順從是愛的自然結果。約14:23類似的句子顯然就用了陳述語氣，可以作為這種概念的佐證。
耶穌的命令也是父的命令，因為耶穌不是憑著自己說的（約12:49；14:10）。祂認同從前傳給古以色列人的道德律法（見太5:17-19註釋）並使其尊大（見賽42:21註釋）。祂給出祂自己的命令，比如說那條新命令（約13:34），不是要取代道德律法中的任何一條，因為那律法是反照不變上帝之品格的。祂這樣做是要顯出律法的真意，並告訴人們這些原則在不同的生活情況中如何應用。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第143，283頁；《歷代願望》第668頁；《基督教育原理》第125頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–17節）**。《證言》卷五第432頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–19節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第137頁。

21.en:
**Hath my commandments.** That is, knows and understands them. But this is not sufficient. It is necessary also to keep them. A conviction of Christian duty must be followed by prompt obedience.
**Loveth me.** This statement is the converse of v. 15. Love manifests itself in obedience; obedience is a mark of love (cf. 1 John 2:3–6).
**Loved of my Father.** . Compare ch. 16:27. In ch. 3:16 the Father’s love for the world was emphasized. Here His love for His own is highlighted. Where there is a response to divine love there can be a greater manifestation of that love. Satan had led men to look upon God as severe and unforgiving. Jesus had come to alter that concept. He taught men that His Father’s love was like His own.
**Manifest myself.** Probably primarily a reference to the fuller revelation of Christ through the Spirit.
21.zh:
有了我的命令又遵守的，這人就是愛我的；愛我的必蒙我父愛他，我也要愛他，並且要向他顯現。

**有了我的命令。**即知道和理解它們。但這還不夠，還必須要遵守。認識基督徒的職責必須伴隨著果斷的順從。
**愛我的。**這是從反面陳述第15節的內容。愛在順從裡面彰顯出來；順從是愛的標誌（參見約壹2:3-6）。
**必蒙我父愛他。**將這裡與約16:27進行比較。約3:16強調了天父對世人的愛。這裡強調的是天父對屬祂自己之人的愛。哪裡有對上帝之愛的回應，哪裡就有這愛更大的彰顯。撒但誘導世人看上帝是嚴厲而不肯饒恕人的。耶穌來就是要改變這種觀念。祂教導世人，祂父的慈愛和祂對他們的愛是一樣的。
**顯現。**可能主要指基督通過聖靈更充分的啟示。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第85頁；《基督比喻實訓》第143，283頁；《給管家的勉言》第346頁；《歷代願望》第669頁；《基督教育原理》第125，399頁；《給青年人的信息》第409頁；《給傳道人的證言》第68，137頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–24節）**。《證言》卷五第432頁。

3.en:
**If I go.** This conditional clause was not intended to introduce an uncertainty. The word translated “if” (ean) here has temporal force, and should probably be translated “when,” as in 1 Cor. 14:16; 1 John 3:2.
**I will come again.** The Greek expresses this promise in the present tense. This so-called futuristic present gives emphasis to the certainty of the event. The event is thought of as being so certain as to be already taking place. The reference is clearly to the personal advent of Jesus vividly described a few days earlier in answer to the question, “What shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” (see on Matt. 24:1–3; see vs. 30, 31).
**Receive.** Gr. paralambanō, literally, “to receive to the side of” (see on Matt. 24:40).
**Where I am.** The disciples were directed to the time of the second advent as the moment when they would be reunited with their Lord. There is no hint here of the popular doctrine that believers go to be with their Lord at the time of death. Nor is this doctrine upheld elsewhere in the Scriptures. Paul also directed the attention of believers to the time of the second advent as the moment of grand reunion (1 Thess. 4:16, 17).
Jesus has gone to His Father’s house. He is waiting with longing desire for the manifestation of Himself in His church. When His image shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come (COL 69). It is our privilege to hasten the day of glorious home-coming (2 Peter. 3:12; cf. DA 633, 634; COL 69).
3.zh:
我若去為你們預備了地方，就必再來接你們到我那裡去，我在哪裡，叫你們也在那裡。

**我若去。**這個條件狀語從句不是要提出一種不確定性。“若”的希臘文詞語ean含有時間的意思，可譯為“當……的時候”，參林前14:16；約壹3:2。
**就必再來。**希臘文表達這個應許時用現在時態。這種所謂的將來現在時強調事件的確定性。這件事被認為是非常確定的，就像已經發生一樣。這顯然是指耶穌的再來，就是幾天前在回答“你降臨和世界的末了有什麼預兆呢？”（見太24:1-3註釋；見太24:30,31）時所生動描述的。
**接。**paralambanō，直譯是“接到……的身邊”（見太24:40註釋）。
**我在那裡。**門徒們得到指示，耶穌再來之時就是他們與他們主的重逢之日。這裡絲毫沒有暗示可以證明一種非常流行的學說，即，信的人在他們死的時候就與主在一起了。聖經其他地方也沒有證據支持這種觀點。同樣，保羅也提醒信徒注意，耶穌再臨時才是莊嚴偉大的重逢之日（帖前4:16,17）。
耶穌去了祂父的家裡。祂一直在迫切地等待，等待祂自己在祂的教會中彰顯出來。當祂的子民完全再現了祂的形象時，祂就會回來了（《基督比喻實訓》69頁）。我們有權催促榮耀天家來臨的日子（彼後3:12；參《歷代願望》633，634頁；《基督比喻實訓》69頁）
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第34，536頁；《健康勉言》第213頁；《基督比喻實訓》第40頁；《歷代願望》第832頁；《善惡之爭》第339頁；《給傳道人的證言》第130頁。

25.en: **Present with you.** That is, in the flesh, before His departure and before the coming of the other “Comforter” (v. 16). Jesus was limited as to the information He could impart to them at the present time (ch. 16:12).
25.zh:
我還與你們同住的時候，已將這些話對你們說了。

**與你們同住。**即，在祂離開和“訓慰師”（第16節）到來之前，以血肉之體與他們同住。耶穌現在所能給他們的信息是有限制的（約16:12）。

6.en:
**I am the way.** Another of the famous “I am” sayings of Jesus (see on ch. 6:35; see chs. 8:12; 10:7, 11; 11:25). For the use of the expression “I am” without the pronoun “he” see on ch. 8:24.
Christ is the way from earth to heaven. By His humanity He touches this earth, and by His divinity He touches heaven. He is the ladder connecting earth and heaven (ch. 1:51; cf. PP 184). Because of His incarnation and death “a new and living way” has been consecrated for us (Heb. 10:20). There is no other means of salvation (Acts 4:12; 1 Tim. 2:5).
**Truth.** See on ch. 8:32.
**Life.** See on chs. 1:4; 8:51; 10:10.
6.zh:
耶穌說我就是道路、真理、生命；若不藉著我，沒有人能到父那裡去。

**我就是道路。**這是耶穌又一次著名的“我是”（見約6:35註釋；見約8:12；10:7,11；11:25）。關於不帶代詞“他”的“我是”，其用法見約8:24註釋。
基督是從地上通向天國的道路。祂用祂的人性觸摸這世界，用祂的神性握住天國。祂是連接天地的梯子（約1:51；參《先祖與先知》184頁）。藉著道成肉身和受死，耶穌為我們“開了一條又新又活的路”（來10:20）。祂是唯一的拯救（徒4:12；提前2:5）。
**真理。**見約8:32註釋。
**生命。**見約1:4；8:51；10:10註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《文字佈道士》第63頁；《基督比喻實訓》第40，105，173頁；《安息日學訓言》第85頁；《對作者和編輯的勉言》第120頁；《歷代願望》第24，353頁；《佈道論》第290頁；《基督教育原理》第239，251，399，405，466頁；《傳道良助》第154，263頁；《今日的生活》第260頁；《醫療佈道論》第22，327頁；《拾級就主》第21頁；《給傳道人的證言》第105，332頁；《證言》卷二第170頁；《證言》卷三第193頁；《證言》卷四第230，316頁；《證言》卷五第49頁；《證言》卷六第67頁；《證言》卷七第38頁；《證言》卷八第210頁；見羅8:31懷愛倫註釋。

2.en:
**My Father’s house.** A beautiful representation of heaven. The word for “house” (Gr. oikia) may also be translated “home.” It is thus rendered in Matt. 8:6. The masculine form, oikos, is translated “home” in Mark 5:19; Luke 15:6; 1 Cor. 11:34; 14:35. Jesus was returning to His home. Eventually the disciples would be permitted to join Him there.
**Mansions.** Gr. monai (singular monē) literally, “abiding places.” In non-Biblical Greek literature the word sometimes has the meaning of temporary stopping places. From this concept Origen drew his false notion that the mansions were halting places in the soul’s journey to God (see De Principiis ii. 11. 6). But such is not the scriptural meaning of monai. This is clear from v. 23, the only other occurrence of the word in the Bible. Certainly the abode of Christ and the Father with the Christian is no temporary affair. The idea of permanence in monē is reflected in 1 Macc. 7:38, the only occurrence of the word in the LXX.
Our English word “mansion” is from the Latin mansio, in meaning almost equivalent to the Gr. monē. Mansio, as does monē, means “a remaining place,” “a place of abode.” The idea of a building of some size or pretentiousness does not attach to the Latin, nor, of course, to the Greek. That idea was a later development of the English word and the meaning should not be introduced into the present verse. Either “mansion” should be understood in its archaic sense of “a dwelling place,” or “abode,” or one of these meanings should be substituted in a translation of the verse.
The fact that there are “many” dwelling places makes certain of sufficient room in the Father’s house for all who heed the Father’s invitation.
**I go.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the insertion before “I go” of the Greek conjunction hoti, meaning, “for,” “that,” or “because.” If it is omitted there is a complete stop after the preceding clause, as in the KJV. If it is included there is some question as to how the clause that it introduces should be connected to the preceding. Several translations are possible: (1) “If it were not so I would have told you that I go to prepare a place for you.” This translation is ruled out because, according to v. 3, such was one of the objects of Jesus’ departure. (2) “If it were not so, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you?” This translation overcomes the difficulty of No. 1, but introduces a new problem in that there is no record of Jesus’ having told His disciples that He was going to prepare a place for them. It is, of course, possible that such a statement was simply left unrecorded. (3) “There are many abiding places (and if it were not so I would have told you), for I go to prepare a place for you” (see C. K. Barrett, The Gospel According to St. John, on ch. 14:2). If textual evidence is held to be in favor of including the hoti, the last translation seems to be the most natural. However, the text is perfectly intelligible if the conjunction is omitted.
These words were designed to comfort the disciples. Jesus was leaving, but He would not forget them. He would eagerly anticipate His reunion with them in the Father’s house. In the interval He would prepare for the glorious home-coming.
2.zh:
在我父的家裡有許多住處；若是沒有，我就早已告訴你們了。我去原是為你們預備地方去。

**我父的家裡。**這是對天國的美稱。家（oikia）也可譯成“屋子”。參太8:6。其陽性形式oikos在可5:19；路15:5；林前11:34；14:35等中都譯成了“家”。耶穌是要回祂自己的家了。最終門徒們也要得到允許與祂同在那裡。
**住處。**monai（單數是monē）。該詞在非聖經的希臘文學作品中有時指暫時停留的地方。奧利金據此得出一種錯誤的看法，即這個詞是指人的靈魂前往上帝那裡去的旅途中暫時歇息的地方（見De Principiis ii. 11. 6）。但這不是monai在經文中的意思。這一點從第23節中可以清楚地看出來。monai在聖經中只在出現這裡和第23節中。基督和天父為基督徒準備的住所肯定不是臨時性的。monē的永久性在《馬加比上》7:38中反映出來。該詞在七十士譯本中只出現在那裡。
英語的“住宅”（mansion）就來自於拉丁語的mansio，意思上基本上相當於希臘語的monē。Mansio，和monē一樣，意為“一個住處”。該詞在拉丁文和希臘文中不是指一定大小或裝飾的建築物，故不要從這方面來理解。
有“許多”住處的事實，確定在天父家裡有足夠的空間為所有接受天父邀請的人存留。
**我去。**有文本在“我去”之前還有“因為”（hoti）。如果沒有這個連詞，前面的句子結束後就是一個完全的停頓。如果有這個連詞，就會把前後的句子連接起來。有幾種可能的譯法：（1）“若是沒有，我會告訴你們我去是為你們預備地方去。”這種譯法要排除，因為根據第3節，為他們預備地方是耶穌離去的目的之一。（2）“若是沒有，我豈不是早告訴你們我去是為你們預備地方去嗎？”這種譯法克服了第一種譯法的困難，但產生了一個新的問題，從來沒有記載說耶穌曾經告訴祂的門徒祂將要去為他們預備地方。當然，也有可能是因為沒有留下記錄。（3）“有許多住的地方（若是沒有我就告訴你們了），因為我去是為你們預備地方去”（見C. K.巴雷特《約翰福音》14:2註釋）。如果按照原文的證據加上hoti這個連詞，最後一種譯法似乎是最自然的。但即便沒有這個連詞，上下文的意思也是完全可以理解的。
耶穌這些話是要安慰祂的門徒。耶穌將要離開，但祂卻不會忘掉他們。祂熱切期望著與他們在祂父的家裡重新團聚。在這個間隙他要為將來榮耀的家做準備。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第120，146，287頁；《早期著作》第18頁；《傳道良助》第259頁；《今日的生活》第84，337，338頁；《醫療佈道論》第327頁；《給青年人的信息》第410頁；《救贖的故事》第430頁；《證言》卷八第140頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《安息日學訓言》第79頁；《早期著作》第190頁；《善惡之爭》第548頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第50頁；《證言》卷一第41頁；《證言》卷四第490頁；《證言》卷五第732頁；《證言》卷六第368頁；見徒1:11懷愛倫註釋。

27.en:
**Peace.** Gr. eirēnē, corresponding to the Heb. shalom, the common Oriental greeting used by Jesus in His postresurrection appearances (ch. 20:19, 21, 26). Here Jesus speaks of inward peace of soul such as comes to him who is “justified by faith” (Rom. 5:1), whose sense of guilt has been laid at the foot of the cross, and whose anxieties about the future have been swallowed up in his implicit trust in God (Phil. 4:6, 7). Such a peace Jesus terms “my peace.” Such a peace the world, with all its boasted science, cannot bestow. Compare John 16:33.
**Troubled.** Compare v. 1.
**Be afraid.** Gr. deiliaō, “to be fainthearted,to be cowardly.”
27.zh:
我留下平安給你們；我將我的平安賜給你們。我所賜的，不像世人所賜的。你們心裡不要憂愁，也不要膽怯。

**平安。**eirēnē，相當於希伯來文詞語shalom，是耶穌在復活之後顯現時常用的一種東方式問候語（約20:19,21,26）。耶穌這裡所說的是一種心靈內在的平安，就是臨到那些“因信稱義”（羅5:1）之人的平安。他們的負疚感已放在十字架的腳下，他們對將來的憂慮，也被他們對上帝的絕對信靠所吞滅（腓4:6,7）。耶穌將這種平安稱作“我的平安”。這個世界，就是用上它所誇耀的一切科學，也不能給人這樣的平安。將這裡與約16:33進行比較。
**憂愁。**將這裡與第1節進行比較。
**膽怯。**deiliaō，“懦弱的，膽小的”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第84頁；《歷代願望》第659，672頁；《福山寶訓》第16頁；《服務真詮》第123，247頁；《今日的生活》第77，176頁；《拾級就主》第124頁。

14.en:
**If ye shall ask.** As this verse reads in the KJV it is an emphatic repetition of the promise of v. 13. However, textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 146) for the insertion of the pronoun “me” after the verb “ask.” This reading would imply that petitions may be directed to Jesus as well as to the Father, as chs 15:16; 16:23 indicate. There are several NT examples of prayers directed to Jesus (Acts 7:59; Rev. 22:20). However, the expression “ask me any thing in my name” is awkward, and hence the reading that includes the pronoun “me” should probably be rejected.
**I will do it.** The “I” is emphatic in the Greek, whereas in v. 13 it is not.
14.zh:
你們若奉我的名求什麼，我必成就。

**你們若……求什麼。**這是第13節應許的重複。有文本在“求”後面加上“我”，參約15:16；16:23，暗示祈求即呈到父那裡，也呈到耶穌那裡。在《新約》中有許多直接向耶穌禱告的例子（徒7:59；啟22:20）。但是“奉我的名求我什麼”似乎不合情理，因此不宜採用“我”字。
**我必成就。**這裡的“我”在希臘原文中是強調的，但它在第13節中就沒有強調。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第226頁；《善惡之爭》第477頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《基督教育原理》第399頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–21節）**。《歷代願望》第377-382頁。

28.en:
**I go away.** See vs. 2, 3; cf. ch. 7:33.
**Come again.** See vs. 3, 18.
**If ye loved me.** The disciples loved Jesus, but not with the fullness of love with which they would have loved Him had they more fully understood Him and His mission.
**Ye would rejoice.** Had the disciples understood more fully the humiliation of Jesus in His incarnation, and also more fully His exaltation to follow His resurrection, and had they contemplated more fully the loneliness of Jesus during His separation from the Father, they would have rejoiced at the fact that He was returning to His Father. Furthermore, had they understood that the departure of Jesus would be to their own advantage (ch. 16:7), and that His ascension and mediation in the heavenly sanctuary was an important step in the working out of the plan of salvation, they would have further rejoiced. At the moment their thoughts seemed to be selfishly concentrated on themselves. They were fearful as they contemplated meeting life’s problems without the bodily presence of their Master.
**My Father is greater than I.** With reference to His preincarnation state the Scriptures declare that Christ “thought it not robbery to be equal with God” (Phil. 2:6; see on John 1:1–3). Yet He “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant” (Phil. 2:7; cf. Heb. 2:9; see Additional Note on John 1). However, even in His incarnation Jesus declared that He was one with the Father (John 10:30). Any inferiority the statement in ch. 14:28 seems to assign to Christ should be understood with reference to His incarnation, for after the crucifixion God highly exalted Him, and gave Him a name that is above every name (Phil. 2:9). He was “equal with the Father” (8T 268). See further on 1 Cor. 15:27, 28.
28.zh:
你們聽見我對你們說了，我去還要到你們這裡來。你們若愛我，因我到父那裡去，就必喜樂，因為父是比我大的。

**我去。**見第2,3節；參約7:33。
**還要……來。**見第3,18節。
**你們若愛我。**門徒們愛耶穌，但是他們若不能充分了解祂和祂的使命，就不能用全部的愛來愛祂。
**就必喜樂。**如果門徒能完全瞭解耶穌在祂道成肉身中所有的屈辱，如果他們能瞭解他復活之後的尊榮，如果他們能認識到耶穌在這段與父分離時期中所有的孤獨，當他們看到祂回到祂父那裡去時，他們就會滿心喜樂了。此外，當他們認識到耶穌的離去是與他們有益的（約16:7），認識到祂的昇天以及祂在天上聖所中的中保工作是實現救贖計劃重要一步的時候，他們就要更加喜樂了。現在他們的思想好像都自私地集中在他們自己身上。他們一想到將來要面對的生活中的困難，又沒有他們肉身的主與他們同在，就恐慌懼怕起來。
**父是比我大的。**提到耶穌道成肉身之前的地位，經上說基督“不以自己與上帝同等為強奪的”（腓2:6；見約1:1-3註釋）。祂“反倒虛己，取了奴僕的形像”（腓2:7；參來2:9；見《約翰福音》第1章補充註釋）。但即便成為肉身，耶穌還是宣佈祂與父原為一（約10:30）。約14:28中似乎說耶穌為的話，應從祂道成肉身的角度來理解，因為在祂被釘十字架後，上帝使祂高升，並賜給他一個超乎萬名之上的名（腓2:9）。祂“與父是平等的”（《教會證言》卷八第268頁）詳見林前15:27,28註釋。

17.en:
**Spirit of truth.** This expression occurs again in chs. 15:26; 16:13. The emphasis seems to be upon the fact that the Spirit defines, imparts, and defends truth. For a definition of truth see on ch. 8:32. The Spirit would guide the disciples “into all truth” (ch. 16:13).
**World.** Gr. kosmos (see on Matt. 4:8).
**Seeth him not.** The pronoun “him” refers to the Spirit, as is clearly evident in the Greek. The world lacks spiritual perception. “The natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God” (1 Cor. 2:14).
**Neither knoweth him.** If the disciples at Ephesus baptized “unto John’s baptism” had “not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost” (Acts 19:1–3), much less would the world have any knowledge concerning Him. The world neither knew of His existence nor recognized His call to repentance (see Gen. 6:3; Rev. 22:17).
**Ye.** The pronoun is emphatic in the Greek. The disciples are strongly contrasted with the world.
**With you.** That is, with the church. The phrase “in you” emphasizes the indwelling of the Spirit in the hearts of individual Christians.
17.zh:
就是真理的聖靈，乃世人不能接受的；因為不見他，也不認識他。你們卻認識他，因他常與你們同在，也要在你們裡面。

**真理的聖靈。**這個短語還出現在約15:26；16:13中。這裡強調聖靈顯明真理，聖靈傳授並維護真理。關於真理的定義，見約8:32註釋。聖靈將引導門徒們“進入一切的真理”（約16:13）。
**世人。**kosmos見太4:8註釋。
**不見祂。**希臘文清楚地顯示，這裡的代詞“祂”是指聖靈。世人缺乏屬靈的見解。“屬血氣的人不領會上帝聖靈的事”（林前2:14）。
**也不認識祂。**連以弗所受了“約翰的洗”的門徒都“未曾聽見有聖靈賜下來”（徒19:1-3），那就更不用說世人了，他們對聖靈的認識會更少。世人既不知道祂的存在，也沒有意識到祂呼籲他們悔改（見創6:3；啟22:17）。
**你們。**這個代詞在希臘文中是強調。門徒與世人形成強烈的對比。
**常與你們同在。**即與教會同在。“在你們裡面”強調聖靈住在每一個基督徒心裡。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第494，671頁；《拾級就主》第74頁。

30.en:
**Prince of this world.** For this title see on ch. 12:31.
**Cometh.** A reference to approaching events—Gethsemane, the arrest, trial, condemnation, and crucifixion of the Son of man, in which the prince of this world would make his supreme effort to defeat the plan of salvation. But Jesus drank the cup to the bitter end, and when He declared, “It is finished” (ch. 19:30), the death knell of the prince of darkness was sounded. Satan had found nothing in Jesus that responded to his sophistry (see DA 123).
30.zh:
以後我不再和你們多說話，因為這世界的王將到。他在我裡面是毫無所有；

**世界的王。**關於這個稱呼，見約12:31註釋。
**將到。**這是指即將發生的大事──人子在客西馬尼，祂的被捕、審訊、定罪以及被釘。在這所有的事中，這世界的王要用盡一切努力來挫敗救贖的計劃。但是耶穌喝盡了苦杯。當祂宣佈“成了”（約19:30）的時候，那黑暗之君的喪鐘就敲響了。耶穌至死忍耐，絲毫沒有回應撒但的詭計（見《歷代願望》123頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《論飲食》第153頁；《歷代願望》第123，679頁；《善惡之爭》第623頁；《論節制》第286頁；《證言》卷五第293，422頁。

1.en:
**Let not your heart be troubled.** Or, “stop letting your heart be troubled.” The disciples were troubled because Jesus had announced that He would soon leave them (ch. 13:33). He now proceeded to tell them that His absence would be only temporary, and that His departure would be for their benefit. Chapter 14 continues the conversational sequence begun in ch. 13:31 (see comment there).
**Ye believe.** Gr. pisteuete, which may be translated either “ye believe,” or “believe,” as in the next clause. In form pisteuete may be either imperative (believe [ye]) or indicative (ye believe). In Greek the imperative and indicative forms in the tense here employed are identical. Hence the context must determine the choice of mood. This allows for several possible combinations: (1) both verbs imperative, “Believe in God, believe also in me”; (2) both verbs indicative, “Ye believe in God and ye believe also in me”; (3) the first verb indicative and the second imperative, as in the KJV; (4) the first imperative and the second indicative, “believe in God and ye believe in me”; this last combination makes for a somewhat awkward construction and is the least likely of the four, but the other three are entirely consistent with the context. When the first element is regarded as imperative the admonition is in harmony with instruction earlier given to “have faith in God” (Mark 11:22).
The discourse of ch. 14 was given in the upper room prior to the departure to the Mount of Olives and Gethsemane (see on ch. 13:31).
1.zh:
你們心裡不要憂愁；你們信神，也當信我。

**你們心裡不要憂愁。**門徒心裡憂愁是因為耶穌說祂快就要離開他們（約13:33）。祂現在接著告訴他們，祂的離去只是暫時的，並且他的離開是為了他們的益處。第14章繼續了約13:31開始的談話（見該處註釋）。
**你們信。**pisteuete，可以是陳述語氣：“你們相信”，也可以是祈使語氣：“你們要相信”。因此必須根據上下文來確定。這就出現以下幾種可能的組合：（1）兩個動詞都是祈使語氣：“要信上帝，也要信我”；（2）兩個動詞都是陳述語氣：“你們信上帝，你們也信我”；（3）第一個動詞是陳述語氣，第二個是祈使語氣：“你們信上帝，也當信我”。（4）第一個動詞是祈使語氣，第二個是陳述語氣：“你們當信上帝，你們信我”。這最後一種組合不太合適，因此是四種組合裡面可能性最小的一個。而其他三種組合則完全符合上下文。若把第一個成分被看作祈使語氣，這裡的教訓就與先前的命令“當信服上帝”（可11:22）相一致了。
第14章的教訓是他們起身往橄欖山和客西馬尼園去之前在最後晚餐的樓上賜下的（見約13:31註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第123頁；《論福利工作》第22頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–33節）**。《善惡之爭》第301頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第293頁；《證言》卷八第254頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–4節）**。《使徒行述》第21頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–9節）**。《歷代願望》第663頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–10節）**。《服務真詮》第419頁；《證言》卷八第266頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–31節）**。《歷代願望》第662-673頁。

23.en:
**If a man love me.** Jesus does not answer Judas’ question directly. He calls attention to the conditions upon which the manifestation to which He referred (see on v. 22) will be made to the individual believer.
**Words.** Literally, “word,” here synonymous with “commandments” (see vs. 15, 21).
**We will come.** The plural emphasizes the oneness of the Father and the Son. They “come,” here, to dwell mystically in the heart of the believer. Thus there is a oneness not only between the Father and the Son but between the Father, the Son, and the believer (see TM 519).
**Abode.** Gr. monē (see on v. 2).
23.zh:
耶穌回答說：人若愛我，就必遵守我的道；我父也必愛他，並且我們要到他那裡去，與他同住。

**人若愛我。**耶穌沒有直接回答猶大的問題。祂讓他們注意祂所提到（見第22節註釋）要向信徒個人顯現的條件。
**道。**這裡與“命令”是同義詞（見第15,21節）。
**我們要到他那裡去。**複數“我們”強調父與子的合一。祂們要“到”他們那裡去，以一種奇異的方式住在相信之人的心裡。因此，不僅父與子之間有合一，父、子與相信的人之間也是合一的（見《給傳道人的證言》第519頁）。
**住。**monē（見第2節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第61頁；《給傳道人的證言》第169頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（23–24節）**。《基督教育原理》第125頁；《給傳道人的證言》第137頁。

19.en:
**A little while.** Compare chs. 13:33; 16:16–22.
**But ye see me.** After the crucifixion and burial the world would see Jesus no more. But the disciples would see Him in His resurrected body. The words doubtless have also a spiritual significance. Even after the ascension the disciples would continue to see Jesus with their spiritual faculties.
**Ye shall live.** Both in a spiritual and in a literal sense (ch. 6:57).
19.zh:
還有不多的時候，世人不再看見我，你們卻看見我；因為我活著，你們也要活著。

**不多的時候。**將這裡與約13:33；16:16-22進行比較。
**你們卻看見我。**耶穌被釘以及埋葬之後世人就再也看不見祂了。但是門徒能夠看見他復活之後的身體。這些話顯然還有一層屬靈的意義。即便在耶穌昇天之後，門徒們也能用他們屬靈的感官繼續看見祂。
**你們也要活著。**這是指屬靈和字面兩層意思（約6:57）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第244頁；《今日的生活》第295頁；《給傳道人的證言》第95頁。

26.en:
**Comforter.** Gr. paraklētos (see on v. 16).
**Holy Ghost.** Rather, “Holy Spirit.” “Ghost” is an obsolete form of “Spirit.” The expression “Holy Ghost” occurs 89 times in the NT, and the expression “Holy Spirit” 4 times. Both are translations of the same Greek phrase. The word “Spirit” without the qualifying adjective is frequent.
**He.** Literally, “that one.” The antecedent is “Comforter,” which in the Greek is masculine and hence calls for the personal pronoun “he.”
**Teach you all things.** One of the principal functions of the Holy Spirit is teaching. Much of Jesus’ work was teaching (see on Luke 4:15). Forty-one times the word “Master” in the NT is from the Gr. didaskalos, meaning, “teacher.” For three years the disciples had been under the instruction of the Master Teacher, but there were still many things for them to learn. They were unable in their present state of mind to comprehend many of the truths (John 16:12). They would need further instruction, and this the Holy Spirit would give to them. The Spirit of God knows the “things of God” and “searcheth all things, year, the deep things of God” (1 Cor. 2:10, 11), and He is able to impart them to men who are willing to be instructed.
**To your remembrance.** Not only would the Spirit reveal new truths; He would also call to mind truths that had slipped from the mind, of those things Jesus had taught, or of those things that had earlier been revealed in the Scriptures of truth. In moments of crisis, such as when the disciples would be haled into court, the Spirit would bring the appropriate ideas into mind (Matt 10:19, 20). When asked to give a reason for the hope that is in them (1 Peter 3:15), Christians who have been diligent students of the Bible may have the confidence that the Holy Spirit will call to mind passages suited to the occasion.
26.zh:
但保惠師，就是父因我的名所要差來的聖靈，他要將一切的事指教你們，並且要叫你們想起我對你們所說的一切話。

**保惠師。**paraklētos（見第16節註釋）。
**聖靈。**“聖靈”在《舊約》中出現過93次。經常單用“靈”，
**祂。**直譯是“那一位”，指“保惠師”，在希臘文中是陽性的。
**將一切的事指教你們。**聖靈的主要職責之一便是教導。耶穌的大部分工作也是教導（見路4:15註釋）。“夫子”在《新約》中出現了41次，它來自希臘詞語didaskalos，意思是“教師”。門徒們在他們的夫子門下受教達三年之久，但他們還有許多東西需要去學習。以他們現在的思想狀態來說，他們還有許多真理不能理解（約16:12）。他們還需要進一步的指導，而這種指導就是聖靈要賜給他們的。上帝的靈知道“上帝的事”並“參透萬事，就是上帝深奧的事也參透了”（林前2:10,11），聖靈還將這些事指示凡願受教的人。
**叫你們想起。**聖靈不僅啟示新的真理；還要使人們回想起已經忘記的真理，就是那些耶穌教導過的或真理的經文中所啟示過的。在危急的時刻，比如門徒們被帶到審判庭前時，聖靈就會將合適的思想放進他們的頭腦之中（太10:19,20）。當被問到心中盼望的緣由（彼前3:15），那些平時殷勤學習聖經的基督徒就會確信，聖靈要使他們想起合適的章節來應對當前的局面。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第52頁；《健康勉言》第371，561頁；《安息日學訓言》第39，41，160頁；《基督教育之研究》第357，450頁；《歷代願望》第670頁；《教育論》第94頁；《基督教育原理》第433，473頁；《善惡之爭》第八章，600頁；《今日的生活》第45頁；《給青年人的信息》第259頁；《先知與君王》第627頁；《給傳道人的證言》第111，476頁；《證言》卷六第249頁；《證言》卷八第19頁；見羅2:4懷愛倫註釋；.。

31.en:
**That the world may know.** There is an ellipsis here, and some such words as “these things are taking place that the world may know, etc.,” should be supplied. The purpose clause may also be understood as a clause of result (see on ch. 9:3); that is, as a result of the events about to take place the world would be given a demonstration of Jesus’ love for the Father.
**Arise, let us go hence.** After Jesus and His disciples “had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives” (Matt. 26:30). The hymn was part of the Passover Hallel (see on Matt. 26:30). Many scholars think that the discourse of John 15; 16 and the prayer of ch. 17 were also given in the upper room, but there is no need to suppose a transposition in these chapters. The instruction of these chapters would have been as appropriate or even more so among the scenes of nature on the way to Gethsemane, especially with flourishing grapevines to illustrate the allegory of the vine and its branches (see DA 674). The slopes of Olivet had been the scene of extended instruction only two nights before (see on Matt. 24:1).
31.zh:
但要叫世人知道我愛父，並且父怎樣吩咐我，我就怎樣行。起來，我們走吧！

**但要叫世人知道。**這是一個省略句，前面應加上“這些事發生”。這裡既可以理解為目的狀語從句，也可以理解為結果狀語從句（見約9:3註釋）。即由於即將發生的事情，世人知道了耶穌對天父的愛。
**起來，我們走吧。**耶穌和祂的門徒“唱了詩，就出來往橄欖山去”（太26:30）。讚美詩是逾越節詩歌的一部分（見太26:30註釋）。許多學者認為《約翰福音》第15；16章的教訓以及第17章的禱告都是在逾越節晚餐的樓上發生的，但不必要推測這幾章順序的調換。這些章節的教訓和往客西馬尼園去沿途的自然景色非常相配，特別是茁壯茂盛、果實累累的葡萄園，正好用來說明葡萄樹和枝子的比喻（見《歷代願望》674頁）。橄欖山的山坡正是兩天前耶穌賜下長篇教訓的地點（見太24:1註釋）。

13.en:
**Whatsoever ye shall ask.** As the disciples would cooperate with Heaven in the promulgation of the gospel, they could rest assured that the boundless resources of Omnipotence were at their disposal. God would supply their every need and honor the petitions lodged before the throne in the name of Jesus.
**In my name.** For the significance of praying in the name of Jesus see DA 667, 668. Compare chs 14:26; 15:16; 16:23, 24.
**That will I do.** The fact that men are to petition the Father in the name of Jesus, but that Jesus is the one who brings about the answer, emphasizes the oneness of the Son with the Father. In chs. 15:16; 16:23 the Father is said to answer the petitions presented before Him.
13.zh:
你們奉我的名無論求什麼，我必成就，叫父因兒子得榮耀。

**你們……無論求什麼。**門徒們在傳播福音的過程中與上天合作，同時他們也可以仰賴那無窮能力的源泉。上帝會供給他們一切的需要，並且會應允那奉耶穌之名而呈到祂寶座前的懇求。
**奉我的名。**關於奉耶穌之名禱告的意義，見《歷代願望》667，668頁。將這裡與約14:26；15:16；16:23,24進行比較。
**我必成就。**人奉耶穌的名祈求，而耶穌帶給他們答案，這一事實強調子與父的合一。約15:16；16:23中說到父回答那些呈到祂面前的祈求。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第28頁；《基督比喻實訓》第148頁；《今日的生活》第18頁；《證言》卷八第23，177頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–14節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第111頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–15節）**。《早期著作》第29頁。

24.en:
**Loveth me not.** The converse of the statement in v. 23. The world could not enjoy the fellowship here brought to view. The Father and the Son do not force their company upon anyone.
**Sayings.** Literally, “words,” synonymous with “commandments” (cf. on v. 23).
**Not mine.** Compare ch. 7:16; see on ch. 4:34.
24.zh:
不愛我的人就不遵守我的道。你們所聽見的道不是我的，乃是差我來之父的道。

**不愛我的。**從反面表述第23節的意思。世人不能享受這裡所呈現的親密友誼，父和子並不強迫任何人與祂們在一起。
**道。**與“命令”是同義詞（參第23節註釋）。
**不是我的。**將這裡與約7:16進行比較；見約4:34註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第139，283頁。

4.zh:
我往哪裡去，你們知道；那條路，你們也知道（有古卷作：我往哪裡去，你們知道那條路）。

**我往哪裡去，你們知道。**門徒們已經聽到了，他們應該瞭解。他們已在救主門下受教超過三年的時間（見本卷註釋第193頁）。事實上，耶穌剛剛還告訴他們祂要往祂父那裡去（第2節），儘管祂從前告訴過他們（見約7:33）。但是門徒心中的先入之見使他們很難完全理解耶穌教訓中的含義。
那條路，你們也知道（有古卷作“我往哪裡去，你們知道那條路”）。後者在希臘文裡卻涉及到一個語法方面的困難。因此採用更多的還是前者。耶穌已經解釋清楚了通向天父家裡的道路，但門徒悟性的遲鈍使他們不能完全理解祂話中的意思。
4.en:
**Whither I go ye know.** The disciples had been told, and ought to have understood. They had been under the Saviour’s instruction for more than three years (see p. 193). In fact, Jesus had just now informed them that He was going to His Father (v. 2), though He had earlier informed them (see ch. 7:33). But preconceived opinion made it difficult for the disciples to grasp the full import of much of Jesus’ instruction.
**The way ye know.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between this and the reading, “And you know the way where I am going” (RSV). However, the latter involves a grammatical difficulty in the Greek. Hence the reading of the KJV is probably to be preferred. Jesus had made plain the way to the Father’s house, but dullness of comprehension prevented the disciples from grasping the full import of His words.

5.zh:
多馬對他說：主啊，我們不知道你往哪裡去，怎麼知道那條路呢？

**多馬。**關於多馬的性格，見可3:18註釋。他的問題顯明瞭他的多疑和不信。
**我們不知道。**他們應該是知道的，因為主已經告訴他們了（見第4節註釋）。他們很難放棄猶太人關於彌賽亞王國的觀念（見太16:22；路4:19註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–8節）**。《歷代願望》第293頁。
5.en:
**Thomas.** For a character sketch of Thomas see on Mark 3:18. His doubting spirit and slowness of heart to believe are clearly revealed in his question.
**We know not.** They should have known, for they had been clearly told (see on v. 4). It was hard for them to divest themselves of the Jewish concept of the Messianic kingdom (see on Matt. 16:22; Luke 4:19).

7.zh:
你們若認識我，也就認識我的父。從今以後，你們認識他，並且已經看見他。

**你們若認識我。**將這裡與約8:19進行比較。希臘文中的句子結構顯示這裡的情況與事實是相反的。門徒們並不認識祂。他們如果認識耶穌，就會認識基督來要啟示的那一位（見約1:18註釋）。
**從今以後。**基督的死在啟示天父的過程中是重要的一步。接下來聖靈將要進一步啟示祂的品格（約14:26；15:26；16:13,14）。關於基督徒，約翰在公元1世紀將近結束的時候寫道：“你們認識那從起初原有的”（約壹2:13）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第123頁。
7.en:
**If ye had known me.** Compare ch. 8:19. The construction in the Greek shows the condition here expressed to be contrary to fact. The disciples had not known Him. If they had, they would have known Him whom Christ came to reveal (see on ch. 1:18).
**From henceforth.** Or, “from now.” The death of Christ would be an important step in the revelation of the Father. The subsequent revelations of the Spirit would further unveil the divine character (chs. 14:26; 15:26; 16:13, 14). Of Christians near the close of the 1st century John wrote, “Ye have known the Father” (1 John 2:13).

8.zh:
腓力對他說：求主將父顯給我們看，我們就知足了。

**腓力。**關於腓力的性格，見可3:18註釋。
**將父顯給我們看。**腓力或許期望能像摩西那樣（出33:18-23）看到上帝神聖榮耀的顯現。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《拾級就主》第11頁；《證言》卷五第739頁。
8.en:
**Philip.** For a character sketch of Philip see on Mark 3:18.
**Shew us the Father.** Perhaps Philip hoped for a revelation of divine glory such as was given to Moses (Ex. 33:18–23).

9.zh:
耶穌對他說：腓力，我與你們同在這樣長久，你還不認識我嗎？人看見了我，就是看見了父；你怎麼說將父顯給我們看呢？

**我……同在。**耶穌的門徒領悟力如此遲鈍令祂非常失望。但祂仍舊以忍耐對待他們的無知。
**就是看見了父。**關於基督向人顯示上帝的品格，見約1:18。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–10節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第123頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–11節）**。《服務真詮》第32頁。
9.en:
**Have I been?** It was disappointing to Jesus to have His disciples so dull of comprehension. Yet He dealt patiently with their ignorance.
**Hath seen the Father.** On Christ’s revealing to men the character of God see on ch. 1:18.

10.zh:
我在父裡面，父在我裡面，你不信嗎？我對你們所說的話，不是憑著自己說的，乃是住在我裡面的父做他自己的事。

**在父裡面。**耶穌先前強調過祂與天父的合一（見約10:30註釋）。
……話。耶穌的話語和工作都見證了祂的神性。門徒們應該相信耶穌的話。如果這對他們來說是困難的，那他們看到祂所做的事也該相信祂的話。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《拾級就主》第75頁。
10.en:
**In the Father.** Jesus had earlier stressed His unity with the Father (see on ch. 10:30).
**The words.** The words and works of Jesus both bore testimony to His divinity. The disciples should have believed the word of Jesus. If this was difficult for them, they should have accepted His word on the basis of His works.

11.zh:
你們當信我，我在父裡面，父在我裡面；即或不信，也當因我所做的事信我。

**信我。**希臘文的動詞是複數，表明現在耶穌是在向所有的門徒說話。
**因我所作的事。**見第10節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《歷代願望》第664頁。
11.en:
**Believe me.** The Greek verb is plural, showing that Jesus now addresses all the disciples.
**Works’ sake.** See on v. 10.

12.zh:
我實實在在的告訴你們，我所做的事，信我的人也要做，並且要做比這更大的事，因為我往父那裡去。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18；約1:51註釋。
**更大的事。**即，信祂的人無論在數量還是質量上都要做比這更大的事。基督工作的範圍僅僅是（這個世界）較小的一片區域。而祂昇天之後，祂的門徒要走遍世界的每一個角落。
**因為我……去。**基督離開之後，祂會差遣聖靈前來（第16節；約16:7），聖靈要賦予門徒們力量（路24:49）。五旬節聖靈沛降以及後來多次的降下，使福音以大能傳揚，以致大約40年後保羅能說福音“傳與普天下萬人聽”（西1:23；參《歷代願望》633頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第22頁；《論福利工作》第297頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–14節）**。《歷代願望》第667頁。
12.en:
**Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18; John 1:51.
**Greater works.** That is, greater in quantity rather than quality. Christ’s activity had extended over a relatively small area (of the world). After the ascension the gospel would spread to all parts of the world.
**Because I go.** After His departure He would send the Holy Spirit (v. 16; ch. 16:7), who would endue the disciples with power (Luke 24:49). As a result of the Pentecostal outpouring, and subsequent ones, the gospel was heralded with great power, so that about 40 years later Paul could say that the gospel was “preached to every creature which is under heaven” (Col. 1:23; cf. DA 633).

18.zh:
我不撇下你們為孤兒，我必到你們這裡來。

**為孤兒。**源於希臘詞語orphanos，意思是，“失去父母的”。英語中的“孤兒（orphan）”就是由這個希臘詞語的拉丁文形式演化過來的。Orphanos在七十士譯本中通常表示希伯來詞語yatom（“沒有父親的”或“沒有父親的孩子”，出22:22,24；申10:18等）。orphanos在《新約》其他地方只出現在雅1:27中。約14:18的意思是耶穌不會丟下祂的門徒，使他們與他們的主分離。祂將會再到他們那裡。這裡指的不是祂的二次來臨（第1-3節），而是指基督通過聖靈與他的門徒同在。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第517頁；《證言》卷八第19頁。
18.en: **Comfortless.** From the Gr. orphanos, properly, “bereft of parents.” Our English word “orphan” comes to us through the Latin from this Greek word. Orphanos is common in the LXX for the Heb. yatom, “fatherless,” or “fatherless children” (Ex. 22:22, 24; Deut. 10:18; etc.). In the NT orphanos occurs elsewhere only in James 1:27, where it is translated “fatherless.” In John 14:18 the idea is that Jesus would not leave the disciples bereft of their Master. He would come to them. The reference here is not to the second coming (vs. 1–3), but to Christ’s presence with His disciples through the Spirit.

20.zh:
到那日，你們就知道我在父裡面，你們在我裡面，我也在你們裡面。

**到那日。**即“保惠師”來到並與他們同在的那一天（見第16節）。在屬靈的領域內有許多事情是門徒們現在所不能理解的。這些事後來要向他們顯明。
**我在父裡面。**將這裡與第11節進行比較。
**你們在我裡面。**見約15:4註釋。
20.en:
**At that day.** That is, the day when the “Comforter” would come and abide with them (see v. 16). There were many things in the spiritual realm that the disciples did not at present understand. These would later be made plain to them.
**I am in my Father.** Compare v. 11.
**Ye in me.** See on ch. 15:4.

22.zh:
猶大（不是加略人猶大）問耶穌說：主啊，為什麼要向我們顯現，不向世人顯現呢？

**猶大。**一般被認為就是利比（太10:3）或達太（可3:18），但證據並不是非常明確（見可3:18註釋）。
**不是加略人。**加略人猶大已經走了一段時間了（約13:30）。
**問耶穌說。**耶穌在樓上的講話經常被這樣的提問所打斷（見約13:36；14:5,8）。
**不向世人。**無疑猶大心中想到的一定是人們普遍期待的彌賽亞來臨時可以看見的榮耀的顯現。很明顯，當他瞭解到這種顯現只是針對少數人時他是很失望的。他沒有明白基督所指的在榮耀的國以先的恩典的國。他在他那種猶太人的愛國主義情緒中期待著彌賽亞能夠在審判外邦人時顯現出來，並重新建立神權國家。
22.en:
**Judas.** Generally identified as Lebbaeus (Matt. 10:3) or Thaddaeus (Mark 3:18), though the identification is not entirely certain (see on Mark 3:18).
**Saith unto him.** The discourse in the upper room has been marked by frequent interruptions (see chs. 13:36; 14:5, 8).
**Not Iscariot.** Judas Iscariot had left the upper room some time before this (ch. 13:30).
**Not unto the world.** Judas doubtless had in mind a visible manifestation of glory such as was expected to attend the advent of the Messiah. It was apparently disappointing to him that the manifestation was to be made to only a few. He did not grasp Christ’s reference to the kingdom of grace, which was to precede the kingdom of glory. In common with his Jewish compatriots he doubtless shared the hope that the Messiah would manifest Himself in judgment over the Gentiles and in the re-establishment of the spiritual theocracy.

29.zh:
現在事情還沒有成就，我預先告訴你們，叫你們到事情成就的時候就可以信。

耶穌知道即將發生的事會讓祂的門徒陷入極大的困惑和憂愁之中，就像將來他們在傳道過程中要遇到的考驗一樣。因此祂事先警告他們，使他們好早作預備（見約13:19註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷九第235頁。
29.en: **Ye might believe.** Jesus knew that the events of the immediate future would throw the disciples into great perplexity, as would the trials they would meet in their later evangelism. Hence He sought to forewarn them, that they might be forearmed (see on ch. 13:19).

14.en:
**Glorify me.** That is, by a revelation of the majesty and glory of the risen Christ and an unveiling of the mysteries of the plan of salvation.
**Of mine.** It is possible to impart a portion of the full fund of truth (see on v. 12).
14.zh:
他要榮耀我，因為他要將受於我的告訴你們。

**榮耀我。**憑藉復活之基督的威嚴和榮耀的啟示和救贖計劃奧秘的揭開。
**我的。**將全部真理的一部分傳授給門徒是可能的（見第12節註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第52頁；《歷代願望》第671頁；《今日的生活》第49頁；《拾級就主》第91頁；《給傳道人的證言》第95，396頁。

21.en:
**A woman.** Literally, “the woman,” a typical woman. The figure of a travailing woman is found in the advertising OT (Isa. 26:17; 66:7; etc.). But only here is mention made of her sorrow turning into joy.
**Man.** Gr. anthrōpos, man in a generic sense, that is, a human being.
21.zh:
婦人生產的時候就憂愁，因為他的時候到了；既生了孩子，就不再記念那苦楚，因為歡喜世上生了一個人。

**婦人。**這是一個象徵意義的女人。產難疼痛婦人的比喻也出現在廣為人知的《舊約》經文中（賽26:17；66:7等）。但只有這裡提到她的憂傷變為喜樂。
**人。**anthrōpos，人類中的一個。

10.en: **Go to my Father.** While on earth Jesus had pointed the way to the perfect righteousness required of those who enter the kingdom of heaven (Matt. 5:48; 6:33). After His departure this would be the special work of the Spirit (see on John 16:8).
10.zh:
為義，是因我往父那裡去，你們就不再見我；

**我往父那裡去。**耶穌在地上的時候指出了那些要進入天國的人如何才能達到所要求的完全公義（太5:48；6:33）。當祂離開之後，這項特殊的工作就由聖靈來完成了（見8節註釋）。

13.en:
**Spirit of truth.** See on ch. 14:17.
**Into all truth.** See on chs. 14:26; 16:12. “Truth” is here used primarily in its theological sense (see on ch. 8:32). However, it is also true that all right scientific discoveries and inventions have their source in God (see CT 277).
**Not speak of himself.** Jesus declared the same concerning Himself (chs. 12:49; 14:10). The ultimate source of authority was God.
**Things to come.** Jesus had revealed things to come (Matt. 24; etc.). But more light concerning the future was to be given. The prophecies of Revelation are an outstanding example of how this was fulfilled. Concerning the messages to the churches John declared, “Let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches” (Rev. 2:7, 11; etc.).
13.zh:
只等真理的聖靈來了，他要引導你們明白（原文作進入）一切的真理；因為他不是憑自己說的，乃是把他所聽見的都說出來，並要把將來的事告訴你們。

**真理的聖靈。**見約14:17註釋。
**明白（原文作“進入”）一切的真理。**見約14:26；16:12註釋。這裡主要使用的是“真理”的神學意義（見約8:32註釋）。然而一切正確的科學發現和發明也都來源於上帝（見《基督教育之研究》第277頁）。
**祂不是憑自己說的。**耶穌過去關於自己說過同樣的話（約12:49；14:10）。權威的最終泉源是上帝。
**將來的事。**耶穌曾經啟示將來的事（《馬太福音》第24章等）。但是更多有關將來的亮光有待賜下。《啟示錄》的預言就是這件事如何應驗的範例。關於給教會的信息，約翰宣稱：“聖靈向眾教會所說的話，凡有耳的，就應當聽”（啟2:7,11等）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第38，51，53頁；《安息日學訓言》第35頁；《教育論》第134頁；《佈道論》第167頁；《早期著作》第190頁；《基督教育原理》第473頁；《善惡之爭》第八章，469頁；《傳道良助》第284頁；《給傳道人的證言》第111頁；《證言》卷五第439頁；《證言》卷六第163頁；《證言》卷八第19頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–14節）**。《歷代願望》第671頁；《傳道良助》第297頁；《拾級就主》第109頁；《證言》卷五第703頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–15節）**。《教育論》第94頁。

5.en:
**I go my way.** [The Coming of the Comforter, John 16:5–33.] Compare chs. 7:33; 13:33; 14:2.
**Asketh.** Literally, “keeps on asking.” Understood in this way this verse does not contradict chs. 13:36 and 14:5. The disciples had earlier made inquiry concerning this matter, but had ceased to do so. They were absorbed in selfish thoughts and did not think of the joy of their Master at the prospect of returning to His Father and carrying the plan of salvation one step nearer completion. It was expedient that He go away (ch. 16:7).
5.zh:
現今我往差我來的父那裡去，你們中間並沒有人問我：你往哪裡去？

**我往……去。**將這裡與約7:33；13:33；14:2進行比較。
**問。**直譯是“不斷地問”。本節這樣理解與約13:36；14:5並不矛盾。門徒們原先曾詢問過這方面的問題，但後來他們不問了。他們專注於自私的想法，並不考慮他們的主在展望自己回到父那裡去以及在完成救贖計劃的道路上又進了一步的快樂。祂離開是與他們有益的（約16:7）。

9.en: **Believe not on me.** God has provided only one means of salvation (Acts 4:12; 1 Cor. 3:11), namely, faith in Jesus Christ (John 3:16, 18, 36). Those who are enlightened, as the Jews had been, are without excuse when they refuse to believe in Him whom God sent into the world (see on ch. 15:22).
9.zh:
為罪，是因他們不信我；

**不信我。**上帝只提供了一種得救的方法（徒4:12；林前3:11），就是信耶穌基督（約3:16,18,36）。那些蒙教導的人，比如說猶太人，當他們拒絕相信祂──上帝差遣進入世界的一位──時，就再沒有什麼藉口了（見約15:22註釋）。

11.en:
**Of judgment.** Gr. krisis, the act of judging. The vindication of the divine character at the cross assured that Satan would be brought to trial and condemned. And if this were true of the archrebel himself, it would also be true of all his accomplices. See on v. 8.
**Prince of this world.** See on ch. 12:31; cf. ch. 14:30.
11.zh:
為審判，是因這世界的王受了審判。

**審判。**krisis，審判的行動。十字架所證明的上帝品格註定了撒但要受審判並定罪。如果這對於那叛逆的魁首是確定的，那麼對於他的跟隨者也是確定的。見第8節註釋。
**世界的王。**見約12:31註釋；參約14:30。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第679頁。

6.en: **Sorrow.** See on ch. 14:1. They should, instead, have rejoiced at the prospect of the glory to which their Master was returning. Instead the thought of their own separation from Him filled their hearts with anxious forebodings.
6.zh:
只因我將這事告訴你們，你們就滿心憂愁。

**憂愁。**見約14:1註釋。他們不應憂愁，反倒應因展望到他們主回來時的榮耀而感到喜樂。但恰恰相反，他們的心裡充滿了與祂分離的焦急的預感。

33.en:
**Peace.** See on ch. 14:27.
**Have tribulation.** See on chs. 15:20; 16:2.
**Be of good cheer.** Gr. tharseō, “to be of good courage,” “to be full of courage.” Compare Matt. 9:2; 14:27; etc.
**I have overcome the world.** Jesus looked forward with confidence to the cross, fully assured that He would triumph over the powers of darkness (see Col. 2:15). The prince of this world would be defeated (see on chs. 12:31; 14:30; cf. ch. 16:11), and the disciples had nothing to fear.
33.zh:
我將這些事告訴你們，是要叫你們在我裡面有平安。在世上，你們有苦難；但你們可以放心，我已經勝了世界。

**平安。**見約14:27註釋。
**有苦難。**見約15:20；16:2註釋。
**可以放心。**tharseō，“要充滿勇氣”。參太9:2；14:27等。
**我已經勝了世界。**耶穌帶著信心展望到十字架，祂深信祂將戰勝黑暗的權勢（見西2:15）。這世界的王將要被打敗（見約12:31；14:30註釋；參約16:11），門徒們不需要懼怕什麼。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第23，84，86頁；《歷代願望》第123，679頁；《基督教育原理》第465頁；《傳道良助》第39頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第265頁；《今日的生活》第69，324頁；《拾級就主》第123頁；《證言》卷二第122頁；《證言》卷三第115，423頁；《證言》卷五第82頁；《證言》卷六第307頁；《證言》卷八第127，212頁。

20.en:
**Weep and lament.** Jesus does not give a direct reply to the inquiry of the disciples, but sheds further light on the circumstances surrounding the events to take place in “a little while.” For a fulfillment of the prediction see Luke 23:27; John 20:11.
**World shall rejoice.** The enemies of Jesus rejoiced when He was silenced. However, their exulting was short-lived, as was the sorrow of the friends of Jesus.
**Turned into joy.** See ch. 20:20.
20.zh:
我實實在在的告訴你們，你們將要痛哭、哀號，世人倒要喜樂；你們將要憂愁，然而你們的憂愁要變為喜樂。

**痛哭、哀號。**耶穌沒有直接回答門徒的詢問，而是進一步將亮光投射到“不多時”就要發生之事的背景上。關於這段預言的應驗，見路23:27；約20:11。
**世人倒要喜樂。**當耶穌的聲音終止時，祂的仇敵就要歡喜快樂了。然而，他們的歡樂是短暫的，就像耶穌朋友的憂傷一樣短暫。
**要變為喜樂。**見約20:20節。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第82頁。

22.en:
**Heart shall rejoice.** This is the application Jesus makes of the figure introduced in v. 21. It is therefore stretching the figure too far to see in the travail of the woman the birth pains of a new order of the kingdom. The disciples’ rejoicing came on the day of the resurrection.
**No man.** Gr. oudeis, “no one,” the devil and his agents included. The disciples’ joy would be complete and permanent in spiritual fellowship with the risen Lord, who would be with them “always, even unto the end of the world” (Matt. 28:20).
22.zh:
你們現在也是憂愁，但我要再見你們，你們的心就喜樂了；這喜樂也沒有人能奪去。

**心就喜樂了。**這就是耶穌第21節比喻的意義。這樣就延伸了比喻的意義，不至於把女人生產的疼痛視為一個國家新秩序建立時的痛苦。門徒們在耶穌復活的時候歡喜快樂。
**沒有人。**oudeis，包括魔鬼和他的使者在內。門徒們的喜樂在與他們復活之主的屬靈友誼中是充足而持久的。祂要“常”與他們同在，“直到世界的末了”（太28:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第788頁。

8.en:
**Reprove.** Gr. elegchō, “to convict.” The word is so translated in ch. 8:9. In ch. 8:46 it is translated “convince” (cf. 1 Cor. 14:24; Titus 1:9; James 2:9), but “convict” would be preferable. In Luke 3:19; Eph. 5:11, 13; 2 Tim. 4:2 elegchō is translated “reprove,” and in 1 Tim. 5:20; Titus 1:13; Heb. 12:5; Rev. 3:19 “rebuke.”
**Of sin.** This Jesus had also done (ch. 7:7). The day of Pentecost, the day when the gift of the Spirit was bestowed, provided a striking exhibit of this aspect of the Spirit’s work. Those who heard Peter’s address were “pricked in their heart” (Acts 2:37). One of the first evidences of the operation of the Holy Spirit is the deep conviction that one is a sinner.
**Of righteousness.** Not only does the Spirit expose sin; He convicts of positive righteousness. He urges men to accept the righteousness of Christ, both the imputed (Rom. 10:3–10) and the imparted (Gal. 2:20; Phil. 2:13).
**Of judgment.** Jesus also warned men of the judgment to come (Matt. 5:21, 22; 10:15; 11:22, 24; 12:36). None can escape the judgment; it is as sure as death (Heb. 9:27). Though fear of judgment is not to be the prime motive of doing right, it is, nevertheless, a powerful agency in awakening sin-darkened minds and is frequently, and rightly, appealed to (see Mark 9:43–48; Rev. 14:9–11). See on John 16:11.
Thus the Spirit convicts men of their sin, points them to the salvation and righteousness that is in Jesus, and warns them of the consequences of continuing in their sins and of neglecting the salvation freely proffered.
8.zh:
他既來了，就要叫世人為罪、為義、為審判，自己責備自己。

**為罪。**耶穌已經作過這件事了（約7:7）。五旬節的日子，聖靈的恩賜降下的時候，聖靈這方面的工作得到了極大的展現。那些聽彼得講道的人“覺得扎心”（徒2:37）。聖靈工作的首要證據之一便是使人深信自己是個罪人。
**為義。**聖靈不僅暴露罪惡，還肯定積極的義行。祂催促世人接受基督的義；這義無論是歸給我們（羅10:3-10），還是分給我們的（加2:20；腓2:13）。
**為審判。**耶穌警告世人將來的審判（太5:21,22；10:15；11:22,24；12:36）。沒有人能夠避免審判。這與死亡一樣確定（來9:27）。儘管對審判的懼怕不是人行義的主要動機，然而，它卻是喚醒人黑暗有罪心靈的強有力工具，並且經常正確地發出呼籲（見可9:43-48；啟14:9-11）。見11節註釋。
聖靈就這樣使人知罪，向他們指出耶穌裡的救恩和公義，並警告他們繼續犯罪以及忽略白茨之救恩的後果。
**責備。**elegchō，“使人知罪”。該詞在約8:10中譯為“定罪”，在約8:46中譯為“指證有罪”（參林前14:24；多1:9；雅2:9）。elegchō在路3:19；弗5:11,13；提後4:2；提前5:20；多1:13；來12:5；啟3:19中譯為“責備”。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第52頁；《歷代願望》第671頁；《佈道論》第283頁；《基督教育原理》第197頁；《傳道良助》第284頁；《今日的生活》第332頁；《給傳道人的證言》第65頁；401頁；《證言》卷三第428頁；《證言》卷六第319頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《今日的生活》第43頁。

7.en:
**Expedient for you.** Or, “profitable for you.” The death, resurrection, and ascension of Christ were important events in the outworking of the plan of salvation. Without these the era of the Spirit would not have become a reality. His departure was thus to the disciples’ profit and advantage. In His incarnate body Jesus could not be everywhere present, but through the medium of the Spirit Jesus could be with each one of His followers at all times and in all places (see Matt. 28:20).
**Comforter.** See on ch. 14:16.
**I will send him.** According to the plan of God, Jesus was to complete His work on earth and ascend to the Father’s throne before the Spirit should come.
7.zh:
然而，我將真情告訴你們，我去是於你們有益的；我若不去，保惠師就不到你們這裡來；我若去，就差他來。

**與你們有益的。**基督的死，復活，和昇天都是救贖計劃裡重要的事件。沒有這些，聖靈的時代就不會成為現實。因此祂的離開對門徒來說是有益處是有幫助的。耶穌在祂的肉身中不能同時出現在所有的地方，但祂以聖靈為媒介就可以隨時隨地與祂的跟從者在一起（見太28:20註釋）。
**保惠師。**見約14:16註釋。
**就差祂來。**根據上帝的計劃，耶穌在地上完成祂的工作，並在聖靈來臨之前升到天上祂父的寶座前。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第38頁；《教育論》第94頁；《服務真詮》第104頁；《喜樂的泉源》第75頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–8節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第392頁。

12.en:
**Many things to say.** The human mind is capable of acquiring truth at a limited rate. Jesus had spent more than three years with the disciples, during which time He had faithfully instructed them in divine things. They had learned much, but there were many things yet to be revealed (see on ch. 14:26). The wisdom of God is infinite and cannot be exhausted. A lifetime of diligent study enables one to gain but a limited concept of the infinite treasures of spiritual knowledge.
Sometimes a spiritual lethargy prevents the acquisition of further divine truth. This was the case with the Corinthians, whom Paul designated as “carnal,” who needed to be fed with “milk” rather than with solid food, because they were unable to endure a substantial spiritual diet (1 Cor. 3:1, 2). Christians are urged to leave the first “principles of the doctrine of Christ” and to “go on unto perfection” (Heb. 6:1; cf. Heb. 5:11–14).
12.zh:
我還有好些事要告訴你們，但你們現在擔當不了（或作：不能領會）。

**好些事要告訴。**人類的思想只能以有限的速度獲得真理。耶穌與祂的門徒在一起超過三年，在此期間祂誠懇地將神聖的事情教導他們。他們學習了很多，但仍有許多事情還沒有向他們啟示（見約14:26註釋）。上帝的智慧無限，不能完全詳盡闡述。一生勤勉的學習只能使一個人從屬靈知識無限的寶庫獲得有限的認識。
有時屬靈上的昏睡會阻礙進一步獲得神聖的真理。哥林多人就曾面臨這種情況，保羅稱他們為“屬肉體的”，還不能吃飯，而需要用“奶”來餵養，因為他們還不吃堅硬的靈糧（林前3:1,2）。基督徒奉命要離開“基督道理的開端，竭力進到完全的地步”（來6:1；參來5:11-14）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第271頁；《歷代願望》第507頁；《佈道論》第57，202，369頁；《服務真詮》第245頁；《給傳道人的證言》第476頁；《證言》卷六第55頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–14節）**。《歷代願望》第670頁。

1.zh:
我已將這些事告訴你們，使你們不至於跌倒。

**跌倒。**skandalizō（見太5:29註釋）。關於就逼迫預先提出警告，免得他們灰心失望，見約15:20註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–4節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第69頁。
1.en: **Offended.** Gr. skandalizō (see on Matt. 5:29). On forewarnings concerning persecution, so as to prevent discouragement, see on John 15:20.

2.zh:
人要把你們趕出會堂，並且時候將到，凡殺你們的就以為是事奉神。

**會堂。**見約9:22註釋。
**侍奉上帝。**逼迫門徒的猶太人推論說，傳福音的是一群褻瀆的人，目的是要推翻上帝親自設立的宗教（見徒6:13,14；21:28-31）。猶太人對待他們宗教的熱忱和維護他們崇拜的小心反映在《密西拿》的一條規則中：“如果一個人偷竊了罩幕，或者陷於迷惑之中，或者與一個外邦女子（比如說，敘利亞女子）同居，他就要受到熱心分子的懲罰。如果一個祭司在聖殿中服侍時不潔淨，他的兄弟祭司不在伯丁控告他，而由年輕的祭司將他帶到聖殿外院，用木棍打碎他的頭骨。如果一個俗人在聖殿中服侍，亞基巴說：要把他絞死；眾賢人說：（他的死）是出於天意”（Sanhedrin 9. 6，《塔木德》松奇諾版第542頁）。史書記載多次假宗教之名進行的逼迫。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《佈道論》第339頁；《證言》卷六第120頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–4節）**。《使徒行述》第79頁。
2.en:
**The synagogues.** See on ch. 9:22.
**Doeth God service.** The Jews who persecuted the apostles reasoned that these evangelists were blasphemers who sought to overthrow the religion that God had established (see Acts 6:13, 14; Acts 21:28–31). A reflection of the Jews’ zeal for their religion and the jealousy with which they sought to protect its worship is found in one of the precepts of the Mishnah: “If one steals the Ḳiswah, or curses by enchantment, or cohabits with a heathen [lit., Syrian] woman, he is punished by zealots. If a priest performs the Temple service whilst unclean, his brother priests do not charge him therein at Beth Din, but the young priests take him out of the Temple Court and split his skull with clubs. [Of] a layman who performed the service in the Temple, R. Akiba said: He is strangled; the Sages say: [His death is] at the hands of Heaven” (Sanhedrin 9. 6, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 542). The pages of history record repeated persecutions carried out in the name of religion.

3.zh:
他們這樣行，是因未曾認識父，也未曾認識我。

**未曾認識。**將這裡與約15:21進行比較。
3.en: **Have not known.** Compare ch. 15:21.

4.zh:
我將這事告訴你們，是叫你們到了時候可以想起我對你們說過了。我起先沒有將這事告訴你們，因為我與你們同在。

**時候。**有文本是“他們的時後”，即這些逼迫者的時候。見路22:53。
**你們……可以想起。**這些預先的警告會增強他們在逼迫時的力量（見約15:20註釋）。
**我與你們同在。**原先沒有必要告訴他們，因為當逼迫來臨的時候，耶穌會與他們同在鼓勵他們。實際上，當耶穌在地上時，逼迫的矛頭一直是對準他的。但是當祂離開後，仇敵的憎恨就要針對祂的代表了。
[保惠師的來臨：約16:5-33] 。
4.en:
**The time.** Literally, “the hour.” Textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 146) for the reading “their hour,” that is, the hour of these persecutors. See Luke 22:53.
**Ye may remember.** The forewarning would strengthen them in the hour of persecution (see on ch. 15:20).
**I was with you.** There was no need to tell them earlier, for if persecution had come, Jesus would have been with them to encourage them. In fact, while Jesus was on earth the persecution was directed against Him. But after His departure the hatred of the enemy would be directed against His representatives.

15.zh:
凡父所有的，都是我的；所以我說，他要將受於我的告訴你們。

**凡……所有的。**見約3:35註釋；參約17:10。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第24頁。
15.en: **All things.** See ch. 3:35; cf. ch. 17:10.

16.zh:
等不多時，你們就不得見我；再等不多時，你們還要見我。

**就不得見我。**第一個“不多時”通常被認為是指主受難前的一小段時間，第二個“不多時”被認為是指釘十字架和復活之間的三天。有人認為基督的話裡有雙關的意思，第一個是指死和復活，第二個是指升到父那裡去並在世界末了的時候回來（約14:1-3）。其他地方描述耶穌再來不是很遙遠的事：“證明這事的說：‘是了，我必快來！’”（啟22:20；參啟1:3）。然而，考慮到約16:20-29解釋，似乎最好將這段經文當成是在指馬上發生的事件。
16.en: **Shall not see me.** The first “little while” is generally understood to refer to the short time intervening until the Passion, and the second “little while” to the three days between the crucifixion and the resurrection. Some have suggested a dual meaning in Christ’s words, first, that they refer to the death and resurrection, and second that they refer to the ascension to the Father and His return at the end of the age (ch. 14:1–3). This return is elsewhere represented as not far away: “He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly” (Rev. 22:20; cf. ch. 1:3). However, in view of the explanation in John 16:20–29 it seems best to consider the passage a reference to the events of the immediate future.

17.zh:
有幾個門徒就彼此說：他對我們說：等不多時，你們就不得見我；再等不多時，你們還要見我；又說：因我往父那裡去。這是什麼意思呢？

**彼此。**他們顯然不願意直接問耶穌。耶穌的話引起了他們心中的好奇。
這是什麼意思呢？耶穌曾經說過祂的死和復活，但是門徒們沒有完全理解祂話的意思（見太16:21註釋），因此他們現在感到了困惑。
17.en:
**Among themselves.** They were apparently reluctant to ask Jesus directly. His enigmatic statement had effectively aroused their curiosity.
**What is this?** Jesus had earlier spoken of His death and resurrection, but the disciples had not fully grasped the significance of His words (see on Matt. 16:21); hence their perplexity at His statement.

19.zh:
耶穌看出他們要問他，就說：我說等不多時，你們就不得見我；再等不多時，你們還要見我，你們為這話彼此相問嗎？

**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《歷代願望》第277頁。

23.zh:
到那日，你們什麼也就不問我了。我實實在在的告訴你們，你們若向父求什麼，他必因我的名賜給你們。

**到那日。**即賜下聖靈的日子（約14:16,17,26；15:26；16:7-14）。
**什麼也就不問我了。**“問”字在本節中出現了兩次，第一次為erōtaō，第二次為aiteō。Erōtao一般是指問一個問題，而aiteō的意思是要求什麼東西。本節中就存在這種區別。耶穌告訴門徒，在聖靈的恩典降下的時候他們就不必再問問題了，因為聖靈要指教他們一切的事（約14:26）。門徒們在這最後一夜問了許多問題，表現出他們悟性明顯的遲鈍（約14:5,8,9,22；16:17）。聖靈將要啟發他們的思想。他們要明白那些現在他們看來還是謎一樣的事情。
