**What have I to do with thee?** Literally, “What to you and to me?” The expression implies that the one thus addressed has exceeded the bounds of what properly concerns him (see Judges 11:12; 2 Sam. 16:10; 1 Kings 17:18; 2 Kings 3:13; 2 Chron. 35:21; Matt. 8:29; Mark 1:24; Luke 8:28; etc.). That Mary did not understand Jesus’ reply as a refusal is evident from her instructions to the servants (see John 2:5). She was satisfied that Jesus would supply the need in His own good time and way. Throughout His private life in Nazareth, Jesus had honored the authority of His mother; in fact He ever remained a dutiful son in the sphere where that relationship properly prevailed (see ch. 19:26, 27). But now He was no longer a private individual, and Mary did not appreciate fully the limits this placed on her authority over Jesus. She might feel she had the right, in some degree at least, to direct Him in His mission (see on Matt. 12:46–50). Accordingly, in these clear-cut but courteous words Jesus sought to make clear to her the distinction between His relation to her as the Son of man and as the Son of God (DA 147). His love for her was unchanged, but now He must labor from day to day under the direction of His heavenly Father (see DA 208; see on Luke 2:49).
As with Mary and Jesus, parents today often find it difficult to relax, and eventually relinquish, authority over their children, in order that the latter may gain experience in meeting the problems of life for themselves and learn to accept responsibility for their decisions. Wise are the parents and fortunate the children when this transition of authority takes place naturally and without friction.
**Mine hour.** Compare chs. 7:6, 8, 30; 8:20; etc. Mary apparently hoped that Jesus would, upon this occasion, proclaim Himself the Messiah (see DA 145), but the time for such an announcement had not arrived (see on Mark 1:25). There was an appointed time for each event in His life (DA 451; see on Luke 2:49). Not until the very close of His ministry did Jesus publicly claim to be the Messiah (see on Matt. 21:1, 2), and because of this claim He was crucified (Matt. 26:63–65; Luke 23:2; John 19:7; see on Matt. 27:63–66). Not until the night of the betrayal did Jesus say, “My time is at hand” (Matt. 26:18; cf. John 12:23; 13:1; 17:1).
4.zh:
耶穌說：母親（原文作婦人），我與你有什麼相干？我的時候還沒有到。

**母親（原文作：**婦人）。“婦人”在東方是對女性一個常用的、表示恭敬的稱呼（約19:26；參《歷代願望》146頁）。祂曾吩咐百姓要尊敬他們的父母（出20:12；參《先祖與先知》366頁）。祂自己就是這一原則活的例證。三十多年耶穌一直是個順從，殷勤，對母親充滿愛的兒子（見路2:51,52註釋；參《歷代願望》147頁）。
我與你有什麼相干？直譯是“這與你我有何相干呢？”暗示眼下提出來的事情已經超出了祂應管的範圍（見士11:12；撒下16:10；王上17:18；王下3:13；代下35:21；太8:29；可1:24；路8:28等）。從馬利亞對僕人的吩咐（見約2:5）中就可以看出她沒有將耶穌的回答當作是拒絕。耶穌將會在自己合適的時間以自己合適的方式滿足筵席的需要，如此馬利亞就心滿意足了。耶穌早年在拿撒勒的家庭生活中一直都尊重祂母親的權威；事實上祂後來也是一個負責任的兒子，在各個方面都為祂的母親著想（見約19:26,27）。但現在祂不是一個私有的人，馬利亞也沒有完全瞭解她對耶穌所有權威的界限何在。她也許覺得，至少在某種程度上，她有權利在耶穌的使命中指教祂（見太12:46-50註釋）。因此，耶穌在這些清楚簡潔但又不失敬意的話語中向她表明祂作為人子之於她，和祂作為上帝兒子之於她之間關係的區別（《歷代願望》147頁）。他對自己母親的愛並沒有改變，但他現在每天必須在他天父的指示之下工作（見《歷代願望》208頁；見路2:49註釋）。
就像馬利亞對耶穌那樣，今天的父母經常發現自己很難放鬆和最終放棄他們在自己孩子身上的權威，而那樣對子女獲得實際生活經驗以及學習如何為自己的決定負責卻是有益的。如果這一權利的交接發生的自然而又沒有摩擦，那是父母的明智，子女的幸運。
**我的時候。**參約7:6,8,30；8:20節等。馬利亞顯然希望耶穌在這個場合宣佈自己就是彌賽亞（見《歷代願望》145頁），但作這樣聲明的時候還沒有到（見可1:25註釋）。祂生命中的每一件事都有定時（《歷代願望》451頁；見路2:49節註釋）。耶穌不到祂傳道工作的最後一刻是不會公開宣佈自己彌賽亞之身份的（見太21:1,2註釋），也正是因為這種宣告祂他人釘在十字架上（太26:63-65；路23:2；約19:7；見太27:63-66註釋）。直到被出賣的那夜，耶穌才說，“我的時候快到了”（太26:18；參約12:23；13:1；17:1）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第147，486頁。

11.en:
**This beginning.** The first miracle was performed about one week after the call of the first disciples (see v. 1). The second recorded miracle was also performed at Cana, on the occasion of Jesus’ next visit about one year later (see ch. 4:43–54).
**Miracles.** Gr. sēmeia, “signs” (see p. 208).
**His glory.** That is, the evidence of His divine character and power (see p. 209; see on ch. 1:14).
**His disciples believed.** This miracle provided the early disciples with the first visible evidence of divine power working through Christ, fortified them against the unbelief and antipathy of the Jewish leaders, and provided them with their first opportunity to testify to their new-found faith. Also, it honored Mary’s trust. In a practical way it expressed the sympathetic interest of Jesus in human happiness.
11.zh:
這是耶穌所行的頭一件神蹟，是在加利利的迦拿行的，顯出他的榮耀來；他的門徒就信他了。

**頭一件。**頭一件神蹟發生在呼召第一批門徒大約一個星期之後（見第1節）。第二件記載的神蹟也發生在迦拿，那是大約一年之後耶穌再次訪問迦拿的時候（見約4:43-54）。
**神蹟。**sēmeia，（見第208頁）。
**祂的榮耀。**即，祂神聖品格和能力的證據（見第209頁；見約1:14節註釋）。
**祂的門徒就信。**這個神蹟為早期的門徒提供了那運行在基督身上之神能的明顯證據，堅固他們以防止不信和猶太領袖的嫌憎，並給他們第一次機會來驗證他們新近建立起來的信心。同樣，這也報賞了馬利亞對耶穌的信賴，用一個實際的方法展現了耶穌對人類福祉深深的關懷。

10.en:
**Every man.** The “ruler of the feast” was embarrassed at what appeared to be a departure from standard practice and feared that the guests would blame him for such a breach of custom. By calling the groom, he sought to make clear that the responsibility was not his.
**Well drunk.** When men were “well drunk” their senses would be dulled, and they would not be able to distinguish good from bad.
**Good wine.** This wine was superior to any the steward of the feast had ever tasted (DA 148). The guests also noted the quality of the wine—incidental evidence that they were not “well drunk” at the time—and made inquiry as to its origin (DA 149). Heaven always provides its best things last, for those who patiently wait.
10.zh:
對他說：人都是先擺上好酒，等客喝足了，才擺上次的，你倒把好酒留到如今！

**人都是。**“管筵席的”對這一違反習俗的事情感到很詫異並擔心賓客有可能會因為這件事而責怪他。他叫新郎來就是要讓新郎知道目前出現這樣的事不是他的責任。
**喝足了。**當人把酒“喝足了”的時候，他們的感覺就遲鈍了，也就不辨酒的好壞了。
**好酒。**這酒是任何管筵席的人從來都沒有嘗過的（《歷代願望》148頁）。賓客們顯然也注意到了這酒的甘美品質，此時他們好像還沒有“喝足”──因為他們也詢問這酒的來歷（《歷代願望》149頁）。對於那些耐心等待的人，天國總是在最後才提供最好的東西。

8.en: **Governor of the feast.** Gr. architriklinos, literally, “ruler of the three reclining couches.” On formal social occasions the guests at a feast reclined on sloping couches placed on three sides of a low table, the fourth being left open for table service. This arrangement of table and couches was called a triklinion (see on Mark 2:15).
8.zh:
耶穌又說：現在可以舀出來，送給管筵席的。他們就送了去。

**管筵席的。**直譯是“三張斜靠椅的管理者”。在正式的社交場合，賓客參加筵席一般都是斜倚在長椅上，三條長椅放在一張矮桌的三面，桌子剩下的一面留給僕人上酒上菜。這種桌子和靠椅的佈置方式叫做triklinion（見可2:15註釋）。

9.en:
**Ruler of the feast.** Gr. architriklinos, translated “governor of the feast” in v. 8.
**Wine.** This was “the pure juice of the grape” (DA 149). Jesus would act consistently with principles revealed to earlier Bible writers (see Prov. 20:1; 23:29–32; cf. 1 Cor. 3:16, 17; 6:19). See on Matt. 26:27.
**Drew the water.** It seems that the water remained water as long as it was in the jars, for it is said to have been “water” when the servants drew it. Perhaps it was during the process of taking water from the jars that it became wine. Compare on Mark 6:41.
**Called the bridegroom.** In Oriental lands the groom, or his family, or his family, was expected to provide all the supplies necessary for a wedding feast.
9.zh:
管筵席的嘗了那水變的酒，並不知道是哪裡來的，只有舀水的用人知道。管筵席的便叫新郎來，

**管筵席的。**architriklinos，參第8節。
**酒。**這是“純淨的葡萄汁”（見《歷代願望》149頁）。耶穌一定會嚴格按照先前啟示給聖經作者們的原則行事（見箴20:1；23:29-32；參林前3:16,17；6:19）。見太26:27註釋。
**舀水。**這水在水缸裡時好像仍舊是水，因為這裡說僕人舀出來的依然是水。可能這水是在從缸裡舀出來送到管筵席的人那裡去的過程中變成酒的。比較可6:41節。
**叫新郎來。**在東方，新郎或他的家庭要承擔婚筵的全部費用。

5.en: **Servants.** Gr. diakonoi, whence our word “deacon.” The servants apparently looked to Mary as the one responsible for providing more wine, for even “the ruler of the feast” did not yet know of the lack (see DA 148).
5.zh:
他母親對用人說：他告訴你們什麼，你們就做什麼。

**用人。**diakonoi，“執事”一詞就是由此而來。顯然僕人們指望馬利亞能提供更多的酒，因為連“管筵席的”都不知道缺酒了（見《歷代願望》148頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷六第415頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–10節）**。《歷代願望》第148頁。

2.en:
**Jesus was called.** That is, invited. He had known of the wedding and apparently returned to Galilee at this time in order to be present (DA 144).
**His disciples.** There were five of them—John, Andrew, Peter, Philip, and Nathanael (see ch. 1:40–45). Possibly they were friends or relatives of the two families. Otherwise they received their invitation when they appeared in Cana as companions of Jesus. Their presence testified to the fact that Jesus had entered upon His work as a teacher. See on ch. 1:37, 40.
2.zh:
耶穌和他的門徒也被請去赴席。

**耶穌……也被請。**祂顯然已經得到消息並在此時返回加利利準備出席這場婚禮（《歷代願望》144頁。
**祂的門徒。**他們一共五個人──約翰，安得烈，彼得，腓力和拿但業（見約1:40-45）。他們也許是婚禮兩個家庭的朋友或親戚。否則當他們作為耶穌的隨從出現在迦拿時也會收到邀請。他們的出席證明了那時耶穌已經開始了祂作為教師的工作。見約1:37,40註釋。

3.en:
**Wanted wine.** Literally, “the wine failed.” Having assisted in arrangements for the wedding (see DA 146), Mary felt responsible to supply the lack, and sought to avoid the embarrassment that would otherwise follow.
Mary’s confidence in coming to Jesus with the problem is worthy of note. As a dutiful son Jesus had always been attentive to her desires, and had found an appropriate solution to every problem. Whether Mary expected Jesus to perform a miracle, which He had not done before (see v. 11), is not clear from the Gospel narrative (cf. DA 145, 146). Possibly the presence of Jesus and His disciples had attracted a crowd.
3.zh:
酒用盡了，耶穌的母親對他說：他們沒有酒了。

**酒用盡了。**馬利亞負責協助婚筵上的一切事宜（見《歷代願望》146頁），她感到有責任去補足酒席所用之物的缺乏，以避免那隨之而來的尷尬。
馬利亞遇到困難去找耶穌，她的信心是值得讚賞的。作為一個孝順、有責任感的兒子，耶穌總是注意到祂母親的需要和願望，並能找到合適的解決辦法。福音書的記錄（參《歷代願望》145，146頁）沒有說明馬利亞是否期望耶穌行一個神蹟。這是祂先前從未行過的（見第11節）。耶穌和祂門徒的出席可能引起了大家的注意。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《歷代願望》第146頁。

7.en:
**Fill the waterpots.** All that human power could accomplish was to be done by human hands (see p. 209). Divine power was about to be revealed, but conscientious human effort was to be united with it. God never does for men what they can do for themselves, as this would make spiritual weaklings out of them. Like Moses (see Ex. 4:2), the widow (2 Kings 4:2), and Jesus own disciples (Matt. 15:34), we are to utilize fully the resources we have at hand if we expect God to add His blessing.
**To the brim.** The servants could later testify that nothing but pure water had been placed in the jars.
7.zh:
耶穌對用人說：把缸倒滿了水。他們就倒滿了，直到缸口。

**把缸倒滿了水。**所有人能自己辦到的事都要人自己去做（見第209頁）。神能即將施展，但人該盡的努力必須與之聯合。上帝絕不會為人做人自己能做的事，如果那樣就會造成人屬靈的軟弱。像摩西（見出4:2），那個寡婦（王下4:2），以及耶穌自己的門徒（太15:34）那樣，如果我們想要上帝加福氣給我們，我們必須首先充分利用自己手邊的資源。
**直到缸口。**僕人們後來可能證明說，倒進缸裡的只是清水。
**懷愛倫註釋（7–9節）**。《傳道良助》第206頁；《服務真詮》第333頁。

12.zh:
這事以後，耶穌與他的母親、弟兄、和門徒都下迦百農去，在那裡住了不多幾日。

**這事以後。**meta touto，這是約翰使用的一個過渡性短語（見約11:7,11；19:28），表明時間上的嚴格順序，他並沒有特別提出兩件事之間的時間間隔。
**祂的……弟兄。**見太12:46節註釋。
**下迦百農去。**從加利利山地的迦拿出發，到加利利湖邊低於地中海海平面209米的迦百農，真的是“下”迦百農去（見太4:13註釋）。這次訪問迦百農的目的沒有記錄。
**不多幾日。**可能在公元27-28年的晚冬。
[第一個逾越節: 第一次潔淨聖殿：約2:13-25.參太21:12-17註釋。見本卷註釋217頁地圖；229-231頁圖表]。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《歷代願望》第154頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–22節）**。《歷代願望》第154-166頁。
12.en:
**After this.** Gr. meta touto, a transitional phrase, used by John (see chs. 11:7, 11; 19:28) to indicate strict chronological sequence without specifying the length of the time interval.
**Down to Capernaum.** From Cana, deep in the Galilean hills, it would literally be “down” to Capernaum on the shores of the Lake of Galilee, 685 ft. (209 m.) below the level of the Mediterranean (see on Matt. 4:13). The purpose of this visit is not stated.
**His brethren.** See on Matt. 12:46.
**Not many days.** Probably during the late winter of .. 27–28.

13.zh:
猶太人的逾越節近了，耶穌就上耶路撒冷去。

**猶太人的逾越節。**公元28年的逾越節是耶穌傳道的開始（見第193,247頁）。如果本卷書約翰是為猶太人寫的，那他直接說“逾越節”就行了。關於逾越節的筵席，見出12:3-15；利23:5；申16:1,2。
**上耶路撒冷去。**見路10:30；19:28註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–14節）**。《歷代願望》第157頁。
13.en:
**The Jews’ passover.** [First Passover: First Cleansing of the Temple, John 2:13–25. Cf. on Matt. 21:12–17. See Judean Ministry from First Passover A.D. 28; The Duration of Christ’s Ministry, the Opening of the Galilean Ministry, The Ministry of Our Lord.] This, the Passover of .. 28, was the first of Jesus’ ministry (see pp. 193, 247). Had John been writing for Jewish readers, he would simply have said “the passover.” Concerning the Passover feast see on Ex. 12:3–15; Lev. 23:5; Deut. 16:1, 2.
**Up to Jerusalem.** See on Luke 10:30; 19:28.

14.zh:
看見殿裡有賣牛、羊、鴿子的，並有兌換銀錢的人坐在那裡，

**殿。**hieron，這是指聖殿連它的院子，門廊，以及附屬建築，並不是第20節提到的聖殿的主體建築（naos，見太4:5註釋）。在約2:21中耶穌用naos比喻祂的身體。這裡所描述不聖潔的買賣場指外院或外邦人的院子。
賣……的。這是耶穌頭次潔淨聖殿。祂的第一次具有全國意義的行動。如此祂就宣告了祂管理聖殿事物的權利以及自己彌賽亞的身份。第二次潔淨聖殿發生在三年之後，祂在第四次過逾越節的時候（見本卷註釋第193,247頁；見本卷註釋229頁圖表；見太21:12-17註釋），提醒眾人祂的宣告依然有效。
**兌換銀錢的人。**或莊家（見路19:23註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《福山寶訓》第2頁；《醫療佈道論》第122頁。
14.en:
**The temple.** Gr. hieron, the Temple with its courts, porches, and outlying buildings, not the naos, the main building itself, as in v. 20 (see on Matt. 4:5). In John 2:21 Jesus uses naos of His body. The outer court, or Court of the Gentiles, was the scene of the unholy traffic here described.
**Those that sold.** This was Jesus’ First Cleansing of the Temple, His first act of national importance. By it He declared His right to administer the affairs of the Temple and announced His mission as the Messiah. The second cleansing occurred three years later, at the fourth Passover (see pp. 193, 247; see The Duration of Christ’s Ministry; see on Matt. 21:12–17) as a reminder that His claim was still valid.
**The changers of money.** Or, bankers (see on Luke 19:23).

15.zh:
耶穌就拿繩子做成鞭子，把牛羊都趕出殿去，倒出兌換銀錢之人的銀錢，推翻他們的桌子，

**繩子。**schoinia，“用燈心草編成的繩子”。
**鞭子。**耶穌並沒有真的用鞭子打人。這鞭子是祂權威的象徵，鞭子在空中飛舞能夠使大家注意祂所講的話。在第二次潔淨聖殿時就沒有再提到過鞭子。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–16節）**。《歷代願望》第158頁。
15.en:
**A scourge.** Or, “whip.” Jesus did not actually strike the people. The whip was symbolic of His authority, and a flourish in the air would suffice to make His intention clear. No whip is mentioned in connection with the second cleansing.
**Small cords.** Gr. schoinia, “a cord plaited of rushes.”

16.zh:
又對賣鴿子的說：把這些東西拿去！不要將我父的殿當作買賣的地方。

**我父的殿。**聖殿是上帝在人間的居所（見出25:8）。猶太人多次指責耶穌稱上帝是自己的父（見約5:17,18；8:18,19,38,39；10:30-33）。雖然他們也稱上帝是他們的父（約8:41），但他們顯然意識到耶穌是在一種更高的意義上用這個稱呼。他們注意到耶穌在這些話中聲明瞭自己至高無上的神性。耶穌第二次潔淨聖殿時說這殿是“我的殿”（太21:13），並且在猶太領袖最後拒絕祂請求之後的那一天，當祂再提到聖殿時祂將其稱為“你們的家”（太23:38）。
**買賣的地方。**即市場，一個進行普通商業交易的地方。耶穌第二次潔淨聖殿時稱它為“賊窩”（太21:13）。今天，那些誠心誠意設法使他們天父的殿成為“禱告的殿”（太21:13）的人，要避免將其當成一個用於日常思想，言語或行為的地方。他們應當帶著敬畏和尊重進入祂的殿，意識到這是祂神聖同在的地方，他們應使自己的心靈意念在禱告和讚美中提高（見約4:23,24；參見詩96:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第591頁；《給青年人的信息》第316頁；《證言》卷八第250頁。
16.en:
**My Father’s house.** The Temple was God’s dwelling place among men (see Ex. 25:8). Again and again the Jews criticized Jesus for speaking of God as His Father (see John 5:17, 18; 8:18, 19, 38, 39; 10:30–33). They also claimed God as their Father (ch. 8:41), but realized that Jesus did so in a higher sense. They perceived that, in these words, Jesus set forth an unqualified claim to divinity. At the second cleansing Jesus spoke of the Temple as “my house” (Matt. 21:13), and when the leaders rejected His final appeal the following day He referred to it as “your house” (Matt. 23:38).
**An house of merchandise.** That is, a market place, a place for the transaction of common business. At the second cleansing He used the expression “den of thieves” (see on Matt. 21:13). Those today who conscientiously seek to make their Father’s house a “house of prayer” (Matt. 21:13) will avoid making it a place for common thoughts, words, or actions. They will enter His house with awe and reverence, conscious of His holy presence, heart and mind uplifted in prayer and praise (see John 4:23, 24; cf. Ps. 96:9).

17.zh:
他的門徒就想起經上記著說：我為你的殿心裡焦急，如同火燒。

**祂的門徒就想起。**可能在當時一剎那間就想起來了（參見第22節）。
**焦急。**Zēlos（“熱心”，“熱情”，“憤慨”，“嫉妒”）。這是引用詩69:9（見該處註釋）。耶穌極度渴望祂父的殿能夠專用於它當初建造被獻時的目的（見出25:8,9；太21:13註釋）。
**如同火燒。**即“將我焚燒”。對上帝的忠誠就像烈火一般燃燒著耶穌，我們也該如此。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第158頁；《證言》卷四第396頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–19節）**。《歷代願望》第785頁。
17.en:
**His disciples remembered.** Probably at the very time (cf. v. 22).
**Zeal.** Gr. zēlos, “zeal,” “ardor,” “indignation,” “jealousy.” This is a citation from Ps. 69:9 (see comment there). Jesus earnestly desired that His Father’s house should be used exclusively for the purpose to which it had been dedicated (see on Ex. 25:8, 9; Matt. 21:13).
**Eaten me up.** That is, “consumed me.” With Jesus, loyalty to God was a consuming passion. So it should be with us.

18.zh:
因此猶太人問他說：你既做這些事，還顯什麼神蹟給我們看呢？

**猶太人。**約翰對國家宗教領袖的專稱。
**神蹟。**sēmeion（見本卷註釋第208頁；見賽7:14；太12:38,39註釋）。領袖們要求耶穌拿出憑據來證明祂有權干涉聖殿的事務。耶穌的行為對他們的權威是一個直接的挑戰。這是他們所不能忽視的（參見約1:19,25）。但是這些批評者想看“神蹟”的要求，像往常一樣，沒有得到什麼滿足（見太12:38,39；路23:8註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第192頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–20節）**。《歷代願望》第164頁。
18.en:
**The Jews.** John’s characteristic designation for the religious leaders of the nation.
**Sign.** Gr. sēmeion (see p. 208; see on Isa. 7:14; Matt. 12:38, 39). The leaders demanded evidence that Jesus had the right to assume direction of the affairs of the Temple. His act posed a direct challenge to their authority, one that they could not overlook (cf. on John 1:19, 25). As usual, the demand for a “sign,” of the kind these critics desired, went unanswered (see on Matt. 12:38, 39; Luke 23:8).

19.zh:
耶穌回答說：你們拆毀這殿，我三日內要再建立起來。

**拆毀這殿。**這裡的殿是naos，指聖所本身（見第14節註釋）。耶穌在這句話中第一次暗示在祂人生道路臨近終了時等待著祂的命運。猶太人已經在密謀要殺害祂了（見《歷代願望》164頁）。在對祂的審判中他們歪曲這句話，控告祂企圖拆毀聖殿，並自我辯護說他們這樣做是要實現基督的預言（參見可14:58；見太26:61節註釋）。
這裡不是第一次將聖殿與基督的身體進行比較。聖所以及後來的聖殿都是上帝在地上的居所（見25:8,9註釋）。在施恩座上方有榮光顯現，是上帝神聖同在的榮耀象徵（見創3:24；出25:17註釋）。但就像約翰已經指出的那樣（見約1:14註釋），這上帝的榮耀也居住在我們主耶穌基督的身上。參林前3:16。
**三日。**見第248-250頁。
**建立起來。**耶穌是指祂的復活（見約10:18註釋）。但猶太人因為不明白這項聲明的含義，就認為耶穌是在說字面上的聖殿建築。他們到最後還是不明白耶穌所說的話，見太27:63,64。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第165，777頁；見可16：6懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–21節）**。《歷代願望》第705頁。
19.en:
**Destroy this temple.** Here the word for temple is naos, the sanctuary proper (see on v. 14). In these words Jesus intimates for the first time the fate that awaited Him at the end of His earthly pathway. The Jews were already plotting His death (see DA 164). At His trial they distorted this declaration into the charge that He purposed to destroy the Temple, and made the charge their excuse for fulfilling Christ’s prophecy (cf. Mark 14:58; see on Matt. 26:61).
The analogy between the literal Temple and Christ’s body is not as remote as might at first appear. The sanctuary, and later the Temple, was designed to be the earthly dwelling place of God (see on Ex. 25:8, 9). There, above the mercy seat, appeared the Shekinah, glorious symbol of the sacred abiding presence of God (see on Gen. 3:24; Ex. 25:17). But, as John has already pointed out (see on John 1:14), this same divine glory tabernacled in human flesh in the person of our Lord. Compare 1 Cor. 3:16.
**Three days.** See pp. 248-250.
**Raise it up.** Jesus referred to His resurrection (see on ch. 10:18). But the Jews, not fully understanding the import of the declaration, thought of the literal Temple structure. That eventually they did discern the true import of Jesus’ words appears from Matt. 27:63, 64.

20.zh:
猶太人便說：這殿是四十六年才造成的，你三日內就再建立起來嗎？

**四十六年。**見本卷註釋第242,243頁。如果照著字面理解聖殿，耶穌明顯的比喻就成了無稽之談。猶太人堅持不去理解耶穌的言下之意，也不肯看祂外表之下究竟本質如何（見約7:15,20,33-36；見約5:17,18；8:52-59；9:29註釋）。這種對耶穌生活和教訓的膚淺理解就猶太教的典型態度，直到如今。
20.en: **Forty and six years.** See pp. 242, 243. Taken literally of the Temple, Jesus’ obviously figurative statement became a manifest absurdity. The Jews consistently refused to see beneath the surface meaning of His words, or to see in Him anything more than the common man He appeared to be (see ch. 7:15, 20, 33–36; see on chs. 5:17, 18; 8:52–59; 9:29; etc.). This superficial interpretation of the life and teachings of Jesus has been typical of Judaism down to the present time.

21.zh:
但耶穌這話是以他的身體為殿。

**但耶穌這話。**見約2:19,20；參林前3:16,17。
21.en: **But he spake.** See on John 2:19, 20; cf. 1 Cor. 3:16, 17.

22.zh:
所以到他從死裡復活以後，門徒就想起他說過這話，便信了聖經和耶穌所說的。

**到……以後。**即這預言應驗之後（參見太17:9）。門徒們只有從耶穌傳道工作全局角度出發才能理解一些祂的話和行為中所蘊涵的深層次意義。耶穌復活之後，聖靈引導他們更深入地明白了祂言語和行為的意義（見約14:26；15:26；16:13）。
**聖經。**約翰似乎想到一些特別的聖經章節，可能是第17節所引的詩16:10或69:9。他可能泛指所有《舊約》中關於彌賽亞的預言，門徒們在耶穌復活之後對這些預言的意思有了更深入的理解（參見路24:25-27,44；約12:16註釋）。
**所說的。**即第19節記載的耶穌的話。
22.en:
**When therefore.** That is, when the prediction had been fulfilled (cf. on Matt. 17:9). It was only from the viewpoint of Jesus’ ministry as a whole that the disciples were able to understand the deeper meaning of some of His words and acts. After the resurrection the Holy Spirit led them into a more perfect understanding of the meaning of His words and deeds (see John 14:26; 15:26; 16:13).
**The scripture.** John seems to have in mind a particular passage of Scripture, possibly Ps. 16:10, or 69:9, cited in v. 17. He may refer in a general way to all the OT Messianic prophecies, whose import the disciples understood more fully after the resurrection (cf. on Luke 24:25–27, 44; John 12:16).
**The word.** That is, the saying of Jesus recorded in v. 19.

23.zh:
當耶穌在耶路撒冷過逾越節的時候，有許多人看見他所行的神蹟，就信了他的名。

**逾越節。**見第13節註釋。
**許多人……就信了。**這是公眾對耶穌信息之反應的第一個記錄。約翰在不同場合再三地提到“好些人信了耶穌”（見約4:39；11:45；12:42；見約1:12註釋）。這標誌著猶太地傳道的開始，這一過程持續了數月之久，在公元29年的逾越節時結束（見《路加福音》第4章補充註釋；見本卷註釋230頁圖表；見太4:12註釋）。
**神蹟。**這是猶太地傳道期間唯一有關神蹟的記載。唯一提到的一個具體的神蹟發生在這一傳道時期將近結束的時候即治好畢士大池邊躺著的那人（約5:1-9）。
23.en:
**The passover.** See on v. 13.
**Many believed.** This is the first report of public response to Jesus’ message. John repeatedly notes that, upon various occasions, “many believed” (see chs. 4:39; 11:45; 12:42; see on ch. 1:12). This marks the opening of the Judean ministry, which continued for many months and formally closed at the Passover of .. 29 (see Additional Note on Luke 4; The Ministry of Our Lord; see on Matt. 4:12).
**The miracles.** This is the only record of miracles during the period of the Judean ministry. The only specific miracle mentioned is the one that marked its close, the healing of the man at the Pool of Bethesda (ch. 5:1–9).

24.zh:
耶穌卻不將自己交託他們；因為他知道萬人，

**將自己交託。**即交付給承認相信祂的人（第23節）。祂知道現在這些急切向祂歡呼的人，就像兩年後加利利人那樣，轉離再也不跟從祂了（參見約6:66）。祂知道人心易變，也知道有多少不可共患難之信徒的草率和虛偽（見約6:64）。見約7:2-9註釋。
24.en: **Commit himself.** Or, “trust himself,” that is, to those who professed to believe in Him (v. 23). He knew that many of those now so eager to acclaim Him would, like the people of Galilee two years later, turn away and walk no more with Him (cf. ch. 6:66). He knew the fickleness of the human heart, and how many fair-weather converts were heedless or hypocritical (see ch. 6:64). See on ch. 7:2–9.

25.zh:
也用不著誰見證人怎樣，因他知道人心裡所存的。

**人心裡所存的。**耶穌經常讀懂人的心思，好給他們證據證明祂的神性（見可2:8註釋）。
25.en: **What was in man.** Jesus often read men’s thoughts, thereby giving them evidence of His divinity (see on Mark 2:8).

9.en:
**Fire of coals.** Compare ch. 18:18.
**Fish.** Gr. opsarion (see on ch. 6:9). Compare prosphagion (see on ch. 21:5). Jesus anticipated the weariness and hunger of the disappointed fishermen. The disciples did not inquire where the articles of food and the fire came from.
9.zh:
他們上了岸，就看見那裡有炭火，上面有魚，又有餅。

**炭火。**將這裡與約18:18進行比較。
**魚。**opsarion（見約6:9註釋）。參prosphagion（見5節註釋）。對於失望的門徒，耶穌預料到了他們的疲憊和飢餓。門徒們沒有詢問食物和火從哪裡來。

10.en: **Bring of the fish.** To supplement the supply being prepared on the coals.
10.zh:
耶穌對他們說：把剛才打的魚拿幾條來。

**把……魚拿幾條來。**來補充炭火上預備的食物。

11.en:
**Went up.** Peter responded in his characteristic impulsiveness.
**Hundred and fifty and three.** The odd number indicates that the fish were actually counted. Some commentators have placed mystical and fanciful interpretations upon these numbers, such as that the “three” represents the Trinity. Such interpretations are not worthy of consideration.
11.zh:
西門彼得就去（或作：上船），把網拉到岸上。那網滿了大魚，共一百五十三條；魚雖這樣多，網卻沒有破。

**就去。**彼得的性格比較急躁衝動。
**一百五十三條。**數字有整有零，這表明魚的數量確實被數算過了。有的註釋者將一些奇怪的解釋富裕這個數字上，比如說“三”代表三位一體之類的。但其實這樣的一些解釋根本不值得我們考慮。

12.en:
**Dine.** Gr. aristaō, here, “to eat breakfast.”
**Durst ask him.** The disciples ate in silence, awed and reverent. Through their minds passed many thoughts that they dared not express.
12.zh:
耶穌說：你們來吃早飯。門徒中沒有一個敢問他：你是誰？因為知道是主。

**吃早飯。**aristaō。
**敢問他。**門徒們在敬畏之中默默地吃飯。他們的頭腦中閃過了許多的想法，但是卻不敢表達出來。

1.zh:
這些事以後，耶穌在提比哩亞海邊又向門徒顯現。他怎樣顯現記在下面：

**這些事以後。**即在樓上的顯現（約20:26-29）和加利利山邊顯現（太28:16-20）之間的這段時間。這一點從以下這個事實可以看出來，這次相見被描述為“耶穌……向門徒顯現，這是第三次”（約21:14）。見《馬太福音》第28章補充註釋。
**提比哩亞海。**見約6:1註釋。
**顯現。**或作顯示。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–22節）**。《歷代願望》第809-817頁。
1.en:
**After these things.** [Appearance by the Lake of Galilee, John 21:1–23.] That is, between the second appearance in the upper room (ch. 20:26–29) and the appearance on a mountain in Galilee (Matt. 28:16–20). This is evident from the fact that the incident is described as “the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples” (John 21:14). See Additional Note on Matt. 28.
**Sea of Tiberias.** See on ch. 6:1.
**Shewed.** Or, manifested.

2.zh:
有西門彼得和稱為低土馬的多馬，並加利利的迦拿人拿但業，還有西庇太的兩個兒子，又有兩個門徒，都在一處。

**西門彼得。**見可3:16註釋。
**低土馬。**見約11:16註釋。
**多馬。**見可3:18註釋。
**加利利的迦拿。**見約2:1註釋。
**拿但業。**見可3:18；約1:45註釋。
**西庇太的兩個兒子。**就是雅各和約翰，他們在《約翰福音》中只在此處提到（太4:21；可10:35）。
2.en:
**Simon Peter.** See on Mark 3:16.
**Thomas.** See on Mark 3:18.
**Didymus.** See on ch. 11:16.
**Nathanael.** See on Mark 3:18; John 1:45.
**Cana in Galilee.** See on ch. 2:1.
**Sons of Zebedee.** That is, James and John, thus designated only here in John (Matt. 4:21; Mark 10:35).

3.zh:
西門彼得對他們說：我打魚去。他們說：我們也和你同去。他們就出去，上了船；那一夜並沒有打著什麼。

**我打魚去。**打魚是彼得成為耶穌門徒之前的職業（見太4:18-20）。雅各和約翰也是漁夫（太4:21）。彼得的這個建議無疑是想要彌補他們的生計。他們沒有忘記耶穌更高的呼召，他們已經來到加利利要見他們的主了（見太28:16註釋；見《歷代願望》809，810頁）。
**那一夜。**夜晚的湖面波瀾不起，水清風靜，非常適合下網打魚（見路5:5註釋）。
**沒有打著什麼。**就像先前的那次一樣（見路5:5註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–13節）**。《歷代願望》第810頁。
3.en:
**I go a fishing.** Fishing had been Peter’s trade prior to becoming a disciple of Jesus (see Matt. 4:18–20). James and John had also been fishermen (Matt. 4:21). The purpose of the suggestion was doubtless to replenish their meager funds. The disciples were not abandoning their higher calling. They had come to Galilee to meet their Master (see on Matt. 28:16; see DA 809, 810).
**That night.** Because of its clear waters, night was the suitable time for fishing on the lake (see on Luke 5:5).
**Caught nothing.** As on a previous occasion (see on Luke 5:5).

4.zh:
天將亮的時候，耶穌站在岸上，門徒卻不知道是耶穌。

**天將亮的時候。**意思是天剛開始發亮。有文本為“天已經亮了”。
**不知道。**可能他們的眼也和那兩個往以馬忤斯去的門徒的眼一樣，“迷糊了”（路24:16）。或者可能當時是拂曉，光線還不很清晰。馬利亞在耶穌第一次向她顯現的時候也沒能認出祂來（約20:14-16）。
4.en:
**Was now come.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between this and the reading “was now coming,” suggesting, perhaps, that it was just beginning to be light.
**Knew not.** Perhaps their eyes were “holden” like those of the disciples on the way to Emmaus (Luke 24:16). Perhaps the light was as yet indistinct. Mary, also, had not recognized Jesus when He first appeared to her (John 20:14–16).

5.zh:
耶穌就對他們說：小子！你們有吃的沒有？他們回答說：沒有。

**小子。**在福音書中，耶穌只在這裡用“小子”稱呼祂的門徒。約翰在他的書信中使用過這個稱呼（約壹2:13,18）。莫爾頓和米利根提出，該稱呼在這裡相當於“小夥子，”他們還引證了一首歌謠，裡面把該詞用在士兵身上（《希臘新約詞彙》）。但無論如何這種稱呼無法使人確認說話的人。門徒無疑把祂當成陌生人。
**吃的。**prosphagion，指除餅之外如肉，魚，雞蛋，蔬菜等食物（參見約6:9註釋）。餅是猶太人的主食。這裡既是問漁夫，prosphagion就可能指魚了。希臘原文問句的形式暗示指望否定的回答。
5.en:
**Children.** In the gospel records Jesus addresses the disciples by this title only here. John uses the title in his epistle (1 John 2:13, 18). Moulton and Milligan suggest that here the title may be equivalent to “lads,” and cite a ballad in which the term is used of soldiers (The Vocabulary of the Greek Testament). At any rate the form of address did not identify the speaker. The disciples doubtless took Him to be a stranger.
**Meat.** Gr. prosphagion, that which is eaten in addition to bread, such as flesh, fish, eggs, vegetables, etc. (cf. on ch. 6:9). Bread was the principal article of diet of the Jew. Here, where the question is put to fishermen, prosphagion refers most probably to fish. The form of the question in Greek shows that a negative answer is expected.

6.zh:
耶穌說：你們把網撒在船的右邊，就必得著。他們便撒下網去，竟拉不上來了，因為魚甚多。

**右邊。**耶穌站在岸上的一邊，藉著吩咐門徒將網撒在這邊，祂是要教導他們關於信心和與上帝能力合作的功課（見《歷代願望》811頁）。
**魚甚多。**這次神蹟使門徒們想起了早先那次使他們捨棄一切跟從主時的神蹟（見路5:11註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第436頁；《證言》卷七第213頁。
6.en:
**Right side.** This was the side on which Jesus stood on the shore, and by asking them to cast the net on this side He designed to teach the lesson of faith and cooperation with divine power (see DA 811).
**Multitude of fishes.** This miracle would remind the disciples of the earlier miracle at which time they forsook all to follow the Master (see on Luke 5:11).

7.zh:
耶穌所愛的那門徒對彼得說：是主！那時西門彼得赤著身子，一聽見是主，就束上一件外衣，跳在海裡。

**耶穌所愛的。**關於約翰的這個稱呼，見約13:23註釋。約翰是第一個承認主並第一個相信主已復活（約20:8）。
**西門彼得。**彼得的急躁，衝動，熱誠，同情心以及真摯的愛都在他鮮明的風格中體現出來了。
**赤著身子。**gumnos，該詞既可指一個人完全光著身子，它可指一個人只是沒有穿上衣，這裡用的是後一種意思。顯然，彼得為了急著去向他的主問安就顧不得穿上衣了。
**一件外衣。**ependutēs。
**在海里。**這片水域可能很淺，足以涉過去，這裡沒有說他是在水面上走過去的。
7.en:
**Whom Jesus loved.** For this designation of John see on ch. 13:23. John was the first to recognize the Master as he was also the first to believe in the resurrection (ch. 20:8).
**Simon Peter.** Peter, impulsive, fervent, warmhearted, impetuous, and affectionate, responded in his characteristic fashion.
**Fisher’s coat.** Gr. ependutēs, “an outer garment.”
**Naked.** Gr. gumnos, which, though it may describe one completely unclothed, may also describe one whose outer garment only is removed, and so probably here. Doubtless, Peter desired to greet his Master respectfully clad.
**Into the sea.** The water was probably shallow enough for wading, for the record says nothing of his walking on the water.

8.zh:
其餘的門徒離岸不遠，約有二百肘（古代以肘為尺，一肘約有今時尺半），就在小船上把那網魚拉過來。

**二百肘（古時以肘為尺，一肘約有今時尺半）。**約等於91.4米。
**小船。**ploiarion。第3節中的“船”是ploion。有些人歸納說，第8節用ploiarion，表明門徒們因為水淺而捨棄了大船，改用小船將網拖到岸邊。然而，ploion和ploiarion指的可能是同一條船，就像在約6:17,19,21,22,24中一樣。那次只涉及一條船。
8.en:
**Little ship.** Gr. ploiarion, literally, “a little boat.” In v. 3 the word for “ship” is ploion. Some have concluded that because ploiarion is used in v. 8 the larger boat was abandoned because of the shallow water, and a smaller boat used to drag the net to land. However, it is possible that ploion and ploiarion are used synonymously as, apparently, in ch. 6:17, 19, 21, 22, 24. In that event only one boat was involved.
**Two hundred cubits.** About 100 yds.

13.zh:
耶穌就來拿餅和魚給他們。

**拿餅。**耶穌熱情親切地款待他們。有文本前面還加上“耶穌祝謝了”。但即便沒有這句話，從上下文我們也可以知道必定是會有感恩的禱告。
13.en: **Taketh bread.** Jesus was the gracious host. There is slight textual evidence (cf. p. 146) for adding, “and having given thanks he gave to them.” But even without this textual support the prayer of thanksgiving may be presupposed.

14.zh:
耶穌從死裡復活以後，向門徒顯現，這是第三次。

**第三次。**約翰這裡數算的只是耶穌向門徒們顯現的次數，而不是向婦女們顯現的次數（太28:9；約20:14-17）。這三次分別是：（1）復活那天的晚上在樓上向門徒顯現（約20:19），（2）一週後在同一個地方向門徒們顯現（約20:26），（3）在加利利湖邊向門徒們顯現。見《馬太福音》第28章補充註釋。
14.en: **Third time.** John enumerates only the appearances to the disciples, not those to the women (Matt. 28:9; John 20:14–17). The appearances enumerated are: (1) to the disciples in the upper room on the evening of the resurrection day (John 20:19), (2) to the disciples a week later in the same upper room (John 20:26), (3) to the disciples by the Lake of Galilee. See Additional Note on Matt. 28.

15.zh:
他們吃完了早飯，耶穌對西門彼得說：約翰（在太16：17稱約拿）的兒子西門，你愛我比這些更深嗎？彼得說：主啊，是的，你知道我愛你。耶穌對他說：你餵養我的小羊。

**吃完了早飯。**或“吃完了”（見第12節註釋）。
**愛。**agapaō。彼得在回答耶穌的問題時用了另一個詞來表示“愛”，即phileō。這兩個詞有的時候意思是有區別的，agapaō指一種更高形式上的愛，一種受原則控制而不是受情緒控制的愛；而phileō指的是一種自發的、出於情感的愛。關於這兩個詞語意思上的區別，見太5:43；約11:3節註釋。關於這兩個詞在這裡的用法，學者們的意見也存在分歧：有的認為它們的意思是不同的，也有的認為它們在這裡的意思是一樣的，就像在約14:23中一樣；參約16:27。
耶穌在前兩次提問時用的是agapaō，彼得用phileō進行回答。耶穌第三次用的是phileō，彼得的回答和前兩次一樣，還是用phileō。如果這兩個詞的意思在此是有區別的，它們的目的又不能確定，那麼這三個問題或許可以這樣解釋：耶穌兩次問彼得他是不是用一種更高形式的愛（agapaō）來愛他。然而，彼得只敢承認他對祂的愛是出於一種普通的友誼。“你知道我愛[phileō]你”。第三次耶穌用彼得已經用過兩次的詞來問他是否像一個朋友（phileō）那樣愛祂，而這個問題是彼得已經兩次承認過的。對彼得來說，第三次問題顯然暗含著一種懷疑。根據這種解釋，他的憂愁不是因為耶穌向他三次提出同樣的問題，而是因為耶穌第三次改變了祂的問題，並似乎是在質疑彼得回答的真誠。
耶穌的三個問題可能指的是彼得三次的否認。彼得三次否認他的主，現在給他三次機會來承認他的主。
**比這些更深。**從語法上來說，“這些”可以指其他的門徒，也可以指漁船和上面的工具。但是，既然緊挨的上下文中沒有提到後者，我們還是認為“這些”指的是門徒。
**你知道。**彼得的回答是謙卑的，他的驕傲和自誇都沒有了。
**你餵養我的小羊。**小羊代表那些信心上沒有太多經驗的人。彼得後來將教會的長老比作牧人，而將那些在他們照管之下的人比作群羊，這些人是要長老們來餵養的（彼前5:1-4）。上帝的傳道人是在牧長領導下的牧人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第154頁；《基督教育之研究》第42頁；《歷代願望》第811頁；頁；《佈道論》第345頁；《傳道良助》第182，207頁；《證言》卷六第205，284頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–16節）**。《安息日學訓言》第76頁；《基督教育之研究》第255頁；《證言》卷五第335頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–17節）**。《使徒行述》第515，538頁。
15.en:
**Had dined.** Or, “had finished breakfast” (see on v. 12).
**Lovest.** Gr. agapaō. In his reply to Jesus’ question Peter uses another word for “love,” namely phileō. These two words are at times distinguished, agapaō refers to a higher form of love, a love controlled by principle rather than emotion; phileō, to spontaneous, emotional love. For a discussion of the difference in meaning between these two words see on Matt. 5:43; John 11:3. There is a difference of opinion among scholars as to whether the two words are to be distinguished in meaning here or whether they are used synonymously as they are, for example, in John 14:23; cf. ch. 16:27.
In His first two questions Jesus used agapaō, and Peter replied with phileō. The third time Jesus used phileo, and Peter replied, as previously, with phileō. If the two words are to be distinguished, which intent cannot be determined with certainty, the following interpretation is possible: Jesus asked Peter twice whether he loved Him with the higher form of love (agapaō). Peter, however, admitted no more than common friendship, “Thou knowest that I love [phileō] thee.” The third time Jesus used the word Peter had twice employed and asked him whether he really loved Him as a friend (phileō), which the apostle had already twice admitted. Apparently to Peter there was an implied doubt in the third question. According to this interpretation, he was grieved, not because the same question had been put to him thrice, but because the third time Jesus changed His question and appeared to question the sincerity of Peter’s replies.
The three questions of Jesus possibly had reference to the three denials of Peter. Thrice the apostle had denied his Lord. He was given opportunity thrice to confess Him.
**More than these.** Gramatically, “these” could refer either to the other disciples or to the boat and fishing gear. However, since the latter have not been mentioned in the immediate context, it is preferable to consider the reference to be to the disciples.
**Thou knowest.** Peter’s reply is humble. All arrogant boasting is gone.
**Feed my lambs.** The lambs represented those new in the faith. Peter later compared the elders of the church to shepherds and those under their charge to a flock whom the elders were to feed (1 Peter 5:1–4). Ministers of God are shepherds serving under the leadership of the Chief Shepherd.

16.zh:
耶穌第二次又對他說：約翰的兒子西門，你愛我嗎？彼得說：主啊，是的，你知道我愛你。耶穌說：你牧養我的羊。

**第二次。**這個問題是第一個問題的重複，但沒有了“比這些更深”（見第15節）。彼得的愛受到了直接的質疑。彼得的回答和上次一樣謙卑。
**牧養。**poimainō，“放牧”，當然也包括餵養。第15節中表示“餵養”的詞是boskō，“（像一個牧人那樣）去餵養。”這兩個詞用在這裡是一個意思。彼得作為牧人的責任被進一步強調了。如果“小羊”是那些信心上沒有太多經驗的人，那麼“羊”就是指普遍意義上的群羊。儘管彼得失敗過，但他將來仍舊是一個“得人”的漁夫（路5:10）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第815頁；《佈道論》第346頁；《傳道良助》第183頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–17節）**。《歷代願望》第812頁。
16.en:
**The second time.** The question is repeated but without the addition of “more than these” (see v. 15). Peter’s love is directly challenged. Peter gives the same humble answer.
**Feed.** Gr. poimainō, “to shepherd,” which, of course, includes feeding. In v. 15 the word for “feed” is boskō, “to feed [as a herdsman].” The two words were used synonymously. Peter’s responsibility as a shepherd is further emphasized and perhaps enlarged. If the “lambs” were those new in the faith, “sheep” would refer to the flock generally. Despite his failure, Peter was not to be deprived of his call to be a “fisher” of men (Luke 5:10).

17.zh:
第三次對他說：約翰的兒子西門，你愛我嗎？彼得因為耶穌第三次對他說你愛我嗎，就憂愁，對耶穌說：主啊，你是無所不知的；你知道我愛你。耶穌說：你餵養我的羊。

**第三次。**耶穌第三次提問中表示“愛”的詞與前兩次不同。不知道是否表示不同的意思。如果表示“愛”的新詞確實要與前兩次有所區別，其意義見第15節註釋。
**憂愁。**關於彼得憂愁可能的原因見第15節註釋。彼得知道別人有理由懷疑他對主的愛。這一而再、再而三的提問使他清楚地回想起了他對主可恥的否認，這就像一支帶倒鉤的箭刺入他受傷的心靈。
**你是無所不知的。**彼得第三次不再像前兩次那樣說“是的”（見第15,16節）。他請求主用祂那洞察一切的眼睛看透他靈魂最深處的秘密。
**餵養我的羊。**耶穌在這裡重複了前一次的命令（參見第15,16節）。彼得已經顯示出他完全悔改了。他的心裡柔和並且充滿了愛。主現在可以將群羊交託給他了。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第154頁；《教育論》第90頁；《證言》卷四第353頁。
17.en:
**The third time.** In His third question Jesus used a word for “love” different from that which He used in the first two. Whether a difference of meaning is intended is open to question. See on v. 15 for the significance of the question if the new word for “love” is to be distinguished from the preceding.
**Grieved.** See on v. 15 for a possible cause of grief. Peter knew he had given cause for others to doubt his love for his Master. The repeated questions brought his shameful denials vividly to mind, and like a barbed arrow must have cut his wounded heart.
**Knowest all things.** The third time Peter omitted the “yea,” or “yes” (see vs. 15, 16). He appealed to the all-seeing eye that read the innermost secrets of his life.
**Feed my sheep.** Jesus here repeats the charge (cf. vs. 15, 16). Peter had shown himself to be fully repentant. His heart was tender and full of love. He could now be entrusted with the flock.

18.zh:
我實實在在的告訴你，你年少的時候，自己束上帶子，隨意往來；但年老的時候，你要伸出手來，別人要把你束上，帶你到不願意去的地方。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18；約1:51註釋。
**你要伸出手來。**顯然指釘十字架（見第19節）。根據比較可信的傳統說法，彼得是自己要求頭朝下倒釘十字架的，因為他覺得與自己曾經否認過的主以同一種方式釘十字架，這種尊榮是他不配擁有的（見《使徒行述》537，538頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第537頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（18–19節）**。《歷代願望》第815頁。
18.en:
**Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18; John 1:51.
**Stretch forth thy hands.** An obvious reference to crucifixion (see v. 19). According to tradition, which there seems to be little reason to doubt, Peter met death by crucifixion with his head down, on the plea that to be crucified like his Master was too great an honor for the one who had denied his Lord (see AA 537, 538).

19.zh:
耶穌說這話是指著彼得要怎樣死，榮耀神。說了這話，就對他說：你跟從我吧！

**指著。**將這裡與約12:33進行比較。
**榮耀上帝。**即作為殉道者，默默見證基督教的力量。參彼前4:16。
**你跟從我吧。**彼前2:21反映了這個命令。
19.en:
**Signifying.** Compare ch. 12:33.
**Glorify God.** That is, by dying a martyr’s death, silently testifying to the power of Christianity. Compare 1 Peter 4:16.
**Follow me.** See a reflection of this charge in 1 Peter 2:21.

20.zh:
彼得轉過來，看見耶穌所愛的那門徒跟著，（就是在晚飯的時候，靠著耶穌胸膛說：「主啊，賣你的是誰？」的那門徒。）

**轉過來。**“轉過來”和“跟著”這個詞提示我們，耶穌帶著彼得離開其他的門徒，私下裡告訴他關於他死的事，就像他們過去在湖邊散步一樣。而約翰可能就在後面一定的距離跟著他們。
**靠著耶穌胸膛。**見約13:23註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第539頁；《成聖的人生》第53，79頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（20–21節）**。《歷代願望》第816頁。
20.en:
**Turning about.** This phrase and the word “following” suggest that Jesus had taken Peter apart from the others and had communicated with him privately concerning the nature of his death, perhaps as they were walking along the shore of the lake. John probably followed at some distance.
**On his breast.** See on ch. 13:23.

21.zh:
彼得看見他，就問耶穌說：主啊，這人將來如何？

這人將來如何？彼得已經得到了關於自己將來的奇異啟示，他本應因主向他啟示的事情而滿足。但他卻好奇，還想要知道約翰將來如何。耶穌就用這次機會教導彼得學習重要的一課：集中精力做好當做的事。
21.en: **This man do.** Peter had received a remarkable revelation regarding his own future and should have rested content with what the Lord had chosen to unveil to him. But the apostle was curious as to what the future held in store for John. Jesus took the opportunity to impress upon Peter the important lesson of making first things first.

22.zh:
耶穌對他說：我若要他等到我來的時候，與你何干？你跟從我吧！

**我若要。**基督的話是一個假設句。這在第23節中已經顯明瞭。但一些人誤會了這句話並將其當作一個對事實的陳述。耶穌實際上是在說，“假設我要讓他逗留，這件事與你有什麼關係呢，彼得？”這個回答對彼得來說是個責備。他不應該對他的同胞的未來過於好奇。他的任務就是跟從他的主。這並不是說我們不應該關心我們弟兄的福利。但是這種擔心不應該使我們的注意力轉離耶穌。過於注意我們的弟兄會使我們在他們跌倒的地方同樣跌倒。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第817頁；《教育論》第90頁；《給傳道人的證言》第332頁；《證言》卷三第65頁；《證言》卷四第39頁；                    【 SDA6.1051】。
22.en: **If I will.** Christ’s saying was a supposition. This is made clear in v. 23. Some misunderstood it and took it as a statement of fact. Jesus had simply said, in effect, “Suppose I should will that he tarry, that would not be a matter of concern to you, Peter.” The reply came as a reproof to Peter. He was not to become too anxious about his fellow men. His matter of concern was to follow his Lord. This does not mean that we should not have a loving interest in a brother’s welfare. But such solicitude must never take the place of keeping our eyes upon Jesus. Looking too intently upon our brother may lead us to fail where he fails.

23.zh:
於是這話傳在弟兄中間，說那門徒不死。其實，耶穌不是說他不死，乃是說：我若要他等到我來的時候，與你何干？

**不死。**弟兄們將耶穌的一種假設（見第22節註釋）當成了對事實的敘述。他們顯然相信耶穌很快就要再來（徒1:6,7）。
23.en: **Should not die.** The brethren took as a statement of fact that which Jesus had set forth merely as a supposition (see on v. 22). They apparently believed the coming of Jesus to be very near (Acts 1:6, 7).

24.zh:
為這些事作見證，並且記載這些事的就是這門徒；我們也知道他的見證是真的。

**這門徒。**見約20:30註釋。“耶穌所愛的那門徒”（約21:20）被認定為這卷福音書的作者（見本卷註釋第891頁）。第24,25節是整卷福音書一個適當的高潮（見約20:30註釋）。
**這些事。**指本章的敘述，無疑也指整卷福音書。
**我們也知道。**沒有說明這裡的“我們”指的是誰。其他人，可能是以弗所的長老（見本卷註釋第892頁），希望證實這卷書寫的是事實。偽造的講述，無良作者的著作當時都已經出現並有氾濫的趨勢。約翰迫切期望人們能夠知道事情的真相。
24.en:
**The disciple.** See on ch. 20:30. The “disciple whom Jesus loved” (ch. 21:20) is identified as the writer of the Gospel (see p. 891). Verses 24, 25 are a fitting climax to the entire Gospel (see on ch. 20:30).
**These things.** Referring to the narrative of this chapter, and doubtless also to the entire Gospel.
**We know.** We are not informed to whom the “we” refers. Others, probably the elders at Ephesus (see p. 892), wished to affirm that what had been written was, in very fact, the truth. Spurious narratives, the work of unscrupulous authors, were afloat, and John was anxious that the true facts should be known.

25.zh:
耶穌所行的事還有許多，若是一一的都寫出來，我想，所寫的書就是世界也容不下了。

**還有許多。**約翰在這最後一節中充滿激情地宣稱他的主還有許多值得注意的言行。他寫作這卷福音時，心中帶有一定的屬靈目標。他將與此相關的主說過的話語和發生的事件寫進書中（見本卷註釋第892頁）。其他福音書的作者也是這樣。結果耶穌的好多行為和事蹟就沒能記錄下來。
**也容不下了。**這裡採用誇張的語氣，有效地強調了耶穌的言行之多。據說與約翰寫作大約同時期的拉本撒該也說過一句類似誇張的話：“就是以整個天空當作羊皮卷，把所有的樹木當筆，有整個海洋的墨水，這也不足以讓我寫下我從我老師那裡學得的智慧”（見斯特拉克和比勒貝克，《新約註釋》，卷二第587頁）。這個猶太人的比喻後來通過F. M.雷曼所寫的讚美詩《真神之愛》得以流傳開來。關於《約翰福音》的結束語，加爾文說，“福音書的作者既注意到基督威嚴的偉大，在激動中叫喊，即便整個世界也不足以容納全部的敘述，我們難道不驚訝嗎？”
25.en:
**Many other things.** In this final verse John breaks forth in impassioned declaration concerning the many remarkable things his Master had said and done. He composed his Gospel with certain spiritual objectives in mind and related those events and recorded those sayings that would contribute to these objectives (see p. 892). The other gospel writers did likewise. Consequently many of Jesus’ deeds and acts were left unrecorded.
**Could not contain.** The language here is hyperbolic, but effectively serves to emphasize the vastness of the words and works of Jesus. A similar hyperbole from about the period in which John wrote has come to us from Rabban Jochanan ben Zakkai. He is reported to have said, “If the entire heaven were parchment and all the trees writing reeds, and the entire sea ink, that would not be sufficient to write down the wisdom I have learned from my teachers” (see Strack and Billerbeck, Kommentar zum Neuen Testament, Vol. 2 p. 587). This Jewish figure has since been popularized in the gospel song “The Love of God,” by F. M. Lehman. In writing of these concluding words of John, Calvin observes, “If the Evangelist, casting his eyes on the mightiness of the majesty of Christ, exclaims in astonishment, that even the whole world could not contain a full narrative of it, ought we to wonder?”
**Amen.** See on Matt. 5:18.

**I told you.** If Jesus had given a straight Yes answer to the question, the Jews would have misunderstood Him, for He was not the messiah of Jewish expectations (see on Luke 4:19). He could not have said No without, in a sense at least, denying His divine mission. As far as the record goes He had never publicly laid claim to that title (cf. John 4:26). However, He had repeatedly affirmed His kinship with His Father so as to leave no doubt in the mind of the honest seeker as to His identity (see chs. 5:17–47; 7:14–44; 8:12–59).
**Works that I do.** See on ch. 5:36.
25.zh:
耶穌回答說：我已經告訴你們，你們不信。我奉我父之名所行的事可以為我作見證；

**我已經告訴你們。**如果耶穌給猶太人一個直接肯定的答案，他們必要誤解祂，因為祂不是他們期望中的彌賽亞（見路4:19節註釋）。祂也不能給出一個否定的答案，如果那樣，祂就否認了祂神聖的使命。就聖經的記載而言，耶穌還從來沒有公開主張過自己彌賽亞的稱號（參約4:26）。然而，祂曾多次肯定祂與父的親緣關係，因此那些真誠尋求的人對耶穌的身份便不會再有疑惑（見約5:17-47；7:14-44；8:12-59）。
**我我父之名所行的事。**見約5:36註釋。

17.en:
**Therefore.** Demonstrations of unselfish love such as Jesus’ voluntary offering of Himself to redeem mankind became added reasons for the Father’s love.
**Take it again.** The plan of salvation had been laid before the creation of the earth (Rev. 13:8; PP 63). The resurrection of Jesus was as much a part of the eternal plan as the crucifixion. Jesus would pass under the dominion of death for but a brief period (Ps. 16:10; cf. Acts 2:31, 32) and then come forth glorified to be the resurrection and the life (John 11:25) and to be man’s intercessor (Heb. 7:25). As a result of His humiliation the Father would highly exalt Him and give Him a name above every name (Phil. 2:9).
17.zh:
我父愛我；因我將命捨去，好再取回來。

耶穌為救贖人類而甘願放棄自己的生命，這種無私之愛也是天父愛他的原因。
**再取回來。**救贖計劃在創造世界之前就已經定下了（啟13:8；《先祖與先知》63頁）。耶穌的復活和祂的被釘一樣，都是這永恆計劃中的一部分。耶穌要落在死亡的權下，但這段時間極其短暫（詩16:10；參徒2:31,32），之後就要在榮耀中復活，重得生命（約11:25），並要作人類的中保（來7:25）。祂謙卑的結果就是上帝將祂升為至高，又賜給祂那超乎萬名之上的名（腓2:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《拾級就主》第14頁；《成聖的人生》第82頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–18節）**。《歷代願望》第484，785頁。

15.en:
**Know I the Father.** On the close relationship between the Father and the Son see on Matt. 11:27; John 1:1, 18; cf. John 7:29; John 8:55.
**Lay down my life.** See on v. 11.
15.zh:
正如父認識我，我也認識父一樣；並且我為羊捨命。

**父認識我。**關於天父和祂愛子的親密關係，見太11:27；約1:1,18註釋；參約7:29；約8:55。
**捨命。**見第11節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《成聖的人生》第82頁。

16.en:
**Other sheep.** These were the Gentiles, Isaiah had predicted that the Messiah would be “a light of the Gentiles” (Isa. 42:6; cf. Isa. 49:6). Jesus declared Himself to be that light (Matt. 12:16–21). He was the light not of the Jewish nation only but of the world (John 8:12). “God so loved the world, that He gave” Jesus (ch. 3:16). At the time the Gentiles would take their place in the spiritual kingdom many of the Jews would be rejected (Matt. 8:11, 12; Rom. 11:1–26). The teaching of Jesus was explicit on this subject though it was not distinctly understood. The true position of the Gentile in the early church was a point much discussed (see on Acts 15:1).
**Hear my voice.** As do the other sheep (v. 3).
**One fold.** Literally, “one flock.” The reading “fold” has no support in any Greek manuscript and was introduced by Jerome, who translated both aulē (fold) and poimnē (flock) by the Latin ovile (fold). Jerome’s reading accords with the Roman Catholic assumption that that church is the one true fold. On the other hand the interpretation given to this passage by many Protestant commentators that there are many folds in which the one flock is housed is not hinted at in this passage.
16.zh:
我另外有羊，不是這圈裡的；我必須領他們來，他們也要聽我的聲音，並且要合成一群，歸一個牧人了。

**另外有羊。**指外邦人，以賽亞曾預言彌賽亞要“作外邦人的光”（賽42:6；參賽49:6）。耶穌宣稱祂就是那光（太12:16-21）。祂不僅是猶太人的光，更是全世界的光（約8:12）。“上帝愛世人，甚至將祂的獨生子賜給他們”（約3:16）。將來外邦人要進那屬靈的國度，而許多猶太人卻要被拒絕（太8:11,12；羅11:1-26）。儘管人們還沒有清楚地理解，但耶穌在這個問題上的教訓是明顯的。外邦人在早期教會中的真實地位是一個討論較多的問題（見徒15:1註釋）。
**聽我的聲音。**就像別的羊一樣（第3節）。
**一群。**有文本為“一欄”。任何希臘文手稿中都找不到“一欄”。它是哲羅姆引進來的。他將aulē（欄）和poimnē（群）都譯成拉丁語的ovile（欄）。哲羅姆的譯法符合羅馬天主教說他們教會是唯一的真羊欄的獨斷主張。另一方面，這裡也沒有暗示許多改正教的註釋家所解釋的，說有許多羊欄供一群羊居住。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷六第315頁。

14.en:
**The good shepherd.** See on v. 11.
**Know my sheep.** He knows His sheep by name (v. 3). They know not only His voice (v. 4), but they know Him. Knowledge leads to action. The good shepherd who knows the sheep of his flock, takes a personal, loving interest in each one of them; the sheep, in turn, knowing the character of their shepherd, place implicit confidence in their guardian and render loving, unquestioning obedience. See DA 479.
14.zh:
我是好牧人；我認識我的羊，我的羊也認識我，

**好牧人。**見第11節註釋。
**認識我的羊。**祂按著名字認識祂的羊（第3節）。他們不僅認得祂的聲音（第4節），他們還認識祂。認識導致行動。認識祂羊群中羊的好牧人以個人的慈愛照顧他們；反過來，羊也瞭解他們牧人的品格，完全信賴祂的保護並向祂表現出可愛的、毫無懷疑的順從。見《歷代願望》479頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給傳道人的證言》第158頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。《歷代願望》第476頁；《傳道良助》第181頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–17節）**。《歷代願望》第483頁。

1.zh:
我實實在在的告訴你們，人進羊圈，不從門進去，倒從別處爬進去，那人就是賊，就是強盜。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18；約1:51註釋。本段接續醫治瞎子的記敘。法利賽人作為以色列公認的牧人，沒有忠心於自己的職責。他們將一個向彌賽亞表示忠心的人趕了出去（約9:34）。
**羊圈。**aulē，一個環繞房屋、四面圈上籬笆、沒有頂棚的圍場，就像個院子（見太26:58節註釋）。常用作羊圈。有些學者認為這是指鄉下一種沒有頂的棚子。
**賊。**kleptēs，就像猶大從公共錢包裡盜竊那樣（約12:6）。做這樣事的人或許使用暴力或許不使用。暴力的概念更適合於“強盜”（ lēsteôs），比如巴拉巴（約18:40）。一個人翻牆進入羊圈，這種行為就證明了他不是羊的主人。他可能是個鬼鬼祟祟的毛賊，趁著夜色前來偷竊，也可能是個強盜，使用暴力來搶奪別人的財物。但不論從哪方面來說，他都是個假牧人。
耶穌這裡所說的賊和強盜特別指法利賽人，這些人宣稱他們是以色列的牧者。他們能決定誰可以留下，誰將要被趕出。他們“正當人前，把天國的門關了”，正要進去的人，他們也不容他們進去（太23:13）。他們走遍海洋陸地，勾引一個人入教，既入了教，卻使他作地獄之子，比他們還加倍（太23:15）。他們把“知識的鑰匙”奪了去（路11:52），因為他們對經文虛假的解釋阻擋了許多人認識並接受那光。
賊和強盜就是那些為人提供耶穌基督以外得救方法的人（徒4:12）。這個世界過去和將來都有假彌賽亞出現。他們不是通過基督耶穌這道門進來的（約10:9）。他們的主張是虛假的，他們精心策劃的詭計終必破產。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第477頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–30節）**。《歷代願望》第476-484頁。
1.en:
**Verily.** [The Good Shepherd, John 10:1–21.] See on Matt. 5:18; John 1:51. The present passage is a sequel to the healing of the blind man. The Pharisees, the recognized shepherds of Israel, had been unfaithful to their trust. They had cast out one from the fold who had expressed faith in the Messiah (John 9:34).
**Sheepfold.** Gr. aulē, a fenced-in, unroofed enclosure around a house, such as a courtyard (see on Matt. 26:58). This was sometimes used as an enclosure for sheep. Some scholars think that an uncovered enclosure in the country is referred to.
**Thief.** Gr. kleptēs, one who pilfers, or steals,as did Judas from the common purse (ch. 12:6). He may or may not employ violence. The idea of violence is more prominent in the word for “robber,” lēstẽs, “one who plunders.” Such was Barabbas (ch. 18:40). The one who climbs up and over the wall of the enclosure by a way of his own making gives evidence that he is not the owner of the sheep. He may be a lone sneak thief carrying out his pilfering under cover of darkness, or he may be one of a gang of robbers who acquires property by violence. In any case he is a false shepherd.
By thieves and robbers Jesus was here designating especially the Pharisees, who claimed that they were the shepherds of Israel. They decreed who should be admitted to, and who should be expelled from, the fold. They “shut up the kingdom of heaven against men” and prevented those who sought to enter (Matt. 23:13). They compassed land and sea to make one proselyte, but when he was made he was twofold more a child of hell than they (Matt. 23:15). They took away the “key of knowledge” (Luke 11:52), and by their false interpretation of the Scriptures prevented men from recognizing and accepting the light.
Thieves and robbers are they who offer men any other means of salvation than that which has been provided through Jesus Christ (Acts 4:12). The world has had, and will continue to have, its false messiahs. They do not enter by the door, Christ Jesus (John 10:9). Their claims, are false, and their carefully laid schemes will end in disaster.

2.zh:
從門進去的，才是羊的牧人。

**羊的牧人。**真牧人從門進入羊圈。他靠近他的羊，領它們出來，在日光之下放牧。這裡牧人和門是有區別的。後面耶穌稱祂自己是“門”（第9節）和“牧人”（第14節）。
聖經中經常使用牧人的比喻。耶和華被稱為神聖的牧人（詩第23篇；賽40:11），而以色列那些不忠心的領袖被稱為假牧人（結34:1-10；參耶23:14）。在弗4:11中牧人被稱為“牧師”。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–4節）**。《歷代願望》第478頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–5節）**。見太24：23、24懷愛倫註釋。
2.en:
**The shepherd of the sheep.** The true shepherd makes use of the door regularly provided for such an enclosure. He approaches it and leads out his sheep in broad daylight. The shepherd and the door are here distinguished. Later Jesus identified Himself as both the “door” (v. 9) and the “shepherd” (v. 14).
The figure of the shepherd is common in the Scriptures. Jehovah is presented as the divine Shepherd (Ps. 23; Isa. 40:11), and the unfaithful leaders of Israel as false shepherds (Eze. 34:1–10; cf. Jer. 23:14). In Eph. 4:11 the shepherds are spoken of as “pastors.”

3.zh:
看門的就給他開門；羊也聽他的聲音。他按著名叫自己的羊，把羊領出來。

**看門的。**直譯是“守門人”。這個詞的陰性形式譯為“看門的使女”（約18:16）。“看門的”在夜間照管羊群。到了早晨，牧人回來，按著名字呼喚他的羊，引領它們到牧場上。
**自己的羊。**暗示除了他自己的羊群之外，還有別的羊群。可能是兩到三個羊群同在一個牧場之內。但只有那屬於那個牧人的羊才會回應他的呼喚。至今東方的土地上，夜間仍有數個羊群在一起露營，到了早晨，每個羊群的牧人從不同的地方趕來，帶出他的羊群。
**把羊領出來。**參民27:17的話。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第479，480頁；《基督教育原理》第273頁；《今日的生活》第160頁；《醫療佈道論》第181頁；《證言》卷四第444，503頁；《證言》卷五第346，435頁。
3.en:
**Porter.** Literally, “doorkeeper.” The feminine form is translated “her that kept the door” (ch. 18:16). The “porter” had charge of the flock during the night. In the morning the shepherd would return, call his sheep by name, and lead them out to pasture.
**His own sheep.** This phrase implies that there were other flocks besides his own that were sheltered there. Perhaps two or three flocks were housed in a single enclosure. Only the sheep belonging to the shepherd would respond to his call. In Oriental lands today several flocks bivouac together at night, and in the morning each shepherd sets out in a different direction, calling out to his sheep.
**Leadeth them out.** Compare the language in Num. 27:17.

4.zh:
既放出自己的羊來，就在前頭走，羊也跟著他，因為認得他的聲音。

**羊也跟著他。**東方國家牧人的生活與他的羊群非常緊密。當最後一隻羊被聚攏了來，牧人站在羊群的前頭，羊就跟著他走，沒有絲毫的勉強。《米德拉西》描述這種習慣說：“‘你曾引導你的百姓，好像羊群一般’（詩77:20）。就像羊群只要看見牧人在前頭走就會跟從，同樣，只要摩西和亞倫指示以色列人前行的道路，他們就會跟從”（拉巴，民33:1節註釋，第865頁）。“這對於那些像趕牲口一樣驅使教會的牧人來說是何等大的教訓啊，真牧人是在愛中，在言語上，在行為裡引導他的羊群的”（羅卜遜）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第479，480頁；《基督教育原理》第271頁；《證言》卷一第232頁；《證言》卷三第228頁；見林後11：14懷愛倫註釋。
4.en: **The sheep follow him.** The Eastern shepherd lives very close to his flock. When the last sheep has been brought from the fold the shepherd places himself at the head of the flock and the sheep follow him, normally without hesitancy. The custom is referred to in the Midrash: “‘Thou didst lead Thy people like a flock’ [Ps. 77:20]. As a flock follows the shepherd so long as the shepherd leads it, so Israel, wherever Moses and Aaron made them journey, followed them” (Rabbah, on Num. 33:1, Soncino ed., p. 865). “What a lesson for pastors who seek to drive the church like cattle and fail. The true pastor leads in love, in words, in deeds” (Robertson).

5.zh:
羊不跟著生人；因為不認得他的聲音。必要逃跑。

**生人。**特指第1節中提到的賊和強盜，當然，也包括其他羊群的牧人。
**羊不跟著。**希臘原文表達強烈的否定。伴隨著牧人熟悉聲音的是保護、引導和牧草，而陌生的聲音則是一種危險的警報。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第191頁；《證言》卷二第142頁；《證言》卷五第512頁。
5.en:
**A stranger.** Particularly the thief and robber mentioned in v. 1, though, of course, anyone, even the shepherd of another flock.
**Will they not follow.** The negative is strongly expressed in the Greek. With the familiar tones of the shepherd’s voice the sheep associate protection, guidance, and pasture. The strange voice arouses, alarm.

6.zh:
耶穌將這比喻告訴他們，但他們不明白所說的是什麼意思。

**比喻。**paroimia，不是通常用來指“寓言”的parabolē，定義見本卷註釋第203頁。在七十士譯本中，paroimia和parabolē都是譯自希伯來文詞語mashal。關於mashal的定義見《SDA聖經註釋》卷三第945頁。Paroimia在新約中只出現過五次：本節，約16:25中兩次，第29節一次，彼後2:22中一次。它在彼後2:22中的意思是“俗語”，但這種定義不適合它在《約翰福音》中的用法。約翰用這個詞描述一種象徵性的、比喻性的、也許還帶有神秘性的格言。第10章的講話不同於一般的比喻，因為它沒有把外表的事實與理想的真理完全分開，象真正的比喻那樣。
**他們不明白。**即他們沒有理解耶穌話中的真義。他們只理解了祂話語的表面意思，而其中所蘊涵的屬靈真理對他們來說還是隱藏的。他們在屬靈上是瞎眼的（約9:40,41）。
6.en:
**Parable.** Gr. paroimia, not parabolē, the usual word for “parable,” for a definition of which see p. 203. In the LXX paroimia and parabolē oth translate the Heb. mashal, for a definition of which see Vol. III, p. 945. Paroimia occurs only five times in the NT: here, in John 16:25 (twice), 29, and in 2 Peter 2:22. In this last reference it clearly means “proverb,” but this definition does not suit the usages of the word in John. John uses the word to describe a symbolic or figurative, perhaps enigmatic, saying. “Allegory” or “figure” would be a close English equivalent. The discourse of John 10 differs from what is usually termed a parable in that it does not keep the outer facts wholly distinct from the ideal truths as is done in true parables.
**They understood not.** That is, they did not grasp the truth Jesus was illustrating. They understood the outer facts, of course, but the spiritual truths remained hidden from them. They were spiritually blind (ch. 9:40, 41).

7.zh:
所以，耶穌又對他們說：我實實在在的告訴你們，我就是羊的門。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18；約1:51註釋。
**羊的門。**這是羊進出的門。後面耶穌說祂也是好牧人（第11節）。現在祂宣稱祂是進出屬靈牧場唯一的真門（參見第9節）。只有通過祂才能進入屬靈的國度。那些教訓說還有其他辦法進到上帝面前的人都是假牧人，假師傅。這些話是對法利賽人說的。他們堅持認為只要遵守律法救恩就會臨到他們（見太19:16註釋）。他們拒絕了耶穌，就是拒絕了“道路、真理、生命”（約14:6），他們還想要阻止別人──比如第9章裡那個被治好的瞎子──接受祂。
7.en:
**Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18; John 1:51.
**Door of the sheep.** That is, the door by which the sheep enter. Later Jesus identifies Himself also as the shepherd (v. 11). He now declares Himself to be the only true entrance to the spiritual fold (cf. v. 9). Access to the spiritual kingdom is possible only through Him. Those who hold forth any other means of access to God are false shepherds, false teachers. Such were the Pharisees to whom these words were addressed. They clung to the teaching that salvation comes to those who observe the torah (see on Matt. 19:16). They rejected Jesus, “the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14:6), and tried to prevent others, such as the blind man ofch. 9, from accepting Him.

8.zh:
凡在我以先來的都是賊，是強盜；羊卻不聽他們。

**是賊，是強盜。**見第1節註釋。

9.zh:
我就是門；凡從我進來的，必然得救，並且出入得草吃。

**我就是門。**見第7節註釋。
**凡從我進來的。**祂的呼召非常廣泛。這門為所有願意進來的人敞開（參啟22:17）。
**出入。**凡進到基督裡的人將要享受真救贖所能提供的一切特權──保護，安寧，以及為他的心靈預備的屬靈糧食。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–10節）**。《歷代願望》第477頁。
9.en:
**I am the door.** See on v. 7.
**Any man.** The call is universal. The door is open to all who desire to enter (cf. Rev. 22:17).
**Go in and out.** He shall enjoy all the privileges that true salvation offers—protection, safety, security, and peace, as well as spiritual food for his soul.

10.zh:
盜賊來，無非要偷竊，殺害，毀壞；我來了，是要叫羊（或作：人）得生命，並且得的更豐盛。

**盜賊。**見第1節註釋。牧人總是不斷地進出照顧他的羊，但盜賊只是偶爾到來，純粹是出於自私的目的，且要毀滅羊群。
**我。**“我”在希臘文中是強調的，與盜賊形成對比。
**生命。**zōē，這裡用它的神學意義，等同於永生。亞當和夏娃在被造之初就擁有zōē，但當他們犯罪時就失去了。他們肉體的生命或許暫時存留，但他們已經不是不朽的了（見創2:17註釋）。耶穌來就是要恢復亞當所失去的zōē（見約8:51註釋）。
**更豐盛。**“生命”包括靈、智、體三方面。肉體生命的豐盛在於身體充滿精力，完全健康。耶穌所行的醫治肉體的神蹟使那些生命力量正在消退的人重新獲得強盛的精力。但是人肉體上精力和健康的恢復並不能完全實現耶穌的使命。人還有智力和屬靈的生命，這兩部分也必須活躍強盛起來，因為“人活著不是單靠食物，乃是靠耶和華口裡所出的一切話”（申8:3）。就像肉體和智力兩方面對於一個均衡飽滿之生命的重要性一樣，一個人的生命若想完全，他的屬靈本性也需得到培養。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第270，787頁；《今日的生活》第295頁。
10.en:
**The thief.** See on v. 1. The shepherd constantly goes in and out among his sheep. The thief visits the flock only on rare occasions and for purely selfish motives, and ruins the flock.
**I.** Emphatic in the Greek in contrast with the thief.
**Life.** zōē, here used in its theological sense, equivalent to eternal life. When Adam and Eve were created they possessed zōē, but lost it when they sinned. True, their physical life was extended, but they were no longer conditionally immortal (see on Gen. 2:17). Jesus came to restore the zōē that Adam had forfeited (see on John 8:51).
**More abundantly.** “Life” includes the physical, intellectual, and spiritual. Physical life is regarded as abundant in a body that is full of vigor and in perfect health. Jesus’ miracles of physical healing gave an abundant physical life to those whose life forces were ebbing. But physical restoration was by no means the complete fulfillment of Jesus’ mission. Man also has intellectual and spiritual life, which must also be made alive and abundant, for “man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord” (Deut. 8:3). Important as the physical and the intellectual aspects of a well-rounded life are, no life is fully complete unless the spiritual nature is nurtured.

11.zh:
我是好牧人；好牧人為羊捨命。

**好牧人。**關於牧人的比喻，見第2節註釋。耶穌作為牧人的形象已經深深地烙印在教會的記憶中，在它的文學、藝術、音樂和雕刻中都體現出來。形容詞“好”（kalos）表示一個人行使職責盡善盡美，是一個非常傑出、優秀和不一般的人。kalos在提前4:6節中描述一個好執事，在提後2:3中描述一個好士兵。
將彌賽亞比作牧人，這對於猶太人來說並不感到新鮮。大致寫於公元前一世紀中葉的《所羅門詩篇》這樣描述受膏者：“（祂將要）忠心正直地牧養耶和華的羊群，祂使它們在草地上不失腳。祂正確地引導它們，它們中間沒有驕傲，在它們中間也沒有受欺壓的”（17:45,46）。
**捨命。**這裡是和盜賊進行對比，盜賊來是要“偷竊，殺害，毀壞”（第10節）。《舊約》中沒有關於牧人真正為他的羊犧牲性命的記載，但撒上17:34-37反映了這個職業的危險。那種引導牧人為他的羊群甘冒生命危險的自我犧牲精神在好牧者身上得到了完美的體現，即便地上只有一個人需要拯救，祂也會捨棄祂的生命（見《歷代願望》483頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第261頁；《歷代願望》第24，476頁；《傳道良助》第181頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第186頁；《證言》卷五第346頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–14節）**。《先祖與先知》第191頁。
11.en:
**The good shepherd.** For the figure of the shepherd see on v. 2. The image of Jesus as the shepherd has impressed itself deeply upon the mind of the church, in its literature, art, music, and statuary. The adjective “good” (Gr. kalos) designates one who performs his service well, one who is extraordinary,outstanding, excellent. In 1 Tim. 4:6 kalos describes a good minister and in 2 Tim. 2:3 a good soldier.
The figure of Messiah as a shepherd was not new to the Jews. In the Psalms of Solomon, written about the middle of the 1st century .., the Anointed One is spoken of as follows: “(He will be) shepherding the flock of the Lord faithfully and righteously, and will suffer none among them to stumble in their pasture. He will lead them all aright, And there will be no pride among them that any among them should be oppressed” (17:45, 46).
**Giveth his life.** This is in contrast with the thief, who comes “to steal, and to kill, and to destroy” (v. 10). There is no OT example of a shepherd actually laying down his life for his sheep, although the hazards of the occupation are reflected in 1 Sam. 17:34–37. The self-sacrifice that leads the shepherd to hazard his life for a member of his flock has its ideal fulfillment in the Good Shepherd, who would have given His life for even one member of the human race (see DA 483).

12.zh:
若是僱工，不是牧人，羊也不是他自己的，他看見狼來，就撇下羊逃走；狼抓住羊，趕散了羊群。

**僱工。**《密西拿》列舉了四種受託人（監護人）：“無償的監護人，借用的監護人，僱傭的監護人，租來的監護人。一個無償的監護人必須為一切東西起誓（如果託付物丟失或損壞，除了監護人的過失之外，無償的監護人必須為所發生的事起誓，就可以免除責任）。借用的監護人必須賠付所有的損失。僱傭的監護人或租來的監護人必須為受傷的，或（在搶劫中）被擄掠或死亡的牲畜起誓；但他必須為丟失和偷竊承擔責任”（Baba Mezi'a7. 8，《塔木德》松奇諾版，第537頁）。《密西拿》還列舉了監護人所要承擔的責任：“（如果）一隻狼（攻擊），這不是不可避免的事件；如果兩隻（攻擊），這是不可避免的事件。……兩隻狗的（攻擊）不是不可避免的。……一個強盜的（攻擊）是不可避免的。獅子，熊，豹，蛇造成的（損失）列為不可避免的事件。什麼時候是這種情況呢？當這些猛獸和蛇自己前來並（攻擊）的時候。但如果他（牧人）將羊群引到猛獸經常出沒的地方，那就不是不可避免的事件了”（出處同上7. 9，《塔木德》松奇諾版，第540頁）。
僱工關心他的工資過於關心羊群。他個人的利益並不在羊群中（參彼前5:2）。危險的時刻將把他和真牧人區別開來。
**狼抓住羊。**根據《密西拿》，如果只有一隻狼攻擊羊群，那麼牧人要為羊群負責；如果有兩隻，就算作不可避免的意外事故（見上面“僱工”註釋）。但是真牧人卻會不惜自己的生命去保護羊群。將這裡和太10:6；徒20:29進行比較。
**趕散了羊群。**將這裡與亞13:7進行比較。
12.en:
**Hireling.** The Mishnah mentions four kinds of bailees (guardians): “a gratuitous bailee, a borrower, a paid bailee, and a hirer. A gratuitous bailee must swear for everything [if the bailment is lost or destroyed through any cause, excepting negligence, the unpaid trustee must swear to the occurrence, and is free from liability]. A borrower must pay for everything. A paid bailee or a hirer must swear concerning an animal that was injured, captured [in a raid] or that perished; but must pay for a loss or theft” (Baba Meẓi’a 7. 8, in Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 537). The same tractate sets forth the responsibility of the guardian as follows: “[If] one wolf [attacks], it is not an unavoidable accident; if two [attack], it is an unavoidable accident. … [The attack of] two dogs is not an unavoidable accident. … A robber’s [attack] is an unavoidable accident. [Damage done by] a lion, bear, leopard, panther and snake ranks as an unavoidable accident. When is this? If they came [and attacked] of their own accord: but if he [the shepherd] led them to a place infested by wild beasts and robbers, it is no unavoidable accident” (ibid. 7. 9, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 540).
The hireling cares more for his hire than for the sheep. He does not take a personal interest in the flock (cf. 1 Peter 5:2). The hour of danger distinguishes him from the true shepherd.
**The wolf catcheth them.** According to the Mishnah, if only one wolf attacked, the shepherd was held accountable for the flock; if two, it was counted as an unavoidable accident (see above under “Hireling”). But the true shepherd would risk his life to protect the flock. Compare Matt. 10:6; Acts 20:29.
**Scattereth the sheep.** Compare Zech. 13:7.

13.zh:
僱工逃走，因他是僱工，並不顧念羊。

**僱工逃走。**原文的證據（參見第146頁）傾向於刪去這句話。然而這句話對於整個句子的完整還是需要的。關於僱工，見第12節註釋。
13.en: **Hireling fleeth.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the omission of this clause. However, some clause is needed to complete the thought of the sentence. The RSV supplies “he flees.” For a discussion of the hireling see on v. 12.

18.zh:
沒有人奪我的命去，是我自己捨的。我有權柄捨了，也有權柄取回來。這是我從我父所受的命令。

**沒有人。**直譯是“沒有一個”，還可以包括超自然的生靈。耶穌為了救贖人類而放下自己的生命完全是出於自願。祂的父一點也沒有勉強祂（見第17節註釋）。祂若不是自願放下自己的生命，撒但也不能將祂怎麼樣。
**奪。**有文本為過去時態，可以理解為基督的死是“創世以前”（彼前1:20）就預定了。祂是“創世以來……被殺之羔羊”（啟13:8）。但祂獻出生命卻是出於自願。
**權柄。**exousia，“權威”，“權利”，“特權”，而不是能力或力量（見約1:12註釋）。
**從我父所受的。**整件事的程序都和父上帝的旨意和諧一致。同時承擔起這個責任也是基督自願的選擇，這是祂自由的行動。父與子的合作完全是按照創世以前（彼前1:20；《先祖與先知》63頁）的約定進行的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第295頁；見約1：4；20：17懷愛倫註釋。
18.en:
**No man.** Literally, “no one,” a term that might include supernatural beings. The laying down of Jesus’ life for the salvation of man was entirely voluntary. There was no compulsion on the part of His Father (see on v. 17). Nor could Satan have touched His life had He not laid it down voluntarily.
**Taketh.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between this and the reading “took.” This latter reading could be understood in the sense that Christ’s death was “foreordained before the foundation of the world” (1 Peter 1:20). He was the “Lamb slain from the foundation of the world” (Rev. 13:8). But the offering of His life was voluntary.
**Power.** Gr. exousia, “authority,” “right,” “privilege,” rather than ability or strength (see on ch. 1:12).
**Received of my Father.** The procedure was in harmony with the will of God the Father. At the same time it was Christ’s own will to take it up again; it was His free act. The Father and Son were working in full accord with the agreement entered into before the foundation of the world (1 Peter 1:20; PP 63).

19.zh:
猶太人為這些話又起了紛爭。

**紛爭。**同法利賽人在那生來眼瞎之人的事上所起的爭論一樣（約9:16；參約7:43）。
19.en: **Division.** As there had been in the case of the man born blind (ch. 9:16; cf. ch. 7:43).

20.zh:
內中有好些人說：他是被鬼附著，而且瘋了，為什麼聽他呢？

**祂是被鬼附著。**還是那個老的的控告（約7:20；8:48；參可3:21,22）。關於被鬼附著的，見《馬可福音》第1章補充註釋。發瘋被認為是鬼附身的一種表現。
20.en: **He hath a devil.** An old charge (John 7:20; 8:48; cf. Mark 3:21, 22). For a discussion of demon possession see Additional Note on Mark 1. Madness was considered one of the results of demon possession.

21.zh:
又有人說：這不是鬼附之人所說的話。鬼豈能叫瞎子的眼睛開了呢？

**鬼附之人。**這部分人推論說耶穌的言行決不像被鬼附著的人。惡魔控制了一個人必然會使他的思想失常，攪亂並矇蔽他的思維，外在的表現就是胡言亂語。一個被邪靈附著的人無論如何也不能行這樣的神蹟使一個天生瞎眼的人恢復視力。這一節證明，當前在公會里的確有一批主持正義的人。
[在修殿節上：約10:22-42。見本卷註釋223頁地圖；231頁圖表]。
21.en: **That hath a devil.** This group reasoned that the speech and actions of Jesus were very different from those of one demon possessed. When a demon takes control it usually disorders the mind, confuses and beclouds the thinking, and produces incoherent speech and reasoning. Under no circumstances could one possessed by an evil spirit perform a miracle so outstanding as the opening of the eyes of a man born blind. There is evidence in this verse of the presence of the presence of a better group among the Sanhedrin.

22.zh:
在耶路撒冷有修殿節，是冬天的時候。

**修殿節。**這個節期是猶大-馬加比設立的，為的是紀念在安條克四世汙穢聖殿之後聖殿的潔淨以及聖殿崇拜的恢復（見但11:14註釋）。根據《馬加比上》4:59“隨後，猶大和他的兄弟們以及以色列全體會眾宣告，把每年基斯流月二十五日的連續八天作為慶祝聖壇重新供奉的幸福快樂的節期”。約瑟弗斯說這個節期叫作“燈光節”（《猶太古代史》 xii. 7.7 [325頁]）。它的慶祝方式和住棚節有些相似（《馬加比下》10:6,7）。基斯流月處於我們現在公曆的11/12月間（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷二第116頁）。在拉比們的文學作品中這個節期被稱為哈奴卡，意思是“奉獻”。
**是冬天的時候。**根據《塔木德》（Baba Mezi`a 106b，松奇諾版第608頁），冬季是從基斯流月中旬開始，持續到細罷特月中旬（大概是十二月中旬到次年二月中旬）。用作冬天的這個詞（cheimōn）可以是指冬季，也可以指潮溼多雨的天氣。約翰這裡的話只是在說耶穌因為天氣的惡劣而在所羅門的廊下（第23節）。
22.en:
**Feast of the dedication.** [At the Feast of Dedication, John 10:22–42. See Closing Peraean Ministry; The Ministry of Our Lord] This feast was instituted by Judas Maccabaeus to celebrate the cleansing of the Temple and the restoration of its services following the defilement by Antiochus Ephiphanes (see on Dan. 11:14). According to 1 Macc. 4:59 “Judas and his brethren with the whole congregation of Israel ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.” Josephus says the festival was called “the festival of Lights” (Antiquities xii. 7.7 [325]). It was celebrated in somewhat the same manner as the Feast of Tabernacles (2 Macc. 10:6, 7). The month of Casleu (Kislev, or Chisleu) corresponds to our Nov./Dec. (see Vol. II, p. 116). In rabbinical literature the feast is called Hanukkah, meaning “dedication.”
**It was winter.** According to the Talmud (Baba Meẓi‘a 106b, Soncino ed., p. 608) winter extended from about the middle of Kislev to the middle of Shebat (about the middle of December to the middle of December to the middle of February). The word for winter (cheimōn) may refer either to the season or simply to wet, stormy weather. John may have introduced the remark simply to show that Jesus was in Solomon’s porch (v. 23) because the weather was inclement at that season.

23.zh:
耶穌在殿裡所羅門的廊下行走。

**所羅門的廊。**這是聖殿東面的一道柱廊，它在公元前586年的浩劫中倖存下來，成為所羅門時代藝術技巧的象徵（見約瑟弗斯《猶太古代史》 xx. 9. 7；《猶太戰爭史》5. 1 [185頁]）。徒3:11；5:12中也提到了這個走廊。
23.en: **Solomon’s porch.** A colonnade to the east of the Temple proper that was supposed to have survived the destruction of the Temple in 586 .. and thus to have been a part of the workmanship of Solomon (see Josephus Antiquities xx. 9. 7; War v. 5. 1 [185]). The porch is mentioned also in Acts 3:11; 5:12.

24.zh:
猶太人圍著他，說：你叫我們猶疑不定到幾時呢？你若是基督，就明明的告訴我們。

**叫我們猶疑不定。**直譯是“叫我們懸著心”。意思是“使我們處在懸念之中”或“使我們苦惱[焦急，憂慮]”。從猶太人的態度判斷他們所顯示出來的不是一種真誠的求問。
**基督。**就是彌賽亞（見太1:1註釋）。耶穌避免用這個稱呼稱自己，主要可能是因為這個稱呼的政治涵義（見路4:19註釋）。
24.en:
**Make us to doubt.** Literally, “lift up our soul.” The expression is thought to mean “keep us in suspense,” or possibly “trouble [annoy, or vex] us.” Judging from the attitude the Jews had manifested up to this point, this was not a sincere inquiry.
**Christ.** That is, the Messiah (see on Matt. 1:1). Jesus avoided applying this title to Himself, perhaps largely because of its political connotations (see on Luke 4:19).

26.zh:
只是你們不信，因為你們不是我的羊。

**不是我的羊。**信心和順從是跟從真牧者之人的特徵。猶太人的不信並不是他們不屬於基督羊圈的結果，他們的不信只證明了他們不是他的羊。
26.en:
**Not of my sheep.** Faith and obedience are the earmarks of the followers of the True Shepherd. The unbelief of the Jews was not the result of their not belonging to Christ’s fold, but it was evidence that they were not His sheep.
**As I said unto you.** Textual evidence favors the omission (cf. p. 146) of this clause. No essential point is involved. Whether stated or not, Jesus was referring to the discussion of the good shepherd in vs. 1–18.

27.zh:
我的羊聽我的聲音，我也認識他們，他們也跟著我。

**聽我的聲音。**見第4節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第307頁；《兒童教育指南》第467頁；《基督教育之研究》第114頁；《證言》卷六第401頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（27–28節）**。《歷代願望》第480頁。

28.zh:
我又賜給他們永生；他們永不滅亡，誰也不能從我手裡把他們奪去。

**我又賜給。**用的是現在時態，表明恩典是現在賜下的（見約8:51；10:10註釋）。
**他們永不滅亡。**這句話在希臘文中表達強烈的否定。這裡的“滅亡”指的是最後的、不可避免的、第二次的死亡（啟20:14；參太10:28；約3:16）。第一次的死只是一個短暫的睡眠（詩146:4；林後5:1-4；帖前4:13-18），一段“免了將來的禍患”（賽57:1,2）的休息，在這段時間裡義人的生命要“與基督一同藏在上帝裡面”（西3:3）。肉體的死亡既臨到義人，也臨到惡人，從這一點上來說，“羊”是不受保護的。然而，給他們的應許是，他們必不受第二次死的“害”（啟2:11；參啟20:6）。見約3:16；5:25-29註釋。
**誰。**直譯是“任何一個”，包括撒但在內。羊只有在一種情況下才會被從牧人手中奪去，那就是他們自願離去。當羊完全是出於自願離開時，他們除了自己誰都不能責備。他們不能將自己的背叛歸因於撒但，因為撒但儘管能教唆引誘他們，但他決不能強迫人犯罪（見《教會證言》卷五第177頁）。有人相信，人一朝得救便不可能失喪了，本節決沒有支持這種致命的推斷。如果羊執意偏行己路，非要離開牧人的照顧，便沒有什麼能阻攔它的了。
**懷愛倫註釋（28–29節）**。《使徒行述》第553，586頁；《基督教育原理》第308頁；《服務真詮》第182頁；《先知與君王》第587頁；《拾級就主》第72頁；《證言》卷一第97頁；《證言》卷六第367頁。
28.en:
**I give.** The tense is present. The gift is bestowed now (see on chs. 8:51; 10:10).
**They shall never perish.** The negative is very strongly expressed in the Greek. In its fullest significance “perish” here has reference to the final, irrevocable death, the second death (Rev. 20:14; cf. Matt. 10:28; John 3:16). The first death is only a short sleep (Ps. 146:4; 2 Cor. 5:1–4; 1 Thess. 4:13–18), a brief laying to rest “from the evil to come” (Isa. 57:1, 2), during which time the life of the righteous is “hid with Christ in God” (Col. 3:3). Physical death comes to the righteous and the wicked alike and from this the “sheep” are not protected. They are, however, given the promise that they will not be “hurt” by the second death (Rev. 2:11; cf. ch. 20:6). See on John 3:16; 5:25–29.
**Any man.** Literally, “anyone,” Satan included. There is only one way in which the sheep may be removed from the shepherd’s hand, and that is by their own voluntary choice. When the sheep depart they do so voluntarily, and have no one to blame but themselves. They cannot charge against Satan their defection, for though he may solicit he cannot force men to apostatize (see 5T 177). This verse lends no support to the fatal presumption that once a man is saved it is impossible for him to be lost. There is nothing to prevent the sheep from wandering away from the shepherd’s care if they choose to do so.

29.zh:
我父把羊賜給我，他比萬有都大，誰也不能從我父手裡把他們奪去。

**有文本是“羊比萬有都大”。**但這裡討論的重點顯然是，天父超乎萬有的權柄和尊榮是羊得安全的基礎和保證，而不是在說羊是超乎萬有的。
29.en: **My Father, which gave them me.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between this and the reading, “As for my Father, that which he has given me is greater than all.” The context seems definitely to favor the reading that appears in the KJV, RSV, etc. The point of discussion is apparently the superiority of the Father over all as the basis for the security of the sheep, not the superiority of the sheep.

30.zh:
我與父原為一。

**原為一。**原文的“一”是中性的，表明這裡不是討論位格一致的問題。耶穌不是這裡討論的重點。耶穌主張祂與父在意志、決心和目的上是一致的。耶穌的言行是天父旨意的彰顯。除此之外，這句話還暗示著耶穌與天父的親密關係。耶穌的話在猶太人看來就是祂主張自己是神（約10:32,33；參約5:18,19）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第419頁；《證言》卷八第265頁；《證言》卷九第68頁。
30.en: **Are one.** The word for “one” is neuter, showing that unity of person is not the point under discussion. Jesus is not the point under discussion. Jesus asserted His unity with the Father in will, purpose, and objectives. The Father was behind the words and actions of Jesus. Beyond that the words carried the implication of Jesus’ close relationship with the Father. The Jews understood His words to be a claim to divinity (ch. 10:32, 33; cf. ch. 5:18, 19).

31.zh:
猶太人又拿起石頭來要打他。

**拿起石頭來。**他們大約兩個月前住棚節時也這樣做過（約8:59）。
31.en: **Took up stones.** They had done so about two months before at the Feast of Tabernacles (ch. 8:59).

32.zh:
耶穌對他們說：我從父顯出許多善事給你們看，你們是為哪一件拿石頭打我呢？

**我從父。**將這裡與約5:19,36；9:4進行比較。
**為哪一件。**直譯是“為哪一種”。
**拿石頭打。**按照希臘文的意思，是企圖拿石頭去打。猶太人打算這樣做，但還沒有動手。
32.en:
**From my Father.** Compare chs. 5:19, 36; 9:4.
**For which.** Literally, “for what kind.”
**Stone.** That is, attempt to stone, as the Greek may be interpreted. The action is attempted but not carried out.

33.zh:
猶太人回答說：我們不是為善事拿石頭打你，是為你說僭妄的話；又為你是個人，反將自己當作神。

**為你說僭妄的話。**猶太人感覺到了耶穌話中責備的力量，他們也承認耶穌的善行對他們來說不是沒有意義的。儘管如此，事實卻是祂的好行為反倒使他們的惡念變的更加強烈了。然而，他們還用一種高尚的動機來掩飾自己；他們冒充為上帝的榮耀大發熱心。後來他們又在彼拉多面前控告耶穌犯了僭妄的罪（約19:7）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第470頁。
33.en: **For blasphemy.** The Jews felt the force of Jesus’ reproach and would not admit that His good works were without meaning to them. It was true, nevertheless, that His good works had stimulated their ill will into more intense activity. However, they credited themselves with a higher motive than a doctrinal one; they affected great jealousy for the honor of God. The charge of blasphemy was later lodged before Pilate (ch. 19:7).

34.zh:
耶穌說：你們的律法上豈不是寫著我曾說你們是神嗎？

**你們的律法。**有文本無“你們的”。但即便保留“你們的律法”，也不能看作是耶穌否定祂親自頒佈的律法。“你們的”可以強調是你們自己承認為權威的律法說的。將這裡與約8:17進行比較。這裡的“律法”（nomos），就像在約12:34；15:25等一樣，是指整個《舊約》而言的，並不像它經常被認為的那樣（約1:17等），單指摩西五經。“律法”的這種用法還出現在拉比的文學作品中。例如，在回答妥拉（律法）在哪裡證明死人將要復活的問題時，《塔木德》松奇諾版引用了詩84:4作為證據（Sanhedrin 91b，第614頁）。
**你們是神。**這裡引用詩82:6。這首詩是在指控不公正的法官，說他們是“神”（見《詩篇》第82篇前言和第1,6節註釋）。拉比的遺傳將“神”用在接受律法的人身上：“以色列人接受了律法，所以死亡的使者在他們身上沒有權柄（詩82:6,7）”（《塔木德》松奇諾版`Abodah Zarah5a，第21頁）。耶穌好像是在用他們遺傳的話來回答他們（見35節註釋）。然而，耶穌是“上帝”，與詩82:6的意思完全不同。
34.en:
**In your law.** Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between retaining or omitting the pronoun “your.” However, even if the reading “in your law” is accepted it need not be taken as a disavowal by Jesus of the law that He Himself had given. The “your” could emphasize the thought that the law that you yourselves recognize as authoritative says, etc. Compare ch. 8:17. The word “law” (Gr. nomos), here as in chs. 12:34; 15:25; etc., is used of the entire OT Scriptures as they were then recognized, and not of the Pentateuch only, as frequently was the case (ch. 1:17; etc.). Such a use of “law” is found also in rabbinical literature. For example, in answer to the question as to where the Torah (Law) attests the resurrection of the dead, the Talmud quotes Ps. 84:4 as evidence (Sanhedrin 91b, Soncino ed., p. 614).
**Ye are gods.** The quotation is from Ps. 82:6. The Psalm is an arraignment of unjust judges, spoken of as “gods” (see Introduction to Ps. 82, and on vs. 1, 6). Rabbinical tradition applied the term “gods” to those who received the law: “The Israelites accepted the Torah only so that the Angel of Death should have no dominion over them [Ps. 82:6, 7]” (Talmud ‘Abodah Zarah 5a, Soncino ed., p. 21). Jesus seems to make His reply in terms of this tradition (see on John 10:35). However, He was “God” in an altogether different sense from that of Ps. 82:6.

35.zh:
經上的話是不能廢的；若那些承受神道的人尚且稱為神，

**廢。**luō，“解開”，“打破”，“廢除”，“取消”（見太5:19註釋）。這個原則猶太人還是承認的。因此基於這個原則的結論他們也必須承認。如果經上稱以色列人是“神”，那麼耶穌說自己是上帝的兒子，猶太人又怎能控告祂說了褻瀆的話呢？
**承受上帝道的。**耶穌這時可能想到拉比們對詩82:6的解釋（見34節註釋），所以祂是泛指接受律法的以色列人。
35.en:
**The word of God came.** If, as seems likely, Jesus was thinking of the rabbinical interpretation of Ps. 82:6 (see on John 10:34), then the Israelites generally, who received the law, are referred to.
**Broken.** Gr. luō, “to loose,” “to break,” “to annul,” “to cancel” (see on Matt. 5:19). This principle the Jews acknowledged. Therefore the conclusions based on this principle they must also acknowledge. If the Scriptures called the Israelites “gods,” how could the Jews accuse Jesus of blasphemy for claiming to be the Son of God?

36.zh:
父所分別為聖、又差到世間來的，他自稱是神的兒子，你們還向他說你說僭妄的話嗎？

**分別為聖。**即，分別出來作特殊的用途（見創2:3註釋）。
**又差到世間來。**見約3:17；20:21。耶穌來到世間絕對是出於甘心情願。
**上帝的兒子。**祂沒有直接說自己是神，而是通過暗示（見約2:16；5:19-30；10:30）。
36.en:
**Sanctified.** That is, set aside for a special purpose (see on Gen. 2:3).
**Sent into.** See chs. 3:17; 20:21. At the same time the coming of Jesus into this world was voluntary (cf. on ch. 5:18).
**Son of God.** He had not claimed divinity directly, but by implication (see chs. 2:16; 5:19–30; 10:30).

37.zh:
我若不行我父的事，你們就不必信我；

**就不必信我。**“上帝從來沒有要我們相信無憑無據的事”（《拾級就主》105頁）。耶穌所行的神蹟就是要為信心提供必要的基礎（見本卷註釋第209頁）。此外，耶穌的品格與父完全和諧一致。同樣，早期教會中使徒的工作以及聖靈賜給信徒的超自然的恩典也堅定了“基督的見證”（林前1:6）。
37.en: **Believe me not.** “God never asks us to believe, without giving sufficient evidence upon which to base our faith” (SC 105). The miracles that Jesus performed were designed to provide the necessary basis of faith (see p. 209). Furthermore, the character of Jesus was wholly consistent with that of the Father. Likewise in the early church the works of the apostles and the supernatural gifts of the Spirit bestowed upon the believers confirmed “the testimony of Christ” (1 Cor. 1:6).

38.zh:
我若行了，你們縱然不信我，也當信這些事，叫你們又知道又明白父在我裡面，我也在父裡面。

**當信這些事。**見第37節註釋。
**又知道又明白。**有文本為“知道，而且相信”。
**在我裡面。**耶穌再次主張祂與父的合一（見第30節註釋）。
38.en:
**Believe the works.** See on v. 37.
**Know, and believe.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the reading “know, and understand,” that is, come to know, and continue in the knowledge. The literal meaning of the reading reflected in the KJV is “come to know and fix your faith.”
**In me.** Once more Jesus asserts His oneness with the Father (see on v. 30).

39.zh:
他們又要拿他，他卻逃出他們的手走了。

**又要拿祂。**將這裡與約7:30,32,44；8:20,59進行比較。
**逃出。**將這裡與約8:59進行比較。

40.zh:
耶穌又往約但河外去，到了約翰起初施洗的地方，就住在那裡。

**約旦河外。**關於耶穌在比哩亞傳道，見太19:1註釋。
**約翰起初施洗的地方。**見約1:28註釋。
**就住在那裡。**修殿節（見第22節註釋）和幾個月後逾越節之間的大部分時間，耶穌似乎都是在比哩亞度過的（見太19:1註釋）。
40.en:
**Beyond Jordan.** For a discussion of Jesus’ ministry in Peraea see on Matt. 19:1.
**Where John.** See on ch. 1:28.
**There he abode.** Jesus seems to have spent the major portion of the time between the Feast of Dedication (see on v. 22) and the Passover some months later in Peraea (see on Matt. 19:1).

41.zh:
有許多人來到他那裡。他們說：約翰一件神蹟沒有行過，但約翰指著這人所說的一切話都是真的。

**有許多人來到祂那裡。**與在耶路撒冷遭到拒絕形成了鮮明的對比（第39節）。
**約翰一件神蹟沒有行過。**與耶穌相比，耶穌在那裡行過神蹟（太19:2）。關於施洗約翰為自己所作的見證，見約1:19-28。約翰宣稱自己只是一個聲音。然而他的工作卻在那地百姓心中留下了深刻的印象。現在他們接受耶穌顯然大部分要歸因於他的工作。當地的百姓還記得那先鋒的信息。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第219頁。
41.en:
**Many resorted.** In refreshing contrast with the rejection at Jerusalem (v. 39).
**John did no miracle.** In contrast with Jesus, who wrought miracles there (Matt. 19:2). For the testimony of John concerning himself see ch. 1:19–28. John claimed to be merely a voice. Nevertheless his ministry had made a deep impression upon the people in the region of his labors, and the reception now accorded Jesus was doubtless due largely to John’s work. The people remembered the message of the forerunner.

42.zh:
在那裡，信耶穌的人就多了。

**信耶穌的人就多了。**這是《約翰福音》中常用的一句話（見約4:41；7:31；8:30）。
42.en: **Many believed.** A common phrase in John (see chs. 4:41; 7:31; 8:30).

35.en:
**I am the bread.** Now Jesus clearly declared Himself to be the heavenly bread of which He had been speaking. Three times in the present discourse He repeated this statement concerning Himself (vs. 41, 48, 51).
**He that cometh.** Gr. ho erchomenos, literally, “the one coming.” The Greek form of the verb implies, not a single act of coming to Christ, but a consistent habit of life. “He that cometh to me” is here clearly in parallel with “he that believeth on me,” for coming to Christ can be accomplished only by faith (see on v. 29). Coming and believing are both “works of God.”
**Shall never hunger.** Jesus’ words are in sharp contrast with those found in Ecclesiasticus (a book familiar to the Jews of His time), where wisdom is made to declare: “They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty” (ch. 24:21).
35.zh:
