50.en: **Life everlasting.** See on ch. 3:16. The Father’s commandment was that men should believe in Christ, whom He had sent into the world. Only thus could they be saved (see Acts 4:12). In a parallel statement John declared, “This is his commandment, That we should believe on the name of his Son Jesus Christ” (1 John 3:23). The Jews believed that salvation would come to them because they exercised themselves in the study and the observance of the Torah. Many of them rested their hope of eternal life upon their descent from Abraham. Jesus warned that only those who accepted Jesus Christ as the Son of God, the Saviour of the world, would be saved. “This is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent” (John 17:3).
50.zh:
我也知道他的命令就是永生。故此，我所講的話正是照著父對我所說的。

**永生。**見約3:16註釋。天父的命令是，人應當信祂所差到這個世界上來的基督。惟有如此他們才能得救（見徒4:12）。約翰在另一段話中說： “上帝的命令就是叫我們信他兒子耶穌基督的名”（約壹3:23）。猶太人相信救恩會臨到他們，因為他們嚴格學習並遵行妥拉（律法）。許多人將他們永生的希望建立在自己是亞伯拉罕後裔的基礎上。耶穌卻警告說，只有那些接受耶穌基督是上帝的兒子並世界救贖主的人，才能得救。“認識你──獨一的真神，並且認識你所差來的耶穌基督，這就是永生”（約17:3）。

31.en:
**Now.** A momentous hour in the history of the world had come. Jesus was about to die for the guilty race, thus assuring the salvation of men and making certain the defeat of Satan’s kingdom. The expression “now” was thus fraught with the most weighty significance.
**Judgment of this world.** Not that Jesus was about to sit as judge, “for God sent not his Son into the world to condemn [or, “judge,” as krinō is most commonly rendered] the world; but that the world through him might be saved” (see on ch. 3:17). However, by their relationship to the Son, men were deciding their eternal destiny (see on ch. 9:39). By refusing to accept Jesus as the Messiah of prophecy and as the Saviour of the world the Jewish nation sealed its fate and incurred condemnation.
**Prince of this world.** This title for Satan is found only in John (cf. chs. 14:30; 16:11). Other titles given him are “god of this world” (2 Cor. 4:4) and “prince of the power of the air” (Eph. 2:2). On Satan’s usurped authority of this world see on Matt. 4:8, 9.
**Cast out.** There had been an earlier casting out at the time Lucifer fell from his high estate (see PP 42). Now his work would be further restricted. By his attitude toward the Son of God, Satan stood revealed in his true character. He could henceforth “no longer await the angels as they came from the heavenly courts, and before them accuse Christ’s brethren” (DA 761). See further on Rev. 12:7–9.
31.zh:
現在這世界受審判，這世界的王要被趕出去。

**現在。**這個世界歷史的關鍵時刻到了。耶穌將要為有罪的人族去死，以此確保人類的得救和撒但王國的徹底敗亡。“現在”這個詞語包含了太多重要的意義。
**這世界受審判。**這裡不是說耶穌馬上要作審判者，“因為上帝差祂的兒子降世，不是要定（或krinō經常被譯成的“審判”）世人的罪，乃是要叫世人因祂得救”（見約3:17註釋）。但人類永久的命運卻是依據他們與聖子的關係來決定的（見約9:39註釋）。猶太民族拒絕接受耶穌是預言中的彌賽亞以及這個世界的救贖主，因此他們也就決定了自己的厄運並招致了刑罰。
**這世界的王。**只有《約翰福音》採用中撒但的這個稱呼（參約14:30；16:11）。他還有其他的稱呼：“這世界的神”（林後4:4），“空中掌權者的首領”（弗2:2）。關於撒但篡奪這個世界的權柄，見太4:8,9註釋。
**趕出去。**當初路錫甫從他的高位上墜落時就曾被趕出過一次了（見《先祖與先知》42頁）。現在他的工作要受到進一步的限制。從撒但對上帝兒子的態度就可以看出他真實的品格。從今往後“他再也不能向那些從天庭下來的使者控告基督的弟兄了”（《歷代願望》761頁）。詳見啟12:7-9註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第679頁；《證言》卷九第22頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（31–32節）**。《先祖與先知》第68頁。

32.en:
**Lifted up.** That is, upon the cross. The same verb occurs in ch. 3:14 (see comment there), where Jesus compares His being lifted up to the lifting up of the serpent in the wilderness. In ch. 8:28 Jesus again refers to His being lifted up, and speaks of the act as being performed by the Jews. This shows clearly that He is not referring to His ascension.
**Will draw.** The cross has, in thousands of lives, proved to be more magnetic than all the fascinations of the world. After his rather fruitless efforts in Athens, where he had met logic with logic, Paul determined in Corinth “not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified” (1 Cor. 2:2; cf. AA 244). As a result, his labors were highly successful. The magnetism of the cross has by no means diminished with the passing of the centuries. It is still “the power and wisdom of God to gather souls for Christ” (6T 67).
**All men.** The word “men” is supplied, and its inclusion limits the application of the verse to members of the human family only. It should be omitted, for not only were members of the human race drawn to Christ by the sacrifice of Himself, but angels, and the inhabitants of the other worlds, were drawn to Him anew by the demonstration of the sacrificial love of God (Col. 1:20).
32.zh:
我若從地上被舉起來，就要吸引萬人來歸我。

**被舉起來。**這是指被掛在十字架上。這個動詞還出現在約3:14中（見該處註釋），那裡耶穌將自己被舉起來和銅蛇在曠野被舉起來進行比較。在約8:28中耶穌再次指出祂要被舉起來，並說明做這件事的正是猶太人。這清楚地顯示出他並不是在說祂的昇天。
**就要吸引。**無數人的生活證明十字架比這世界上一切的蠱惑更具有吸引力。保羅在雅典以哲學對哲學無功而返，之後當他在哥林多的時候，他決定“在你們中間不知道別的，只知道耶穌基督並祂釘十字架”（林前2:2；參《使徒行述》244頁）。結果，他的勞苦大得功效。多少個世紀過去了，十字架的吸引力沒有絲毫的減退。它仍舊是“上帝的權能與智慧，要招聚生靈歸於基督”（《教會證言》卷六第67頁）。
**萬人。**“人”這個字是後加的，這使得本節的應用範圍只限制在人類之中。應當刪去這個字，因為不僅是人類的成員被基督的犧牲所吸引，還有天使以及其他世界的居民全都因上帝自我犧牲的愛被吸引到基督這裡來（西1:20）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第249頁；《基督教育之研究》第434頁；《歷代願望》第626頁；《教育論》第192頁；《傳道良助》第160頁；《福山寶訓》第9，44頁；《給青年人的信息》第137頁；《拾級就主》第26頁；《給傳道人的證言》第226，378頁；《證言》卷四第418，624頁；《證言》卷六第237，449頁；《證言》卷七第11，29頁。

1.zh:
逾越節前六日，耶穌來到伯大尼，就是他叫拉撒路從死裡復活之處。

**逾越節前六日。**這次筵席可能是在基督被釘之前那個安息日的晚上（見太21:1；26:3註釋）。那時從法律上來說已經是一週的第一日了（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷二第101頁）。這樣，從星期日到逾越節的前一天，即星期五（見《馬太福音》第26章補充註釋一），算上星期日（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷一，第182頁），正好是六天。
**耶穌。**關於這次筵席和記載在其他福音書記載的關係，見《路加福音》第7章補充註釋。
**就是拉撒路從死裡復活之處。**見約11:1註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第557頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–8節）**。見太26：6-13懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–11節）**。《歷代願望》第557-568頁。
1.en:
**Then Jesus.** [Simon’s Feast, John 12:1–9=Matt. 26:6–13=Mark 14:3–9=Luke 7:36–50. Major comment: Matthew and Luke. See Closing Ministry at Jerusalem; The Duration of Christ’s Ministry, the Opening of the Galilean Ministry, The Ministry of Our Lord .] For a discussion of the relationship of this feast to that recorded in the other Gospels see Additional Note on Luke 7.
**Six days before the passover.** The dinner probably took place the night of the Sabbath preceding the crucifixion (see on Matt. 21:1; 26:3), which would technically be on the first day of the week (see Vol. II, p. 101). This would be exactly six days, inclusive reckoning (see Vol. I, p. 182), before the Passover, which fell on Friday (see Additional Notes on Matt. 26, Note 1).
**Where Lazarus was.** See on ch. 11:1.

2.zh:
有人在那裡給耶穌預備筵席；馬大伺候，拉撒路也在那同耶穌坐席的人中。

**有人……預備。**筵席設在西門的家中（太26:6）。
**筵席。**deipnon（見路14:12）。
**馬大伺候。**這似乎是她的特點（見路10:40）。
2.en:
**They made.** The feast was in Simon’s house (Matt. 26:6).
**Supper.** Gr. deipnon (see on Luke 14:12).
**Martha served.** As seems characteristic of her (see Luke 10:40).

3.zh:
馬利亞就拿著一斤極貴的真哪噠香膏，抹耶穌的腳，又用自己頭髮去擦，屋裡就滿了膏的香氣。

**斤。**希臘語litra，相當於拉丁文語libra，約有我們現在的六兩半（見本卷註釋第50頁）。《新約》中該詞只出現在本節和約19:39。
**真哪噠香膏。**murou nardou pistikēs。參可14:3。形容詞pistikos譯成了“真”。有人認為它的意思是“液體的”。還有些人認為pistikos是一個當地的名字。關於香膏，見路7:37註釋。
**腳。**馬太（26:7）和馬可（14:3）的記載都說膏油倒在了頭上。顯然馬利亞是將膏油倒在了耶穌的頭上和腳上，而每一卷福音書的作者只注意到了一點。路加和約翰一樣，提到馬利亞將膏油倒在了耶穌的腳上（路7:38）。
**香氣。**她的這件行為是不能隱藏的。強烈的香味瀰漫了整個房間，使大家注意到了馬利亞的行為。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第80頁；《證言》卷六第84頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–6節）**。《早期著作》第165，268頁；《歷代願望》第559頁；《證言》卷四第485，487頁。
3.en:
**Pound.** Gr. litra, equivalent to the Latin libra, about 11 1/2 oz. avoirdupois (see p. 50). The word occurs in the NT only here and in ch. 19:39.
**Ointment of spikenard.** Gr. murou nardou pistikēs. The same combination of words is translated “ointment of pure nard” in Mark 14:3, margin. “Pure” is the translation of the adjective pistikos. This word is missing in the KJV translation of John 12:3, and should probably be supplied. However, not all agree that pistikos means “pure,” “genuine.” Some suggest the meaning “liquid.” Others consider pistikos a local name. For a description of the ointment see on Luke 7:37.
**The feet.** Matthew (ch. 26:7) and Mark (ch. 14:3) state that the ointment was poured on the head. Doubtless Mary performed both operations, with each gospel writer noting but one. Luke, like John, mentions the anointing of the feet (Luke 7:38).
**The odour.** The act could not be hidden. The strong odor permeating the room called attention to Mary’s act.

4.zh:
有一個門徒，就是那將要賣耶穌的加略人猶大，

**有一個門徒。**馬太特別提到，那“門徒……很不喜悅”（太26:8）。批評和指責起源於猶大，但隨即這種精神散佈在眾門徒中間。
**賣耶穌。**見約6:71註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《歷代願望》第720頁；《證言》卷一第192頁；《證言》卷四第550頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–7節）**。《證言》卷四第42頁。
4.en:
**One of his disciples.** Matthew notes that the “disciples … had indignation” (Matt. 26:8). The criticism originated with Judas, but spread among other disciples.
**Betray him.** See on ch. 6:71.

6.zh:
他說這話，並不是掛念窮人，乃因他是個賊，又帶著錢囊，常取其中所存的。

**錢囊。**glōssokomon，直譯是管樂器吹口的存放袋，但該詞一般也用於指存放普通物品的袋子，特別是指放錢的袋子。因此，這裡譯為“錢袋”非常合適。該詞還出現在七十士譯本的代下24:8。
**取。**bastazō，一般指“抬著”（路7:14；22:10等）或者“拿起”（約10:31）。這裡指“偷竊”，得到草紙文獻的證實。
6.en:
**Bag.** Gr. glōssokomon, literally, a receptacle for the mouthpieces of wind instruments, but the word came to be used also to describe a receptacle for general articles, and more particularly for the storing of money. Hence “money box” would be a suitable translation. The word occurs in the LXX of 2 Chron. 24:8.
**Bare.** Gr. bastazō, generally meaning “to carry” (Luke 7:14; 22:10; etc.), also “to pick up” (John 10:31). Here the meaning is “to pilfer,” a definition clearly attested in the papyri.

7.zh:
耶穌說：由他吧！他是為我安葬之日存留的。

**為我安葬之日。**其實這句話的原文意思並不是太清楚。耶穌不可能是說讓她將膏油的一部分留到祂下葬的時候再用。祂可能指馬利亞購買膏油的動機（見太26:12；可14:8註釋）。關於馬利亞用油膏耶穌的動機，見太26:12註釋；參《歷代願望》559，560頁。
7.en: **Against the day.** Textual evidence here favors the reading (cf. p. 146), “that against the day of my burial she may keep it,” or “let her keep it for the day of my burial” (RSV). However, the precise meaning of the Greek clause thus translated is uncertain. It appears unlikely that Jesus refers to a preservation of a part of the contents to be used at the time of His burial. He alludes rather to the motive that prompted the purchase of the ointment (see Matt. 26:12; Mark 14:8). For a discussion of Mary’s motive in the anointing see on Matt. 26:12; cf. DA 559, 560.

8.zh:
因為常有窮人和你們同在，只是你們不常有我。

**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第640頁。

9.zh:
有許多猶太人知道耶穌在那裡，就來了，不但是為耶穌的緣故，也是要看他從死裡所復活的拉撒路。

**許多多猶太人。**指一般平民。這個短語也出現在第12節。
**知道。**或“發現”。
**看……拉撒路。**這個理由夠充分了。今天如果有個人從死裡復活，那將吸引大批的群眾。
[ 陷害主的陰謀：約12:10,11=太26:1-5,14-16=可14:1,2,10,11=路22:1-6。註釋主要在《馬太福音》。見本卷註釋233頁圖表]。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–11節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第265頁。
9.en:
**Much people.** In general, the common people. The expression occurs again in v. 12.
**Knew.** Rather, “found out.”
**Might see Lazarus.** A sufficient reason. A man raised from the dead would attract great crowds today.

10.zh:
但祭司長商議連拉撒路也要殺了；

**但祭司長。**祭司長陰謀要殺害耶穌的同時也想要將拉撒路置於死地。他們沒有什麼正式理由控告拉撒路。拉撒路的存在就是耶穌神性的見證，而耶穌是祭司們判定應該受死罪的，同時只要拉撒路活著，就是對他們主要教訓──即沒有復活（見約11:47註釋）──的一種否定，因此他們覺得有必要將他一塊殺了。
10.en: **But the chief priests.** [The Betrayal Plot, John 12:10, 11=Matt. 26:1–5, 14–16=Mark 14:1, 2, 10, 11̄Luke 22:1–6. Major comment: Matthew. See Passion Week] In connection with the plot to put Jesus to death the chief priests plotted also the death of Lazarus. They could bring no formal charge against Lazarus. However, because his life was a witness to the divinity of the One whom they had condemned to death and a denial of the doctrine that many of them held, namely, that there was no resurrection (see on ch. 11:47), they deemed it necessary to kill him also.

11.zh:
因有好些猶太人為拉撒路的緣故，回去信了耶穌。

**回去。**或“開始離開”（羅伯遜）。即他們離棄了猶太教而加入了耶穌門徒的行列。
[榮入聖城：約12:12-19=太21:1-11=可11:1-11=路19:29-44。註釋主要在《馬太福音》。見本卷註釋224頁地圖；233頁圖表]。
11.en: **Went away.** Or, “began to withdraw” (Robertson). That is, they withdrew from Judaism and joined the ranks of the disciples of Jesus.

12.zh:
第二天，有許多上來過節的人聽見耶穌將到耶路撒冷，

**第二天。**第二天應該就是筵席結束後的第二天，即星期天的第二天（見第1節註釋）。
**許多……人。**見第9節註釋。儘管約瑟弗斯所說在特殊的逾越節時會有超過2,500,000的人聚集到耶路撒冷（戰爭vi. 9. 3 [420-427]）有些誇張，但本節無疑表明有大量的群眾這段時期聚集到耶路撒冷。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–19節）**。《歷代願望》第569-579頁。
12.en:
**The next day.** [The Triumphal Entry, John 12:12–19=Matt. 21:1–11=Mark 11:1–11=Luke 19:29–44. Major comment: Matthew. See Closing Ministry at Jerusalem; Passion Week.] The next day would be the day following the feast, or Sunday (see on v. 1).
**Much people.** See on v. 9. Though Josephus’ statement that on a particular Passover more than 2,500,000 were gathered at Jerusalem (War vi. 9. 3 [420–427]) is probably exaggerated, it nevertheless indicates that huge crowds must have gathered at Jerusalem during this period.

13.zh:
就拿著棕樹枝出去迎接他，喊著說：和散那！奉主名來的以色列王是應當稱頌的！

**枝。**直譯是“棕樹枝”。《馬加比上》13:51節提到棕樹枝時將它和大祭司西門光榮進入耶路撒冷塔樓聯繫在一起。啟7:9中百姓手中所拿的棕樹枝是勝利的象徵（見《善惡之爭》665頁）。
**喊。**譯為“不斷地呼喊”更合適一些。
**以色列王。**這句話的語序在希臘文中是倒裝的：“和散那：奉主名來的是應當稱頌的，就是以色列的王”。這句話的前半部分顯然引自詩118:25,26，後半部分“應當向以色列王歡呼”是出自亞9:9。關於根據猶太人的期望彌賽亞為王，見路4:19註釋；參約18:37；19:19。關於百姓欣喜若狂的呼喊，不同的作者有不同的記錄，他們顯然用了不同的表達方式。
13.en:
**Branches.** Literally, “palm branches.” Palm branches are mentioned in 1 Macc. 13:51 in connection with the triumphal entry of Simon the high priest into the tower of Jerusalem. The palms in the hands of the great multitude of Rev. 7:9 are a symbol of triumph (see GC 665).
**Cried.** Rather, “kept on crying.”
**King of Israel.** The clauses are reversed in the Greek: “Hossana: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, even the king of Israel.” The first part is apparently a quotation from Ps. 118:25, 26, and the last phrase, “even the king of Israel,” an allusion to Zech. 9:9. On Messiah as king according to Jewish expectations see on Luke 4:19; cf. John 18:37; 19:19. The ecstatic cries of the multitudes are variously reported by the gospel writers. Doubtless a variety of expressions were used.

14.zh:
耶穌得了一個驢駒，就騎上，如經上所記的說：

**一個驢駒。**約翰在這裡沒有記載獲得驢駒的細節（見可11:1-7）。
14.en: **A young ass.** John omits the details as to how the ass was obtained (see Mark. 11:1–7).

15.zh:
錫安的民（原文作女子）哪，不要懼怕！你的王騎著驢駒來了。

**不要懼怕。**希伯來文或七十士譯本的亞9:9都沒有這個短語。這裡所引用的經文可能出自賽40:9。
15.en: **Fear not.** This phrase is not in the Hebrew or LXX of Zech. 9:9, the passage of Scripture here cited, but may have come from Isa. 40:9.

16.zh:
這些事門徒起先不明白，等到耶穌得了榮耀以後才想起這話是指著他寫的，並且眾人果然向他這樣行了。

**不明白。**門徒們不理解耶穌當前行為的目的和意義。關於這一行動的目，見太21:5註釋；參《歷代願望》571，572頁。儘管耶穌已經清楚地告訴門徒祂的死期近了（太17:22,23等），但他們似乎在當前欣喜和激動的時刻把祂的話給忘了。祂沒有前例地允許自己被稱為“以色列王，”這激起了門徒們的希望。或許他們的夫子最終將滿足他們和百姓的期望，宣佈自己是王，並且承擔起彌賽亞政治上的任務。門徒們在耶穌復活之後，在聖靈的指引之下通過研究預言，終於明白了耶穌這一舉動的目的。
16.en: **Understood not.** The disciples did not understand the purpose and import of Jesus’ present action. For a discussion of the purpose see on Matt. 21:5; cf. DA 571, 572. Even though Jesus had clearly told His disciples of His approaching death (Matt. 17:22, 23; etc.), they seem to have forgotten this in the excitement of the moment. His unprecedented act in permitting Himself to be declared “King of Israel” roused their hopes that He would, after all, fulfill their expectations and those of the multitude, declare Himself king, and assume the role of a political messiah. After the resurrection, through a study of the prophecies, guided by the illumination of the Holy Spirit, they understood the purpose of the act.

17.zh:
當耶穌呼喚拉撒路，叫他從死復活出墳墓的時候，同耶穌在那裡的眾人就作見證。

**作見證。**那些親眼見過拉撒路復活的人和大批百姓混雜在一起，對他們作見證。這樣，激動和興奮的情緒就迅速蔓延開來。
17.en: **Bare record.** Those who had been eyewitnesses of the resurrection of Lazarus mingled with the multitudes and bore their testimony. Thus the enthusiasm spread.

18.zh:
眾人因聽見耶穌行了這神蹟，就去迎接他。

**迎接祂。**迎接耶穌的人有兩種，一是陪伴祂來的人，二是從耶路撒冷出來去見祂的人。
18.en: **Met him.** There were two crowds, the one accompanying Jesus and the other coming out from Jerusalem to meet Him.

19.zh:
法利賽人彼此說：看哪，你們是徒勞無益，世人都隨從他去了。

**益。**ōpheleō，在這裡的意思是“成就”（參約6:63）。
**世人。**有文本為“全世界”。都是指“每一個人”。所用的語言是誇張的。說這話的人無疑是困惑生氣了。他們找不到人願意下手去拿住耶穌並把祂交到他們那裡。反之，他們發現百姓聚集在耶穌身邊，向祂歡呼，向祂致敬，承認他是他們的王。在這種情況下，任何企圖逮捕耶穌的舉動必將引起騷亂。猶太人的領袖們要求耶穌使百姓安靜下來，但卻沒有成功（路19:39,40）。他們唯一能做的就是呆呆地看著隊伍，眼見他們所恨的仇敵在百姓表示效忠的歡呼聲中進入耶路撒冷。他們現在的感受可能和哈曼給末底改牽馬時的感受有些類似（斯6:11）。領袖們不知道耶穌的目的是什麼，他們想象著耶穌馬上就要宣佈作王，剝奪他們的權力並率領以色列人反抗羅馬人的統治。
[與希臘人的談話：約12:20-36a]。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第571頁。
19.en:
**Prevail.** Gr. ōpheleō, used here in the sense, “to accomplish” (cf. ch. 6:63).
**The world.** Textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 146) for the reading “the whole world.” Either expression simply means “everybody.” The language is hyperbolic. It comes from men baffled and angry. Instead of finding the people willing to lay hands on Jesus and to deliver Him into their power, they find the multitudes surrounding Him with joyful acclamations and saluting Him as their king. Under the circumstances, any attempt to arrest Jesus would have raised a tumult. The leaders appealed to Jesus to quiet the multitudes, but without success (Luke 19:39, 40). All they could do was watch the procession and see their hated enemy enter Jerusalem in royal triumph. They probably felt somewhat like Haman leading Mordecai about on a royal horse (Esther 6:11). Not knowing what His purpose actually was, they no doubt imagined Jesus about to proclaim Himself king, abolish their power, and lead a revolt against Rome.

20.zh:
那時，上來過節禮拜的人中，有幾個希利尼人。

**幾個希臘人。**這件事可能發生在耶穌被釘之前的星期二，祂最後一次訪問聖殿的時候（見太23:1註釋；參《歷代願望》621頁）。
**禮拜。**這幾個希臘人是來禮拜的，而不是來參加逾越節的，這說明他們並不是完全的改信猶太教的人。約瑟弗斯曾提到在逾越節時來耶路撒冷禮拜的外國人（《猶太戰爭史》vi. 9. 3 [427]）。半皈依者和外邦人一樣，被嚴格限制在只允許外邦人進入的院子。關於聖殿的院落，見《密西拿》Middoth，《塔木德》松奇諾版（Soncino ed.）第1-23頁；參Kelim 1. 8，《塔木德》松奇諾版第11頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（20–23節）**。《歷代願望》第621頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（20–43節）**。《歷代願望》第621-626頁。
20.en:
**Certain Greeks.** [Interview With the Greeks, John 12:20–36.] This incident probably occurred on the Tuesday preceding the crucifixion, in connection with Jesus’ last visit to the Temple (see on Matt. 23:1; cf. DA 621).
**To worship.** The fact that they came to worship rather than to partake of the Passover suggests that these Greeks were not full proselytes. Josephus mentions foreigners who came to Jerusalem to worship at the Passover season (War vi. 9. 3 [427]). Half proselytes, like the Gentiles, were restricted to the Court of the Gentiles. For a description of the Temple courts see Mishnah Middoth, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 1–23; cf. Kelim 1. 8, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 11.

21.zh:
他們來見加利利伯賽大的腓力，求他說：先生，我們願意見耶穌。

**伯賽大。**見太11:21註釋。
**腓力。**見可3:18註釋。
**我們願意。**譯為“我們渴望”或“我們希望”更合適一些。
**見。**這裡的意思是“會見”，和路8:20一樣。關於這次訪問的目的，見《歷代願望》622頁。
21.en:
**Philip.** See on Mark 3:18.
**Bethsaida.** See on Matt. 11:21.
**We would.** Rather, “we desire,” or “we wish.”
**See.** Here used in the sense of “to have an interview,” as in Luke 8:20. On the purposes of the proposed interview see DA 622.

22.zh:
腓力去告訴安得烈，安得烈同腓力去告訴耶穌。

**告訴安得烈。**腓力和安得烈兩個人都是希臘文的名字，他們的希臘血統可能是他們得以參與這件事的原因。腓力為什麼要請教安得烈這一點並沒有說明，但顯然他是在就幾個希臘人求見耶穌的事（見約6:8註釋）向安得烈徵詢意見。在使五千人吃飽的敘述中（約6:1-14），安得烈比腓力表現得更實際幹練，而腓力顯得不僅猶豫並且小信。
22.en: **Telleth Andrew.** Both Philip and Andrew bore Greek names, and their Hellenistic ancestry may account for their part in the present incident. The reason why Philip consulted Andrew is not given, but he apparently sought Andrew’s advice in presenting to Jesus the case of the inquiring Greeks (see on ch. 6:8). In the narrative of the Feeding of the Five Thousand (ch. 6:1–14) Andrew reflects a more practical turn of mind than Philip, who is there shown to be not only cautious but slow of heart to believe.

23.zh:
耶穌說：人子得榮耀的時候到了。

**說。**這句話更像是對當前希臘人求見自己這種情況的反應，而不是對門徒直接的回答。
**人子。**見太1:1；可2:10註釋。
**時候到了。**稍早前耶穌宣稱祂的時候還沒有到（見約2:4；7:30；8:20；見約2:4註釋）。但是現在，祂的死期近了。加上今天，到耶穌被釘，僅剩四天。這幾個希臘人的拜訪無疑使耶穌聯想到祂的死將要帶來的結果，即無數的外邦人將要歸向祂。
23.en:
**Answered them.** The words were rather a response to the situation suggested by the visit of the Greeks than a direct answer to them.
**The hour is come.** Earlier Jesus had announced that His hour had not yet come (see chs. 2:4; 7:30; 8:20; see on ch. 2:4). Now, however, the hour of His death was near. It was only four days, inclusive, until the crucifixion. The visit of the Greeks doubtless suggested to Jesus what would be the result of His death, namely, the conversion of many from the Gentile nations.
**Son of man.** See on Matt. 1:1; Mark 2:10.

24.zh:
我實實在在的告訴你們，一粒麥子不落在地裡死了，仍舊是一粒，若是死了，就結出許多子粒來。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18；約1:51註釋。
**死了。**這是大自然中一個簡單的例證。一粒麥子落在泥土裡，作為一粒麥子它是死了，但是生命並沒有被毀滅。胚芽的生命是麥子子粒的消解所不能毀滅的。在新長出的植株裡，一粒麥子變成了許多粒。然而，如果種子不播撒在土裡，便不會有這種增加。耶穌也是這樣。如果祂選擇不為有罪的人類捨命，那祂仍舊是“一粒”。人類也必滅亡，天國不會再有生命的收穫。但耶穌藉著祂的死將生命帶給相信祂的人。將這裡與保羅在林前15:36中的論述進行比較。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第86頁；《教育論》第110頁；《證言》卷六第186頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–25節）**。《歷代願望》第623頁。
24.en:
**Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18; John 1:51.
**Corn of wheat.** Rather, “grain of wheat.”
**Die.** A simple illustration from nature. A kernel of wheat placed in the soil dies as a grain of wheat, but life is not destroyed. There is in the kernel a germ of life that the dissolution of the kernel cannot destroy. In the growth of the new plant the one kernel becomes many kernels. However, such multiplication does not take place if the seed is not cast into the ground. So it was with Jesus. If He had chosen not to die for the guilty race, He would have remained “alone.” The human race would have perished and there would have been no harvest of souls for the kingdom. By His death Jesus brought life to all who would fix their faith in Him. Compare Paul’s argument in 1 Cor. 15:36.

25.zh:
愛惜自己生命的，就失喪生命；在這世上恨惡自己生命的，就要保守生命到永生。

**愛惜自己生命的。**見太10:39節註釋；參可8:35；10:39。這裡的“生命”是psuchē（見太10:28註釋），通常譯為“靈魂”（可8:36,37等）。追求拯救和保守自己今世肉身生命的人，必喪失“生命”或永生。而願意在今生奉獻自己服侍上帝的人，必保守自己的“生命”，並在來生享受永生。因此，“自我犧牲的定律，就是保全自己的定律”；“專求利己的定律，就是自取滅亡的定律”（《歷代願望》623，624頁）。那些準備在今生捨棄最寶貴之一切的人就走上了屬靈成長的道路，並且最終他們必將發現他們沒有失去什麼有價值的東西，反倒獲得了真實的財富（見腓3:8-10）。這個世界將自我犧牲看作愚蠢和浪費，就像一個小孩子看把糧食扔在地上是毫無意義的浪費似的。但未來的世界將會顯明，熱中於當前這個世界的人才是愚蠢，上帝的兒女是有真智慧的。太10:28中有關於“靈魂”最終喪失和毀滅的描述。
**恨惡。**這裡的意思是“勝過愛……”（見路14:26註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第626頁；《給青年人的信息》第302頁；《證言》卷九第56頁。
25.en:
**Loveth his life.** See on Matt. 10:39; cf. Mark 8:35; 10:39. The word for “life,” here, is psuchē (see on Matt. 10:28), frequently translated “soul” (Mark 8:36, 37; etc.). He who is bent on saving and preserving his physical life here will lose his “soul,” or eternal life. He who is willing to sacrifice himself in service for God in this world will preserve his “soul” and enjoy life everlasting in the world to come. Thus “the law of self-sacrifice is the law of self-preservation”; “the law of self-serving is the law of self-destruction” (DA 623, 624). He who is ready to cast away everything most dear in this life that stands in the way of his spiritual growth will find at length that he has lost nothing worth while and that he has gained the true riches (see Phil. 3:8–10). The world looks upon the way of self-denial and self-sacrifice as foolishness and waste, even as a small child might regard the casting of good grain into the ground a senseless waste. But the future world will reveal that the devotee of this present world was indeed foolish and that the child of God was truly wise. The final loss and destruction of the “soul” is described in Matt. 10:28.
**Hateth.** Here used in the sense of “love less” (see on Luke 14:26).

26.zh:
若有人服事我，就當跟從我；我在哪裡，服事我的人也要在那裡；若有人服事我，我父必尊重他。

服侍。見25節註釋；參見可9:35；10:43-45。
**跟從我。**見太16:24註釋；參可8:34節。
**我在哪裡。**與他的主有屬靈的友誼和交通，是那在今生服侍主之人的特權（太28:20），而在來生他要享受與主面對面的交流。
**我父必尊重。**關於服務的報賞，見可10:29,30註釋。這裡列出了作門徒的條件和報賞，無疑是涉及那幾個希臘人，他們顯然是在考慮作主的門徒。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《佈道論》第686頁；《服務真詮》第226頁；《證言》卷二第40，148頁；《證言》卷六第312，415頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–28節）**。《歷代願望》第624頁。
26.en:
**Serve me.** See on John 12:25; cf. Mark 9:35; 10:43–45.
**Follow me.** See on Matt. 16:24; cf. Mark 8:34.
**Where I am.** Spiritual fellowship and communion with his Lord will be the privilege of him who serves the Lord in this life (Matt. 28:20), and face to face communion will be his to enjoy in the world to come.
**My Father honour.** For the rewards of service see Mark 10:29, 30. The conditions and rewards of discipleship are here given, doubtless with reference to the Greeks, who were apparently contemplating discipleship.

27.zh:
我現在心裡憂愁，我說什麼才好呢？父啊，救我脫離這時候；但我原是為這時候來的。

**我……心裡。**這是一個習語，實際上等於“我”（見詩16:10註釋）。
**憂愁。**tarassō。該詞還出現在約11:33；13:21中，以耶穌為主語。在約14:1,27中，耶穌勸慰祂的門徒不要“憂愁”。耶穌的禱告顯明瞭祂現在憂愁的原因：“父啊，救我脫離這時候”。希臘人的來訪使祂想到了外邦人的得救，但在他們的得救和當前的時刻之間卻橫亙著一個十字架以及與它聯繫在一起的心靈和肉體上的極度痛苦。耶穌的人性在這一刻退縮了。主現在突然感到精神上的痛苦，就是因為清楚地看到了前面即將臨到的景象（參太26:38註釋）。
**救我。**這個禱告和幾天之後在客西馬尼園的禱告（太26:39）類似。我們可以確信，如果還存在任何其他少一些犧牲就能拯救人類的手段，耶穌的禱告將會蒙垂聽。但是，若要完成救贖計劃，就必須付上無限的犧牲（見《先祖與先知》68，69頁）。正因為這個原因，耶穌便自己順服，要把救贖的計劃執行到底。
27.en:
**My soul.** And idiomatic expression practically equivalent to “I” (see on Ps. 16:10).
**Troubled.** Gr. tarassō. The same verb occurs in chs. 11:33; 13:21, with Jesus as the subject. In ch. 14:1, 27 Jesus counsels His disciples not to be “troubled.” The cause of Jesus’ present distress is indicated by His prayer, “Father, save me from this hour.” The visit of the Greeks had called to mind the ingathering of the Gentiles. But between the gospel harvest and the present moment lay the cross and the mental and physical agony that would be associated with it. From this the humanity of Jesus recoiled. A vivid contemplation of the scenes that lay ahead was the cause of the Lord’s sudden mental anguish (cf. on Matt. 26:38).
**Save me.** This prayer is similar to that offered a few days later in Gethsemane (Matt. 26:39). We may rest assured that if any other means to save man, involving less sacrifice, could have been found, the prayer of Jesus would have been answered. But the infinite sacrifice was necessary to accomplish all that the plan of salvation was designed to accomplish (see PP 68, 69). In view of this Jesus submitted Himself to carry the plan through to completion.

28.zh:
父啊，願你榮耀你的名！當時就有聲音從天上來，說：我已經榮耀了我的名，還要再榮耀。

**父啊。**見太6:9；約1:14註釋。
**榮耀你的名。**希臘原文中“你的”是強調的。這個禱告和祂先前關於祂與祂父之間關係的教導相一致，即他始終尋求他父的榮耀（見約7:18；8:50）。關於“名”代表品格，見太6:9註釋。
**當時就有聲音從天上來。**先前兩次有聲音從天上下來──耶穌受洗（太3:17）和登山變像（太17:5）時。
**已經榮耀了我的名。**天父的名得榮耀是通過耶穌的生活，傳道和所行的神蹟（例如，約11:4）。
**還要再榮耀。**這是指耶穌的死和祂的復活。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第409頁；《證言》卷八第202頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（28–33節）**。《歷代願望》第625頁。
28.en:
**Father.** See on Matt. 6:9; John 11:14.
**Glorify thy name.** The Greek places emphasis on the pronoun “thy.” This prayer was in harmony with what Jesus had earlier taught regarding His relationship to the Father, whose glory He consistently sought (see chs. 7:18; 8:50). For “name” representing character see on Matt. 6:9.
**Then came.** On two previous occasions a voice was heard from heaven—at the baptism (Matt. 3:17) and at the Transfiguration (Matt. 17:5).
**Glorified it.** Through the life, ministry, and miracles of Jesus (see, for example, ch. 11:4).
**Glorify it again.** In the death and resurrection of Jesus.

29.zh:
站在旁邊的眾人聽見，就說：打雷了。還有人說：有天使對他說話。

**打雷了。**百姓聽到了從天而來的聲音，但他們卻不理解其中的意思。這與那些聽到向保羅說話之聲音的人的情形類似（見徒23:9註釋）。
**天使……說話。**有些人解釋說這聲音是一道上帝的信息。這似乎暗示著他們明白那聲音的含義。耶穌回答說，這聲音“是為你們來的”，由此判斷，那幾個希臘人，顯然還有其他的人，聽見並理解了那聲音的意思（見《歷代願望》625頁）。對他們來說，這聲音是要使他們堅信，耶穌的確是上帝的兒子。
29.en:
**It thundered.** The people heard the sound of the voice from heaven, but they could not comprehend the meaning, as was the case of those who heard the voice that spoke to Paul at the time of his conversion (see on Acts 23:9).
**An angel spake.** Some interpreted the sound as a divine message. This seems to imply that they understood what was being said. Judging by the reply of Jesus that the voice came “for your sakes,” it appears that the Greeks, and doubtless others, heard and comprehended the voice (see DA 625). To them it would come as confirming evidence that Jesus was indeed the Sent of God.

30.zh:
耶穌說：這聲音不是為我，是為你們來的。

**是為你們。**見第29節註釋；參《歷代願望》625頁。
30.en: **For your sakes.** See on v. 29; cf. DA 625.

34.zh:
眾人回答說：我們聽見律法上有話說，基督是永存的，你怎麼說人子必須被舉起來呢？這人子是誰呢？

**律法。**希臘語nomos，該詞在《舊約》中普遍使用，還出現在約10:34中（見該處註釋）。
**基督是永存的。**說這話的人可能指以下章節：詩89:36；110:4；賽9:6；但7:13,14。啟示文學曾清楚地展望到彌賽亞的統治將是永遠的。例如，次經《以諾書》（見本卷註釋第87頁）關於那被揀選的一位宣稱，“智慧如水傾出，祂面前的榮耀永不退去”（49:1）。“諸靈的主將要與他們同在，他們吃飯，躺下，站立，都與人子在一起”（62:14）。
**人子。**見太1:1；可2:10註釋。
**必須被舉起來。**這些提問的人認為耶穌說自己死的話，不符合他們所相信聖經關於彌賽亞永恆統治的教訓。耶穌所說的“人子”，如果是指彌賽亞，就像猶太人理解的那樣（見上面“基督是永存的” 註釋所引述的《以諾書》62:14；另見本卷註釋第87頁），那怎麼又說到祂的死呢？這個問題表明百姓明白“被舉起來”是指著死說的。
**懷愛倫註釋（34–36節）**。《歷代願望》第626頁。
34.en:
**Law.** Gr. nomos, here used of the OT generally as in ch. 10:34 (see comment there).
**Christ abideth for ever.** The speakers may have referred to such passages as Ps. 89:36; 110:4; Isa. 9:6; Dan. 7:13, 14. The apocalyptic literature of the period clearly envisioned the reign of the Messiah to be eternal. For example, the pseudepigraphal book of Enoch (see p. 87) declares concerning the Elect One, “For wisdom is poured out like water, and glory faileth not before him for evermore” (49:1). “And the Lord of Spirits will abide over them, and with that Son of Man shall they eat and lie down and rise up for ever and ever” (62:14).
**The Son of man.** See on Matt. 1:1; Mark 2:10.
**Must be lifted up.** The questioners could not harmonize Jesus’ reference to His death with what they believed the Scriptures to teach concerning the eternal reign of the Messiah. If by the term “Son of man,” Jesus meant the Messiah, as the Jews evidently understood Him to mean (see Enoch 62:14, quoted above under “Christ abideth for ever”; see also p. 87), then what was this reference to His death? The question shows that the people understood the term “lifted up” to refer to death.

35.zh:
耶穌對他們說：光在你們中間還有不多的時候，應當趁著有光行走，免得黑暗臨到你們；那在黑暗裡行走的，不知道往何處去。

**還有不多的時候。**耶穌沒有直接回答他們的問題。此刻他們還有更重要的事情需要明白。時間就快要到了。耶穌──這世界的光（約8:12）──即將離開這個世界。最後的光芒正在閃耀。六個月前耶穌曾說，“我還有不多的時候和你們同在”（約7:33）。但現在只有幾天的時間了。祂呼籲人們現在就接受他。他們應該善加利用他們現在的機會而不應把時間浪費在問題和疑惑之中。
**行走。**peripateō（見約7:1註釋）。
**臨到。**或“降臨”。
**在黑暗裡行走。**見約8:12註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》第215，450頁；《善惡之爭》第312頁；《給青年人的信息》第334頁；《先祖與先知》第269頁；《給傳道人的證言》第163頁；《證言》卷一第262頁；《證言》卷三第63，65，230，436頁；《證言》卷八第143頁；《證言》卷九第154頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（35–36節）**。《基督教育之研究》第369頁。
35.en:
**Yet a little while.** Jesus did not answer the question directly. There were other more important things for them to understand at the moment. Time was running out. Jesus, the Light of the world (ch. 8:12), would soon leave this world. The last rays of light were shining. Six months before, He had said, “Yet a little while am I with you” (ch. 7:33). Now only a few days remained. He appealed to men to accept Him now. They were to take advantage of their present opportunities and not spend time in questions and doubts.
**Walk.** Gr. peripateō (see on ch. 7:1).
**Come upon.** Or, “overtake.”
**Walketh in darkness.** See on ch. 8:12.

36.zh:
你們應當趁著有光，信從這光，使你們成為光明之子。耶穌說了這話，就離開他們隱藏了。

**光明之子。**見路16:8註釋。信徒會變得像他們所相信的主。那些接受耶穌，就是真光的人，自己也會變成光源，照射別人（見太5:14-16節釋）。
**隱藏了。**將這裡和約8:59進行比較。這是耶穌最後一次在聖殿中出現。這也是祂公開傳道的最後一天。在最後一次向以色列的領袖發出呼籲之後，耶穌永遠地離開了聖殿。見太23:38註釋。
[ 最後被猶太領袖拒絕：約12:36b-50。見本卷註釋224頁地圖]。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第40頁；《證言》卷三第50頁。
36.en:
**Children of light.** See on Luke 16:8. The believer becomes like Him in whom he believes. Those who receive Jesus, the Light, themselves become centers from which light radiates to others (see on Matt. 5:14–16).
**Did hide himself.** Compare ch. 8:59. This was Jesus’ last day at the Temple. It was, as well, His last day of public ministry. After one final appeal to the leaders of Israel Jesus left the Temple forever. See on Matt. 23:38.

37.zh:
他雖然在他們面前行了許多神蹟，他們還是不信他。

**還是不信。**關於神蹟作為信心的基礎，見本卷註釋第208,209頁。
37.en: **Believed not.** [Final Rejection by the Jewish Leaders, John 12:36b–50. See Closing Ministry at Jerusalem.] For miracles as a basis of faith see pp. 208, 209.

38.zh:
這是要應驗先知以賽亞的話，說：主啊，我們所傳的有誰信呢？主的膀臂向誰顯露呢？

**這是要應驗先知以賽亞的話。**原文可成結果狀語從句，像約9:3中一樣（見該處註釋；參約11:4註釋），而不譯成目的狀語從句。這樣就理解為：“他們不信祂，結果，先知以賽亞的話應驗了。”詳見太1:22；約12:39註釋。
**主啊，……有誰信呢。**引自七十士譯本的賽53:1，而不是希伯來原文。這兩個版本的區別在於“主啊”這個稱呼，希伯來文版本中沒有這個稱呼。見賽53:1註釋。
38.en:
**Might be fulfilled.** The Greek may be translated as a clause of result rather than of purpose, as in ch. 9:3 (see comment there; cf. on ch. 11:4). The passage would then read, “They believed not in him: as a result, the saying of Esaias the prophet was fulfilled, etc.” See further on Matt. 1:22; John 12:39.
**Lord, who hath believed?** A quotation from Isa. 53:1, from the LXX rather than the Hebrew. The two readings are identical except for the title “Lord,” which does not appear in the Hebrew. See on Isa. 53:1.

39.zh:
他們所以不能信，因為以賽亞又說：

**不能信。**這句話對照第38節註釋就好理解了。上帝的預見並不妨礙人們自由的選擇。以賽亞的預言只是說明上帝的預見是什麼樣子的。“預言並不塑造應驗之人的性格。人的行動出於他們的自由意志”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1900年11月13日）。見太1:22；約3:17-20註釋。
39.en: **Could not believe.** This statement should be understood in the light of the comment on v. 38. God’s foreknowledge does not preclude free choice. The prophecy of Isaiah was simply a prediction of what God’s foreknowledge had seen would be. “The prophecies do not shape the characters of the men who fulfill them. Men act out their own free will” (EGW RH Nov. 13, 1900). See on Matt. 1:22; John 3:17–20.

40.zh:
主叫他們瞎了眼，硬了心，免得他們眼睛看見，心裡明白，回轉過來，我就醫治他們。

**叫他們瞎了眼。**引自賽6:10，儘管與現在七十士譯本和希伯來文版本不盡相同。約翰是自由引用，或在他之前有不同的版本。見賽6:10；太13:15註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第626頁；《基督教育原理》第450頁。
40.en: **Blinded their eyes.** A quotation from Isa. 6:10, though not agreeing exactly with our present Hebrew and LXX texts. John was probably quoting freely or had before him a variant text. For comment see on Isa. 6:10; Matt. 13:15.

41.zh:
以賽亞因為看見他的榮耀，就指著他說這話。

**因為看見祂的榮耀。**有文本為“當他看見祂的榮耀時”。聯繫到約12:40的話，這裡似乎是在指《以賽亞書》第6章的異象。
41.en: **When he saw his glory.** Textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 46) for, “because he saw his glory.” In any case the reference seems to be the vision of Isa. 6, in connection with which the words of John 12:40 were spoken.

42.zh:
雖然如此，官長中卻有好些信他的，只因法利賽人的緣故，就不承認，恐怕被趕出會堂。

**官長中。**與民族的盲目形成對照。
**不承認。**或“繼續不承認”。這裡是早些時候所提問題的回答：“官長或是法利賽人豈有信祂的呢”（約7:48）？有些人後來公開信了祂，比如尼哥底母（約19:39；參約3:1）和亞利馬太的約瑟（見太27:57註釋）。
**趕出。**見約9:22註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第105頁；《歷代願望》第626頁。
42.en:
**Among the chief rulers.** In contrast with the blindness of the nation.
**Did not confess.** Rather, “continued not to confess.” Nevertheless here was the answer to the question posed some time earlier, “Have any of the rules or of the Pharisees believed on him?” (ch. 7:48). Some later did confess Him openly, as, for example, Nicodemus (ch. 19:39; cf. ch. 3:1) and Joseph of Arimathaea (see on Matt. 27:57).
**Put out.** See on ch. 9:22.

43.zh:
這是因他們愛人的榮耀過於愛神的榮耀。

**愛人的榮耀。**見太23:5註釋。《密西拿》有以下的話，說明人的稱讚和榮耀的價值：“你弟子的榮耀就是你自己的榮耀，你同事的榮耀就是對你老師的尊敬，對你老師的尊敬就是對上天的敬畏”（Aboth,4 12，《塔木德》松奇諾版第50,51頁）。
43.en: **Loved the praise of men.** See on Matt. 23:5. The Mishnah has the following, showing the value placed on the praise and honor of men: “Let the honour of thy disciple be as dear to thee as thine own, and the honour of thy colleague as the reverence for thy teacher, and the reverence for thy teacher as the fear of Heaven” (Aboth, 4 12, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 50, 51).

44.zh:
耶穌大聲說：信我的，不是信我，乃是信那差我來的。

**耶穌大聲說。**鑑於第36節所提耶穌的離開和隱藏，這次講話的具體時間並不清楚。第37-50節似乎是約翰對人們拒絕彌賽亞的評論。這一天在聖殿中的教訓結束了耶穌公開的傳道。後來祂就只在私下裡教訓祂的門徒了。
**那差我來的。**這個分句經常出現在《約翰福音》中（約5:24,30,37；6:38,39,40,44等），強調了子與父完全的合一（見約3:17；10:30註釋）。
44.en:
**Jesus cried.** The specific moment of this address, with reference to Jesus’ departure and concealment mentioned in v. 36, is uncertain. Verses 37–50 appear to be John’s comment on the rejection of the Messiah. This day’s teaching in the Temple concluded Christ’s public ministry. Henceforth His teaching was in private to His disciples.
**On him that sent me.** The clause “that [or, “which”] sent [or, “hath sent”] me” is frequent in John (chs. 5:24, 30, 37; 6:38, 39, 40, 44; etc.). This clause emphasizes the complete unity of the Son with the Father (see on chs. 3:17; 10:30).

45.zh:
人看見我，就是看見那差我來的。

**那差我來的。**基督來，是要向這世界彰顯祂父的品格（見約1:18節註釋）。當腓力說，“求主將父顯給我們看”時，耶穌宣稱：“人看見了我，就是看見了父”（約14:8,9）。父與子在他們的計劃，目的和步驟上都是完全一致的（見約10:30節註釋）。
45.en: **Him that sent me.** Christ came to represent the character of His Father to the world (see on ch. 1:18). When Philip said, “Lord, shew us the Father,” Jesus declared, “He that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (ch. 14:8, 9). The Father and the Son were perfectly united in their aims, purposes, and procedures (see on ch. 10:30).

46.zh:
我到世上來，乃是光，叫凡信我的，不住在黑暗裡。

**光。**關於耶穌是光，見約1:4；8:12註釋。
**在黑暗裡。**見約壹2:11註釋；參約12:35,36。
46.en:
**Light.** On Jesus the Light see on chs. 1:4; 8:12.
**In darkness.** See on 1 John 2:11; cf. John 12:35, 36.

47.zh:
若有人聽見我的話不遵守，我不審判他。我來本不是要審判世界，乃是要拯救世界。

**不審判。**見約3:17；9:39註釋。

48.zh:
棄絕我、不領受我話的人，有審判他的─就是我所講的道在末日要審判他。

**有審判他的。**將這裡與約5:45進行比較。施行審判的不是摩西，而是基督的道。耶穌同時代的人從他那裡聽到了關於祂身份和使命的真理，這一事實令他們無可推諉。對於得蒙拯救的條件他們不能再說自己是無知的。如果他們沒有聽到真理他們就不用承擔責任（見約9:39-41註釋）。這對於今天聽見上帝之道的人也是一樣。上帝將極大的責任放在那些聽到真理的人身上！他們或許輕視甚至譏誚主的教訓，但最終他們必悲傷地發現自己一定要為自己所聽所做的負責。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第626頁；《證言》卷五第434頁。
48.en: **One that judgeth.** Compare ch. 5:45. Here it is not Moses, but the word of Christ, that judges. The fact that the contemporaries of Jesus had heard from Him the truth concerning His identity and mission left them without excuse. They could not claim ignorance as to the requirements for salvation. If they had not heard the truth, they would not have been held responsible (see on ch. 9:39–41). Thus it is with those who hear the Word of God today. Great is the responsibility placed by God upon the hearers! They may ridicule and even despise sermons, but they will find to their sorrow at last that they must give an account of what they of what they have done in view of what they have heard.

49.zh:
因為我沒有憑著自己講，惟有差我來的父已經給我命令，叫我說什麼，講什麼。

**憑著自己。**猶太人拒絕耶穌的道就是拒絕了他們自稱敬拜的父上帝。關於這一點，耶穌想要警告他們。人拒絕了使者的信息，也就是拒絕從天上發出信息的那一位。他們不只是拒絕使者，還拒絕了那位賜他們信息並差遣他們的一主（見太10:40註釋）。
49.en: **Of myself.** In rejecting the words of Jesus the Jews were rejecting God the Father, whom they professed to worship. Of this, Jesus sought to warn them. Thus it is also when men refuse the words of the messengers but also the One who gave of Heaven. They reject not merely the messengers but also the One who have them their message and sent them forth (see on Matt. 10:40).

1.en:
**In the beginning.** [Prologue to John’s Gospel, John 1:1–18.] The Greek phrase lacks the definite article, but is nevertheless definite in meaning. If the definite article were used in the Greek it would tend to imply some particular point of time, or “beginning.” Without the definite article, and in the context of vs. 1–3, the phrase denotes the most remote time conceivable, before the creation of “all things” (v. 3), before any and every other “beginning,” that is, eternity past.
The account of creation opens with the equivalent Hebrew words (see on Gen. 1:1). As Gen. 1 sets forth the nature of creation and the fact that man was originally formed in the image of God, so the prologue to the Gospel of John sets forth the nature of the Creator (vs. 1–4) and the means by which God purposed to make possible the re-creation of His image in man (vs. 5–14). Gen. 1:1 refers to “the beginning” of this world. But the “Word” of John 1:1–4 is the Creator of all things, and therefore antedates “the beginning” of Gen. 1:1. Thus “the beginning” of John 1:1 is prior to “the beginning” of Gen. 1:1. When everything that had a beginning began, the “Word” already “was.”
**Was.** Gr. ēn, a form of the verb eimi, “to be,” expressing continuity of existence, or being. The Word was, throughout all eternity; He never became such. But, in time, the Word “was made [literally, “became,” Gr. egeneto, a form of ginomai, “to become,” expressing action initiated and completed at a given time] flesh” (v. 14). Thus, Christ has ever been God (John 1:1; Heb. 1:8); but, in contrast, He became man (John 1:14; cf. Phil. 2:7). Thus, both in the words and in their form, John stresses the continuous, timeless, unlimited existence of Christ prior to His incarnation. In eternity past there was no point before which it could be said that the Word was not. The Son was “with the Father from all eternity” (AA 39). “There never was a time when He was not in close fellowship with the eternal God” (Ev 615). Compare Rev. 22:13, where Jesus proclaims Himself “the beginning and the end.” He is “the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever” (Heb. 13:8).
The word ginomai, used in v. 14, appears also in v. 3 of the creation of all things (literally, “by him everything became”). Jesus declared, “Before Abraham was [Gr. ginomai, literally, “became,” or “came to be”], I am [Gr. eimi]” (ch. 8:58). The same contrast appears in the LXX of Ps. 90:2: “Before the mountains came into being [Gr. ginomai], from age to age thou art [Gr. eimi] God.”
Ēn occurs three times in John 1:1, first of the eternity of the Word, then of His eternal fellowship with the Father, and finally of His eternal equality of nature with the Father. Verse 2 reaffirms the duration of this state of being throughout all eternity.
**Word.** Gr. logos, “utterance,” “saying,” “speech,” “narrative,” “account,” “treatise,” with emphasis on the systematic, meaningful arrangement of the thoughts thus expressed. Here John uses the term as a designation for Christ, who came to reveal the character, mind, and will of the Father, even as speech is the expression of ideas. In the LXX the word logos is commonly used of both creative (Ps. 33:6; cf. Gen. 1:3, 6, 9, etc.) and communicative (Jer. 1:4; Eze. 1:3; Amos 3:1) expressions of the divine mind and will. No doubt these OT uses of logos were in the mind of John as he wrote. God has expressed His divine will and purpose through creation and through revelation; now (John 1:14) He has done so through the incarnation, His supreme and perfect revelation (see EGW Supplementary Material on v. 18). The word Logos thus epitomizes the dominant theme of the book of John (see ch. 14:8–10; also below under “Word was God”; also Additional Note on Chapter 1). In v. 18 John states his reason for speaking of Christ as “the Word”—He came to “declare” the Father. As a designation for Christ the word Logos is used in the NT only by John, in his Gospel (ch. 1) and in 1 John 1:1; Rev. 19:13. The term identifies Christ as the incarnate expression of the will of the Father that all men should be saved (see 1 Tim. 2:4), as “God’s thought made audible” (DA 19).
**With God.** Gr. pros ton theon. The word pros denotes close association and fellowship. Had John meant simply that in the beginning the Word was in proximity to God, he might have been expected to use either the word para, “beside,” or the word meta, “with” (cf. on ch. 6:46). But John intended more than either of these words would convey, as when he wrote, “we have an advocate with [Gr. pros] the Father” (1 John 2:1)—not in the sense that Jesus is simply in the Father’s presence, but that He is closely associated with the Father in the work of salvation. Pros is used in the same sense in Heb. 4:13: “with whom we have to do,” that is, “with whom we have dealings.” The word here implies close personal fellowship in an enterprise of mutual interest and concern. Compare John 17:5.
The fact that the Word was “with God,” that is, with the Father, emphatically declares Him to be a being altogether distinct from the Father. As the context makes clear, the Word was associated with God in a unique and exclusive sense. The Word was “with God” in the eternity past, but He became “flesh” in order to be with “us” (see on v. 14; cf. DA 23–26). He was Immanuel, “God with us” (see on Matt. 1:23). It is impossible to understand the import of the incarnation except against the background of the eternal pre-existence of Christ as God and as associated with God (see EGW Supplementary Material on Rom. 1:20–25).
**Word was God.** The absence, in the Greek, of the definite article before the word “God” makes it impossible to render the statement, “God was the Word.” Thus to render it would equate God with the Word and thus limit Deity exclusively to the Word. The two terms, “Word” and “God,” are not altogether interchangeable. It would be no more proper to say that “God was the Word” than to say that “love is God” (cf. 1 John 4:16), or, “flesh was made the Word” (cf. John 1:14). Although here in v. 1 the word “God” lacks the definite article, it is still definite. The statement cannot be translated “the Word was a God,” as if the Word were one God among many other gods. In Greek the absence of the article often emphasizes quality expressed by, or inherent in, a word. Accordingly, John means that the Word partook of the essence of Deity, that He was divine in the ultimate and absolute sense. Thus in one terse declaration John denies that the Word was either a God, one among many, or the God, as if He alone were God.
In the prologue (vs. 1–18) John states the objective that guided him in writing the Gospel; namely, to present the man Jesus as God incarnate (cf. 1 John 1:1). From incident to incident and discourse to discourse he faithfully pursues this objective. In his conclusion he observes that his purpose in writing was to lead others to “believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God,” and that believing they “might have life through his name” (John 20:30, 31). In the introduction to his first epistle John again refers to his personal experiences with “the Word” (1 John 1:1–3). Likewise the opening words of the Revelation declare it to be “the Revelation of Jesus Christ” (ch. 1:1). See Additional Note at end of chapter; see on Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9.
Christ is eternally God in the supreme and unqualified sense of the term (see Additional Note at end of chapter). For comment on the fiction that Jesus was merely a great and good man see on Matt. 16:16.
Evidences of the deity of Christ are many and irrefutable. These may be summed up briefly: (1) the life He lived (Heb. 4:15; 1 Peter 2:22), (2) the words He spoke (John 7:46; 14:10; cf. Matt. 7:29), (3) the miracles He wrought (John 5:20; 14:11), (4) the prophecies He fulfilled (Luke 24:26, 27, 44; John 5:39; DA 799). See DA 406, 407.
1.zh:
太初有道，道與神同在，道就是神。

約1:1-18：《約翰福音》的前言
**太初。**原文沒有定冠詞，但意思卻很明確。如果前面加上定冠詞，那就是指某個特定的時間或“最初之時”。 該詞在1-3節中不加定冠詞，就是指最遙遠的過去，“萬物”（約1:3）被造以先，一切“開始”之前，也就是萬古之先。
創造的記錄也是以這個希伯來詞開頭的（見創1:1節註釋）。正如《創世紀》第1章說明了創造的性質和人類按上帝的形象被造的事實，《約翰福音》的開篇說明了創造主的本質（約1:1-4）和上帝在人身上恢復祂形象的方法（約1:5-14）。創1:1說的是這個世界的“起初”。約1:1-4中的“道”則是萬物的創造者，所以在創1:1的“起初”之前。也就是說，約1:1的“太初”要比創1:1的“起初”早。在萬物“開始”以先，“道”已經“有”了。
**有。**ēn，是動詞eimi的一種形式，表示一直存在。道是永存的，絕不是變成的。但到了時候，道“成了（egeneto，是ginomai的一種形式，表示在一定的時間內開始和完成的行為）肉身”（約:1:14）。所以基督一直就是上帝（約1:1；來1:8），但祂卻成了人（約1:14；參腓2:7）。約翰所用的詞語和詞語的形態都強調基督成為肉身之前是無限，永恆和持續存在的。在萬古之先，沒有任何時候是道所不存在的。聖子“從太初就與父同在”（《使徒行述》39頁）。“基督沒有一刻不與永恆的上帝保持親密的關係”（《佈道論》615頁）。參啟22:13耶穌稱自己是“初”和“終”。“耶穌基督昨日、今日、一直到永遠，是一樣的”（來13:8）。
Ginomai還出現第14節中。它在第3節中指萬物的創造（“萬物是藉著祂造的”）。耶穌宣稱：“還沒有（ginomai）亞伯拉罕，就有（eimi）了我”（約8:58）。這種對比也出現在詩90:2中，“諸山未曾生出（ginomai），……你是（eimi）上帝。”
在約1:1中，ēn出現三次，第一次指道的永恆性，第二次指祂與父永遠同在，第三次指祂與父永遠同等。第2節重申這種狀態從太初就存在。
**道。**logos，“話語”，“講述”，“論述”，強調思維有條理，有意義的表達。約翰在這裡指基督。祂來表顯天父的品格，思想和旨意，就像言語表達思想那樣。logos在七十士譯本里通常指創造（詩33:6；參創1:3,6,9,等）和上帝旨意的表達（耶1:4；結1:3；摩3:1）。約翰在寫作時無疑想到logos在《舊約》中的這些用法。上帝曾藉著創造和啟示來表達祂神聖的旨意；現在（約1:14）祂通過成為肉身來表達祂完美的最高啟示（見第18節懷愛倫註釋），Logos就這樣概括了整卷《約翰福音》的主題（見約14:8-10；又見下面“道就是上帝”註釋；《約翰福音》第1章補充註釋）。約翰在第18節說明了他稱基督為“道”的原因，就是要將父“表明”出來。《新約》中只有約翰在《約翰福音》第1章，約壹1:1和啟19:13中用logos來指基督。該詞表明基督是天父意志在肉身的表達，為了使萬人得救（見提前2:4），“使我們聽見上帝的旨意”（《歷代願望》19頁）。
**與上帝同在。**pros ton theon。Pros指親密的關係。如果約翰只是要表達道起初就與上帝同在，他可以用para（“在旁邊”）或meta（“在一起”，參約6:46註釋）。但這兩個詞語不足以表達約翰的意思。就像他說“在（pros）父那裡我們有一位中保”（約壹2:1），不只是說耶穌在父的面前，而是說祂與天父在救贖工作中的緊密聯繫。Pros在來4:13中也是這個意思：“與我們有關係的主”。該詞在這裡表示在涉及雙方利益的事業中個人的親密關係。參約17:5。
道“與上帝同在”，就是與天父同在，強調祂有別於父的位格。正如上下文所表明的那樣，“道”是在獨特的意義上與上帝同在的。“道”在萬古之先就“與上帝同在”。但祂為了與“我們”同在，就成了“肉身”（見第14節註釋；參《歷代願望》23-26頁）。祂是以馬內利──“上帝與我們同在”（見太1:23節註釋）。只有在基督萬古之先就是上帝，並且與上帝同在的背景下，我們才能理解道成肉身的重要性（見羅1:20-25懷愛倫註釋）。
**道就是上帝。**原文的“上帝”沒有定冠詞，故不能譯為“上帝就是道”。否則會把上帝與道等同起來，使“上帝”侷限於“道”了。“道”和“上帝”這兩個詞的位置是不能互換的。說“上帝就是道”就如說“愛就是上帝”（參約壹4:16）或“肉身成了道”（參約1:14）一樣不合適。本節的“上帝”雖然沒有定冠詞，但依然很明確。這句話也不能譯為“道是一位上帝，”似乎上帝是諸神中的一位。在希臘文中不加冠詞，往往是強調該詞的特性。所以約翰指的是“道”擁有上帝的本質。祂絕對是上帝。約翰就這樣否定了“道”是諸神中的一位，或只有道（聖子）是上帝。
約翰在開頭語（約1:1-18）中指出他寫這卷書的目的，就是向人說明耶穌是道成肉身的上帝（參約壹1:1）。約翰所記錄的一件一件事情，和一次一次談話，都忠實地圍繞著這個目標。他最後歸納說，他寫作的目的就是要引導別人“信耶穌是基督，是上帝的兒子，”並相信他們“可以因祂的名得生命”（約20:30,31）。約翰在他第一封書信的開頭語再次指出他對於“道”的個人體驗（約壹1:1-3）。《啟示錄》的開篇也稱這是“耶穌基督的啟示”（啟1:1）。見本章補充註釋；見腓2:6-8；西2:9註釋。
基督是崇高無限的永恆上帝（見本章補充註釋）。關於耶穌只是一個大好人的說法，見太16:16註釋。
關於基督的神性，有許多無可辯駁的證據。簡單歸納如下：一，祂所過的生活（來4:15；彼前2:22）；二，祂所說過的話（約7:46；14:10；參太7:29）；三，祂所行的神蹟（約5:20；14:11）；四，祂所應驗的預言（路24:26,27,44；約5:39；《歷代願望》799頁）。見《歷代願望》406，407頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《佈道論》第615頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《先祖與先知》第34頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《歷代願望》第281頁；《基督教育原理》第406頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第63，138頁。

2.en: **The same.** Verse 2 repeats the essential facts of v. 1, for emphasis.
2.zh:
這道太初與神同在。

第2節為強調而重述了第1節的基本事實。

29.en:
**Next day.** That is, the day after the events of vs. 19–28. Detailed and often precise chronological information is characteristic of John (see chs. 1:29, 39, 43; 2:1, 12; 4:43; 6:22; 11:6, 17; 12:1, 12; 20:26).
**John seeth Jesus.** The delegation from Jerusalem had departed. Evidently they did not take John seriously, or they would have pressed their investigation further, to discover, if possible, of whom he spoke (see v. 26). The preceding day Jesus had not been identified by John’s indirect reference to Him as the Messiah (v. 26). Now He is singled out from the crowd.
**Behold.** What a privilege to be the first to herald (see on Matt. 3:1) Jesus, the One to whom all the prophets of old bore witness, as the true sacrifice! Which of the prophets would not have thrilled at the privilege! Little wonder that Jesus later spoke of John as a prophet than whom no greater had arisen in Israel (Luke 7:28)!
**Lamb of God.** That is, the Lamb provided by God. John alone uses this designation for Christ, though Luke (Acts 8:32) and Peter (1 Peter 1:19) have similar comparisons (cf. Isa. 53:7). John the Baptist introduced Jesus as “the Lamb of God” to John the evangelist (see on John 1:35, 36), and for the disciple this title must have held deep significance. The figure, which stresses Jesus’ innocence and perfection of character, and thus the vicarious nature of His sacrifice (Isa. 53:4–6, 11, 12; see on Ex. 12:5), is reminiscent of the paschal lamb of Egypt, which typified deliverance from the bondage of sin. “Christ our passover is sacrificed for us” (1 Cor. 5:7). By the figure of a lamb John identifies the suffering Messiah as the one in whom the sacrificial system of OT times reaches reality and has meaning. In the divine foreknowledge and purpose He was “the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world” (Rev. 13:8).
In view of the fact that contemporary Jewish thought found no place for a suffering Messiah, critics doubt that John could have held such a concept (see John 12:34; cf. Mark 9:31, 32; Luke 24:21). But as Robertson has well remarked (Word Pictures in the New Testament, on John 1:29), “Certainly the Baptist did not have to be as ignorant as the rabbis.” John had the Messianic prophecy of Isa. 53 (see on Isa. 53:1, 4–6; see DA 136). Furthermore, it would be strange indeed for God to ordain John the Baptist as herald of the coming of Messiah and not impart to him the knowledge of this fundamental aspect of Messiah’s mission.
**Taketh away.** Gr. airō, “to lift up,” “to bear away,” “to remove.” Only by virtue of the fact that the Lamb of God was without sin (Heb. 4:15; 1 Peter 2:22) could He “take away [Gr. airō] our sins” (1 John 3:5). Because the burden of sin was too heavy for us to bear, Jesus came to lift the load from our shattered lives.
**Sin.** By the singular form of the word John places emphasis on sin as a principle, rather than on particular sins (see 1 John 2:2; 3:5; 4:10).
29.zh:
次日，約翰看見耶穌來到他那裡，就說：看哪，神的羔羊，除去（或作：背負）世人罪孽的！

**次日。**即第19-28節事件的第二天。約翰的記載以詳細和時間準確而著稱（見1:29,39,43；2:1,12；4:43；6:22；11:6,17；12:1,12；20:26）。
**約翰看見耶穌。**耶路撒冷的代表團走了。他們顯然不太在意施洗約翰，否則就會深入調查下去，可能的話，找到約翰所說的那個人（見第26節）。前一天約翰間接地指出耶穌是彌賽亞（第26節），但祂沒有被認出來。現在祂要從人群中被識別出來了。
**看哪。**第一個宣佈（見太3:1註釋）耶穌是古代眾先知所預言的真正犧牲，這是多麼光榮的特權啊！在先知中誰不會為這項特權而興奮不已呢！無怪耶穌說，在以色列興起的先知中沒有一個大過約翰的（路7:28）！
**上帝的羔羊。**即上帝所提供的羔羊。只有約翰用“上帝的羔羊”來代表基督，路加（徒8:32）和彼得（彼前1:19）也用過類似的比喻（參賽53:7）。施洗約翰把“上帝的羔羊”耶穌介紹給使徒約翰（見約1:35,36註釋）。對於使徒約翰而言，這個稱號具有更深的意義。這個比喻強調耶穌純潔完全的品格以及祂代替我們犧牲（賽53:4-6,11,12；見出12:5註釋），使人想起了那在埃及逾越節上預表脫離罪惡奴役的羔羊。“因為我們逾越節的羔羊基督已經被殺獻祭了”（林前5:7）。約翰用羔羊的比喻，說明受苦的彌賽亞正應驗和實現了舊約時代的獻祭制度。根據上帝的預見和旨意，基督是“從創世以來……被殺之羔羊”（啟13:8）。
鑑於當時的猶太人沒有彌賽亞受苦的概念，批評家們不太相信施洗約翰持這樣的觀點（見約12:34註釋；參可9:31,32；路24:21）。但正如羅伯遜所指出的（《新約句解》Word Pictures in the New Testament，約1:29註釋）：“施洗約翰肯定不會像拉比們那樣無知。”他了解《以賽亞書》第53章彌賽亞的預言（見賽53:1,4-6註釋；見《歷代願望》136頁）。況且上帝既然指定施洗約翰宣報彌賽亞的來臨，就不大可能不把彌賽亞使命的這種基本知識告訴他。
**除去（或作“揹負”）。**airō，“承擔”，“消除”。只有靠上帝無罪羔羊的功勞（來4:15；彼前2:22），祂才能“除掉（airō）人的罪”（約壹3:5）。因為罪擔太沉重，我們無法承擔，耶穌就來把重擔從我們破碎的生活上除去。
**罪孽。**系單數形式，約翰用它來強調罪的原理，而不是強調具體的罪行（見約壹2:2；3:5；4:10）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第422，528頁；《基督比喻實訓》第77，222，250，274頁；《給管家的勉言》第289頁；《給管家的勉言》第212，109頁；《基督教育之研究》第648頁；《歷代願望》第112，136，137，175，180，216，385，439，477，579，594，622，651，750頁；《佈道論》第134，188，291，299，444，578，582頁；《早期著作》第154頁；《基督教育原理》第97，239，383頁；《善惡之爭》第399頁；《傳道良助》第26，56，148，155，172頁；《懷氏傳略》第345頁；《福山寶訓》第2，8頁；《今日的生活》第171，220頁；《服務真詮》第157頁；《醫療佈道論》第31頁；《拾級就主》第19，79頁；《給傳道人的證言》第155，214，218頁；《證言》卷二第30頁；《證言》卷四第395頁；《證言》卷五第449，729頁；《證言》卷六第20，32，39，54，67，81，95，105，279，314頁；《證言》卷七第238頁；《證言》卷八第334頁；《證言》卷九第23，48，60，81，203頁。

10.en:
**In the world.** That is, among men. See on v. 9.
**Made by him.** See on v. 3.
**Knew him not.** That is, “the world” did not recognize Jesus as the Messiah, “the true Light.” Not only so; it rejected and crucified Him. See on v. 11.
10.zh:
他在世界，世界也是藉著他造的，世界卻不認識他。

**在世界。**就是在世人中間。見第9節註釋。
**藉著祂造的。**見第3節註釋。
**不認識祂。**這個“世界”不承認耶穌是彌賽亞，是“真光”。更有甚者，“世界”還拒絕祂，將祂釘在十字架上。見第11節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第737頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–14節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第138頁。

17.en:
**The law.** That is, the system of revealed religion under which the Jews lived in OT times, divinely ordained but gradually perverted by human tradition (see on Mark 7:9–13). In the days of Christ the term “law” included not only the Decalogue but all that Moses and the prophets had written (Luke 24:27, 44)—as interpreted by the rabbis. In and of itself, as originally given by God, “the law” was good (cf. Rom. 3:1, 2). It was designed to lead men to salvation through faith in the coming Messiah (John 5:39, 45–47; Luke 24:25–27, 44). The fact that “some did not believe” (Rom. 3:3), but sought salvation “by the works of the law” (ch. 9:32) rather than by faith, and as a result failed to enter into the spiritual rest God intended for them (Heb. 3:18, 19; 4:2), does not mean that the system itself as ordained by God was faulty. All that God does is “perfect” (Deut. 32:4). Many there were in OT times who “obtained a good report through faith” (Heb. 11:39). In fact, there never has been any other way to obtain a “good report” than “through faith.”
Concerning the manner in which human tradition had perverted the plan of salvation by emphasizing the forms of religion rather than its spiritual and moral objectives see on Mark 7:1–13. For Christ’s exposition of the true spirit of the law as applied to the problems of daily living see on Matt. 5:17–22. For a discussion of the word “law” itself see on Gal. 3:24. Concerning the means of salvation in OT times see on Eze. 16:60.
**By Moses.** Literally, “through Moses.” “The law” did not originate with Moses, but with God. Moses was simply the agent through whom the revealed will of God was imparted to men (see Deut. 5:22 to 6:1; Heb. 1:1).
**But.** This word has been supplied by the translators. It implies a stronger contrast between “law” and “grace” than John apparently intended. John does not mean to imply that the system revealed through Moses was bad, as compared with that now revealed through Christ, but that, good as Moses’ system was, that of Christ’s is better (see Heb. 7:22; 8:6; 9:23; 10:34).
**Grace and truth.** See on vs. 14, 16. These divine attributes were inherent in the system of revealed religion in OT times (see Ex. 34:6, 7), but had, for practical purposes, been lost under a thick layer of human tradition. The contrast between “law” and “grace” is not so much a contrast between the system of religion in OT times, which looked forward to a coming Messiah, and that revealed by Christ (cf. Heb. 1:1, 2), as between the perverted interpretation placed upon the revealed grace and truth of God by the official exponents of the law, the rabbis (cf. Rom. 6:14, 15; Gal. 5:4), and the truth as revealed through Jesus Christ.
By affirming that “truth” comes through Christ, John identifies Him as the reality toward whom pointed all OT types and ceremonies, which were no more than a shadow of better things to come. Type met antitype in Christ (Col. 2:16, 17). In no sense does John imply that the OT system was false or in error.
**By Jesus Christ.** It was Christ who had spoken through Moses and the prophets (1 Peter 1:9, 10; PP 366). Now He appeared in person to reaffirm the great eternal truths revealed to these holy men of old, and to restore them to their original luster, untarnished by human tradition (see on Matt. 5:17–19). He came to reveal the Father in His true character (cf. Ex. 34:6, 7), to prevail upon men to practice justice and mercy and to be humble before God (Micah 6:6–8). He who “spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets” now spoke to men through His own Son (Heb. 1:1, 2).
Here, for the first time, John refers to our Lord by the historical name, Jesus Christ (see on Matt. 1:1). The eternal “Word” has become incarnate, a man among men, and John henceforth speaks of Him as such.
17.zh:
律法本是藉著摩西傳的；恩典和真理都是由耶穌基督來的。

**律法。**指上帝所設立，舊約時代的猶太人所遵行的成文宗教體制，但它逐漸被人的遺傳所代替（見可7:9-13註釋）。在基督的時代，“律法”不僅包括十誡，也包括摩西和眾先知的一切著作（路24:27,44），以及拉比們的解釋。律法原出於上帝，本來是好的（參羅3:1,2）。它的目的是引人因相信將要來臨的彌賽亞而得救（約5:39,45-47；路24:25-27,44）。“有不信的”（羅3:3）人，想“憑著行律法”（羅9:32），而不憑著信心而得救，結果未能進入上帝為他們所預備的有缺陷。上帝所作的盡都“完全”（申32:4）。許多舊約時代的人“因信得了美好的證據”（來11:39）。事實上，根本沒有別的辦法比“因信”更能得到“美好的證據。”
關於人的遺傳曲解了救恩的計劃，強調宗教的形式而忽略了其屬靈和道德的目標，見可7:1-13註釋。關於基督所闡述律法對於日常生活問題的屬靈意義，見太5:17-22註釋。關於“律法”的含義，見加3:24註釋。關於舊約時代救恩的意義，見結16:60註釋。
**藉著摩西。**“律法”出於上帝，而不是出於摩西。摩西只是向人傳達上帝啟示之旨意的媒介（見申5:22至6:1節；來1:1）。
有的文本在這裡加上“然而”，暗示律法和恩典之間形成了強烈的對比。約翰並沒有說，藉著摩西所啟示的體制與耶穌所啟示的體制相比之下，是不好的。摩西的制度是好的，但基督的制度更加美好（見來7:22；8:6；9:23；10:34）。
**恩典和真理。**見第14,16註釋。上帝的這些品質包含在舊約時代所啟示的宗教體系之中（見出34:6,7），但實際上卻掩蓋在人厚厚的遺傳之下。“律法”和“恩典”之間的反差，主要不是舊約時代盼望彌賽亞來臨的宗教體系與基督所啟示宗教體系（參來1:1,2）之間，而是在律法官方的解釋者拉比對上帝恩典和真理的曲解（參羅6:14,15；加5:4），和耶穌基督所啟示的真理之間。
約翰肯定“真理”來自基督，指出祂是舊約中一切儀式和表號的實體，而那些儀式和表號只不過是將來更美之事的影子。表號在基督身上遇見了實體（西2:16,17）。約翰絕沒有暗示舊約的制度是虛假或錯誤的。
**由耶穌基督。**藉著摩西和眾先知說話的乃是基督（彼前1:9,10；《先祖與先知》366頁）。現在祂親自顯現，肯定祂曾啟示古聖先賢的偉大真理，恢復它們在沒有被人的遺傳所玷汙之時的光彩（見太5:17-19註釋）。祂來是要顯示天父的真正品格（參出34:6,7），勸世人行公義，好憐憫，在上帝面前存謙卑的心（彌6:6-8）。上帝曾“在古時藉著眾先知多次多方地曉諭列祖”，現在祂又藉著自己的兒子曉諭我們（來1:1,2）。
約翰在這裡第一次提到我們主“耶穌基督”的名字（見太1:1註釋）。永生之“道”已成為肉身，住在世人中間，所以約翰稱呼祂“耶穌基督”。

41.en:
**His own brother.** Andrew became the first disciple to begin bringing others to Jesus. He did so “first,” that is, before he did anything else. This testifies to the profound impression made on his mind and heart by that first conversation with Jesus.
**Messias.** See on Matt. 1:1.
**Interpreted.** See on v. 38.
41.zh:
他先找著自己的哥哥西門，對他說：我們遇見彌賽亞了。（彌賽亞翻出來就是基督。）

**自己的哥哥。**安得烈是第一個帶人歸向耶穌的門徒。他“先”找著自己的哥哥，即在他作任何事之前，證明了他和耶穌的第一次交談在他心中留下了非常深刻的印象。
**彌賽亞。**見太1:1註釋。
**翻出來。**見第38節註釋。

3.en:
**All things.** A common philosophical phrase denoting the entire universe (see 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16; cf. Heb. 1:1, 2; see on John 1:9).
**Were made.** Gr. ginomai, “became,” “came into being,” “came to be” (see on v. 1). John describes creation as a completed act. Material things are not eternal; there was a time when they “were made.”
**By him.** John was not thinking of the Logos, or “Word,” in the abstract, metaphysical sense of Greek philosophy. The association of Christ with the Father in the work of creation is set forth again and again in the NT (see Rom. 11:36; 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16, 17; Heb. 1:1, 2; cf. Rev. 3:14). Here John presents Christ as the Creator of all things, as in John 1:14 he sets Him forth as the agent of divine mercy and grace for the restoration, or re-creation, of all things. In eternity past the Word was not a passive, inactive entity, but was actively and intimately associated with the Father in the development and administration of “all things.”
**Without him.** The same truth stated negatively. Uniquely and exclusively, the “Word” is Creator.
3.zh:
萬物是藉著他造的；凡被造的，沒有一樣不是藉著他造的。

**萬物。**一個普通的哲學用語，指全宇宙（見林前8:6；西1:16；參來1:1,2；見約1:9註釋）。
**藉著祂。**約翰所想到的，不是“道”（ logos）在希臘哲學中抽象神秘的含義。《新約》一再提到基督在創造大工中與天父的聯合（見羅11:36；林前8:6；西1:16,17；來1:1,2；參啟3:14）。約翰在這裡描述基督是萬物的創造者。他還在約1:14中指出，上帝的憐憫和恩典藉著基督使萬物得到恢復和再造。在萬古之先，“道”並不是被動而消極的。在“萬物”的創造和管理中，祂積極與天父親密合作。
**造。**ginomai，或“成為”（見第1節註釋）。約翰把創造描述為已經完成的事。物質不是永恆的，它們有“被造”的時間。
**沒有一樣不是藉著祂造的。**採用雙重否定的方法重複同一真理：唯有“道”是創造主。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第530頁；《歷代願望》第288頁；《教育論》第134頁；《喜樂的泉源》第88頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–4節）**。《醫療佈道論》第7頁。

14.en:
**Made flesh.** Finite understanding halts at the threshold of infinite love, wisdom, and power—baffled and unable to go further. Paul speaks of the incarnation as a great mystery (1 Tim. 3:16). To stray beyond the bounds of what Inspiration has made known is to delve into mysteries the human mind lacks capacity to comprehend. See on John 6:51; 16:28.
John has already affirmed the true deity of Christ (see on v. 1), and now affirms His true humanity. Christ is divine in the absolute and unqualified sense of the word; He is also human in the same sense, except that He “knew no sin” (2 Cor. 5:21). The Scriptures repeatedly and emphatically proclaim this fundamental truth (see Luke 1:35; Rom. 1:3; 8:3; Gal. 4:4; Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9; 1 Tim. 3:16; Heb. 1:2, 8; 2:14–18; 10:5; 1 John 1:2; etc.; see on Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9). Though Christ was originally “in the form of God” He “did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself,” and, “being born in the likeness of men,” was “found in human form” (Phil. 2:6–8, RSV). In Him was “all the fulness of the Godhead bodily” (Col. 2:9); nevertheless, “in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren” (Heb. 2:17). “From the days of eternity the Lord Jesus Christ was one with the Father,” but “He chose to give back the scepter into the Father’s hands, and to step down from the throne of the universe,” in order “that He might dwell among us, and make us familiar with His divine character and life” (DA 19, 22, 23).
The two natures, the divine and the human, were mysteriously blended into one person. Divinity was clothed with humanity, not exchanged for it. In no sense did Christ cease to be God when He became man. The two natures became closely and inseparably one, yet each remained distinct. The human nature was not changed into the divine nature, nor the divine nature into the human. See Additional Note at end of chapter; see on Matt. 1:1; Luke 1:35; Phil. 2:6–8; Heb. 2:14–17; see EGW Supplementary Material on John 1:1–3, 14; Mark 16:6; Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9; Heb. 2:14–17.
Christ “assumed the liabilities of human nature” (EGW ST Aug. 2, 1905), but His humanity was nevertheless “perfect” (DA 664). Although, as a man, He could have sinned, no taint of, or inclination to, corruption rested upon Him; He had no propensity toward sin (EGW letter 8, 1895, see p. 1128). He was “tempted like as we are, yet without sin” (see on Heb. 4:15). See Additional Note at end of chapter.
**Dwelt.** Gr. skēnoō, literally, “tended,” or “pitched [his] tent,” among us (cf. DA 23). Christ became one of us the better to reveal the Father’s love, to share our experiences, to set us an example, to succor us in temptation, to suffer for our sins, and to represent us before the Father (see on Heb. 2:14–17). The eternal Word, who had ever been with the Father (see on John 1:1). was now to become Immanuel, “God with us” (see on Matt. 1:23).
**Glory.** Gr. doxa, here equivalent to the Heb. kabod, which is used in the OT of the sacred “glory” of the abiding presence of the Lord, the Shekinah (see on Gen. 3:24; Ex. 13:21; cf. on 1 Sam. 4:22). The LXX has doxa 177 times for kabod. John and his fellow disciples bore eyewitness testimony to the historical fact that “the Word was made flesh” (John 1:14; see ch. 21:24; 1 John 1:1, 2). Here John doubtless thinks particularly of experiences such as the Transfiguration, when divinity momentarily flashed through humanity. Peter similarly speaks of being an “eyewitness” to the “majesty” and “excellent glory” of Christ at the Transfiguration (2 Peter 1:16–18). This glory, Peter adds, accompanied the declaration, “This is my beloved Son.” For various occasions during the life of Jesus when the glory of Heaven illumined His countenance see on Luke 2:48. In John 17:5 Jesus prays the Father, “Glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.” The Christian faith rests upon the fact that this divine “glory” rested upon a historical person, Jesus of Nazareth. Secondarily, John may also have in mind the perfection of character exemplified by the Saviour (see below under “Grace and truth”).
**The only begotten.** Gr. monogenēs, from two words meaning “only” and “kind,” and thus properly translated “unique,” “only,” “only one of a kind.” As with the title Logos (see on v. 1), only John uses the word monogenēs of Christ (see John 1:18; 3:16, 18; 1 John 4:9). Absence of the definite article in the Greek either makes monogenēs indefinite, “an only one,” or makes it an expression of quality, in which case John would be saying, “glory as of an only one [who had come] from beside the Father.” This seems evidently the sense here. See on Luke 7:12; 8:42, where monogenēs is translated “only.”
In Heb. 11:17 monogenēs is used of Isaac, who was by no means Abraham’s “only begotten,” or even his first-born. But he was the son of the promise, and as such, the one destined to succeed his father as heir to the birthright (Gen. 25:1–6; Gal. 4:22, 23). “Similarly in respect to the five texts in John’s writings of Christ, the translation should be one of the following: ‘unique,’ ‘precious,’ ‘only,’ ‘sole,’ ‘the only one of his kind,’ but not ‘only begotten’” (Problems in Bible Translation, p. 198).
The translation “only begotten,” here and elsewhere, apparently originated with the early Fathers of the Catholic Church, and entered early English translations of the Bible under the influence of the Latin Vulgate, the official Bible of the Catholic Church. Accurately reflecting the Greek, various Old Latin manuscripts which antedate the Vulgate read “only” rather than “only begotten.” The idea that Christ “was born of the Father before all creation” appears first in the writings of Origen, about .. 230. Arius, nearly a century later, is the first to use gegennemenon, the correct Greek word for “begotten,” when speaking of Christ, and to affirm that He was “begotten of God before all ages” (see Additional Note at end of chapter). This Greek word is never used in the Bible concerning the preincarnate Christ. The idea that Christ was “begotten” by the Father at some time in eternity past is altogether foreign to the Scriptures. For a detailed discussion of this subject see Problems in Bible Translation, pp. 197–204.
Properly understood of Christ’s unique status as the Son of God, the word monogenēs distinguishes between Him and all others who, through faith in Him, are given “power to become the sons of God” (v. 12), and who are specifically declared to be “born … of God” (v. 13). Christ is, and always has been, very “God” (see on v. 1), and by virtue of this fact we “become the sons of God” when we receive Christ and believe on His name.
The statement of v. 14 obviously deals with the incarnation, and its purpose is to emphasize the fact that the incarnate Word retained the divine nature, as evidenced by the manifestation of the preincarnate divine glory (see ch. 17:5). Although the word monogenēs means strictly “unique,” or “only,” rather than “only begotten,” John nevertheless here applies it to Christ at His incarnation, to the time when “the Word was made flesh” in order to dwell among us. Paul confirms this application in Heb. 1:5, 6, where he links the words gegenneka, “have I begotten” (from gennaō, “to beget”), and prōtotoktos, “first-born” (from pro, “before,” and tiktō, “to beget”), to the time “when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world.” It seems therefore wholly unwarranted to understand monogenēs as referring to a mysterious begetting of “the Word” at some point of time in eternity past. For a discussion of Christ as the Son of God see on Luke 1:35; and as the Son of man, see on Matt. 1:1; Mark 2:10; see also EGW Supplementary Material on Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9.
**Of the Father.** Gr. para theou, literally “with the Father,” or “beside the Father,” here probably with the force of “from beside the Father.” The Greek preposition para sometimes has the force of ek, “out of,” “from,” which here agrees best with the context. The incarnate Logos had come forth from the presence of the Father when He entered this world. See on ch. 6:46.
**Full of.** This clearly applies to the Word incarnate. Dwelling on earth as a man among men, the Word was “full of grace and truth.”
**Grace and truth.** Gr. charis kai alētheia. Charis here means “good will,” “loving-kindness,” “[undeserved] favor,” “mercy.” Alētheia refers to the “truth” about the love of God the Father for sinners as revealed in the plan of salvation and in the incarnate Saviour. Here, charis is equivalent to the Heb. chesed (see Additional Note on Psalm 36; see on Job 10:12), as alētheia is to the Heb. ’emeth, “faithfulness,” “trustworthiness.” As “mercy” and “truth,” these words appear together in the OT in a clearly Messianic setting, in Ps. 85:10, 11. It was precisely these attributes of God that Christ came particularly to reveal. While on earth He was “full” of them, and could thus give a full and complete revelation of the Father. God is ever faithful to His own character, and His character is revealed most completely in His mercy, or grace.
Fifteen centuries prior to the incarnation God had instructed Israel to build Him a “sanctuary,” or tent, that He might “dwell among them” (Ex. 25:8). As, in times past, the divine presence had appeared in the form of the Shekinah glory above the mercy seat over the ark and elsewhere (see on Gen. 3:24: Ex. 13:21), so now the same glory had been manifested in the person of Jesus. To this fact John and his fellow disciples bore eyewitness, and to them this was incontestable evidence that Jesus had come forth from the Father. Such glory could have come from no other source.
It is worthy of note that in Hebrew the words mishkan, “dwelling place,” “tent,” “tabernacle,” and Shekinah, the glorious “abiding Presence,” are both derived from shakan, “to dwell,” “to abide.” In Greek, skēnē, “tent” “tabernacle,” is similarly related to skēnoō, “to tent,” “to tabernacle,” and thus “to dwell,” or “to abide.” In times past the divine glory, the holy “Presence,” had dwelt among the chosen people in the literal tabernacle; now, John says, the same glorious “Presence,” God Himself, had come to dwell among His people in the person of our Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ. It is thought that the “glory” of which Paul speaks in Rom. 9:4 is to be identified with the Shekinah glory, as possibly also the “bright cloud” that appeared at the Transfiguration (Matt. 17:5). In the clearly Messianic passage of Isa. 11:1–10 the coming of Messiah is foretold, and of Him it is said that, literally, “his abiding shall be glorious.” According to Ps. 85:9, 10, the day of salvation would bring again the “glory” of God to “dwell” in the land, and at that time “mercy [or grace, Heb. chesed, see Additional Note on Psalm 36] and truth [Heb. ’emeth, “faithfulness,” “trustworthiness”]” would meet together (see DA 762). The same two words, chesed and ’emeth, “merciful” and “gracious” are linked together in the proclamation of the “name” of the Lord, when Moses was allowed to behold His “glory [Heb. chabod]” (see on Ex. 33:22; 34:6). These and other Messianic passages of the OT find a very close parallel here in John 1:14, where, at the incarnation, glory that could have come only from the presence of the Father was manifested in the incarnate Word and “dwelt among us,” “full of grace [mercy] and truth.”
Every major aspect of Christ’s life played an important part in the work of salvation. His virgin birth reunited the estranged families of earth and heaven. He brought Deity down to earth in order that He might bear humanity with Him back to heaven. His perfect life as a man provides us with an example of obedience (John 15:10; 1 John 2:6) and sanctification (John 17:19); as God, He imparts to us power to obey (Rom. 8:3, 4). His vicarious death made it possible for us to enjoy a period of probation (CS 137) and for Him to justify “many” (Isa. 53:5, 11; Rom. 5:9; Titus 2:14). By faith in His death we are made free from the guilt of sin, and by faith in His life, from its power (Rom. 5:1, 10; Phil. 4:7). His glorious resurrection assures us that one day we too shall “put on” immortality (1 Cor. 15:12–22, 51–55). His ascension confirms His promise to return and take us with Him to meet the Father (John 14:1–3; Acts 1:9–11), and thereby complete the work of saving “his people.” These five aspects of Christ’s mission to earth were all the subject of prophecy (Isa. 9:6, 7; 53; 61:1–3; Ps. 68:18).
14.zh:
道成了肉身，住在我們中間，充充滿滿的有恩典有真理。我們也見過他的榮光，正是父獨生子的榮光。

**道成了肉身。**人類有限的智力無法充分理解無限的慈愛，智慧和能力。保羅說，上帝在肉身顯現乃是極大的奧秘（提前3:16）。如果探索人類的智力所無法明白的奧秘，那就超越了聖靈所啟示的範圍。見約6:51；16:28註釋。
約翰已經肯定了基督真實的神性（見第1節註釋），現在他又肯定祂真實的人性。基督的神性是絕對意義上的神性。祂的人性也是絕對意義上的人性，只不過祂是“無罪的（“無罪”原文作“不知罪”）”（林後5:21）。聖經一再強調這個基本真理（見路1:35；羅1:3；8:3；加4:4；腓2:6-8；西2:9；提前3:16；來1:2,8；2:14-18；10:5；約壹1:2等；見腓2:6-8；西2:9註釋）。基督“本有上帝的形像”，但祂“不以自己與上帝同等為強奪的，反倒虛己”，“成為人的樣式”，“有人的樣子”（腓2:6-8）。“上帝本性一切的豐盛，都有形有體地居住在基督裡面”（西2:9）；但“祂凡事該與祂的弟兄相同”（來2:17）。“從亙古、從太初主耶穌基督與父原為一，”然而祂“卻選擇將王權交還父手，從祂宇宙君王的寶座上走下來，”為了“住在我們中間，使我們熟悉祂神聖的品格與生活”（《歷代願望》19，22，23頁）。
神性和人性奇妙地結合在一起。神性披上了人性，而不是換成了人性。基督降世為人時，祂依然是神。神人兩性密不可分，但又保持各自的特性。人性沒有換成神性；神性也沒有換成人性。見本章補充註釋；見太1:1；路1:35；腓2:6-8；來2:14-17註釋；見約1:1-3,14；可16:6；腓2:6-8；西2:9；來2:14-17的懷愛倫註釋。
基督“承受了人性的軟弱”（懷愛倫，載《時兆》1905年8月2日），但祂的人性依然是“完全的”（《歷代願望》664頁）。祂作為一個人雖然有可能犯罪，但祂身上絲毫沒有敗壞的汙點。祂根本沒有犯罪的傾向（《懷愛倫信函》1895年第8號，見本卷註釋1128頁）。祂凡事“受過試探，與我們一樣，只是祂沒有犯罪”（見來4:15註釋）。見本章補充註釋。
**住。**skēnoō。直譯是“支搭帳篷”在我們中間（參《歷代願望》23頁）。基督成為我們的一分子，是為了更好地顯示天父的慈愛，體驗我們的感受，為我們樹立榜樣，在我們受試探時幫助我們，在父面前作我們的代表（見來2:14-17註釋）。這位始終與父同在的永生之道（見約1:1註釋），現在又成為以馬內利——“上帝與我們同在”（見太1:23註釋）。
**充充滿滿地。**顯然指成為肉身的道。道成了肉身住在我們中間，“充充滿滿地有恩典有真理”。
**有恩典有真理。**charis kai alētheia。Charis在本節指“善意”，“慈愛”，“（本不配得的）恩典”和“憐憫”。 Alētheia指父上帝在救恩計劃和道成肉身的基督身上所顯示對罪人之愛的“真理”。 這裡的charis相當於希伯來語中的chesed（見《詩篇》第36篇補充註釋；見伯10:12註釋）；alētheia相當於希伯來語中的'emeth（“誠實”，“可靠”）。“慈愛”和“誠實”一同出現顯然是指彌賽亞的《舊約》《詩篇》85:10,11中。基督來，就是為了顯示上帝的這些品性。基督在世上，“充充滿滿地有恩典有真理”，故能完全徹底地將天父彰顯出來。上帝永遠對自己的品格誠實。祂的品格最充分地表現在祂的慈愛或恩典上。
在基督道成為肉身的一千五百年以前，上帝指示以色列人為祂建造“聖所”即會幕，好讓祂“住在他們中間”（出25:8）。正如在過去，上帝的同在是以約櫃施恩座上方等處的榮光（Shekinah）為象徵的（見創3:24；出13:21註釋），現在，這榮光則顯現在耶穌身上。約翰和其他門徒都是目擊的證人。對於他們來說，這是無可爭辯的證據，證明耶穌是從天上父那裡來的。這樣的榮光沒有別的來源。
值得注意的是，希伯來語中的mishkan（“住所”，“帳篷”，“會幕”）和Shekinah（“上帝榮光”）都來自shakan（“居住”）。在希臘語中，skēnē（“帳篷”，“會幕”）和skēnoō（“住帳篷”，“居住”）也很相近。過去上帝的榮光停留在會幕裡，就是祂的選民中間；現在約翰說，這位榮耀的上帝藉著我們主救主耶穌基督，住在祂的子民中間。有人認為保羅在羅9:4所說的“榮耀”就是上帝的榮光（Shekinah），可能也就是耶穌登山變像時所出現的“光明的雲彩”（太17:5）。賽11:1-10有關彌賽亞的經文顯然已經預言了彌賽亞的來臨。經上說“祂安息之所大有榮耀”。詩85:9,10說，在救恩的日子裡，上帝的“榮耀”將再次“住在”地上。那時“慈愛”（chesed，或“恩典”，見《詩篇》36篇補充註釋）與“誠實”（'emeth，或“真理”）將彼此相遇（見《歷代願望》762頁）。摩西當年蒙準瞻仰上帝的“榮耀（chabod）”，上帝在宣告祂的名時，也把chesed和'emeth（“憐憫”，“恩典”）這兩個詞用在一起（見出33:22；34:6註釋）。《舊約》的這些經文和其他有關彌賽亞的經文同約1:14十分相似。約翰說，那隻能來自聖父的榮光，顯在成為肉身的道身上，“住在我們中間，充充滿滿地有恩典（“慈愛”）有真理”。
基督生活的每一個主要方面，都在救恩的工作中發揮重要的作用。祂由童女所生，把疏遠了的天上家庭和地上家庭重新連接起來。祂把神性帶到地上，以便把人性帶到天上。祂作為人完全的生活為我們樹立了順從（約15:10；約壹2:6）和成聖（約17:19）的榜樣。祂作為神，賜給我們順從的力量（羅8:3,4）。祂為我們受死，使我們能享有一段寬容的時期（《論管家》137頁），並使祂能稱“許多人”為義（賽53:5,11；羅5:9；多2:14）。我們藉著相信祂的死，得以脫離罪的感覺；藉著相信祂的生，得以脫離罪的權勢（羅5:1,10；腓4:7）。祂榮耀的復活向我們保證，有一天我們也要“變成”不朽壞的（林前15:12-22,51-55）。祂的昇天確認了祂必回來接我們到天父那裡去的應許（約14:1-3；徒1:9-11），從而完成救贖“祂百姓”的工作。基督到地上來的這五個方面使命，聖經都有預言（賽9:6,7；53；61:1-3；詩68:18）。
**榮光。**doxa，相當於希伯來語的kabod，在《舊約》中表示象徵上帝臨格的榮光（見創3:24；出13:21註釋；參撒上4:22）。七十士譯本有177次把kabod譯成doxa 。約翰和其他門徒都是“道成了肉身”（約1:14；見約21:24；約壹1:1,2）這一歷史事實的目擊證人。約翰在這裡無疑想到了一些特殊的經歷，如耶穌登山變像時，神性頃刻間透過人性閃耀出來。彼得也說自己“親眼見過”基督變像時的“威榮”和“極大榮光”（彼後1:16-18）。彼得還說，伴隨著那榮光的，有上帝的宣告：“這是我的愛子。”關於耶穌生平中天上的榮光顯在祂面上的各種場合，見路2:48註釋。耶穌在約17:5中向天父禱告說：“求你使我同你享榮耀，就是未有世界以先，我同你所有的榮耀。”基督教信仰所依據的事實是，上帝的“榮光”降在拿撒勒人耶穌這個歷史人物身上。約翰還可能想到了救主所表現出來的完美品格（見上面“有恩典有真理”註釋）。
父…..的。para theou，直譯是“與父在一起”或“在父旁邊”，在本節可能指“來自父身邊”。希臘語介詞para有時含有ek（“來自”）的意思，與本節經文相符。成為肉身的道從父面前來到世間。見約6:46註釋
**獨生子。**monogenēs，源於表示“唯一”和“種類”的兩個詞，故應譯為“獨一的”，“唯一的”，“某類中唯一的”。就像“道”（Logos）一樣（見約1:1），只有約翰用monogenēs指基督（見約1:18；3:16,18；約壹4:9註釋）。Monogenēs前面沒有加定冠詞，既能理解為“唯一的那一位”，也能理解為一種屬性，意為“來自父身邊那位唯一者的榮光。”本節顯然是這樣的意思。見路7:12；8:42註釋。這兩處的monogenēs均譯為“獨生的”。
來11:17用monogenēs表示以撒。其實以撒並不是亞伯拉罕“獨生的兒子”，甚至連長子都不是。但以撒是應許之子，註定享有繼承他父親產業的長子權（創25:1-6；加4:22,23）。“同樣，在約翰稱基督為“獨生子”的五處經文裡，均應理解為以下含義中的一種：‘唯一的’，‘寶貴的’，‘單獨的’，‘這類中唯一的’，而不要理解為‘獨生’”（ 《聖經翻譯問題》198頁）。
本節和其他地方“獨生”的譯法顯然源於天主教早期的教父，在天主教官方的聖經版本拉丁文武加大譯本的影響下進入早期的英文譯本。其實好幾個早於武加大譯本拉丁文譯本都是“唯一的”，而不是“獨生的”，準確地反映了希臘文的意思。基督“在創造萬有之前為父所生”的觀點最早出現在公元前230年奧利金的著作中。大約一個世紀之後，阿里烏在提到基督時第一次使用希臘詞語gegennemenon(“生”)，強調，基督是“上帝在萬古以先所生的”（見本章補充註釋）。這個希臘詞語在聖經中從未用來指成為肉身之前的基督。說基督是天父在萬古之先某一時間所“生”的觀點完全不符合聖經。關於這個問題，詳見《聖經翻譯問題》第197-204頁。
要正確理解基督作為上帝兒子的獨特地位。monogenēs將基督和那些因信祂而獲得“權柄作上帝的兒女”（第12節），就是特別宣佈為“上帝生的”（第13節）的人區別開來。基督過去，現在，直到永遠都是“上帝”（見第1節註釋）。所以我們接受基督且相信祂名的時候，就“成為上帝的兒子”。
第14節顯然是涉及道成肉身，其目的是強調成為肉身的道保留著神性，就像成為肉身之前所顯明的上帝榮耀所證明的（見約17:5）。雖然monogenēs嚴格地來說是“唯一的”，“獨一的”，而不是“獨生的”，但約翰在這裡用它來表達基督道“成了肉身”，住在我們中間的時候。保羅在來1:5,6中肯定了這種用法。他將gegenneka（“我……生”，源於gennaō，“生”）和prōtotoktos（“長子”，源於pro，“在…..之前”和tiktō，“生”）以及“上帝使長子到世上來的時候”連繫在一起。因此把monogenēs理解為“道”在萬古之先某一時刻的神秘出生是完全沒有根據的。關於基督為上帝的兒子，見路1:35註釋；關於基督作為人子，見太1:1；可2:10註釋；又見腓2:6-8；西2:9懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第472，520，544頁；《給管家的勉言》第136頁；《基督教育之研究》第259頁；《歷代願望》第23，139，387，507頁；《教育論》第28頁；《基督教育原理》第378，382，400，444頁；《善惡之爭》第六章；《醫療佈道論》第321頁；《先祖與先知》第278頁；《給傳道人的證言》第63頁；《證言》卷五第576，747頁；《證言》卷六第59頁；《證言》卷七第20頁；《證言》卷八第207，286頁；《證言》卷九第228頁；《論福利工作》第53頁。

4.zh:
生命在他裡頭，這生命就是人的光。

**生命。**zōē，指所有生物所擁有的生命原則，與死亡相對應。約翰在這裡顯然也想到了屬靈的生命，特別是人因接受和相信基督而獲得的永生（見第12節）。人因罪而與生命的源泉隔絕，成為死亡的俘虜，但藉著耶穌基督我們重新獲得永生的盼望（羅5:12,18；6:23），以及亞當因犯罪而喪失的一切。見約10:10；11:25；14:6。“生命在基督裡面。這生命是祂本來擁有的，不是借來或源於他處的”（《歷代願望》530頁）。
**人的光。**原文“生命”和“光”前面有定冠詞，所以“光”和“生命”是同等的。屬靈的黑暗長期籠罩人的心靈，但現在上帝生命和完全的“真光”（第9節）照亮了每一個人的道路（參賽9:1,2）。不僅天上的光藉著基督照耀出來，祂自己就是那光（約1:9）。約翰一再稱耶穌為真光（見約8:12；9:5；12:35,46；參約壹1:5,6；2:8）。光一直就是上帝臨格的象徵（見創3:24節註釋）。上帝創造的第一步就是使光普照世界（創1:3）。同樣，當上帝啟動在人身上恢復祂形象的工作時，祂也先用祂慈愛的光照耀他們的心靈（林後4:6）。詩人說：“在你那裡有生命的源頭；在你的光中，我們必得見光”（詩36:9）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第270，465頁；《教育論》第28頁；《福山寶訓》第39頁；《服務真詮》第461頁；《拾級就主》第19頁；《證言》卷八第288，324頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《歷代願望》第464頁；《給傳道人的證言》第365頁。
4.en:
**Life.** Gr. zōē, the life principle shared by all living things, the antithesis of death. John evidently thinks also of spiritual life and, more particularly, of everlasting life, to which the one who receives Christ and believes in Him is given access (see v. 12). Through sin man separated himself from the source of life, and therefore became subject to death, but the prospect of eternal life was restored through Jesus Christ (Rom. 5:12, 18; 6:23), and with it all that Adam lost through transgression. See John 10:10; 11:25; 14:6. “In Christ is life, original, unborrowed, underived” (DA 530).
**The light of men.** In Greek the definite article preceding both “life” and “light” equates “light” with “life.” Spiritual darkness had long shrouded men’s souls, but the “true Light” (v. 9) of divine life and perfection now shines forth to illumine the pathway of every man (cf. Isa. 9:1, 2). Not only does the light of Heaven shine forth through Christ, He is that light (John 1:9). Again and again John quotes Jesus to this effect (see John 8:12; 9:5; 12:35, 46; cf. 1 John 1:5, 6; 2:8). Light has ever been a symbol of the divine presence (see on Gen. 3:24). As the first act of creation God flooded the world with light (Gen. 1:3), so when God sets about the work of recreating His image in the souls of men He first illumines their hearts and minds with the light of divine love (2 Cor. 4:6). “With thee,” says the psalmist, “is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light” (Ps. 36:9).

5.zh:
光照在黑暗裡，黑暗卻不接受光。

**光。**就是成為肉身的道所彰顯上帝的光（見第4節註釋）。
**黑暗。**指道德上罪惡的黑暗，心靈中不認識上帝慈愛與憐憫，以及死亡之絕望前景的黑暗（見弗2:12）。生命的光來到世界上，就是要驅散這層黑暗（見林後4:6）。
**接受。**katalambanō，“理解，”“抓住，”指用手抓住，喻指領悟。Katalambanō在徒10:34；25:25；弗3:18節意為“看出”，“查明”，“明白”。但它更多是指“捉住，”“帶，”“臨到”等，如在可9:18；約8:3,4；12:35；帖前5:4等處。“接受”一詞，這兩層意思都有。英文RSV版把它譯為“overcome”（“勝過”），表達了光明戰勝黑暗、真理戰勝邪惡的意思（參見弗6:12；西2:15）。這種譯法可能是受現代派的影響。他們認為《約翰福音》反映了密特拉派和艾賽尼派的二元論觀點（見本卷註釋第54,92頁）。但“接受”的譯法符合約1:9-12的思路。約翰把人心中的黑暗擬人化了，說它既不理解也不接受生命的光（約3:19；《歷代願望》80頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第116頁；《歷代願望》第80，470頁；《基督教育原理》第167頁；《證言》卷一第406頁。
5.en:
**The light.** That is, the light of divine love manifested in the incarnate Word (see on v. 4).
