**Darkness.** That is, the moral darkness of sin, the mental darkness of ignorance concerning the love and mercy of God and the hopeless prospect of death (see Eph. 2:12). It was to dispel this pall of darkness that the Light of life came into the world (see 2 Cor. 4:6).
**Comprehended.** Gr. katalambanō, “to apprehend,” “to seize,” “to comprehend,” whether literally with the hands or figuratively with the mind. Katalambanō is used in the sense of “perceive” or “comprehend” in Acts 10:34; 25:25; Eph. 3:18, but more often in the sense of “take,” “overtake,” or “seize” in Mark 9:18; John 8:3, 4; 12:35; 1 Thess. 5:4; etc. The English word “apprehend” reflects both shades of meaning. The translation “overcome” (RSV) conveys the idea of good triumphant over evil (cf. Eph. 6:12; Col. 2:15). This translation was possibly influenced by the modernist concept that the Gospel of John reflects the dualism of Mithraism and the Essenes (see pp. 54, 92). However, the development of thought in John 1:9–12 favors the translation “comprehend,” in the sense that the personified darkness of men’s souls neither understood nor appreciated the Light of life (ch. 3:19; cf. DA 80).

6.zh:
有一個人，是從神那裡差來的，名叫約翰。

**從上帝那裡差來的。**使徒用這句話強調施洗約翰關於彌賽亞的見證是來自上帝的（見約1:23註釋；參摩7:14,15；約4:34註釋）。
**約翰。**就是施洗約翰。使徒約翰從來不提自己的名字。見太3:1-12；路3:1-18註釋。關於“約翰”一名的意思，見路1:13註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷三第61頁。
6.en:
**Sent from God.** In these dramatic words the evangelist affirms the divine origin of the Baptist’s witness concerning the Messiah (see on John 1:23; cf. on Amos 7:14, 15; John 4:34).
**John.** That is, John the Baptist. John the evangelist never refers to himself by name. See on Matt. 3:1–12; Luke 3:1–18. For the meaning of the name see on Luke 1:13.

7.zh:
這人來，為要作見證，就是為光作見證，叫眾人因他可以信。

**作見證。**人類普遍處於屬靈的盲目中，故忽略和拒絕天上的光（第10,26節）。但施洗約翰的屬靈眼光使他認出了彌賽亞（第32-34節）。參賽6:9；林後4:4；啟3:17,18。
**光。**phōs，就是光的源頭。根據上下文，這裡的光就是基督。第4節稱祂為光（見第4,5節註釋）。
**信。**該詞在《約翰福音》中出現一百多次，強調積極回應上帝聲音的重要性。
7.en:
**Bear witness.** In their state of spiritual blindness men in general were oblivious to the light and not receptive of it (vs. 10, 26). His spiritual perception, however, led John to recognize the Messiah (vs. 32–34). Compare Isa. 6:9; 2 Cor. 4:4; Rev. 3:17, 18.
**Light.** Gr. phōs, a source of light. As the context makes evident, Christ is here said to be the light, as in v. 4 He is said to be the bearer of light (see on vs. 4, 5).
**Believe.** This word appears in the Gospel of John more than 100 times, stressing the vital importance of a positive response to the voice of God.

8.zh:
他不是那光，乃是要為光作見證。

**他不是那光。**見第20節註釋。
8.en: **He was not that Light.** See on v. 20.

9.zh:
那光是真光，照亮一切生在世上的人。

**真光。**凡不出於耶穌基督的所謂“亮光”都是虛假的（參賽50:11；雅1:17）。但約翰這裡所用的“真”不一定是與“假”相對應，認為其他所有的光都是虛假或誤導人的，因為基督後來說到施洗約翰是“點著的明燈”（ 約5:35；luchnos，“燈”，而不是 phōs，“光”，見第7節註釋）。但使徒約翰說施洗約翰不是他這裡所說的“那光” （約1:8）。施洗約翰與基督不是真假之分，而是局部與整體之分（見林前13:10）。可以把約翰的見證比作金星或天狼星（見賽14:12註釋）的光輝。但耶穌裡面的真光卻如正午耀眼的陽光（見瑪4:2；彼後1:19）。約翰還說耶穌是“真糧”（約6:32），“真葡萄樹”（約15:1），真正的“門”（約10:7-9）和真理本身（約14:6）。
**照亮一切生在世上的人。**不是說世上所有的人都一定被這光所照亮，而是說人要得到光照，就必須依靠這光（參約6:68；徒4:12）。人類所有的光都是來自基督（《歷代願望》464，465頁）。真光照亮一切世人的含義，就像耶穌為所有的人死，但並不意味著世人都認識祂，都能得救一樣。約翰在這裡所指的，並不是所有的人，包括聖徒，罪人和外邦人心中的微光，而是關於耶穌基督救恩知識的亮光（《歷代願望》317頁）。約翰在第10-12節中說明，就一般的情況而論，“世界卻不認識祂”，“自己的人倒不接待祂”。這些人自然沒有被“真光”多照亮。約翰接著補充說，他所指的是“凡接待祂的”人，就是信祂名的人（第12節；參《歷代願望》317頁）。
**生。**原文既可指“每一個人”，也可指“真光”。約3:19說“光來到世間”。在約5:43；7:28；10:10；16:28；18:37（參見1:31；6:14；11:27）中，耶穌說自己不是作為伯利恆的嬰兒，而是作為彌賽亞來到世界的。在約12:46中，耶穌說：“我到世上來，乃是光。”
約翰在約1:10中說到真光基督“在世界”。難道他在第9節不會說基督來到這個世界嗎？有人認為，如果“生在世上”是指“一切……人”的話，就顯得累贅，但如果是指“真光”，那就補充了句子的意義，為14節宣佈“道成了肉身”預備了道路。但現有的行文也是完全符合語法的。
**世上。**kosmos，根據上下文，是指 “世界”（見太4:8註釋）。該詞約翰使用了八十來次，而其他三卷同觀福音裡中一共只用了十五次。它指人類的世界，特別是那些反對上帝和真理的人。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第385頁；《基督教育之研究》第28，361，530頁；《歷代願望》第317，464頁；《教育論》第14，29，134頁；《基督教育原理》第181，183，405，427，440，468，470頁；《善惡之爭》第262，461，528頁；《傳道良助》第50頁；《先知與君王》第253，377頁；《拾級就主》第24頁；《給傳道人的證言》第419頁；《證言》卷八第256頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–12節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第365頁。
9.en:
**The true Light.** All other so-called “light” than that which originates with Jesus Christ is false (cf. Isa. 50:11; James 1:17). However it is probable that John does not here use the word “true” in contradistinction to “false,” implying that all other lights are false and misleading, for Christ later spoke of John the Baptist as “a burning and a shining light [Gr. luchnos, “lamp,” “light bearer,” in contradistinction to phōs, the light itself, see on v. 7]” (ch. 5:35). But John the apostle denies (ch. 1:8) that John the Baptist was “that Light” of which he here speaks. The difference between John the Baptist and Jesus was not the difference between false and true, but between partial and complete (see 1 Cor. 13:10). The witness of John might be likened to the brilliance of the planet Venus, or to that of Sirius (see on Isa. 14:12), but in Jesus the light of truth blazed forth like the noonday sun (see on Mal. 4:2; 2 Peter 1:19). John also sets Jesus forth as the “true bread” (ch. 6:32), the “true vine” (ch. 15:1), the true “door” (ch. 10:7–9), and as truth itself (ch. 14:6).
**Lighteth every man.** This does not mean that all men are necessarily illuminated by the light, but that if men are illuminated at all it must be by means of this light (cf. John 6:68; Acts 4:12). All the light that men have comes from Christ (DA 464, 465). The true light shines upon all men in the same sense that Jesus died for all men, but this does not mean that all men know about Him or that they will be saved. John here refers, not to a vague spark of light resident in the souls of all men, saints, sinners, and heathen alike, but to the light of a saving knowledge of Jesus Christ (see DA 317). John makes clear in vs. 10–12 that, for the most part, “the world knew him not” and “his own received him not.” These, then, were not illuminated by the “true Light.” As John hastens to add, it is only “as many as received him” and believed in Him who are here particularly designated (v. 12; cf. DA 317).
**That cometh.** In the Greek this clause may refer either to “every man” (KJV) or to “the true light” (RSV). In ch. 3:19 light is again referred to as coming into the world. In chs. 5:43; 7:28; 10:10; 16:28; 18:37 (cf. chs. 1:31; 6:14; 11:27) Jesus refers to His own coming, not as a babe in Bethlehem, but in His role as the Messiah. In ch. 12:46 Jesus says, “I am come a light into the world.”
In ch. 1:10, John states that Christ, “the true Light,” was in the world. Would it not be appropriate for him to mention His coming into the world in the preceding verse? Some have suggested that if the clause, “that cometh into the world,” refers to “every man,” it would be redundant, whereas if it refers to “the true Light,” it would seem to add meaning to the statement and prepare the way for the incarnation declaration of v. 14. However, the KJV reading is fully as valid grammatically.
**The world.** Gr. kosmos, generally the “world” from the viewpoint of its harmonious arrangement (see on Matt. 4:8). John uses kosmos some 80 times, as compared with only 15 in the three Synoptics, and by it designates the world of men, particularly those who oppose God and truth.

11.zh:
他到自己的地方來，自己的人倒不接待他。

**自己的。**ta idia（見約16:32；19:27；徒21:6；見約1:1-3,14懷愛倫補充註釋）。不大可能直接針對耶穌在自己的故鄉拿撒勒遭到拒絕的事，而是泛指選民“以色列家”（太10:6；15:24；參出19:5；申7:6）。本節第二個“自己的”（ hoi idioi）是以複數形式出現，指“祂自己的百姓”。竟然耶穌自己的弟兄（約7:3-5）和同鄉（路4:28,29）都不承認祂的彌賽亞的身份，但約翰在這裡可能是指 “以色列家”中的成員，特別是它的領袖們。他們是“以色列家迷失的羊”（太15:24）。
**不接待祂。**《約翰福音》有時被稱為“被拒絕的福音”，因為它比其他福音書更充分地追溯了以色列的領袖們拒絕彌賽亞的過程（見約3:11；5:43；6:66；8:13；9:29；10:25；12:37,42；19:15等）。然而各地確實都有誠心的人 “接待祂”（約1:12；見約2:11；3:2；4:29,39,42,53； 6:14；7:31,40,41,43；8:30；10:19,42；11:45等）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第116頁；《對作者和編輯的勉言》第45頁；《歷代願望》第27頁；《先知與君王》第710頁；《證言》卷九第229頁。
11.en:
**His own.** Gr. ta idia, an idiomatic expression here meaning “his own [home]” (see John 16:32; 19:27; Acts 21:6; EGW Supplementary Material on John 1:1–3, 14). This is probably not a direct allusion to Jesus’ rejection at Nazareth, His literal “home,” but to “the house of Israel” collectively (Matt. 10:6; 15:24; cf. Ex. 19:5; Deut. 7:6), the chosen nation. The second occurrence of the expression “his own,” hoi idioi, is in the plural, meaning “his own [people].” Although Jesus’ own brothers (John 7:3–5) and fellow townsmen (Luke 4:28, 29) denied His Messiahship, John here probably refers to the members of “the house of Israel” individually, and particularly to its leaders. These were “the lost sheep of the house of Israel” (Matt. 15:24).
**Received him not.** The Fourth Gospel is sometimes called the Gospel of Rejection because it traces more fully than do the other Gospels the process by which the leaders of Israel rejected the Messiah (see chs. 3:11; 5:43; 6:66; 8:13; 9:29; 10:25; 12:37, 42; 19:15; etc.). To be sure, many sincere hearts here and there “received him” (ch. 1:12; see chs. 2:11; 3:2; 4:29, 39, 42, 53; 6:14; 7:31, 40, 41, 43; 8:30; 10:19, 42; 11:45; etc.).

12.zh:
凡接待他的，就是信他名的人，他就賜他們權柄，作神的兒女。

**凡接待祂的。**耶穌不單是義人或先知。祂是上帝的兒子，是上帝所差來的，是彌賽亞。約翰在這裡否定了那種認為僅靠基督為眾人死，眾人都會得救的觀點。也否定了上帝預定一些人得救，另一些人滅亡的信念。他強調決定的因素在於人自己。“凡”接待相信祂的人，都有權作祂的兒女。關於預定論，詳見賽55:1；弗1:5；啟22:17註釋。
**信祂名的人。**見第7節註釋。
**祂名。**相信一個人不等於相信他的名。相信一個人也許只是相信他所說的話。魔鬼也信有上帝（雅2:19），但這與相信“上帝的名”完全不同。相信上帝的存在只涉及智力，而相信上帝的名卻涉及道德和靈性。信基督的名就是接受基督耶穌救恩的安排。“信心是上帝樂意赦免罪人的條件；信心並無賺取救恩的任何功勞。但信心卻可以握住基督的功勞。這是為解決罪的問題而預備的方法”（《評論與通訊》懷愛倫1890年11月4日）。
這裡的“名”按亞蘭語慣意義，是指祂自己。
**權柄。**exousia，“權威，”“權利，”“選擇權”，不是一般意義上的dunamis（“權力”）。 exousia在約5:27中亦譯為“權柄”。人因罪而喪失了他的權柄，該受死刑的懲罰。救贖的計劃恢復了人認識上帝和選擇侍奉祂的機會。
**作。**上帝並不強迫人作祂的兒女。但如果他們願意，祂就賜給他們權柄作祂的兒女。
**上帝的兒女。**約翰喜歡用這樣的稱呼（見約11:52；約壹3:1,2,10；5:2）。約翰在希臘文中提到基督徒時從來不用“上帝的兒女”。成為上帝的兒女（約3:3），就是通過重生而與上帝立約（見何1:10註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第381頁；《復臨信徒家庭》第36頁；《天路》第314頁；《基督教育之研究》第14頁；《歷代願望》第464頁；《佈道論》第308頁；《基督教育原理》第405頁；《傳道良助》第50頁；《今日的生活》第176頁；《服務真詮》第421頁；《醫療佈道論》第113頁；《給傳道人的證言》第94，221，283，485頁；《證言》卷六第60，363，372頁；《證言》卷七第39頁；《證言》卷八第102，177，207，267頁；《證言》卷九第23，141，152，218，287頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《歷代願望》第509頁；《佈道論》第531頁；見林後5：17懷愛倫註釋。
12.en:
**As many as received.** Not merely as a good man or even as a prophet, but as the Son of God, the Sent of God, the Messiah. John here brands as error the belief that simply because Christ died for all men, all will therefore be saved. Marked equally false is the belief that God predestines certain men to be saved and others to be damned. John emphatically declares that the decisive factor lies with men themselves—“as many” as receive and believe are granted access to sonship. Concerning predestination see further on Isa. 55:1; Eph. 1:5; Rev. 22:17.
**Power.** Gr. exousia, “authority,” “right,” “power of choice,” not dunamis, “power” in the usual sense. In ch. 5:27 exousia is rightly translated “authority.” Because of sin man had lost all his rights and deserved the penalty of death. The plan of salvation restored man’s opportunity to know God and to choose to serve Him.
**To become.** God does not arbitrarily make men His sons; He enables them to become such if they so choose.
**Sons of God.** Literally, “children of God,” which expression is a favorite with John (see John 11:52; 1 John 3:1, 2, 10; 5:2), who never, in the Greek, uses “sons of God” when referring to Christians. To become a son, or child, of God is to enter into the covenant relationship (see on Hosea 1:10) by the new birth (John 3:3).
**Them that believe.** See on v. 7.
**On his name.** To believe on the name of another is not equivalent to believing him. The latter may simply mean that one gives credence to the words of another. The devils give credence to the fact that there is one God (James 2:19), but this is a very different experience from believing “on the name of God.” The former is an intellectual act; the latter a moral and spiritual one. To believe on the name of Christ is to appropriate the provisions of salvation in Christ Jesus. “Faith is the condition upon which God has seen fit to promise pardon to sinners; not that there is any virtue in faith whereby salvation is merited, but faith can lay hold of the merits of Christ, the remedy provided for sin” (EGW RH Nov. 4, 1890).
The word “name” is here used in an Aramaic idiomatic sense, meaning the person himself.

13.zh:
這等人不是從血氣生的，不是從情慾生的，也不是從人意生的，乃是從神生的。

**生。**見約3:3-8註釋。
**不是從血氣生的。**即不是從肉身生的。
**情慾。**可能指性慾。
**人。**anēr，“男子”，這裡可能是指生兒育女的願望。
**從上帝生的。**約翰所說的“生”與人的動機和計劃無關。它與肉身的出生相似之處，只在於兩者都標誌著新生命的開始（見約3:3-8；羅6:3-5註釋）。但它的成就不是靠人的開創和行為。這完全是一種再造，單依靠上帝自己的旨意和作為。上帝在我們心裡運行，使我們“立志行事……成就祂的美意”（腓2:13）。在悔改的問題上，約翰並不排除人的自由選擇權（見第12節註釋），也不否認人神合作的需要。他只是強調其開創和動力都是出於上帝的。
13.en:
**Born.** See on ch. 3:3–8.
**Not of Blood.** That is, not by physical birth.
**Will of the flesh.** Perhaps sexual desire.
**Man.** Gr. anēr, “a male,” probably here a reference to the desire for posterity.
**Of God.** Human motives and human planning play no part in the birth of which John speaks. It resembles physical birth only in the sense that both mark the beginning of new life (see on John 3:3–8; Rom. 6:3–5). It is not accomplished through human initiative and action, but is altogether a new creation, wholly dependent upon the will and action of God Himself. He it is who works in us “both to will and to do of his good pleasure” (Phil. 2:13). John does not exclude the free choice of man with respect to conversion (see on v. 12), nor does he deny the need for human cooperation with divine agencies. He simply affirms that the initiative and the power are God’s.

15.zh:
約翰為他作見證，喊著說：這就是我曾說：那在我以後來的，反成了在我以前的，因他本來在我以前。

**約翰為祂作見證。**施洗約翰為道殉身已有半個多世紀了，但他為基督所作的見證依然在迴響著。他像亞伯一樣，“雖然死了……仍舊說話”（來11:4）。見約1:19-36；3:27-36；見太3:11,12；路3:15註釋。
**這就是。**施洗約翰說耶穌是他從一開始傳道就宣揚的那一位（見第27,30節）。
**在我以後。**就時間而論。這裡的“以後”，不是指門徒們在耶穌“後面”的“跟隨”（見太10:37,38註釋）。
**反成了。**約翰從來沒有懷疑彌賽亞的崇高地位和尊嚴。見約3:28-31。
**在我以前。**emprosthen mou，即“在我前面”，是指地位而言。
**祂本來在我以前。**這裡是指時間。約翰本句的“以前”用的是opisō，而在上面句子裡他用的是emprosthen。鑑於約翰比耶穌大六個月，這裡顯然是指道成肉身之前的耶穌。
一些翻譯者和解經家認為第15節是插入的，中斷了14節與16節的思路。然而使徒在這裡插入施洗約翰的見證，是為了肯定第14節門徒所作有關基督崇高地位和祂自古就存在的見證。我們主自己的話反映了早期教會對施洗約翰見證的重視（見約5:32-36；參太11:11）。
15.en:
**John bare witness.** Literally, “John bears witness,” or “John testifies.” More than a half a century had passed since the martyrdom of John the Baptist, but his witness to the Christ echoed on down the years. It was true of him as it was of Abel, that “he being dead yet speaketh” (Heb. 11:4). See John 1:19–36; 3:27–36; see on Matt. 3:11, 12; Luke 3:15.
**This was he.** The Baptist identifies Jesus as the one of whom he had spoken since the beginning of his ministry (see vs. 27, 30).
**After me.** That is, in point of time. Jesus did not come “after” John in the sense that the disciples, as learners, followed “after” Jesus (see on Matt. 10:37, 38).
**Is preferred.** Literally, “is become,” or here, “takes precedence.” John never questioned the superior rank and dignity of the Messiah. See ch. 3:28–31.
**Before me.** Gr. emprosthen mou, “in front of me,” that is, in relative greatness.
**He was before me.** That is, in point of time. Here, for the word “before” John uses opisō, whereas in the preceding clause he uses emprosthen. In view of the fact that John was about six months older than Jesus, reference here is clearly to Jesus’ preincarnate existence.
Some translators and commentators consider v. 15 an interpolation that interrupts the line of though between vs. 14, 16. However, the apostle manifestly introduces the testimony of the Baptist at this point to confirm that of the disciples already mentioned in v. 14, as to Christ’s exalted position and pre-existence. The importance attached by the early church to the witness of John the Baptist reflects the express statements of our Lord Himself (see John 5:32–36; cf. Matt. 11:11).

16.zh:
從他豐滿的恩典裡，我們都領受了，而且恩上加恩。

**祂豐滿的恩典。**見約1:14註釋；參西1:19；2:9；弗3:19；4:13。
**恩上加恩。**每一位真信徒都要天天到天國的倉庫裡領受上帝豐富的恩典，以滿足當日的需要。他每天都在恩典和上帝為他人生所定旨意的知識上有長進（參彼後3:18）。他穩定地朝著完美品格的目標前進（見太5:48）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第521，544頁；《歷代願望》第250頁；《基督教育原理》第338，362頁；《福山寶訓》第21頁；《給傳道人的證言》第94，205頁；《證言》卷七第20頁；《證言》卷八第207，286頁；見西2：9，10懷愛倫註釋。
16.en:
**His fulness.** See on John 1:14; cf. Col. 1:19; 2:9; EPH 3:19; 4:13.
**Grace for grace.** Probably meaning, “grace added to grace.” Day by day every true believer goes to the heavenly storehouse for divine grace sufficient to meet the needs of the day. Daily he grows in grace and in understanding God’s purpose for his life (cf. 2 Peter 3:18). He advances steadily toward the goal of a perfect character (see Matt. 5:48).

18.zh:
從來沒有人看見神，只有在父懷裡的獨生子將他表明出來。

**沒有人看見上帝。**指天父（參《先祖與先知》366頁）。罪人不能面對面見上帝而存活。就連以色列偉大的立法者摩西也不得見上帝的面（出33:20；申4:12）。一些人見過上帝臨格的榮耀。但除了在異象中之外，沒有人見過上帝的本體（參賽6:5）。基督來將父顯明出來；人看見祂實際上就是看見了父（約14:7-11）。又見約5:37；6:46。
**懷裡的。**可能是一個習語，表達最親密的歡喜（參約13:23）。從天上下來將父顯明給世人看的主最瞭解天父（約14:7-9）。
**子。**見約1:14；3:16註釋。有文本是“上帝”。不管怎樣，都是指基督。如果理解為“上帝”，那就是“在父懷裡的獨一的上帝”或“獨一的上帝，住在父的懷裡。”
**表明出來。**exegēomai，“顯示”，“揭示”或“解釋”。
18.en:
**No man hath seen God.** That is, the Father (cf. PP 366). Sinners cannot see God face to face and live. Not even Moses, the great lawgiver of Israel, was permitted to behold Him (Ex. 33:20; Deut. 4:12). Some have witnessed the glory of the divine presence (see on John 1:14), but, except in vision, none have seen the divine person (cf. Isa. 6:5). Christ came to reveal the Father, and, for all practical purposes, those who saw Him saw the Father (John 14:7–11). See also chs. 5:37; 6:46.
**Son.** See on chs. 1:14; 3:16. Textual evidence is divided (cf. p. 146) between the readings “Son” and “God.” Either way, reference would be to Christ. If the reading “God” is accepted, the sense would then be: “the unique one, very God, the one abiding in the bosom of the Father,” or, “the only one [who is] God, the one who abides in the bosom of the Father.”
**In the bosom.** Probably an idiomatic expression indicating the most intimate association possible (cf. ch. 13:23). He who knows the Father best is the very one who came from heaven to make Him known to men (ch. 14:7–9).
**Hath declared.** Gr. exegēomai, “to lead forth,” “to unfold [in teaching],” “to reveal,” “to interpret.” Our word “exegesis” is from the same Greek word.

19.zh:
約翰所作的見證記在下面：猶太人從耶路撒冷差祭司和利未人到約翰那裡，問他說：你是誰？

耶穌被宣佈為“上帝的羔羊”：約1:19-34。見本卷註釋216頁插圖。
**約翰所作的見證。**就是他關於基督的見證：一，在耶路撒冷代表團前來詢問他的時候（第19-28節）；二，次日他宣佈耶穌是“上帝的羔羊”（第29-34節）；三，再次日，他私下把他的兩個門徒介紹給耶穌（第35,36節）。使徒約翰在《約翰福音》的開頭部分就記錄了主的先鋒施洗約翰見證拿撒勒人耶穌為彌賽亞。參太3:1,2；可1:1-4；路3:1-6；徒10:37,38；見路3:15-18註釋。
**猶太人從耶路撒冷差。**指當時猶太人的最高當局——猶太公會（參約5:15-18；7:13；9:22；18:12；見本卷註釋第67頁）。向約翰所發的問題反映了他當時在百姓中享有極高的威望（太14:5；21:26），以及領袖們十分注意百姓的普遍看法，即認為他是先知，甚至就是彌賽亞（見路3:15）。施洗約翰的聽眾不僅包括廣大群眾（太3:5），還包括許多國內的宗教（太3:7）和政治（見太14:4；《歷代願望》214頁）領袖。群情激昂，猶太公會再也無法迴避了。百姓無疑要讓他們的領袖解釋代表團現在向約翰所發的問題。一旦約翰的身份得到確認（見約1:25註釋），領袖們有可能會承認他先知的權威，即作為上帝直接的代言人，無需他們授權就可以教訓百姓（見太12:38；16:1註釋）。否則他們就會行使權力控制所有的公開講道（見《塔木德》558-600頁，《密西拿》Sanhedrin11）。
**祭司和利未人。**見出28:1；申10:8註釋。雖然祭司和利未人大都是撒都該人，但這個代表團卻是由法利賽人組成的（見約1:24註釋），可能因為法利賽人更加關心這個問題。後來騷擾耶穌的也是法利賽人。祭司和利未人前來調查施洗約翰，可能因為他的父親是祭司，他的母親也是祭司的女兒（路1:5）。約翰自己有擔任祭司的資格；他因此成為一名教師。
**從耶路撒冷。**這裡離耶路撒冷約42公里。
**你是誰。**他們所關心的不是約翰的個人身份，而是他教訓人的權柄（見第25節）。後來當局也向耶穌提同樣的問題（約8:25）。也許代表團有點希望約翰宣佈自己是彌賽亞。他們的問題顯然反映了這種期待。約翰的回答直截了當地否認了這樣的說法（約1:20；參見《歷代願望》134頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–23節）**。《歷代願望》第134頁；見路1：76,77懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–51節）**。《歷代願望》第132-143頁。
19.en:
**The record of John.** [Jesus Declared “the Lamb of God,” John 1:19–34. See Early Ministry and Baptism to First Passover.] That is, his testimony concerning the Christ, on: (1) the day the delegation from Jerusalem came to investigate him (vs. 19–28), (2) the day following, when he publicly identified Jesus as “the Lamb of God” (vs. 29–34), and (3) the third day, when he privately introduced two of his own disciples to Jesus (vs. 35, 36). John the evangelist begins his gospel narrative with an account of the witness of the forerunner to the Messiahship of Jesus of Nazareth. Compare Matt. 3:1, 2; Mark 1:1–4; Luke 3:1–6; Acts 10:37, 38; see on Luke 3:15–18.
**When the Jews sent.** That is, the Sanhedrin, the supreme Jewish authority of the time (cf. chs. 5:15–18; 7:13; 9:22; 18:12; see p. 67). The questions now put to John reflect the high esteem in which he was held by the people generally (Matt. 14:5; 21:26), and the serious attention given by the leaders to the popular belief that he was a prophet, and might, perhaps, even be the Messiah (see Luke 3:15). The extent of John’s influence is apparent from the fact that his audience included not only vast throngs of the common people (Matt. 3:5), but the religious (v. 7) and political (see Matt. 14:4; DA 214) leaders of the nation as well. Excitement had reached such a height that the Sanhedrin could no longer evade the issue. The people had no doubt pressed their leaders for an answer to the very questions with which the delegation now challenged John. Presumably (see on John 1:25), the leaders would acknowledge the right of a prophet, as a spokesman direct from God, to teach without their authorization, once the validity of his credentials was established (see on Matt. 12:38; 16:1). Otherwise, they exercised the right to control all public teaching (see Mishnah Sanhedrin 11, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 558–600).
**Priests and Levites.** See on Ex. 28:1; Deut. 10:8. Although most of the priests and Levites were Sadducees, this delegation was composed of Pharisees (see on John 1:24), perhaps because they felt more concern over the matter. Similarly, it was the Pharisees who later harassed Jesus. Perhaps priests and Levites were assigned to investigate John out of consideration for the fact that his father had been a priest, and his mother the daughter of a priest (Luke 1:5). John was himself eligible to the priesthood, and thus to become a teacher.
**From Jerusalem.** Perhaps some 25 mi. distant.
**Who art thou?** Literally, “You, who are you?” They were not concerned with John’s identity as an individual, but with his authority to preach and teach (see v. 25). Later, the authorities put the same question to Jesus (ch. 8:25). Perhaps the delegation half expected John to claim he was the Messiah. Their question apparently reflected this expectation, for John’s answer was a forthright denial of such a claim (ch. 1:20; cf. DA 134).

20.zh:
他就明說，並不隱瞞，明說：我不是基督。

**他就明說。**約翰明確否認自己是彌賽亞，從而解決了這一部分問題。使徒約翰特地用否定句“不隱瞞”（參約1:3；3:16；6:50；約壹1:5；2:4）來強調這個肯定的聲明。
**我不是基督。**原文的“我”是強調的。
20.en:
**He confessed.** John’s categorical denial that he was the Messiah settled that aspect of the question. Characteristically, John the evangelist fortifies this positive declaration with a corresponding negative statement, “denied not” (cf. John 1:3; 3:16; 6:50; 1 John 1:5; 2:4).
**I am not the Christ.** The personal pronoun “I” is emphatic, as if John said, “I am not the Christ.”

21.zh:
他們又問他說：這樣，你是誰呢？是以利亞嗎？他說：我不是。是那先知嗎？他回答說：不是。

這樣，你是誰呢？約翰否認自己是是彌賽亞。但他還沒有回答有關他講道權柄的基本回答。
是以利亞嗎？當時人們普遍認為以利亞要現身宣佈彌賽亞的來臨（太17:10；《歷代願望》422頁；參《塔木德》第8頁，《密西拿》Sanhedrin2.5；《塔木德》50頁，Eduyoth 8. 7；《塔木德》124，181，223，224頁等，Baba Mezia 1. 8；2. 8；3. 4,5）。
**我不是。**約翰肯定自己來要作的，就是那些古代先知預言以利亞要作的工作（約1:23；參瑪3:1；4:5；可1:2,3），但是人們卻誤會他自稱以利亞。《舊約》預言約翰將行在彌賽亞前面，“有以利亞的心志能力”（路1:17）。關於基督宣稱約翰是以利亞，見太11:14；17:12註釋。
**那先知。**就是摩西在申18:15所預言的先知（見該節註釋）。當時有一種流行的信念，認為摩西將要從死裡復活。有些人顯然在思考，施洗約翰是不是那先知呢（見《歷代願望》135頁）。後來百姓也是這樣看耶穌的（約6:14；7:40；參徒3:22；7:37）。
21.en:
**What then?** John’s denial left unanswered the basic question as to his authority for preaching.
**Art thou Elias?** It was popularly believed that Elijah would appear in person to proclaim the coming of Messiah (Matt. 17:10; DA 422; cf. Mishnah Shekalim 2.5, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 8; Eduyoth 8. 7, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 50; Baba Mezia 1. 8; 2. 8; 3. 4, 5, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 124, 181, 223, 224; etc.).
**I am not.** John affirmed that he had come to do the work the prophets of old had foretold Elijah would do (John 1:23; cf. Mal. 3:1; 4:5; Mark 1:2, 3), but he would have been misunderstood had he claimed to be Elijah. It was foretold of John that he was to go before Messiah “in the spirit and power of Elias” (Luke 1:17). For Christ’s declaration that John was Elias see on Matt. 11:14; 17:12.
**That prophet.** Literally, “the prophet,” that is, the prophet foretold by Moses in Deut. 18:15 (see comment there). There was a popular belief that Moses would be raised from the dead, and some apparently wondered whether John might be he (see DA 135). Later, the people thought the same thing of Jesus (John 6:14; 7:40; cf. Acts 3:22; 7:37).

22.zh:
於是他們說：你到底是誰，叫我們好回覆差我們來的人。你自己說，你是誰？

**你到底是誰。**這是一個籠統的問題，而不是具體的問題（見第19-21節註釋）。
**回覆。**祭司和利未人迄今只得到否定的回答。現在他們要約翰提供一個肯定的回答。
**差我們來的人。**指耶路撒冷的公會（見第19節註釋）。
22.en:
**Who art thou?** The question was now general rather than specific (see on vs. 19–21).
**An answer.** Thus far inquiry had resulted only in negative replies. Now the priests and Levites sought from John a positive declaration.
**Them that sent us.** That is, the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem (see on v. 19).

23.zh:
他說：我就是那在曠野有人聲喊著說：修直主的道路，正如先知以賽亞所說的。

**我就是那在曠野有人聲喊著說。**見太3:3註釋。約翰似乎在引述施洗約翰的原話，因為這裡的經文好像直接源於希伯來語。否則就會與同觀福音一樣，引用七十士譯本了。耶穌被宣佈為“道”（約1:1-3,14）；施洗約翰則說自己是一個“聲音”。他只是上帝的代言人。耶穌才是那成為肉身的道。
**主的道路。**約翰暗示以色列的領袖們應該將注意力從奉命傳報彌賽亞來臨的使者轉到彌賽亞本人身上。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第689頁；《證言》卷八第333頁。
23.en:
**I am the voice.** See on Matt. 3:3. John appears to report the exact words of the Baptist, for the quotation as here reported seems to be directly from the Hebrew, by memory. Otherwise, as in the Synoptics, it would probably be from the LXX. Jesus is declared to be “the Word” (John 1:1–3, 14); the Baptist claimed only to be a “voice.” He was only God’s spokesman; Jesus was the Word incarnate.
**The way of the Lord.** John implies that the leaders of Israel should turn their attention from the one sent to herald Messiah’s coming and begin looking for the Messiah Himself.

24.zh:
那些人是法利賽人差來的（或作：那差來的是法利賽人）；

有人認為這個代表團是奉了法利賽人的差遣，由撒都該人所組成的，但這種解釋沒有確鑿的證據。原文暗示代表團是由“屬於”法利賽教派的人所組成的。見第19節註釋。
24.en: **Of the Pharisees.** That is, they were of the sect known as Pharisees. Some have suggested that the delegation was composed of Sadducees sent by the Pharisees, but there seems to be no valid reason for accepting this interpretation. The force of the Greek implies that the delegation was composed of individuals who were “of,” that is, who “belonged to,” the Pharisees. See on v. 19.

25.zh:
他們就問他說：你既不是基督，不是以利亞，也不是那先知，為什麼施洗呢？

**為什麼施洗呢。**這才是問題的關鍵——約翰的權柄。既然約翰聲稱自己不是彌賽亞，也不是先知裡的一位，憑什麼未經他們許可就以一個改革者的身份出現呢？見第19節註釋。這個問題暗示人們熟悉用水施洗，至少部分理解其意義（見太3:6註釋）。最近在庫姆蘭的發現表明當時已有用水施洗的儀式（見太3:6註釋；見本卷註釋第63,91頁）。關於洗禮，見太3:6；羅6:3-6註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第135頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（25–27節）**。《歷代願望》第136頁。
25.en: **Why baptizest?** Here was the crux of the issue—John’s authority. He did not claim to be Messiah or one of the prophets—what right, then, did he have to pose as a reformer, without their permission? See on v. 19. The question implies acquaintance with the rite of water baptism, and at least a partial understanding of its significance (see on Matt. 3:6). Recent discoveries at Qumrân reveal that the rite of water baptism was practiced at the time (see on Matt. 3:6; see pp. 63, 91). Concerning the rite of baptism itself see on Matt. 3:6; Rom. 6:3–6.

26.zh:
約翰回答說：我是用水施洗，但有一位站在你們中間，是你們不認識的，

**我是用水施洗。**見太3:11註釋。
**有一位站在。**耶穌的受洗至少是在四十天之前（參第29-34節）。最近祂剛從曠野回來（見太3:13至4:11註釋；參《歷代願望》137頁）。約翰說話的時候看見了耶穌，希望祂對自己的宣告作出回應（《歷代願望》137頁）。
《約翰福音》沒有記載耶穌的受洗。有人解釋約翰沒有記錄這件事和其他一些重要事件的原因，是約翰認為他的讀者已通過同觀福音熟悉了這些事件。關於基督的受洗，見太3:13-17註釋。
**是你們不認識的。**“認識”源於希臘文語oida。三年多以後，祭司和長老宣稱他們仍然不“知道”（oida）施洗約翰的權柄是否從天上來的（太21:27）。那些前來詢問約翰的祭司和利未人掃視面前的觀眾，沒有發現他們所認為符合約翰描述的那一位（《歷代願望》136頁）。但約翰主要是說認識耶穌為預言中的彌賽亞。那些屬靈的領袖因為心靈的黑暗而不接受真光（見第5節註釋），“不認識祂”（第10節），所以也“不接待祂”（第11節；參第31-33節；約8:19；14:7,9；16:3）。他們和差他們來的人都不能決定公開表態，故採取一種不明朗的態度（見太21:23-27註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–27節）**。見路3：15,15懷愛倫註釋。
26.en:
**I baptize.** See on Matt. 3:11.
**There standeth one.** Jesus had been baptized (cf. vs. 29–34) at least 40 days before this, and had but recently returned from the wilderness (see on Matt. 3:13 to 4:11; cf. DA 137). John saw Jesus as he spoke and expected Him to respond to the announcement he now made (DA 137).
The Gospel of John says nothing of Jesus’ baptism. One explanation of John’s silence on this and other important incidents is that he pre-supposes acquaintance on the part of his intended readers with accounts already available to them in the Synoptic Gospels. For comment on Christ’s baptism see on Matt. 3:13–17.
**Whom ye know not.** The word “know” is from the Gr. oida. More than three years later the priests and elders declared that they will could not “tell” (Gr. oida whether John the Baptist had been divinely appointed (Matt. 21:27). The priests and Levites who had come to interrogate John scanned the audience, but saw no one to whom they thought John’s description might apply (DA 136). But John spoke primarily of recognizing Jesus as the Messiah of prophecy. In the darkness of their souls these spiritual leaders failed to apprehend the true Light (see on John 1:5), they “knew him not” (v. 10) and therefore “received him not” (v. 11; cf. vs. 31–33; chs. 8:19; 14:7, 9; 16:3). Neither they nor those who sent them were able to reach a decision they were prepared to announce publicly and according took a noncommittal attitude (see on Matt. 21:23–27).

27.zh:
就是那在我以後來的，我給他解鞋帶也不配。

**就是那。**有文本無此三字。這似乎是後加的，因為沒有認識到 “那在我以後來的”與第26節後半部分“但有一位站在你們中間，是你們不認識的”的同位關係。“就是那”是受拉丁文武加大譯本的影響而進入了英文聖經的：“就是那在我以後來的。”
**在我以後。**見太3:11註釋。
**不配。**見太3:11註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第216頁。
27.en:
**He it is.** Important textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 146) for the omission of this clause. It seems to have been inserted later because of a failure to recognize that the following clause, translated “who coming after me,” is in apposition to the last part of v. 26, “there standeth one among you, whom ye know not.” The insertion “he it is” entered English Bibles through the influence of the Latin Vulgate. Accordingly, the first part of v. 27 would read, “even the one coming after me.”
**After me.** See on Matt. 3:11.
**Is preferred before me.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the omission of this clause. It is attested by only a few late manuscripts (cf. DA 136). However, textual evidence attests the expression in vs. 15, 30.
**I am not worthy.** See on Matt. 3:11.

28.zh:
這是在約但河外伯大尼（有古卷：伯大巴喇），約翰施洗的地方作的見證。

“約旦河外的伯大尼”，有別於耶路撒冷附近的伯大尼。奧利金（約公元250年）曾用過“伯大巴喇”的地名，因為當時他在約旦河附近沒有找到名叫伯大尼的城邑，卻找到了一座叫伯大巴喇的。其位置現在已無從查考。在加利利湖以南19公里處有一個渡口叫亞巴那（Abārah），但它太靠北。伯大巴喇（Bethabara）可能是Beth-`arabah的字母順序調換而成。在猶大和便雅憫的邊界上有一座城叫伯亞拉巴（Beth-ha`arabah，見書15:6,61；18:22），但不在約旦河邊。“伯大巴喇”意思是“渡口之屋（或地方）”，很適合約旦河邊眾多渡口附近的村莊。據傳耶穌受洗的地點是離伯曷拉不遠的Mahādet el-Hajlah。伯曷拉現名`Ain Hajlah，在耶利哥東南6.4公里處。見本卷註釋216頁插圖，以及《SDA聖經註釋》卷一961頁插圖
28.en: **Bethabara.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the reading “Bethany,” called “Bethany Beyond Jordan” to distinguish it from Bethany near Jerusalem. “Bethabara” was adopted by Origen (c. 250 ..), who in his day found no town near the Jordan by the name Bethany, but did find one then known as Bethabara. Neither site has been identified in modern times. There is a ford called Abārah about 12 mi. south of the Lake of Galilee, but this is too far north. Bethabara may possibly represent a transposition of letters by which Beth–‘arabah became Beth–‘abarah. There was a town on the borders of Judah and Benjamin by the name of Beth–ha‘arabah (see Joshua 15:6, 61; 18:22), but it is not on the river. Bethabara, literally, “house [or place] of crossing,” would be an appropriate name for a village near any one of numerous fords across the Jordan. The traditional site of Jesus’ baptism is Maḥāḍet el–Ḥajlah, not far from Bethoglah, now ‘Ain Ḥajlah, 4 mi. (6.4 km.) southeast of Jericho. See Early Ministry and Baptism to First Passover; Palestine In Biblical Times.

30.zh:
這就是我曾說：有一位在我以後來、反成了在我以前的，因他本來在我以前。

**這就是我曾說。**直譯是“曾為祂說”。
**在我以後來、反成了在我以前。**見第15節註釋。
30.en:
**Of whom.** Literally, “on behalf of whom,” not “concerning whom.”
**After me … before me.** See on v. 15.

31.zh:
我先前不認識他，如今我來用水施洗，為要叫他顯明給以色列人。

**我先前不認識祂。**似乎是強調“我先前不認識祂”是彌賽亞。施洗約翰原先關於彌賽亞的見證直接來自上帝的啟示。他和耶穌之間沒有來往。他聽說了耶穌早年的生活環境和祂完美的品格，所以相信耶穌就是所應許的一位。但在耶穌受洗之前，約翰還沒有這方面直接的證據（見《歷代願望》109頁）。
**顯明給以色列人。**約翰是來自上帝的“聲音”（見第23節註釋），向世人指出“上帝的羔羊”（見第29節註釋）。耶穌的受洗標誌著約翰使命的高潮，儘管他以後可能繼續工作了一年半多時間。約翰在耶穌的洗禮結束時宣佈，耶穌“必興旺”，而他自己“必衰微”（約3:30）。
31.en:
**I knew him not.** As if with the emphasis, “Even I did not know him” to be the Messiah. John’s early witness on behalf of the Messiah was based on direct revelation. There had been no collusion between Jesus and John. Knowing of the circumstances attending the early years of Jesus’ life and of His perfection of character, John believed Jesus to be the Promised One, but until the baptism he had no positive evidence that this was so (see DA 109).
**Manifest to Israel.** John was the “voice” from God (see on v. 23) directing men to “the Lamb of God” (see on v. 29). The baptism of Jesus marked the climax of John’s mission, though his labors continued for perhaps a year and a half more. He declared, after the baptism, that Jesus “must increase,” and he himself “decrease” (ch. 3:30).

32.zh:
約翰又作見證說：我曾看見聖靈，彷彿鴿子從天降下，住在他的身上。

**約翰又作見證。**見第19節註釋。
**我曾看見聖靈。**見太3:16,17；路3:21,22註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（32–33節）**。見太3：13-17懷愛倫註釋。
32.en:
**John bare record.** See on v. 19.
**I saw the Spirit.** See on Matt. 3:16, 17; Luke 3:21, 22.

33.zh:
我先前不認識他，只是那差我來用水施洗的、對我說：你看見聖靈降下來，住在誰的身上，誰就是用聖靈施洗的。

**我先前不認識祂。**見第29，31節註釋。
**那差我來用水施洗的。**施洗約翰指出，他的權柄來自上帝（見第6節註釋）。
33.en:
**I knew him not.** See on vs. 29, 31.
**He that sent me.** John points to God as the source of his authority (see on v. 6).

34.zh:
我看見了，就證明這是神的兒子。

**我看見了。**施洗約翰將他親眼所見的事說出來（參見約一1:1）。
**上帝的兒子。**有文本為“上帝所揀選的”。見路1:35註釋；參約1:1-3,14註釋。在《舊約》（詩2:7）和寫於約公元前一世紀的偽經（《以諾書》105:2）中，均明確地以“（上帝的）兒子”作為彌賽亞的稱號。只有在《約翰福音》中，耶穌用“上帝的兒子”來稱呼自己（約5:25；10:36；11:4）。基督時代的猶太人顯然明白這個稱呼的最高含義（見約19:7）。約翰寫《約翰福音》的目的，就是要提供確鑿的證據，證明“耶穌是基督，是上帝的兒子”（約20:31）。
34.en:
**I saw.** John speaks as an eyewitness (cf. 1 John 1:1).
**Son of God.** There is some textual evidence (cf. p. 146) for the reading “the Elect of God.” See on Luke 1:35; cf. on John 1:1–3, 14. In the OT (Ps. 2:7) and in the pseudepigraphal Book of (Enoch 105:2,) about the 1st century .., “Son [of God]” appears as a distinctly Messianic title. Only in the Gospel of John is Jesus reported as using the title of Himself (chs. 5:25; 10:36; 11:4). The Jews of Christ’s time clearly understood the title in its highest sense (see ch. 19:7). John’s objective in writing a Gospel was to provide convincing evidence that “Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God” (ch. 20:31).

35.zh:
再次日，約翰同兩個門徒站在那裡。

[第一批門徒：約1:35-51。見本卷註釋216，230頁插圖]。
**再次日。**見第19節註釋。參第29,43節。約翰往往用“再”把新的敘述與前面的內容聯繫起來（見約8:12,21；10:7,19；21:1等），而不是用它來表示重複。
**兩個門徒。**有一個是安得烈（第40節）。在整卷《約翰福音》中，約翰在敘述與自己有關的事件時總是不提自己的名字，這暗示他就是另一位門徒（參約20:2；21:20-25；見《歷代願望》138頁）
35.en:
**Again the next day.** [The First Disciples, John 1:35–51. See Early Ministry and Baptism to First Passover; The Ministry of Our Lord] See on v. 19; cf. vs. 29, 43. John often uses the word “again” more as a connective, by way of relating a new section of his narrative to the preceding section, rather than in a repetitive sense (see chs. 8:12, 21; 10:7, 19; 21:1; etc.).
**Two of his disciples.** One of these was Andrew (v. 40). John’s reticence throughout his Gospel in referring to himself in connection with incidents in which he was a participant strongly implies that he was the other of the two disciples (cf. chs. 20:2; 21:20–25; see DA 138).

36.zh:
他見耶穌行走，就說：看哪！這是神的羔羊！

**看哪。**本節和第42節的“看”都是指真誠地凝視。這是《約翰福音》最後一次記錄施洗約翰與耶穌相遇的場合。
**懷愛倫註釋（36–38節）**。《歷代願望》第138頁。
36.en: **Looking.** Here and in v. 42, fixed, intent, earnest gazing. This is the last occasion on which the gospel record speaks of John’s being with Jesus.

37.zh:
兩個門徒聽見他的話，就跟從了耶穌。

**跟從。**akoloultheō，可能不一定意味著成為門徒（約8:12；10:4,27；12:26；21:19,20,22；見太4:19註釋）。本節的安得烈和約翰“跟從”耶穌是指他們認出祂是“上帝的羔羊”（約1:36）。他們是第一批跟從耶穌的人。不久又有彼得，腓力和拿但業（巴多羅買）加入（見約1:40,43,45；見可3:16-18註釋）。此時跟從耶穌的人還沒有永久放棄自己的職業而成為祂完全的意義上的門徒。直到一年多以後，也就是公元29年的春天，他們才蒙召成為正式的門徒（見路5:1,11註釋）。到了那時他們才算是“撇下所有的，跟從了耶穌”（路5:11）。正式設立十二使徒還要遲一些，是在當年的夏天（見可3:14註釋）。
37.en: **Followed.** Gr. akoloultheō, “to follow,” probably not yet in the sense of becoming disciples (John 8:12; 10:4, 27; 12:26; 21:19, 20, 22; see on Matt. 4:19). Here, Andrew and John “followed” Jesus in the sense that they recognized Him to be “the Lamb of God” (John 1:36). Andrew and John were the first followers. Soon Peter, Philip, and Nathanael (Bartholomew) joined them (see John 1:40, 43, 45; see on Mark 3:16–18). The followers did not at this time permanently discontinue their usual occupation and become disciples in the full sense of the word. Not until more than a year later, in the spring of .. 29, did they receive the call to permanent discipleship (see on Luke 5:1, 11). Only then could it be said that “they forsook all, and followed him” (Luke 5:11). The formal appointment of the Twelve came even later, during the summer of the same year (see on Mark 3:14).

38.zh:
耶穌轉過身來，看見他們跟著，就問他們說：你們要什麼？他們說：拉比，在哪裡住？（拉比翻出來就是夫子。）

**你們要什麼。**這是約翰所記錄的第一句耶穌的話（參路2:49）。
拉比，在哪裡住？安得烈和約翰想要比在公眾場合更多地與耶穌私下交談。
**拉比。**rhabbi，源於亞蘭語rabi，意為“大人”，也用來尊稱律法的教師（見太23:7註釋）。有人認為這第二層意思後來才有的。
在《約翰福音》裡，一些人常稱耶穌為“拉比”。他們承認耶穌是教師，甚至是一位先知，卻沒有認識或不願承認祂是彌賽亞（見約1:38,49；3:2；4:31；6:25；9:2；11:8）。那些蒙耶穌施行了神蹟的人常稱祂為“主”（約9:36；11:3,21,27,32）。約翰說，門徒在最初與耶穌接觸的時候稱呼祂為“拉比”。但隨著進一步確信耶穌就是上帝差來的一位，他們就稱他“主”（約6:68；11:12；13:6,25；14:5,8,22；21:15,20等）。耶穌復活以後，他們就永遠稱祂為“主”（林前16:22），再也不稱祂為“拉比”了。同觀福音的作者不像約翰那樣區分這些稱呼。施洗約翰的門徒稱約翰為“拉比”（約3:26）。
稱耶穌為“拉比”的人表明他們願意向祂學習；而稱他為“主”（亞蘭語Mari，希臘語Kurios）的人則表達了他們的尊敬或無條件的服從。但這兩個詞語有時沒有明顯的差別。
**翻出來。**對於希臘語的讀者，約翰經常提供我們主的亞蘭語原話，但總是將其譯成希臘語（約1:41,42；4:25；5:2；9:7；11:16；19:13,17；20:16,24；21:2）。
**懷愛倫註釋（38–39節）**。《福山寶訓》第131頁。
38.en:
**What seek ye?** These are the first words of Jesus that are reported by John (cf. Luke 2:49).
**Rabbi.** Gr. rhabbi, from the Aramaic rabi, meaning “my great one,” generally equivalent to “sir,” but used also in a more restricted sense as a title of distinction and respect for a teacher of the law (see on Matt. 23:7). It has been suggested that, in the latter sense, the word had but recently come into use.
In John, “rabbi” is consistently the term used in addressing Jesus by those who recognize Him as a teacher, perhaps even a prophet, but who either do not as yet realize, or who are unwilling to admit, that He is the Messiah (see chs. 1:38, 49; 3:2; 4:31; 6:25; 9:2; 11:8). Those for whom Jesus performed miracles often called Him “Lord” (chs. 9:36; 11:3, 21, 27, 32). In the early part of their association with Jesus the disciples are quoted by John as calling Him “Rabbi,” but with a deepening conviction that He is indeed the Sent of God they later call Him “Lord” (chs. 6:68; 11:12; 13:6, 25; 14:5, 8, 22; 21:15, 20; etc.). After the resurrection the title “Lord” is always used of Jesus (1 Cor. 16:22), never “Rabbi.” The synoptic writers do not discriminate between these titles as does John. The Baptist’s disciples called him “rabbi” (John 3:26).
Those who addressed Jesus as “Rabbi” thereby expressed their willingness to learn of Him, whereas those who addressed Him as “Lord” (Aramaic Mari, Gr. Kurios) thereby expressed either common respect, or the unquestioning submission of servants. However, the terms were often used without any clear sense of distinction between them.
**Being interpreted.** Writing for Greek readers, John often provides the original Aramaic words of our Lord, but always translates them into Greek (chs. 1:41, 42; 4:25; 5:2; 9:7; 11:16; 19:13, 17; 20:16, 24; 21:2).
**Where dwellest thou?** Andrew and John desire a more prolonged and personal interview than seems appropriate in a public place.

39.zh:
耶穌說：你們來看。他們就去看他在哪裡住，這一天便與他同住；那時約有申正了。

**申正。**約下午四點鐘。在耶穌的時代，巴勒斯坦所通行的羅馬計時法將白天分為十二個小時（見約11:9；本卷註釋第50頁；參約瑟弗斯《人生》54 [279]）。約翰對時間的清楚記憶表明那一天的事件在他心中留下了深刻的印象。約翰多次記錄準確的時間（見約4:6,52；18:28；19:14；20:19）。這種精確性證明了他所自稱的目擊者身份（約19:35；21:24；約壹1:1,2）。
**懷愛倫註釋（39–43節）**。《歷代願望》第139頁。
39.en: **The tenth hour.** That is, about 4:00 .. In the days of Jesus, Roman usage, then current in Palestine, divided the light part of the day into 12 hours (see ch. 11:9; p. 50; cf. Josephus Life 54 [279]). John’s vivid memory of the hour reflects the profound impression events of this day made upon his memory. John repeatedly notes the time of day (see chs. 4:6, 52; 18:28; 19:14; 20:19). This exactness comports with his claim to being an eyewitness (John 19:35; 21:24; 1 John 1:1, 2).

40.zh:
聽見約翰的話跟從耶穌的那兩個人，一個是西門彼得的兄弟安得烈。

**跟從耶穌。**約翰和安得烈想與耶穌談論施洗約翰在第36節的宣告：“看哪，上帝的羔羊！”他們還沒有想好要正式成為祂的門徒（見第43註釋）。當時可能是公元27年的深秋或初冬（見本卷註釋228頁插圖）。在以後的一年半的時間裡，他們斷斷續續地跟從耶穌，直到祂呼召他們永遠作祂的門徒（見路5:11註釋）。耶穌正式設立十二個使徒要到公元29年的夏天（見可3:13-19註釋）。在約旦河邊“跟從”耶穌的五個人只是接受了施洗約翰有關祂彌賽亞身份的見證。
**那兩個人，一個。**作者只指出兩個中的一個。一般認為另一個就是作者本人，即雅各的兄弟約翰。他謙虛地隱去了自己的名字（見第35節註釋；參約21:20-24；《歷代願望》138頁）。
**西門彼得。**見可3:16註釋。
**安得烈。**可3:18註釋。
40.en:
**One of the two.** The writer identifies but one of the two. It is generally believed that the other was the writer himself, John the brother of James, who modestly refrains from identifying himself (see on v. 35; cf. ch. 21:20–24; DA 138).
**Followed him.** John and Andrew desired to converse with Jesus concerning the declaration of v. 36, “Behold the Lamb of God!” They were not yet thinking of following Him in the formal sense of becoming regular followers (see on v. 43). It was now probably the late autumn or early winter of .. 27 (see The Chronology of Luke 3:1, 2). They followed Jesus intermittently for the next year and a half before He issued the call to permanent discipleship (see on Luke 5:11). Jesus’ formal appointment of the Twelve did not take place till the late summer of .. 29 (see on Mark 3:13–19). The five who “followed” Jesus at the Jordan did so simply in the sense of accepting John’s witness to His Messiahship.
**Andrew.** See on Mark 3:18.
**Simon Peter’s.** See on Mark 3:16.

42.zh:
於是領他去見耶穌。耶穌看著他，說：你是約翰的兒子西門（約翰在馬太16：17稱約拿），你要稱為磯法。（磯法翻出來就是彼得。）

**耶穌看著他。**參第36節註釋。
**西門……磯法。**見太16:18；可3:16註釋。“西門（Simon）”源於希伯來語“西緬（Simeon）”的希臘語形式（見創29:33註釋）。
**翻出來。**見第38節註釋。
42.en:
**Jesus beheld him.** In v. 36 (see comment there) “looking” is from the same Greek word here translated “beheld.”
**Simon … Cephas.** See on Matt. 16:18; Mark 3:16. The name “Simon” is from the Greek form of the Hebrew “Simeon” (see on Gen. 29:33).
**By interpretation.** See on v. 38.

43.zh:
又次日，耶穌想要往加利利去，遇見腓力，就對他說：來跟從我吧。

**又次日。**即第35-42節所記事件的第二天，或第19-28節所記事件的第三天（見第29,35節註釋）。
**想要往。**打算去，即將去。
**遇見腓力。**可能是通過那三位已經找到耶穌之人的努力。關於腓力，見可3:18註釋。
**來跟從我吧。**耶穌的意思是要腓力作祂的門徒（見可2:14註釋），而不是隻是跟在祂後面，如第37節那樣。見路5:11；約1:40註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第292頁。
43.en:
**The day following.** That is, the day after the events of vs. 35–42, and prbably the third day after those of vs. 19–28 (see vs. 29, 35).
**Would go.** That is, purposed to go, or was about to go.
**Findeth Philip.** Perhaps as a result of the efforts of the three who had already found Jesus. Concerning Philip see on Mark 3:18.
**Follow me.** Here, more nearly in the sense of becoming a disciple (see on Mark 2:14), not in the simple sense of walking after someone, as in v. 37. However, see on Luke 5:11; John 1:40.

44.zh:
這腓力是伯賽大人，和安得烈、彼得同城。

**伯賽大。**見太11:21註釋。

45.zh:
腓力找著拿但業，對他說：摩西在律法上所寫的和眾先知所記的那一位，我們遇見了，就是約瑟的兒子拿撒勒人耶穌。

**腓力找著拿但業。**就像日前安得烈帶著他的哥哥來見耶穌，腓力也帶來了一位朋友。真正悔改的人心中的第一個願望就是與別人分享救恩的喜樂和福氣，特別是自己的親友。拿但業一般稱為巴多羅買（見可3:18註釋）。
**律法。**《舊約》頭五卷的通稱（見路24:44註釋）。腓力特指申18:15的預言（見該節註釋），在拿撒勒人耶穌身上應驗了（見約6:14註釋）。
**約瑟的兒子。**見太1:20,21；路2:33,41註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第145，292頁；《基督教育原理》第365頁；《證言》卷六第428頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（45–46節）**。《佈道論》第446頁；《基督教育原理》第142頁；《證言》卷三第566頁；《證言》卷六第37頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（45–49節）**。《歷代願望》第140頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（45–51節）**。《安息日學訓言》第25，26頁。
45.en:
**Philip findeth Nathanael.** As the day before, Andrew brought his brother to Jesus, so Philip now brings a friend. The first impulse in the heart of one who is truly converted is to share the joy and the blessing of salvation with others, particularly with those who are near and dear. Nathanael is commonly identified with Bartholomew (see on Mark 3:18).
**The law.** Here, a technical designation for the first five books of the OT (see on Luke 24:44). Philip refers particularly to the prediction of Deut. 18:15 (see comment there) as meeting its fulfillment in Jesus of Nazareth (see on John 6:14).
**Son of Joseph.** See on Matt. 1:20, 21; Luke 2:33, 41.

46.zh:
拿但業對他說：拿撒勒還能出什麼好的嗎？腓力說：你來看！

**拿撒勒。**見太2:23註釋。
**什麼好的。**拿但業對腓力興奮的報告嗤之以鼻。他來自迦拿（約21:2），離拿撒勒不遠，他的話無疑是依據第一手的材料。
**你來看。**參第29節。親自去見耶穌要比爭執不休更有說服力。今天也是這樣。要獲得信仰基督的明確證據，唯一的方法就是去親身體驗。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第71頁；《告青年書》第78頁；《論節制》第224頁。
46.en:
**Any good thing.** There is a tinge of scorn in Nathanael’s rejoinder to Philip’s thrilling announcement. Nathanael was from Cana (ch. 21:2), but a short distance from Nazareth, and doubtless spoke from firsthand knowledge.
**Nazareth.** See on Matt. 2:23.
**Come and see.** Compare v. 29. To meet Jesus face to face would be more convincing evidence than a lengthy argument. Thus it is today. The only way to obtain positive evidence of the certainty of faith in Christ is to experience it.

47.zh:
耶穌看見拿但業來，就指著他說：看哪，這是個真以色列人，他心裡是沒有詭詐的。

**真以色列人。**即憑著心靈和誠實敬拜上帝（見約4:23,24）而不虛偽（太6:2；7:5；23:13）的人。拿但業屬於少數敬虔熱心等待“以色列的安慰者”（見路2:25註釋）到來的人。他們嚮往上帝擺在他們面前的崇高理想（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷四第26-30頁）。一個真以色列人不一定是亞伯拉罕肉身的後裔（見約8:33-44），而是那些選擇在生活上與上帝的旨意和諧的人（見約8:39；徒10:34,35；羅2:28,29；9:6,7,25-27；10:12,13；加3:9,28,29；彼前2:9,10）。
**詭詐。**dolos，直譯是“誘餌”，如釣魚所用的，喻指“狡計”，“欺詐”，“背信”。偽善者用偽裝和“誘餌”讓人相信他們比實際的情況要好。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷四第534頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（47–48節）**。《喜樂的泉源》第91頁；《給傳道人的證言》第110頁。
47.en:
**An Israelite indeed.** Or, “truly an Israelite,” that is, one who served God in sincerity of heart (see ch. 4:23, 24) and not as a hypocrite (see on Matt. 6:2; 7:5; 23:13). Nathanael was one of that small but devout group who earnestly waited for “the consolation of Israel” (see on Luke 2:25) and aspired to the high ideals set before them by God (see Vol. IV, pp. 26-30). A true Israelite was not necessarily a literal descendant of Abraham (see John 8:33–44), but one who chose to live in harmony with the will of God (see John 8:39; Acts 10:34, 35; Rom. 2:28, 29; 9:6, 7, 25–27; 10:12, 13; Gal. 3:9, 28, 29; 1 Peter 2:9, 10).
**Guile.** Gr. dolos, literally, “bait,” such as for catching fish, but figuratively, “trickery,” “guile,” “treachery.” False pretenses are the “bait” used by the hypocrite to convince men that he is better than he really is.

48.zh:
拿但業對耶穌說：你從哪裡知道我呢？耶穌回答說：腓力還沒有招呼你，你在無花果樹底下，我就看見你了。

**從哪裡知道。**拿但業發現自己的生活像書卷那樣在耶穌眼前展開，感到十分吃驚。。
**無花果樹。**由於所結的果實，無花果樹和橄欖樹是巴勒斯坦最受青睞的植物。“在無花果樹底下”意味著舒適和安寧（見彌4:4；亞3:10等）。
48.en:
**Whence knowest?** Nathanael was startled to find that his life lay open like a book before Jesus.
**Fig tree.** In Palestine the fig and the olive were the favorite trees cultivated for their fruit. To “sit” under one’s “fig tree” meant to be at home and at peace (see Micah 4:4; Zech. 3:10; etc.).

49.zh:
拿但業說：拉比，你是神的兒子，你是以色列的王！

**拉比。**見第38節註釋。
**上帝的兒子。**見路1:35註釋。拿但業明確而坦率的信心表白（第49節），證明基督的話（第47節）在他的心裡產生了深刻的印象。拿但業顯然希望得到更加清晰的亮光，好明白施洗約翰所說耶穌是“上帝的羔羊”（第29,36節）和“上帝的兒子”（第34節）。這種願望引導他去找一個合適的地方默想禱告（見《歷代願望》140頁）。作為對祈禱的回應，他現在得到了明確的證據，證明耶穌的神性。耶穌常常通過揭示人心靈最深處的思想和人生活中隱藏的秘密，來向人證明祂的神性（見可2:8註釋）。關於後來門徒憑著信心承認耶穌的神性，見太14:33；16:16；約6:69；16:30等。
**以色列的王。**這是彌賽亞的另一個稱呼。拿但業承認耶穌是眾先知應許將要“復興以色列國”（徒1:6）的一位。這個稱呼相當於“大衛的子孫”（見太1:1；可10:48；參亞6:13）。
49.en:
**Rabbi.** See on v. 38.
**Son of God.** See on Luke 1:35. The profound impression made by Christ’s declaration (v. 47) is clearly evident from Nathanael’s forthright and unqualified profession of faith (v. 49). Evidently it was his earnest desire for clearer light concerning the Baptist’s identification of Jesus as “the Lamb of God” (vs. 29, 36) and as “the Son of God” (v. 34), that had led him to seek an appropriate place for meditation and prayer (see DA 140). In response to that prayer he was now provided with convincing evidence that Jesus was divine. Jesus often read men’s inmost thoughts and the hidden secrets of their lives, thereby giving them evidence of His divinity (see on Mark 2:8). For later declarations by the disciples of faith in the divinity of Jesus see Matt. 14:33; 16:16; John 6:69; 16:30; etc.
**King of Israel.** An additional Messianic title by which Nathanael acknowledged Jesus as the One the prophets promised should “restore again the kingdom to Israel” (Acts 1:6). This title was equivalent to the expression “son of David” (see on Matt. 1:1; Mark 10:48; cf. Zech. 6:13).

50.zh:
耶穌對他說：因為我說在無花果樹底下看見你，你就信嗎？你將要看見比這更大的事；

**更大的事。**耶穌在這裡指的是拿但業在今後跟從基督時將要看見祂神性的許多確鑿證據（見《歷代願望》142頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第142，148頁。
50.en: **Greater things.** Jesus here refers to the many convincing evidences of divinity Nathanael was to witness during his association with Christ (see DA 142).

51.zh:
又說：我實實在在的告訴你們，你們將要看見天開了，神的使者上去下來在人子身上。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18註釋。在新約的作者中，只有約翰用這個重疊詞組，共用了二十五次，都是引用耶穌的話。
“實實在在”的希伯來語對相詞多次出現在死海古卷（見本卷註釋第91頁）中的《紀律手冊》中，但其意義與約翰的用法略有不同。
**上帝的使者。**耶穌用這個比喻形象地說明了祂對人類的服務（見《歷代願望》142，143頁）。這個比喻顯然依據雅各去哈蘭路上（創28:12）在伯特利所作的夢。參來1:14。
**人子。**見可2:10註釋。這是耶穌使用這個稱呼的首次記錄。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第142頁；《善惡之爭》第19頁；《先祖與先知》第184頁；《喜樂的泉源》第20頁；【 SDA5.1132】。
51.en:
**Verily, verily.** See on Matt. 5:18. Of all NT writers only John doubles the word, as here. He does so altogether 25 times, in each instance quoting Jesus.
The Hebrew equivalent of the expression “verily, verily” occurs repeatedly in the Manual of Discipline (1 QS), one of the Dead Sea scrolls (see p. 91), but in a somewhat different sense from that in which John uses it.
**Angels of God.** In this picturesque figure of speech Jesus envisions His own ministry for mankind (see DA 142, 143). The figure is evidently based on Jacob’s dream at Bethel, while on his way to Haran (Gen. 28:12). Compare Heb. 1:14.
**Son of man.** See on Mark 2:10. This is Jesus’ first recorded use of the title.

900.zh:
《新約》所記載的基督生平，是基督教信仰源泉，中心和確據。就像約1:1-3,14（見該節註釋）所闡述、整部《新約》所一再肯定的，基督是絕對意義上的神。從各方面來說，祂也是真正的人，只是祂沒有犯罪。藉著道成肉身，神性和人性在耶穌基督裡牢不可破地結合在一起。祂是獨一無二的神人（見太1:1註釋）。
但聖經又宣稱“耶和華我們上帝是獨一的主”（申6:4；可12:29）。基督教會所傳承的真理包含深奧的三位一體一神論和上帝道成肉身的奧秘，是我們有限的智慧所無法理解的，也是我們所無法作出最終分析和定義的。然而對於使徒時代熱心的基督徒來說，他們中間許多人親眼看見、親耳聽過的有關被釘、復活、又長久活著的主的活潑事實（見約1:14；彼後1:16；約壹1:1-3），使相關的神學問題顯得無足輕重了。
但是隨著那一代人的過去（見啟2:4；參書24:31），有關永生之主的印象逐漸淡化，起初的純潔和虔誠消退了。人們越來越從福音的實用價值轉向引發好奇心的理論。他們誤以為通過研究深奧的哲理，就有可能找到上帝（見伯11:7；羅11:33）。在興起來困擾教會的各種異端中，最嚴重的是關於基督的本性和位格的學說。在這個問題上的爭論動搖了教會達數百年之久，其標誌就是沒完沒了的異端，會議和分裂。
除了專門研究教會歷史的人士之外，詳細探討這場爭論可能並無益處和實際價值。但今日與使徒時代一樣，基督教信仰的確鑿證據均圍繞著《新約》中基督的生平上。此外，各種古代的異端在形形色色的偽裝之下依然存在，或死灰復燃。簡單回顧這場早期爭論的過程，能使現代的基督徒學會識別和提防曾經困擾他們過去虔誠弟兄的同樣錯誤（見約8:32；約壹4:1）。
這場長時間的爭論表現在兩個方面：三位一體論和基督論。前者涉及基督的上帝身份；後者涉及道成肉身的基督在神性與人性之間的關係。第一世紀到第四世紀的三位一體論之爭圍繞著幻影說，神格唯一論和阿里烏主義。第五到第七世紀的基督論之爭則針對聶斯脫利主義，基督一性論和基督一志論。
使徒時代的教會。彼得所宣佈耶穌是“基督，是永生上帝的兒子”（太16:16），以及保羅簡短的信仰聲明：“耶穌是主”（Kurios，等當於希伯來語的Yahweh，林前12:3），很好地歸納了使徒時代教會對於耶穌的信念。。早期的基督徒相信耶穌是神，並以這個信念作為他們信仰的基石（見太16:18註釋）。“屬血肉”的人不能啟示或說明這個真理。唯有藉著信心才能領受真理（見太16:17）。初期教會確信三位一體和基督神人二性是以耶穌和使徒清楚的教訓為依據的。但基督昇天後不多年，“兇暴的豺狼”開始吞噬羊群。教會內部有人起來說“悖謬的話”，引誘門徒跟從他們（見徒20:29,30）。
幻影說和諾斯替主義。第一個關於基督本性和位格的謬論一般稱為幻影說。這個名稱來自希臘語中一個意為“顯現”的詞語。幻影說有不同的形式，但其基本觀念是，基督只是有人的形狀。祂是一個幻影或，根本不是一個人。道只是在外形上成了肉身。這個異端在使徒時代就已興起，延續到第二世紀末。
信奉幻影說的主要有伊比奧尼派和諾斯替派。前者是猶太籍基督徒。他們嚴格遵守猶太教的禮儀和習俗。後者主要是外邦的基督徒。諾斯替主義只不過是各種異教哲學用基督教的術語偽裝起來的混合品。
一個可能是真實的早期傳說認為，行邪術的西門是最早倡導有關基督本性和位格異端的人（見徒8:9-24）。他是第一個諾斯替派基督徒。幾年之後一個名叫塞林圖斯的基督徒在亞歷山大興起。有些人認為他屬於伊比奧尼派，也有人認為他屬於諾斯替派。他否認基督以肉身來到世間，主張祂所謂的道成肉身只不過是外形上，而不是真實的。伊比奧尼派雖然與諾斯替派不同，但對於基督人性所持的看法是一樣的。他們認為基督只是約瑟的兒子，因為祂的虔誠和遵守律法而被上帝揀選為彌賽亞，並在受洗時被接納為上帝的兒子。伊比奧尼派的一支厄勒克賽派宣稱，基督是天父在萬古之先所“生”的，因此地位要低於天父。
伊比奧尼派實質上是把基督看作一個超人。諾斯替派則完全否認祂是人。他們認為基督只是一個幻影，暫時居住在耶穌這個凡人身上。祂的神性並沒有成為肉身。關於諾斯替主義對基督教的巨大沖擊，教會歷史學家拉圖雷特指出：“在一段時間裡，大多數自稱認為基督徒的人都信奉諾斯替主義的一種或另一種形式”（K.S.來德里《基督教會史》，第123頁）。諾斯替派在使徒的時代逐漸興起，到第二世紀對教會產生了極大的影響。當教會意識到它的嚴重威脅時，就展開了堅決的反擊。
伊裡奈烏斯寫於二世紀下半葉的著作中提到，約翰寫《約翰福音》的主要目的就是要駁斥塞林圖斯的幻影說（伊裡奈烏斯《駁異端》 xi. 1，《前尼西亞時期的教父》卷一第426頁；見約1:1-3,14；約20:30,31註釋）。約翰在他的書信中更明確警告人抵制幻影說的異端，把其倡導者稱之為“敵基督的”（約壹2:18-26；4:1-3,9,14；約貳7,10）。保羅第一次被囚在羅馬的時候（約公元62年），曾警告歌羅西信徒防備幻影說的異端（西2:4,8,9,18），幾乎在同時，彼得發出了更嚴厲的警告（彼後2:1-3）。猶大（猶4）也提到了幻影說的異端。啟2:6中“尼哥拉一黨人”雖然不一定是幻影派，但卻是屬於諾斯替教派的（伊裡奈烏斯《駁異端》 xi. 1，《前尼西亞時期的教父》卷一第426頁）。
在公元二世紀上半葉，有若干諾斯替派的教師興起，用他們的異端危害教會。其中著名的有亞歷山大的巴西里德斯和瓦倫廷。到二世紀下半葉，幻影說最成功，最有影響的倡導者也許就是馬西安了。他不屬於諾斯替派，但他關於基督的觀點與諾斯替派很接近。他認為耶穌的出生，肉身生活，以及受死都不是真實的，而只是真實的幻象而已。
教會對幻影說的重大錯誤進行了堅決的鬥爭。公元二世紀下半葉，伊裡奈烏斯勇敢地站出來反對異端，維護正統的教義。他駁斥異端，特別是諾斯替異端的著作《駁異端》流傳至今。伊裡奈烏斯所強調的是上帝的統一性。
神格唯一論。顧名思義，神格唯一論強調神性的統一。實際上，它是對諾斯底替多神論和馬吉安二神論的反駁。馬西安認為《舊約》中的上帝是邪惡的神；基督則是慈愛的神。但矯枉往往過正，它走向了另一個極端，結果變成了又一個教會需要譴責的異端。神格唯一論的功績在於它清除了教會中諾斯替派的道理，但也產生了與它所要清除的異端一樣嚴重的危害。對神格唯一論的批駁始於公元二世紀末，延續到公元三世紀。神格唯一論有兩派：力本論者（源一個表示“力量”的希臘詞語），宣稱有神的能力支配著耶穌的身體；耶穌沒有自己的神性，也沒有真正人的靈魂；模態論者認為是一位神用不同的形式表現祂自己。
力本論者為了維護神性的統一性就全盤否定了基督的神性，認為基督只是一個上帝所揀選為彌賽亞的人，被提拔到了神的地位。根據力本論的分支嗣子論的說法，凡人耶穌達到了完全，在受洗時被接納為上帝的兒子。
模態論者宣揚一位神以不同的方式表現祂自己。他們否認上帝在位格上的區別，完全放棄了三位一體的信念。他們接受父與子真正的神性，但馬上解釋說這只是同一位神的不同表現而已。這種觀點有時被稱為聖父受苦說，假定聖父在道成肉身時成為子，接著以基督的身份受苦受死。同樣，聖子在復活時變成聖靈。這個觀點最著名的倡導者是撒伯裡烏，因此又叫作撒伯裡烏主義。撒伯裡烏派認為，三位一體真神的名稱只是同一位神在執行不同重大職能時的稱呼而已。在道成肉身之前，這位神就是聖父；道成肉身時聖父變成了聖子；聖子復活時就變成了聖靈。
德爾圖良在第三世紀初駁斥了模態論派的神格唯一論，強調上帝兒子的位格和神性的統一。但他主張基督是次等的上帝，即次位論。
大約在第三世紀中期，奧裡金提出了永世論，主張只有聖父是最高意義上的上帝。聖子與聖父都是永恆的，但只是派生意義上的“上帝”。 奧裡金錯誤地認為，基督的靈魂和所有人類的靈魂一樣，是本已存在的，但不同於未曾墮落的純潔生靈。聖道與耶穌人的靈魂不可分割地結合在一起。奧裡金將約1:1中的theos和ho theos（均為“上帝”）加以區分，歸納說，聖子不是原始絕對的意義上的上帝，而因交流而成為次等的上帝，被稱為theos，而不是ho theos。基督因此就了受造者和非受造者之間的中間體。奧裡金是阿里烏斯主義的鼻祖。
阿里烏斯主義。公元四世紀初，亞歷山大教會的一位長老阿里烏斯秉承了奧裡金關於“道”的理論，但他否認在上帝和受造者之間存在任何中間體。他據此推斷說聖子絕不是神；儘管祂是最高最先的，但從嚴格意義上說，仍是被造者，因而“有一段時期祂是不存在的。”他教導說，只有聖父是永存的，聖父從虛無中創造出聖子。聖子在藉著聖父的旨意被造之前是不存在的。阿里烏斯既否認基督是真正的人，說祂沒有人的靈魂，又否認祂的神性，說祂沒有上帝的本質和屬性。祂只是最高的受造者。凡人耶穌由於上帝預知祂的勝利，而成為基督。
為解決阿里烏斯的爭端，公元325年召開了第一次尼西亞會議。阿塔那修斯作為“正統之父”站出來，支持耶穌基督是永在的，不是來自本來虛無的狀態，其本質與聖父是一樣的。會議將homoousios（“本體同一”）一詞用在基督身上，肯定了基督與聖父為一體和同質的信念。Homoousios不能理解為其他的意義。會議譴責阿里烏斯主義和撒伯裡烏主義是違背真理的兩大異端，並聲稱堅持三位一體並不否認上帝的統一性，堅持上帝的統一性也不否認三位一體。因此尼西亞信經宣佈：聖子是“為父所生（……上帝之上帝，父的本質），出於光而為光，出於真神而為真神，受生而非被造，與父一體（oJmoouvsion）”（引自腓利普.沙夫《基督教信經》卷一第29頁）。這部信經成為正統三位一體論的關鍵性驗證。
阿里烏斯派拒絕接受大會的決議，分了出去。在以後的幾百年時間裡，阿里烏斯派成了羅馬教會最頑固的敵人（見但7:8註釋）。第一次尼西亞會議後，一批有時被稱為半阿里烏斯派的人也給教會帶來麻煩。他們的關鍵詞是homoiousios（“本體相類”），說聖子與聖父是“本體相類”，而不是尼西亞信經的homoousios（“本體同一”）。尼西亞會議以後正統論主要對手是阿波利那裡斯和馬賽盧斯。他們都肯定神性和人性在基督裡的真實合一，但否認基督真實的人性，主張上帝的旨意使耶穌的人性成為被動的工具。這些不同的問題導致了公元381年在君士坦丁堡召開了又一次會議。這次會議重新堅定了尼西亞信經，闡明瞭它的意義，並且宣佈在基督裡面神性和人性的存在。
聶斯脫利主義。君士坦丁堡會議後，教會的注意力轉向了有關基督本質和位格的基督論。人們試圖界定基督裡的神性與人性，說明二者之間的關係。這兩種特性怎麼能存在於一位身上呢？
這方面的爭論圍繞著的兩個對立的學派展開。一個在亞歷山大，另一個在敘利亞的安提阿。他們都承認神性與人性在耶穌基督身上真正地聯合。但亞歷山大學派強調神性與人性的統一，以及神性的重要性；而安提阿學派則強調神性與人性的區別，以及人性的重要性。安提阿派的支持者認為在耶穌身上神性和人性長期共存與合作，但沒有真正融合在一起。他們將基督身上的兩種性質分開，宣稱沒有完全的融合，只有長期的聯合。他們清楚地區分神子基督與人子基督，並更加強調人性。他們認為這兩種性質通過各自意志的統一而完成。他們贊同基督人性的真實和完全，卻不贊同位格的統一。認為這是一種不完美，不完全，鬆散而機械性的結合，這兩種性質不是真正統一在一個具有自我意識的位格身上。在另一方面，亞歷山大學派則認為這兩種性質已神奇而完全地融合在一起，人性與神性融為一體，並從屬於神性。上帝就這樣進入人性，藉著神性與人性的聯合，基督才能將人類帶回到上帝那裡。
這兩個學派的衝突在公元五世紀初的聶斯脫利之爭中達到了高潮。安提阿的聶斯脫利承認耶穌真實的神性和真實的人性，但否認它們統一在一個具有自我意識的位格中。聶斯脫利派認為，基督具有兩個位格，只是在道德和精神上統一。兩者互不施加決定性的影響。神性沒有降格，人性也沒有提高。有上帝，有人，但沒有神人。
教會第三次大公會議於431年在以弗所舉行，目的是要解決安提阿和亞歷山大兩學派的爭端。會議譴責了聶斯脫利和他的教訓，但認為不必制訂新的信條來取代尼西亞信經。會議沒有解決或確定任何問題，反而擴大了分歧，加重了爭端，以致把其他所有的教義問題都擱在了一邊。
基督一性論。以弗所會議之後，出現了另一種學說，叫基督一性論或優迪基安論，提出了與聶斯脫利相反的基督觀。優迪基安是這種學說的主要倡導者。他認為耶穌原來的人性在道成肉身時已融入神性，因此作為人的耶穌和作為上帝的基督已成為一體，具有同一性質。他主張這是具有自我意識的聯合，但兩種性質的融合實際上已使各自的特性消失了。
公元451年召開的卡爾西頓大公會議討論了聶斯脫利主義和基督一性論，決定予以譴責。聶斯脫利和優迪基安均拒絕會議的決定，遂創建獨立的基督教派，像一百多年前阿里烏斯所作的那樣。
卡爾西頓會議確定了基督完全的神性和完全的人性，宣稱祂在神性上與父同為一體，在人性上與我們同為一體，但祂沒有犯罪。兩種性質都得到保留，但宣佈它們是不相混亂，不相交換，不能分開，不能離散的。會議承認神性而非人性是基督人格的基礎。由於一個位格是兩種性質的結合，神人基督所受的苦是無限的。祂在人性中，而非在神性中受苦。因為位格是無限的，所以苦難也是無限的。以下就是後稱《卡爾西頓信條》的一部分：
“我們跟隨聖教父，同心合意教人認識同一位子，我們的主耶穌基督，是神性完全、人性亦完全者； 他真是上帝，也真是人，具有理性的靈魂，也具有身體；按神性說，他與父同體；按人性說，他與我們同體；在凡事上與我們一樣，只是沒有罪；按神性說，在萬世之前，為父所生；按人性說，在晚進時日，為求拯救我們，由天主之母，童女瑪利亞所生；是同一基督，是子，是主，是獨生的，具有二性，不相混亂，不相交換，不能分開，不能離散；二性的區別不因聯合而消失；各性的特點反得以保存，會合於一個位格，一個實質之內”（ 腓利普.沙夫《基督教信經》卷二第62頁）。，
卡爾西頓會議的結果加深了東方教會的分裂。最後羅馬皇帝查士丁尼認定，為了保障帝國的安全，必須解決這些問題。於是他永久關閉了教義爭端的兩個中心──安提阿和亞歷山大──的各所學校。在公元553年的第二次君士坦丁堡會議上，教會決定武力鎮壓基督一性論，結果優迪基安派徹底分出去了，形成不同的基督教派別，直至今日，像雅各教派，科普特教派，阿比西尼亞教派。教會重申卡爾西頓信條，在正統和非正統之間劃出了清晰的界線。
基督一志論。事實上還有一個問題有待解決：神人兩種性質，是在一個意志，還是兩個意志控制下運作？基督一志論認為上帝的意志是支配性的，而人的意志則是從屬性的。在公元680年的第三次君士坦丁堡會議上，教會認定意志是屬於本性的問題，而不是屬於位格的問題，宣佈教會贊同兩種意志共存於一個有意志的位格之中。這就完成了西方教會關於基督性質和位格的正統定義，正式結束了有關三位一體和基督論的長期爭論。大約在公元730年，大馬士革的約翰為東方教會闡明瞭這些道理。無論是東方還是西方，這些會議的決定都成了教義。
宗教改革時代。在宗教改革運動中，羅馬教和新教各教會在三位一體和基督本性問題上的認識基本上是一致的。尼西亞信經和卡爾西頓信條被普遍接受。路德主張神性和人性之間的交替，於是各自的特徵就成了共同的特徵。在基督里人性的一切特徵均為神性所用；人性則接受了神性的特徵。改正教會強調基督裡神性與人性的交流。
有兩個較小的新教派別不贊成尼西亞信經的立場。一個是索齊尼派。他們重新倡導神格唯一論的基本觀點，即無法接受三一真神的教義。現代的上帝一位論秉承了這種觀念。另一個是阿米尼烏斯派。他們在某些方面採取了一些古代宗派的觀點，如聖子低於聖父。這種看法在今天基督教各派中也有所反映。
安息日復臨信徒。本註釋的作者和編者坦率承認聖經中有一些重大的奧秘，是我們有限的智力所無法理解的。我們不可能用人類的語言予以準確地表達。基督裡神性和人性的聯合就是這樣的一個奧秘。安息日復臨信徒在闡述這類神學問題的時候，向來避免猜測和煩瑣的哲學推理，惟恐聖經的教訓因人的語言而變得模糊不清（見《教會證言》卷八279頁）。既然有靈感的聖經作者都沒有解釋清楚這些神聖的奧秘，為什麼未受聖靈啟發的作者還要試圖這麼作呢？但聖靈的啟示已經提供了充分的信息，使我們能部分理解救恩計劃的奧秘。安息日復臨信徒相信：
一，三一真神。上帝有三個位格──永在的父，永在之父的兒子主耶穌基督，和聖靈（見太28:19；約1:1,2；6:27；14:16,17,26；徒5:3,4；弗4:4-6；來1:1-3,8；見約1:1-3,14註釋）。
“天上的三一真神有三個永生的位格──聖父，聖子和聖靈”（《佈道論》615頁）。基督與聖父在“性質，品格，意志上原為一”（《先祖與先知》34頁），但“不是一個位格”（見《教會證言》卷八第269頁；參《教會證言》卷九第68頁）。聖靈“作為上帝也具有自己的位格”（《佈道論》616頁）。
見羅1:20-25懷愛倫註釋。
二，基督的神性和早已存在。無論就本性，智慧，權威和能力而言，基督都絕對是最高意義上的上帝（見賽9:6；彌5:2；約1:1-3；8:58；14:8-11；西1:15-17；2:9；來1:8；見彌5:2；太1:1,23；路1:35；約1:1-3；16:28；腓2:6-8；西2:9註釋）。
“基督是上帝的兒子。祂是早已存在，自有永有的。……祂一貫與永生的天父保持親密的關係。……祂與父同等，是無限的，全能的”（《佈道論》615頁；參《歷代願望》469，470頁；《佈道論》614頁；《先祖與先知》38，63頁）。
“基督實質上是最高意義上的上帝。祂在萬古以先與上帝同在，就是統治萬有，永遠受到稱頌的上帝。上帝神聖的兒子，主耶穌基督，從亙古就存在。祂與父原為一，但祂有獨立的位格”（懷愛倫，《評論與通訊》1906年4月5日；參《歷代願望》19頁）。
見約1:1-3,14；西2:9；3:10懷愛倫註釋。
三，基督的人性。主耶穌基督真正，完全是人，在所有的方面與世人相同，但祂是“無罪”的（林後5:21；見路24:39；約1:14；羅1:3,4；5:15；加4:4；腓2:7；提前2:5；來2:14,17；約壹1:1；4:2；約貳7；見太1:23；約1:14；腓2:6-8註釋）。
“基督是一個真正的人”（懷愛倫，《青年導報》1898年10月13日），“完全是人”（懷愛倫，《時兆》1897年6月17日），“承受了我們的本性”（懷愛倫，《評論與通訊》1890年2月18日）。“祂來作一個無助的嬰孩，承受了我們的人性”（ 《懷愛倫文稿》1895年21號）；“作為人類家庭的一員，祂不能免死”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1900年9月4日）。“祂為祂的門徒和自己禱告，說明祂與我們有一樣的需要，軟弱和缺乏”（《教會證言》卷二508頁；參《服務真詮》422頁）。
見約1:1-3,14；西1:26,27；來2:14-18懷愛倫註釋。
四，基督的道成肉身。道成肉身是神性和人性在耶穌基督這個位格中真實、完全、不能分開的結合。但神性和人性卻仍保持自己完整的特性（見太1:20；路1:35；約1:14；腓2:5-8；提前3:16；約壹4:2,3；見太1:18；約1:14；16:28；腓2:6-8註釋）。
“基督是真正的人。……但祂是上帝在肉身顯現”（懷愛倫《青年導報》1898年10月13日）。“祂的神性披上了人性。不可見的榮耀藏在看得見的人體之內”（《歷代願望》23頁）。“祂有神性和人性雙重性質。祂既是上帝，又是人”（懷愛倫《懷愛倫文稿》1903年76號）。
“馬利亞兒子的人性有沒有變成上帝兒子的神性呢？沒有。這兩種性質奇妙地結合在一個位格身上，那就是基督耶穌這個人”（ 《懷愛倫信函》1904年280號）。“人性不能取代神性，神性也不能取代人性”（懷愛倫，《時兆》1899年5月10日）。“神性不會降格到人性。神性有其自己的地位”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1890年2月18日）。
“祂展示了與神性相結合的完美人性，……每種性質都保持著自己的特點”（懷愛倫《全球總會公報》，1899年第4季，第102頁）。
“基督的人性與祂的神性是不能分離的”（《懷愛倫文稿》1897年106號）。
見約1:1-3,14；弗3:8；腓2:6-8；西2:9懷愛倫註釋。
五，基督的屈尊。主耶穌基督在道成肉身時自願受人性的侷限。所以祂在地上服務時就服從祂的父（見詩40:8；太26:39；約3:16；4:34；5:19,30；12:49；14:10；17:4,8；林後8:9；腓2:7,8；來2:9；見路1:35；2:49；約3:16；4:34；腓2:7,8註釋）。
上帝的兒子“脫下祂的王袍和王冠”（《教會證言》卷九第68頁），“自願將王權交還父手，從宇宙的寶座上走下來”（《歷代願望》22，23頁）。“祂自願披上人性。這是祂自主的行動，是祂自己同意的”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1900年9月4日）。“耶穌屈尊降格，自己卑微，取了人性”（懷愛倫，《時兆》1890年1月20日；參《教會證言》卷五第702頁）。“祂自己降卑，披上了必朽的人性”（懷愛倫，《評論與通訊》1900年9月4日）。
“上帝的兒子順服天父的旨意，倚靠祂的能力。基督將自己完全倒空，絲毫不顧念自己。祂接受了上帝對祂的計劃。天父每天都將自己的旨意啟示祂”（《歷代願望》208頁；參第664頁）。“當祂披上人性時，祂的生命就全然仰仗聖父的全能。祂在人性中握住了上帝的神性”（懷愛倫，《時兆》1897年6月17日）。
見路1:35懷愛倫註釋。
六，基督無罪完全。雖然耶穌“凡事受過試探，與我們一樣，”但祂是完全“無罪”的（見太4:1-11；羅8:3,4；林後5:21；來2:10；4:15；彼前2:21,22；約壹3:5；見太4:1-11；26:38,41；路2:40,52；來2:17；4:15註釋）。
我們的救主“承擔了人性的軟弱，凡事經受試煉和考驗”（懷愛倫，《時兆》1905年8月2日；參《歷代願望》49，117，139頁）。“像亞當的每個兒女一樣，耶穌承受了普遍的遺傳規律所造成的後果”（《歷代願望》49頁）。
“祂有可能犯罪；……但是祂不容自己有片時犯罪的傾向”（《懷愛倫信函》1895年8號，見本冊註釋第1128頁）。祂取了“人性，但沒有犯人的罪”（懷愛倫《時兆》1901年5月29日）。“撒但在伊甸園中曾取得勝利。耶穌則在人性中打敗魔鬼”（懷愛倫，《青年導報》1901年4月25日）。
“凡是世人通過信心不能從祂那裡獲得的能力和品性，耶穌都不曾使用過，祂完美的人性是祂每一個跟隨者都能夠獲得的“（《歷代願望》71頁；參第24頁）。“祂在自己的人性中保持了自己神聖品格的純潔”（《今日的生活》323頁）。“沒有絲毫的罪損毀了上帝在祂裡面的形象”（《歷代願望》73頁；參第123頁）。
見太4:1-11；路2:40,52；西2:9,10；來2:14-18；4:15懷愛倫註釋。
七，基督代人受死。基督的犧牲為世人的罪孽提供了充足而完全的贖價（見賽53:4-6；約3:14-17；林前15:3；來9:14；彼前3:18；4:1；約一2:2；見賽53:4；太16:13註釋）。
“祂因我們的罪受咒詛，這罪在祂本是無分的，使我們因祂的義而得以稱義，這義我們本來是無分的。祂忍受了我們該受的死，使我們能享受祂的生命”（《歷代願望》25頁）。
“基督在客西馬尼園代替人受苦。上帝兒子的人性在罪的恐懼面前猶豫了”（《懷愛倫文稿》1895年35號）。“要不是一位天使來加強祂忍受痛苦的力量，祂的人性很可能此時此地就喪生在罪的恐懼之下”（懷愛倫文稿》1895年35號）。
“基督為人類所付上的犧牲是充足並完全的。贖罪的條件已經履行了。基督到世上來的工作已經完成了”（《使徒行述》29頁；參《教會證言》卷五第575頁）。
見太26:36-46；27:50；西2:9；提前2:5懷愛倫註釋。
八，基督的復活。當祂的父呼喚祂從墳墓裡出來的時候，基督在祂的神性裡不僅有權捨命也有權再取回來（見約10:18；徒13:32,33；羅1:3,4；林前15:3-22；來13:20；彼前1:3；見《馬太福音》第28章補充註釋）。
“當那大能天使的聲音──上帝的兒子啊，出來吧，你的父召喚你──穿過墳墓到達基督的耳中時，救主便憑著在祂裡面的生命走了出來……基督在自己的神性裡有權打碎死亡的枷鎖”（《歷代願望》785頁；參第780頁）。
見可16:6懷愛倫註釋。
九，基督的昇天。我們的救主帶著祂榮耀的身體昇天了。祂在那裡繼續為我們服務（見可16:19；路24:39；約14:1-3；16:28；20:17；徒1:9-11；羅8:34；提前3:16；來7:25；8:1,2；9:24；約壹2:1,2；見徒1:9-11註釋）。
“上帝使祂的獨生子成為人類家庭的一員，永遠保留祂的人性。……上帝在祂兒子身上接受了人性並將其帶到了至高的天上”（《歷代願望》25頁）。
“所有的人都可以更加了解在天上的聖所中所進行的贖罪工作”（《教會證言》卷五第575頁）。
見徒1:9-11；來2:14-18懷愛倫註釋。
十，基督的升高。基督回到天上以後，恢復了祂道成肉身前與父同有的地位（見太28:18；約12:23；17:5；弗1:19-22；腓2:8,9；西1:18；提前2:5；來1:3；2:9；彼前1:11；見腓2:9註釋）。
“當基督穿過天國的城門時，祂在天使的歡呼崇拜中被擁為王。……基督受到尊榮，甚至超過在萬古以先祂與父同在時的榮耀。……作為祭司和君王，祂承受了天上地上所有的權柄”（《使徒行述》38，39頁；參《教會證言》卷八第268,269頁）。
這些奧秘和其他許多與救贖計劃有關的奧秘將是贖民在永恆歲月裡的學科。
900.en:
The Christian faith finds its source, its center, and its certainty in the historical Christ of the NT. As set forth in John 1:1–3, 14 (see comment there) and consistently affirmed throughout the NT, Christ is very God in the absolute and unqualified sense of the word, and truly man in every respect, sin excepted. At the incarnation deity and humanity were inseparably united in the person Jesus Christ, the unique God-man (see on Matt. 1:1).
But the Scriptures also declare that “the Lord our God is one Lord” (Deut. 6:4; Mark 12:29). The legacy of truth to which the Christian church fell heir thus included the paradox of a triune monotheism and the mystery of an incarnate God, both of which concepts transcend finite understanding and defy ultimate analysis and definition. However, to ardent Christians of apostolic times the dynamic fact of a crucified, risen, and living Lord, whom many of them had seen and heard (see John 1:14; 2 Peter 1:16; John 1:1–3), subordinated the related theological problems to a place of minor importance.
But as, with the passing of that generation (see Rev. 2:4; cf. Joshua 24:31), the vision of a living Lord grew dim and pristine purity and devotion waned, men turned increasingly from the practical realities of the gospel to its intriguing theoretical aspects, under the illusion that by searching with the intricate paraphernalia of philosophy they might, perhaps, find out God (see Job 11:7; Rom. 11:33). Among the diverse heresies that arose to trouble the church none were more serious than those concerned with the nature and person of Christ. Controversy over this problem rocked the church for centuries and was marked by a protracted succession of heresies, councils, and schisms.
For any but students of church history a detailed study of this controversy may appear barren of interest and practical value. But today, no less than in apostolic times, the certainty of the Christian faith centers in the historic Christ of the NT. Also, in one guise or another, various ancient heresies either live on or have been revived. From a brief review of the course of this controversy of earlier times modern Christians may learn to recognize, and to be vigilant against, the same errors that perplexed their devout brethren in ages past (see John 8:32; 1 John 4:1).
The two principal phases of this protracted debate are generally known as the Trinitarian and Christological controversies. The first was concerned with the status of Christ as God, and the second with the incarnate relationship between His divine and human natures. The Trinitarian controversy centered in the battles of the church with Docetism, Monarchianism, and Arianism, from the 1st to the 4th century, and the Christological controversy in its struggles with Nestorianism, Monophysitism, and Monotheletism, from the 5th to the 7th century.
The Apostolic Church. The belief of the apostolic church concerning Jesus is well summed up in Peter’s affirmation that Jesus is “the Christ, the Son of the living God” (Matt. 16:16), and in the simple declaration of faith quoted by Paul, “Jesus is the Lord [Gr. Kurios, here equivalent to the Heb. Yahweh]” (1 Cor. 12:3). The early Christians believed Him to be God in the highest sense of the word, and made this belief the cornerstone of their faith (see on Matt. 16:18). “Flesh and blood” could not reveal or explain this truth; it must be accepted by faith (see Matt. 16:17). This implicit certainty of the primitive church concerning the Trinity and the divine-human nature of Christ was founded on the explicit teachings of Jesus and the apostles. It was not many years after Christ had ascended to heaven, however, that “grievous wolves” began to make havoc of the flock, and that within the church itself men arose speaking “perverse things” and drawing disciples away after them (see Acts 20:29, 30).
Docetism and Gnosticism. The first error concerning the nature and person of Christ is generally referred to as Docetism. This name comes from a Greek word meaning “to appear.” Docetism assumed various forms, but its basic idea was that Christ only appeared to have a body, that He was a phantom and not a man at all. The Word became incarnate in appearance only. This heresy arose in apostolic times and persisted well on toward the close of the 2d century.
Docetism was particularly characteristic of such groups as the Ebionites and the Gnostics. The former were Jewish Christians who adhered strictly to the rites and practices of Judaism. The latter were primarily Gentile Christians. Gnosticism was little more than a blend of various pagan philosophies masquerading under the guise of Christian terminology.
An early and possibly authentic tradition identifies Simon Magus (see Acts 8:9–24) as the first proponent of error concerning the nature and person of Christ, and as the first Christian Gnostic. A few years later a Christian by the name of Cerinthus arose in Alexandria, a man who is classed by some as an Ebionite and by others as a Gnostic. He denied that Christ had come in the flesh, maintaining that His supposed incarnation was apparent and not real. The Ebionites were not Gnostics but held similar views concerning the humanity of Christ. They regarded Christ as only the literal son of Joseph, but selected by God as the Messiah because He distinguished Himself for piety and observance of the law, and was adopted as the Son of God at His baptism. One group of Ebionites, the Elkesaites, taught that Christ had been literally “begotten” of the Father in ages past, and was thus inferior to Him.
In contrast with the Ebionites, who looked upon Christ as essentially a superior type of human being, the Gnostics, generally speaking, denied that He was a human being at all. They conceived of Christ as a phantom, or “aeon,” that temporarily took possession of Jesus, an ordinary human being. Divinity was not truly incarnate. Concerning the tremendous impact of Gnosticism upon Christianity the church historian Latourette suggests the possibility that “for a time the majority of those who regarded themselves as Christians adhered to one or another of its many forms” (K. S. Latourette, A History of Christianity, p. 123). Arising gradually in apostolic times, Gnosticism reached the apex of its influence upon the church during the 2d century. Recognizing the grave threat posed by Gnosticism, the church fought back heroically.
Writing during the latter half of the 2d century, Irenaeus remarks that John wrote his Gospel with the specific purpose of refuting the Docetic views of Cerinthus (Irenaeus Against Heresies xi. 1, in Ante-Nicene Fathers, Vol. 1, p. 426; see John 1:1–3, 14; 20:30, 31). In the epistles John even more clearly warns against the Docetic heresy, whose advocates he brands as “anti-christ” (1 John 2:18–26; John 4:1–3, 9, 14; 2 John 7, 10). During his first imprisonment in Rome (c. .. 62), Paul cautioned the believers in Colossae against Docetic error (Col. 2:4, 8, 9, 18), and about the same time Peter voiced an even stronger warning (2 Peter 2:1–3). Jude (v. 4) refers to the Docetic heresy. The “Nicolaitanes” of Rev. 2:6 were Gnostics, though not necessarily Docetists (Irenaeus Against Heresies xi. 1, in Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1, p. 426).
During the first half of the 2d century various Gnostic teachers arose to plague the church with their noxious heresies. Prominent among these were Basilides and Valentinus, both of Alexandria. But perhaps the most influential—and successful— proponent of Docetic ideas was Marcion, during the latter half of the same century. He was by no means a Gnostic, but his views about Christ closely resembled those of the Gnostics. He held that the birth, physical life, and death of Jesus were not real, but merely gave the appearance of reality.
Against the gross errors of Docetism the church struggled courageously. During the latter half of the 2d century Irenaeus came boldly forward as the great champion of orthodoxy against heresy. His polemical work Against Heresies, specifically the Gnostic heresy, has survived to the present day. Irenaeus emphasized the unity of God.
Monarchianism. As the name indicates, Monarchianism stressed the unity of the Godhead. (A “monarch” is literally a “sole ruler.”) It was, in effect, a reaction against the many gods of the Gnostics and the two gods of Marcion—the God of the OT, whom he considered an evil God, and Christ, a God of love. As reactionary movements so often do, it went to the opposite extreme, and as a result became a heresy the church later found it necessary to condemn. The trend of which Monarchianism was characteristic may largely be credited with purging the church of Gnostic teachings, but the cure caused almost as much havoc as the malady it was supposed to remedy. The struggle with Monarchianism began toward the close of the 2d century and continued well into the 3d. There were two types of Monarchians, the Dynamists (from a Greek work meaning “power”), who taught that a divine power animated the human body of Jesus, who supposedly had no proper deity of His own and lacked a true human soul, and the Modalists, who conceived of one God who had revealed Himself in different ways.
In order to maintain the unity of the Godhead the Dynamists utterly denied the deity of Christ, whom they considered a mere man chosen of God to be the Messiah and raised to a level of deity. According to Adoptionism, one variation of this theory, the man Jesus attained to perfection and was adopted as the Son of God, at His baptism.
The Modalists taught that one God had revealed Himself in different ways. Denying any distinction in personality, they abandoned belief in the triune nature of the Godhead altogether. They accepted the true divinity of both Father and Son, but hastened to explain that the two were only different designations for the same divine being. This view is sometimes called Patripassianism, because, presumably, the Father became the Son at the incarnation, and subsequently suffered and died as the Christ. Similarly, at the resurrection, the Son became the Holy Spirit. From the most famous exponent of the theory, Sabellius, this view is also called Sabellianism. The Sabellians held that the names of the Trinity were merely designations by which the same divine person performed various cosmic functions. Thus prior to the incarnation this divine being was the Father; at the incarnation the Father became the Son; and at the resurrection the Son became the Holy Spirit.
Early in the 3d century Tertullian refuted Modalistic Monarchianism, stressing both the personality of the Son of God and the unity of the Godhead. However, he proposed that Christ was a subordinate order of God—a theory known as Subordinationism.
About the middle of the 3d century Origen advanced the theory of eternal generation, according to which the Father alone is God in the highest sense. The Son is coeternal with the Father, but “God” only in a derived sense. Origen believed that Christ’s soul— like all human souls, as he mistakenly supposed—pre-existed, but differed from all others in being pure and unfallen. The Logos, or divine Word, grew into indissoluble union with the human soul of Jesus. Distinguishing between theos, God, and ho theos, the God, in John 1:1, Origen concluded that the Son is not God in the primary and absolute sense, but “God” only by virtue of the communication of a secondary grade of divinity which might be termed theos, but not ho theos. Christ would thus be midway between things created and uncreated. Origen may be called the father of Arianism.
Arianism. Early in the 4th century Arius, a presbyter of the church in Alexandria, adopted Origen’s theory of the Logos, except that he denied any substance intermediate between God and created beings. From this he deduced that the Son is not divine in any sense of the word, but strictly a creature, though the very highest and first of all, and that therefore “there was [a time] when He was not.” He taught that there is only one being— the Father—to whom timeless existence can be attributed, that the Father created the Son out of nothing, and that prior to His generation by an act of the Father’s will the Son did not exist. To Arius, Christ was neither truly human, for He was without a human soul, nor yet truly divine, for He was without the essence and attributes of God. He was simply the most exalted of all created beings. The human being Jesus was chosen, by virtue of God’s foreknowledge of His triumph, to be the Christ.
At the First Council of Nicaea, convened in .. 325 to settle the Arian controversy, Athanasius stepped forward as “the father of orthodoxy,” maintaining that Jesus Christ always was, and that He came, not from the previously nonexistent, but from the very same essence as the Father. Applying the term homoousios, “one substance,” to Christ, the council affirmed its belief that He is of one and the same essence as the Father. Homoousios could not be understood otherwise. The council anathematized both Arianism and Sabellianism as the two principal deviations from exact truth, and declared that it was not denying the unity of the Godhead when it asserted the trinity, nor denying the trinity when it asserted the unity. Thus the Nicene Creed states that the Son is “begotten of the Father [… the essence of the Father, God of God], Light of Light, very God of very God, begotten, not made, being of one substance (ὁμοούςιον) with the Father” (cited in Philip Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, vol. 1, p. 29). This creed became the crucial test of Trinitarian orthodoxy.
The Arians rejected the decision of the council and went into schism, and for centuries Arianism proved to be the most formidable foe of the Roman Catholic Church (see on Dan. 7:8). Following the First Council of Nicaea a group sometimes called semi-Arians also troubled the church. Their key word was homoiousios, by which they described the Son as being of “like substance” with the Father, in contrast with the homoousios (“same substance”) of the Nicene Creed. Prominent among opponents of orthodoxy following the Council of Nicaea were Apollinaris and Marcellus. Both affirmed the true unity of the divine and the human in Christ but denied His true humanity, asserting that the divine will made of the human nature of Jesus a passive instrument. These various problems led to another council in the year 381, at Constantinople. This council reaffirmed the Nicene Creed, clarified its meaning, and declared the presence of two real natures in Christ.
Nestorianism. After the Council of Constantinople the attention of the church turned to the so-called Christological aspect of the problem of the nature and person of Christ. Attempts were made to define the nature of the divine and of the human elements in Christ, and to state the relationship between these two. How could two personal natures exist together in one person?
This phase of the controversy centered in two opposing schools of thought, one in Alexandria and the other in Antioch, in Syria. Both acknowledged the true unity of divinity and humanity in the one person, Jesus Christ, but the Alexandrian school emphasized the unity of the two natures and stressed the importance of deity, whereas the Antiochian school emphasized the distinction between the two natures and stressed the importance of the human aspect. Partisans of Antioch held that divinity and humanity had entered into a relation of constant coexistence and cooperation without actually merging. They separated the two natures in the one person, declaring that there was not a complete union but only permanent association. They made a sharp distinction between Christ as the Son of God and Christ as the Son of man, and gave the human nature more distinct recognition. They conceived of the unity of the two natures as accomplished through the unity of the respective wills. They preserved the reality and completeness of Christ’s human nature, but endangered the unity of the person. It was an imperfect, incomplete, loose, mechanical union, in which the two natures were not truly united in a single self-conscious person. The Alexandrians, on the other hand, conceived of a miraculous and complete commingling of the two natures, the human being fused into one with the divine and made subordinate to it. God thus entered humanity, and by means of this union of Godhood and manhood it became possible for Christ to lead mankind back to God.
The collision between these two schools of thought reached its climax in the Nestorian controversy early in the 5th century. Nestorius, of Antioch, conceded true deity and true humanity, but denied their union in a single self-conscious person. The Nestorian Christ is really two persons enjoying a moral and sympathetic union, neither however being decisively affected by the other. Deity is not humbled; humanity is not exalted. There is God and there is man; but there is no God-man.
The third ecumenical church council was called at Ephesus, in 431, for the purpose of settling this contest between the schools of Antioch and Alexandria. The council condemned Nestorius and his teachings, but did not consider it necessary to draw up a new creed to replace the Nicene Creed. Nothing was really settled or accomplished, except to widen the rift, and the ensuing controversy took on such proportions that all other doctrinal problems were laid aside.
Monophysitism. Following the Council at Ephesus still another theory, known as Monophysitism, or Eutychianism, arose and took the stage to set forth a conception of Christ precisely opposite to that of Nestorius. Eutyches, its leading exponent, contended that the original human nature of Jesus was transmuted into the divine nature at the incarnation, with the result that the human Jesus and divine Christ became one person and one nature. He asserted the unity of self-consciousness but so merged the two natures that, for practical purposes, they lost their individual identity.
Convened in 451 to discuss Nestorianism and Monophysitism, the Council of Chalcedon decided against both. Both Nestorius and Eutyches rejected the decision of the council and founded independent sects of Christianity, as Arius had done more than a century earlier.
The Council of Chalcedon affirmed the perfect divinity and the perfect humanity of Christ, declaring Him to be of one substance with the Father as to His divine nature and of one substance with us as to His human nature, except for sin. The identity of each nature was preserved and the two were declared to be distinct, unmingled, immutable, indivisible, inseparable. Divinity, not humanity, was recognized as the basis of Christ’s personality. Because the one person is a union of two natures, the suffering of the God-man was truly infinite; He suffered in His human nature and not in His divine nature, but the passion was infinite because the person is infinite. What later came to be known as the Chalcedon Symbol reads in part:
“We, then, following the holy Fathers, all with one consent, teach men to confess one and the same Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, the same perfect in Godhead and also perfect in manhood; truly God and truly man, of a reasonable [rational] soul and body; consubstantial [of one substance] with the Father according to the Godhead, and consubstantial with us according to the Manhood; in all things like unto us, without sin; begotten before all ages of the Father according to the Godhead, and in these latter days, for us and for our salvation, born of the Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, according to the Manhood; one and the same Christ, Son, Lord, Only-begotten, to the acknowledged in two natures, inconfusedly, unchangeably, indivisibly, inseparably; the distinction of natures being by no means taken away by the union, but rather the property of each nature being preserved, and concurring in one Person and one Subsistence” (Philip Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, vol. 2, p. 62).
The result of the Council of Chalcedon was to perpetuate and intensify schism in the East.
