Finally the emperor Justinian, convinced that the security of the empire required a settlement of the problem, permanently closed the schools at Antioch and Alexandria, the two centers of controversy. At a second Council of Constantinople, in 553, the church decided upon the forcible suppression of Monophysitism, which went into permanent schism and persists to this day in Christian sects such as the Jacobites, the Copts, and the Abyssinians. Reaffirming the Symbol of Chalcedon, the church achieved a definitive distinction between orthodoxy and heterodoxy.
Monotheletism. It is true that one question remained unsettled: Are the two natures, the divine and the human, actuated by one will controlling both natures, or by two wills? The Monothelites considered the divine will dominant, and the human will submerged in it. At the third Council of Constantinople, in 680, the church decided that the will is a matter of the natures rather than of the one person, and pronounced in favor of two wills in one volitional person. This completed the orthodox definition of the nature and person of Christ for the Western Church, and brought the protracted Trinitarian and Christological controversies formally to a close. About the year 730 John of Damascus recapitulated these doctrines for the Eastern Church. For both East and West the decisions of the councils became a matter of dogma.
In Reformation Times. The Reformation found both Roman and Protestant branches of Christianity in fundamental agreement on the Trinity and the nature of Christ. The Nicene Creed and the Symbol of Chalcedon proved generally acceptable to both. Luther taught a mutual interchange of characteristics between the two natures, so that what was characteristic of each became common to both. Everything human in Christ was appropriated by the divine nature, and humanity received what belonged to the divine nature. The Reformed churches emphasized the fellowship of the divine and the human in Christ.
Two minor Reformation groups differed from the Nicene position. The first of these was the Socinians, who revived the basic Monarchian idea that a divine Trinity is inconceivable. Modern Unitarianism perpetuates this concept. The second group was the Arminians, who took a view similar, in some respects, to that of certain earlier groups, that the Son is subordinate to the Father. This view is similarly reflected by various Christian sects today.
Seventh-day Adventists. The writers and editors of this commentary frankly confess that there are great mysteries in the Scriptures which transcend the limits of finite understanding and thus defy precise statement in human language. The union of the divine and the human in Christ is one such mystery. In dealing with theological questions of this kind Seventh-day Adventists have ever sought to eschew speculation and finespun philosophizing, lest they darken counsel with words (see 8T 279). If the inspired writers of the Bible have not made clear every detail of the divine mysteries, why should uninspired writers attempt to do so? However, Inspiration has provided sufficient information to enable us to understand in part the mystery of the plan of salvation. Seventh-day Adventists believe in:
1. The Godhead. The Godhead, or Trinity, consists of three persons—the eternal Father, the Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the eternal Father, and the Holy Spirit (see Matt. 28:19; John 1:1, 2; 6:27; 14:16, 17, 26; Acts 5:3, 4; Eph. 4:4–6; Heb. 1:1–3, 8; see on John 1:1–3, 14).
“There are three living persons of the heavenly trio … the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit” (Ev 615). Christ and the Father are “one in nature, in character, in purpose” (PP 34), but “not in person” (8T 269; cf. 9T 68). The Holy Spirit “is as much a person as God is a person” (Ev 616).
See EGW Supplementary Material on Rom. 1:20–25.
2. The Deity and Pre-existence of Christ. Christ is God in the supreme and unqualified sense of the term—in nature, in wisdom, in authority, and in power (see Isa. 9:6; Micah 5:2; John 1:1–3; 8:58; 14:8–11; Col. 1:15–17; 2:9; Heb. 1:8; see on Micah 5:2; Matt. 1:1, 23; Luke 1:35; John 1:1–3; 16:28; Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9).
“Christ is the pre-existent, self-existent Son of God. … There never was a time when He was not in close fellowship with the eternal God. … He was equal with God, infinite and omnipotent” (Ev 615; cf. DA 469, 470; Ev 614; PP 38, 63).
“Christ was God essentially, and in the highest sense. He was with God from all eternity, God over all, blessed forevermore. The Lord Jesus Christ, the divine Son of God, existed from eternity, a distinct person, yet one with the Father” (EGW RH April 5, 1906; cf. DA 19).
See EGW Supplementary Material on John 1:1–3, 14; COL 2:9; 3:10.
3. The Humanity of Christ. The Lord Jesus Christ was a true and complete human being, like other men in all respects except that He “knew no sin” (2 Cor. 5:21; see Luke 24:39; John 1:14; Rom. 1:3, 4; 5:15; Gal. 4:4; Phil. 2:7; 1 Tim. 2:5; Heb. 2:14, 17; 1 John 1:1; 4:2; 2 John 7; see on Matt. 1:23; John 1:14; Phil. 2:6–8).
“Christ was a real man” (EGW YI Oct. 13, 1898), “fully human” (EGW ST June 17, 1897), “a partaker of our nature” (EGW RH Feb. 18, 1890). “He came as a helpless babe, bearing the humanity we bear” (EGW MS 21, 1895), and “as a member of the human family He was mortal” (EGW RH Sept. 4, 1900). “He prayed for His disciples and for Himself, thus identifying Himself with our needs, our weaknesses, and our failings” (2T 508; cf. MH 422).
See EGW Supplementary Material on John 1:1–3, 14; Col. 1:26, 27; Heb. 2:14–18.
4. The Incarnation of Christ. The incarnation was a true, complete, and indissoluble union of the divine and human natures in the one person, Jesus Christ, each nature, however, being preserved intact and distinct from the other (see Matt. 1:20; Luke 1:35; John 1:14; Phil. 2:5–8; 1 Tim. 3:16; 1 John 4:2, 3; see on Matt. 1:18; John 1:14; 16:28; Phil. 2:6–8).
“Christ was a real man. … Yet He was God in the flesh” (EGW YI Oct. 13, 1898). “His divinity was veiled with humanity,—the invisible glory in the visible human form” (DA 23). “He has a two-fold nature, at once human and divine. He is both God and man” (EGW MS 76, 1903).
“Was the human nature of the Son of Mary changed into the divine nature of the Son of God? No; the two natures were mysteriously blended in one person—the Man Christ Jesus” (EGW letter 280, 1904). “The human did not take the place of the divine, nor the divine of the human” (EGW ST May 10, 1899). “Divinity was not degraded to humanity; divinity held its place” (EGW RH Feb. 18, 1890).
“He exhibited a perfect humanity, combined with deity; … preserving each nature distinct” (EGW GCB 4th quarter, 1899, p. 102).
“The humanity of Christ could not be separated from His divinity” (EGW MS 106, 1897).
See EGW Supplementary Material on John 1:1–3, 14; Eph. 3:8; Phil. 2:6–8; Col. 2:9.
5. The Subordination of Christ. Voluntarily assuming the limitations of human nature at the incarnation, the Lord Jesus Christ thereby subordinated Himself to the Father for the duration of His earthly ministry (see Ps. 40:8; Matt. 26:39; John 3:16; 4:34; 5:19, 30; 12:49; 14:10; 17:4, 8; 2 Cor. 8:9; Phil. 2:7, 8; Heb. 2:9; see on Luke 1:35; 2:49; John 3:16; 4:34; Phil. 2:7, 8).
“Laying aside His royal robe and kingly crown” (9T 68), the The Son of God “chose to give back the scepter into the Father’s hands, and to step down from the throne of the universe” (DA 22, 23). “He voluntarily assumed human nature. It was His own act, and by His own consent” (EGW RH Sept. 4, 1900). “Jesus condescended to humble Himself, to take human nature” (EGW ST Jan. 20, 1890; cf. 5T 702). “He humbled Himself, and took mortality upon Him” (EGW RH Sept. 4, 1900).
“The Son of God was surrendered to the Father’s will, and dependent upon His power. So utterly was Christ emptied of self that He made no plans for Himself. He accepted God’s plans for Him, and day by day the Father unfolded His plans” (DA 208; cf. 664). “While bearing human nature, He was dependent upon the Omnipotent for His life. In His humanity, He laid hold of the divinity of God” (EGW ST June 17, 1897).
See EGW Supplementary Material on Luke 1:35.
6. The Sinless Perfection of Christ. Though susceptible to temptation and “in all points tempted like as we are,” Jesus was nevertheless altogether “without sin” (see Matt. 4:1–11; Rom. 8:3, 4; 2 Cor. 5:21; Heb. 2:10; 4:15; 1 Peter 2:21, 22; 1 John 3:5; see on Matt. 4:1–11; 26:38, 41; Luke 2:40, 52; Heb. 2:17; 4:15).
Our Saviour “assumed the liabilities of human nature, to be proved and tried” (EGW ST Aug. 2, 1905; cf. DA 49, 117, 131). “Like every child of Adam He accepted the results of the working of the great law of heredity” (DA 49).
“He could have sinned; … but not for one moment was there in Him an evil propensity” (EGW letter 8, 1895, see p. 1128). He took “the nature but not the sinfulness of man” (EGW ST May 29, 1901). “He vanquished Satan in the same nature over which in Eden Satan obtained the victory” (EGW YI April 25, 1901).
“Jesus revealed no qualities, and exercised no powers, that men may not have through faith in Him. His perfect humanity is that which all His followers may possess” (DA 664; cf. 24). “In His human nature He maintained the purity of His divine character” (ML 323). “No trace of sin marred the image of God within Him” (DA 71; cf. 123).
See EGW Supplementary Material on Matt. 4:1–11; Luke 2:40, 52; Col. 2:9, 10; Heb. 2:14–18; 4:15.
7. The Vicarious Death of Christ. The sacrifice of Christ provided full and complete atonement for the sins of the world (see Isa. 53:4–6; John 3:14–17; 1 Cor. 15:3; Heb. 9:14; 1 Peter 3:18; 4:1; 1 John 2:2; see on Isa. 53:4; Matt. 16:13).
“He was condemned for our sins, in which He had no share, that we might be justified by His righteousness, in which we had no share. He suffered the death which was ours, that we might receive the life which was His” (DA 25).
“In the Garden of Gethsemane, Christ suffered in man’s stead, and the human nature of the Son of God staggered under the terrible horror of the guilt of sin” (EGW MS 35, 1895). “Human nature would then and there have died under the horror of the sense of sin, had not an angel from heaven strengthened Him to bear the agony” (EGW MS 35, 1895).
“Christ’s sacrifice in behalf of man was full and complete. The condition of the atonement had been fulfilled. The work for which He had come to this world had been accomplished” (AA 29; cf. 5T 575).
See EGW Supplementary Material on Matt. 26:36–46; 27:50; Col. 2:9; 1 Tim. 2:5.
8. The Resurrection of Christ. In His divinity Christ had power not only to lay down His life but to take it up again, when summoned forth from the grave by His Father (see John 10:18; Acts 13:32, 33; Rom. 1:3, 4; 1 Cor. 15:3–22; Heb. 13:20; 1 Peter 1:3; see Additional Note on Matt. 28).
“When the voice of the mighty angel was heard at Christ’s tomb, saying, Thy Father calls Thee, the Saviour came forth from the grave by the life that was in Himself. … In His divinity, Christ possessed the power to break the bonds of death” (DA 785; cf. 780).
See EGW Supplementary Material on Mark 16:6.
9. The Ascension of Christ. Our Saviour ascended to heaven in His glorified body, there to minister on our behalf (see Mark 16:19; Luke 24:39; John 14:1–3; 16:28; 20:17; Acts 1:9–11; Rom. 8:34; 1 Tim. 3:16; Heb. 7:25; 8:1, 2; 9:24; 1 John 2:1, 2; see on Acts 1:9–11).
“God gave His only-begotten Son to become one of the human family, forever to retain His human nature. … God has adopted human nature in the person of His Son, and has carried the same into the highest heaven” (DA 25).
“All need to become more intelligent in regard to the work of the atonement, which is going on in the sanctuary above” (5T 575).
See EGW Supplementary Material on Acts 1:9–11; Heb. 2:14–18.
10. The Exaltation of Christ. Upon His return to heaven Christ resumed the position that He had with the Father prior to the incarnation (see Matt. 28:18; John 12:23; 17:5; Eph. 1:19–22; Phil. 2:8, 9; Col. 1:18; 1 Tim. 2:5; Heb. 1:3; 2:9; 1 Peter 1:11; see on Phil. 2:9).
“When Christ passed within the heavenly gates, He was enthroned amidst the adoration of angels. … Christ was indeed glorified, even with the glory which He had with the Father from all eternity. … He had, as priest and king, received all authority in heaven and on earth” (AA 38, 39; cf. 8T 268, 269).
These and many other great mysteries connected with the plan of salvation will be the study of the redeemed throughout eternity.

14.en:
**Preparation of the passover.** Gr. paraskeuē tou pascha. This phrase is doubtless equivalent to the Heb. ‘ereb happesach, “eve of the Passover,” a common term in rabbinical literature designating the 14th of Nisan (see Mishnah Pesaḥim 4. 1, 5, 6; 5. 1; 10. 1, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 243, 271, 273; 287; 532; cf. Pesaḥim 1. 1, 3; 3. 6; 4. 7; 5. 4, 9; 7. 9, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 1, 46; 232; 275; 317, 318; 430). The expression may be compared with “eve” of the Sabbath, by which the Jews designated the day before the Sabbath, for which the equivalent Greek expression is paraskeuē (Mark 15:42; Luke 23:54). Paraskeuē is still the name for Friday in modern Greek. In the crucifixion year the paraskeuē for the Passover coincided with the paraskeuē, or “preparation” for the Sabbath (John 19:31, 42).
Thus, John seems to designate the crucifixion day as the 14th of Nisan. Those who hold that the crucifixion took place on the 15th of Nisan explain “preparation of the passover” to mean the Friday of the Passover week. Such a usage cannot be demonstrated elsewhere. For the day before the Sabbath, John elsewhere uses paraskeuē (vs. 31, 42). For a discussion of the problem of the day of the crucifixion see Additional Notes on Matthew 26, Note 1.
The Talmudic reference to the death of Jesus reads thus: “On the eve of the Passover Yeshu [Jesus] was hanged. … Since nothing was brought forward in his favour he was hanged on the eve of the Passover!” (Sanhedrin 43a, Soncino ed., p. 281).
**Sixth hour.** Probably Roman time, that is, about 6:00 o’clock in the morning. John’s Gospel was written near the close of the century, and chiefly for Gentile believers (see on ch. 1:38). Here he gives the time in terms familiar to them (see on Matt. 27:45). Elsewhere, he seems to reckon the hours of the day from sunrise rather than from midnight (see chs. 4:6, 52; 11:9).
**Behold your King!** Doubtless an ironical thrust at the Jews.
14.zh:
那日是預備逾越節的日子，約有午正。彼拉多對猶太人說：看哪，這是你們的王！

**預備逾越節的日子。**paraskeuē tou pascha。顯然相當於希伯來語的`ereb happesach（“逾越節前夕”），這是拉比們的文學作品中一個通常用來指尼散月十四號的詞（見《密西拿》Pesahim 4. 1,5,6；5. 1；10. 1，《塔木德》松奇諾版第243,271,273；287；532頁；參Pesahim 1. 1,3；3. 6；4. 7；5. 4,9；7. 9，《塔木德》松奇諾版第1,46；232；275；317,318；430頁）。這個詞可以與安息日的預備日進行比較。它在希臘語中的對應詞是paraskeuē（可15:42；路23:54）。Paraskeuē在現代希臘語中仍舊是星期五的名稱。在主釘十字架的那一年，逾越節的預備日（paraskeuē）和安息日的預備日（paraskeuē）（約19:31,42）是重合的。
約翰就這樣似乎認定主釘十字架的日子是尼散月十四日。那些認為主釘十字架在尼散月十五號的人解釋說“預備逾越節的日子”是指逾越節那一週的星期五。這種用法不能用在別處。關於安息日前的這一天，約翰在別處用的是paraskeuē（第31,42節）。關於主釘十字架的日子問題，見《馬太福音》第26章補充註釋一。
《塔木德》這樣記錄耶穌的死：“在逾越節的前夕，Yeshu（耶穌）被掛在木頭上。……既然沒有提出什麼對他有利的證據，他就在逾越節的前夕被掛在木頭上！”（Sanhedrin43a，松奇諾版第281頁）。
**午正。**這可能是羅馬時間，即早上六點鐘。《約翰福音》是在公元1世紀將近結束的時候寫成的，主要是為外邦信徒寫的（見約1:38註釋）。這裡他給出的時間對於他們來說是很熟悉的（見太27:45註釋）。而在別的地方他是從日出，而不是從午夜，開始計算一天的時間的（見約4:6,52；11:9）。
看哪，這是你們的王!這無疑是對猶太人一個辛辣的諷刺。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–15節）**。見太27：22.23懷愛倫註釋。

15.en: **No king but Caesar.** These words were not carefully weighed, for the Jews were not ready to throw away their Messianic hope or formally to repudiate God as their king (see Judges 8:23; 1 Sam. 8:7; 12:12). Their subterfuge reflects their anxiety to get rid of Jesus. Nevertheless, by this declaration they withdrew from the covenant relationship with God and ceased longer to be His chosen people (see DA 737, 738).
15.zh:
他們喊著說：除掉他！除掉他！釘他在十字架上！彼拉多說：我可以把你們的王釘十字架嗎？祭司長回答說：除了該撒，我們沒有王。

**除了凱撒，我們沒有王。**他們這些話沒有經過慎重的考慮，因為猶太人還沒有準備要放棄他們關於彌賽亞的希望或正式拒絕上帝作他們的王（見士8:23；撒上8:7；12:12）。他們的謊言反映出他們急於要除掉耶穌。然而，他們這句話卻使他們退出了與上帝所立的約，他們也不再是祂的選民了（見《歷代願望》737，738頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第294頁；《安息日學訓言》第47頁；《歷代願望》第745頁；《先祖與先知》第477頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–16節）**。見太27：25.26懷愛倫註釋。

38.en: **Joseph of Arimathaea.** [The Burial, John 19:38–42=Matt. 27:57–61=Mark 15:42–47=Luke 23:50–56. Major comment: Matthew and Mark.] All four Gospels describe Joseph’s part in the burial of Jesus. John alone observes that he was secretly a disciple.
38.zh:
這些事以後，有亞利馬太人約瑟，是耶穌的門徒，只因怕猶太人，就暗暗的作門徒。他來求彼拉多，要把耶穌的身體領去。彼拉多允准，他就把耶穌的身體領去了。

**亞利馬太人約瑟。**四卷福音書都記載了約瑟參與耶穌的埋葬。只有約翰提到他暗地裡作耶穌的門徒。.
**懷愛倫註釋（38–39節）**。見太27：38懷愛倫註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（38–42節）**。《使徒行述》第104頁；《救贖的故事》第227頁。

39.en:
**Nicodemus** See on ch. 3:1.
**Myrrh.** See on Matt. 2:11.
**Aloes.** An aromatic resin from the tree Aquilaria agallocha. The product is mentioned only here in the NT. In the OT it is mentioned in Num. 24:6; Ps. 45:8; S. of Sol. 4:14.
**Pound.** Gr. litra, about 11 1/2 oz. (see on ch. 12:3). “An hundred pound weight” would therefore be about 72 lb. The large quantity was doubtless purchased at considerable cost.
39.zh:
又有尼哥底母，就是先前夜裡去見耶穌的，帶著沒藥和沉香約有一百斤前來。

**尼哥底母。**見約3:1註釋。
**沒藥。**見太2:11註釋。
**沉香。**這是一種芳香的樹脂，來自一種叫做Aquilaria agallocha的樹木。這種產品《新約》中只在這裡提到過。《舊約》的民24:6；詩45:8；歌4:14有提到。
**斤。**litra，約326克，見約12:3註釋）。“一百斤”約合我們現在的32.7斤。這麼大數量的名貴藥材必定價值不菲。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第773頁。

34.en: **Blood and water.** Various explanations have been offered for this phenomenon. As early as 1847 Dr. W. Stroud (Physical Cause of the Death of Christ) proposed that the blood and water was evidence that Jesus died of a physical rupture of the heart. This theory lacks verification. That Jesus died of a broken heart as a result of the awful pressure of the weight of the sins of the world is evident (see DA 772), but to attempt a precise physical diagnosis from the meager details of the gospel narrative is precarious. The flow of blood and water was indeed remarkable, inasmuch as blood does not normally flow from a corpse, at least not copiously. John calls especial attention to the flow and solemnly attests it (vs. 34, 35). It has been suggested that he notes the fact in order to set forth the true humanity of Jesus, thus to combat the Docetic heresy of his day which claimed that Jesus became incarnate in appearance only. The Church Fathers gave a highly allegorical interpretation to the passage.
34.zh:
惟有一個兵拿槍扎他的肋旁，隨即有血和水流出來。

**血和水。**對於這一現象有不同的解釋。早在1847年，斯特勞德醫生（《基督死亡的自然原因》）就提出，出現血和水證明耶穌死於自然的心臟破裂。但是這種說法缺乏證明。耶穌的心因為全世界罪惡可怕的重壓而撕裂，這一點是可以肯定的（見《歷代願望》772頁），但是想從福音書敘述不完全的細節中得出精確的肉體方面的診斷，這樣做也是很危險的。血和水流出來的確是一件異常的事，因為血不是正常地從屍體裡流出來的，至少不是大量流出來的。約翰叫人特別注意這件事並且嚴肅地為之作證（第34,35節）。有人認為約翰強調這個事實是為了證明耶穌的人性，以此去打擊他那個時代出現的說耶穌僅僅是在外形上道成肉身之幻影說的異端。教父們給予這段經文高度比喻性的解釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《早期著作》第209頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（34–37節）**。《歷代願望》第772頁。

41.zh:
在耶穌釘十字架的地方有一個園子，園子裡有一座新墳墓，是從來沒有葬過人的。

**園子。**只有約翰提到這一點。

30.en: **It is finished.** Jesus had completed the work His Father had given Him to do (ch. 4:34). Every step in the plan of redemption, laid before the foundation of the world, had been completed according to schedule (see on Luke 2:49). Satan had been unsuccessful in his attempts to overthrow the plan. Christ’s victory assured the salvation of man. See DA 758–764.
30.zh:
耶穌嘗（原文作受）了那醋，就說：成了！便低下頭，將靈魂交付神了。

**成了。**耶穌已經完成了祂父交託祂要做的工作（約4:34）。創立世界以先就已制訂的救贖計劃的每一步都已按照時間表完成了（見路2:49註釋）。撒但推翻這個計劃的企圖失敗了。基督的勝利確保了人類的得救。見《歷代願望》758-764頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第490，679，709，732，756，758，764，771，775，787，834頁；《早期著作》第177，180，184，209，253，281頁；《善惡之爭》第348，503頁；《先祖與先知》第70頁；《救贖的故事》第227頁；《證言》卷二第211，212頁；《證言》卷四第82頁。

42.zh:
只因是猶太人的預備日，又因那墳墓近，他們就把耶穌安放在那裡。

**預備日。**paraskeuē（見第14節註釋）。

16.en: **Delivered he him.** John does not mention the incident of the washing of hands (Matt. 27:24). The handling over was not to the Jews but to the Roman authorities responsible for carrying out the sentence of crucifixion.
16.zh:
於是彼拉多將耶穌交給他們去釘十字架。

**彼拉多將耶穌交給。**約翰沒有記錄彼拉多當眾洗手的事（太27:24）。他沒有把耶穌交給猶太人，而是交給羅馬當局負責行刑的人。
**[耶穌釘十字架：**約19:17-37=太27:31b-56=可15:20-41=路23:26-49。註釋主要在《馬太福音》和《約翰福音》。見本卷註釋225頁地圖；232，233頁圖表]。
**懷愛倫註釋（16–30節）**。《歷代願望》第741-757頁。

36.zh:
這些事成了，為要應驗經上的話說：他的骨頭一根也不可折斷。

**不可折斷。**見出12:46註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第277頁。

33.en: **Dead already.** It was most unusual to have death come so soon after crucifixion. Some victims lived for several days. Origen, who lived in the time when crucifixion was still practiced, mentions that the majority of the victims lived through the night and through the next day (Origen, Commentary on Matthew, “Series Veteris Interpretationis,” sec. 140, in J. P. Migne, Patrologia Graeca, vol. 13, col. 1793; cf. Eusebius Ecclesiastical History viii. 8).
33.zh:
只是來到耶穌那裡，見他已經死了，就不打斷他的腿。

**已經死了。**釘十字架後這麼快就死亡實屬罕見。一些被釘十字架的人有的會活上數天之久。奧裡金──十字架的刑罰在他那個時代仍舊存在──提到大多數受刑的人會活過當晚並第二天一整天（奧裡《馬太福音註釋》，“Series Veteris Interpretationis，” 140,in J. P. Migne,Patrologia Graeca，第十三卷，1793；參《優西比烏斯教會史》Eusebius Ecclesiastical History viii. 8）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第771頁。

1.zh:
當下彼拉多將耶穌鞭打了。

**將耶穌鞭打了。**第19章繼續從約18:39開始的敘述。這是第一次鞭打。耶穌在被判釘十字架之後再次遭受鞭打（見太27:26註釋）。彼拉多第一次鞭打耶穌，是希望如果可能的話，能引起那群兇殘暴徒的同情心（見《歷代願望》735頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–16節）**。《歷代願望》第732-740頁。
1.en: **Scourged him.** Chapter 19 continues the narrative begun in ch. 18:39. This was the first flogging. Jesus was flogged again in connection with the sentence of crucifixion (see on Matt. 27:26). The purpose of the first flogging was to elicit, if possible, the compassion of the bloodthirsty mob (see DA 735).

4.zh:
彼拉多又出來對眾人說：我帶他出來見你們，叫你們知道我查不出他有什麼罪來。

**我查不出他有什麼罪來。**參約18:38；19:6；彼前2:21,22。彼拉多的這些話顯出了他的軟弱。如果耶穌是無辜的，他就不應該讓祂遭受鞭打。一次違背良心就會導致下一次，直到彼拉多完全喪失了公義的原則為止。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第749頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《歷代願望》第735頁。
4.en: **I find no fault.** Compare John 18:38; 19:6; 1 Peter 2:21, 22. By these words Pilate revealed his weakness. If Jesus was innocent, he should not have permitted Him to be scourged. One violation of conscience led to another until Pilate surrendered every particle of justice.

5.zh:
耶穌出來，戴著荊棘冠冕，穿著紫袍。彼拉多對他們說：你們看這個人！

**看這個人!。**彼拉多喊這句話的目的無疑是要激起群眾的同情心。耶穌穿著他們侮辱祂給祂套上的王袍站在他們面前，頭上戴著荊棘的冠冕，祂因剛才的鞭打而血流如注、臉色蒼白，但他仍舊保持著君王的風采。彼拉多感覺猶太人領袖的要求可能真的必須予以滿足。但他在這一點上受到了欺騙。
為什麼彼拉多選用“人”這個詞還不得而知。但他在毫無察覺的情況下倒是說出了一個偉大的真理。這位在他面前的，永恆的道（見約1:1註釋），已經成了一個人（見約1:14註釋）。祂的確是人子（見太1:1；可2:10註釋），但祂同時也是上帝的兒子（見路1:35註釋）。祂道成肉身和死亡為我們贏得了永恆的救贖。
5.en:
**Behold the man!** Pilate’s object in this exclamation was doubtless to excite the pity of the multitude. There stood Jesus before them in His mock kingly robes, crowned with a crown of thorns, bleeding and pale from His recent flogging, yet of kingly mien. Surely, Pilate felt, the demands of the Jewish leaders would be satisfied. But in this he was deceived.
Precisely why Pilate chose to use the term “man” cannot be known. Innocently he uttered a great truth. The One before him, the eternal Word (see on ch. 1:1), had become man (see on ch. 1:14). He was, indeed, the Son of man (see on Matt. 1:1; Mark 2:10), but also the Son of God (see on Luke 1:35). His incarnation and death won for us eternal salvation.

6.zh:
祭司長和差役看見他，就喊著說：釘他十字架！釘他十字架！彼拉多說：你們自己把他釘十字架吧！我查不出他有什麼罪來。

**你們自己把祂釘十字架。**這句話說明彼拉多沒有將事情交給公會去處理，因為釘十字架是羅馬人執行死刑的方式。如果讓猶太人選擇執行死刑的方式，他們會選擇用石頭打（見約18:32註釋）。彼拉多似乎是在憤怒地嘲諷中說：“如果你們要求釘祂十字架，你們（在希臘原文中是強調的）就必須執行這項死刑；我在祂身上找不出什麼錯。”
**我查不出祂有什麼罪來。**這是彼拉多第三次申明這一事實（見約18:38；19:4）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第43頁；《早期著作》第109頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–11節）**。《歷代願望》第736頁；【 SDA5.1149】。
6.en:
**Take ye him.** The added words “and crucify him” show that Pilate was not turning the matter over to the Sanhedrin, for crucifixion was a Roman form of capital punishment. Had the Jews inflicted the death penalty it would have been by stoning (see on ch. 18:32). Pilate seems to be speaking in exasperation and in angry sarcasm: “If you demand crucifixion you [emphatic in the Greek] must carry out the sentence; I find no guilt in him.”
**No fault.** This is the third time Pilate mentions the fact (see chs. 18:38; 19:4).

7.zh:
猶太人回答說：我們有律法，按那律法，他是該死的，因他以自己為神的兒子。

**按那律法。**見約18:32註釋；參利24:16。
**上帝的兒子。**見約5:18；10:33註釋。
7.en:
**By our law.** See on John 18:32; cf. Lev. 24:16.
**Son of God.** See on chs. 5:18; 10:33.

8.zh:
彼拉多聽見這話，越發害怕，

**越發害怕。**他的妻子給彼拉多帶信，把她的夢告訴他（太27:19），這是他早先害怕的原因。耶穌超自然身份的暗示使他的心中充滿了不祥之兆。
8.en: **The more afraid.** The letter from his wife informing Pilate of her dream (Matt. 27:19) was the earlier occasion of fear. The implication that Jesus was a supernatural being filled him with foreboding.

9.zh:
又進衙門，對耶穌說：你是哪裡來的？耶穌卻不回答。

**衙門。**見太27:2註釋。
你是哪裡來的？對耶穌超自然身份暗示的恐懼，使彼拉多進一步詢問耶穌的出身。他對基督在地上的家鄉並不感興趣，對於這一點他已經知道了（路23:6,7）。但是有一種奇異的恐懼抓住了他的思想，使他感覺到這位站在他面前的高貴的人可能真的是一位神明。
**卻不回答。**參耶穌在該亞法（太26:63）和希律面前（路23:9）的沉默。彼拉多本來有機會學習真理的（見約18:38註釋）。進一步的啟示已經沒有什麼作用了。耶穌知道什麼時候應該說話，什麼時候應該保持緘默。
9.en:
**Judgment hall.** See on Matt. 27:2.
**Whence art thou?** Fear at the suggestion that Jesus was some supernatural being elicited Pilate’s further inquiry into Jesus’ origin. He was not interested in the country of Christ’s origin; with that he was already familiar (Luke 23:6, 7). But a mysterious fear gripped him at the thought that the noble being standing before him might be divine.
**No answer.** Compare the silence before Caiaphas (Matt. 26:63) and before Herod (Luke 23:9). Pilate had had his opportunity to learn the truth (see on John 18:38). Further enlightenment would have availed nothing. Jesus knew when to speak and when to keep silent.

10.zh:
彼拉多說：你不對我說話嗎？你豈不知我有權柄釋放你，也有權柄把你釘十字架嗎？

你不對我說話嗎？彼拉多認為耶穌藐視他的權柄。因此有些惱火。
**權柄。**exousia，“權力”。
10.en:
**Speakest thou not?** Pilate was provoked at what might be termed contempt of court.
**Power.** Gr. exousia, “authority.”

11.zh:
耶穌回答說：若不是從上頭賜給你的，你就毫無權柄辦我。所以，把我交給你的那人罪更重了。

**賜給你。**見但4:17；羅13:1註釋。
**把我交給你的那人。**這不是指猶大（約6:71；12:4；13:2；18:2），因為猶大沒有將耶穌交給羅馬當局。這裡指的是作為大祭司和猶太人最高官方代表的該亞法（參見約18:35）。
**罪更重了。**該亞法行使公權，同時他自稱敬拜上帝，擁有上帝所賜的權威，向百姓解釋祂的律法。因此他的罪更大了。他還抵擋那更大的光。耶穌已經屢次向他們證明他的神性，但猶太人的領袖硬著心抵擋每一束亮光。
該亞法的“罪更重”並不代表彼拉多沒有罪責。他作為羅馬的巡撫有他的職責所在。他本可以拒絕將耶穌交出去。救贖主是會死去，但那罪就不會歸在他彼拉多的身上了。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–15節）**。《歷代願望》第737頁。
11.en:
**Given thee.** See on Dan. 4:17; Rom. 13:1.
**He that delivered.** This is not Judas (chs. 6:71; 12:4; 13:2; 18:2), for Judas did not deliver Jesus to the Roman authorities. Caiaphas as high priest and highest official representative of the Jews is the one here indicted (cf. ch. 18:35).
**Greater sin.** Caiaphas exercised delegated authority, but at the same time he presumed to be a worshiper of the God who delegated authority and the interpreter of divine law to the people. His guilt was therefore greater. He also sinned against the greater light. Jesus had given repeated evidences of divinity, but the Jewish leaders had steeled their hearts against every ray of light.
The fact that Caiaphas had the “greater sin” did not mean that Pilate was without guilt. The Roman governor bore his share of the responsibility. He might have refused to deliver Jesus. The Saviour would have died, but the guilt would not have rested upon Pilate.

12.zh:
從此，彼拉多想要釋放耶穌，無奈猶太人喊著說：你若釋放這個人，就不是該撒的忠臣（原文作朋友）。凡以自己為王的，就是背叛該撒了。

**釋放耶穌。**耶穌的回答（第11節）加深了彼拉多的恐懼。這個心地剛硬的羅馬巡撫被他面前這個神秘人物的言行所深深震撼。
**凱撒的忠臣（原文作“朋友“）。**就是凱撒的堅定支持者。猶太人最終抓住了彼拉多一個致命的弱點。他們的回答是一種脅迫，因為羅馬皇帝如果知道了彼拉多故意釋放一個自稱是王的人，那他巡撫的位置恐怕就難保了。對於自身安全的顧慮導致彼拉多忘記了他對面前這個犯人良心上的敬畏。
猶太領袖們的回答明顯是虛偽的。他們這些控告耶穌的人就是凱撒的朋友嗎？在所有被佔領國中，猶太人是最仇恨羅馬人統治的，他們虛情假意為之榮譽發熱心的凱撒是他們心底裡最蔑視、最憎恨的人。
12.en:
**To release him.** The answer of Jesus (v. 11) heightened Pilate’s fears. The hardened governor was deeply impressed by the words and conduct of the mysterious person before him.
**Cæsar’s friend.** That is, a stanch supporter of Caesar. The Jews had at last struck upon an argument that was to prove successful. Their reply was a threat, for if the emperor should learn that Pilate had attempted to shield a pretender to the title of king, the governor’s position would be in danger. Fear for his safety led Pilate to forget the religious awe with which he had regarded the prisoner.
The reply of the leaders was conspicuously hypocritical. Were the accusers friends of Caesar? Of all peoples none were more bitter than the Jews against the Roman yoke, and yet they had the duplicity to feign zealous honor for Caesar, whom they so heartily despised.

13.zh:
彼拉多聽見這話，就帶耶穌出來，到了一個地方，名叫鋪華石處，希伯來話叫厄巴大，就在那裡坐堂。

**帶耶穌。**即從羅馬總督府彼拉多剛才與耶穌單獨會面（第9節）的地方出來。猶太人的領袖們不進總督府免得他們受汙穢不能吃逾越節的筵席（約18:28）。
**鋪華石處。**lithostrōton，意思是一條石頭鑲嵌的道路，鋪的可能是大理石。
**厄巴大。**這個詞起源不詳。有人認為它源自亞蘭語geba'（“高的”），因此用它來描述一個位置較高的地方。這個地方很可能就緊挨著總督府。關於總督府的位置，見太27:2註釋。
**坐堂。**可能是外面一個臨時準備好的座位，這樣猶太人就不必進審判廳了。
13.en:
**Brought Jesus.** That is, from the Praetorium into which Pilate had conducted Jesus for a private interview (v. 9). The Jewish leaders would not enter the Praetorium lest they be defiled and prevented from eating the Passover (ch. 18:28).
**Judgment seat.** Perhaps an improvised chair made ready outside, inasmuch as the Jews would not enter the judgment hall.
**Pavement.** Gr. lithostrōton, meaning a mosaic pavement, probably of marble.
**Gabbatha.** A word of uncertain derivation. Some derive it from the Aramaic geba’, “to be high,” and hence describe it as an elevated place. The location was probably immediately outside the Praetorium. For the location of the latter see on Matt. 27:2.

17.zh:
他們就把耶穌帶了去。耶穌背著自己的十字架出來，到了一個地方，名叫髑髏地，希伯來話叫各各他。

**揹著自己的十字架。**關於到髑髏地去路上發生的事，見路23:26-32。
17.en: **Bearing his cross.** [The Crucifixion, John 19:17–37=Matt. 27:31b–56=Mark 15:20–41=Luke 23:26–49. Major comment: Matthew and John. See Betrayal, Trial and Crucifixion of Jesus; Crucifixion In Relation To Passover, Passion Week, Resurrection to Ascension.] For incidents on the way to Calvary see Luke 23:26–32.

18.zh:
他們就在那裡釘他在十字架上，還有兩個人和他一同釘著，一邊一個，耶穌在中間。

**釘祂在十字架上。**見太27:33-35註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第751頁；見太27:38懷愛倫註釋。
18.en: **Crucified him.** See on Matt. 27:33–35.

19.zh:
彼拉多又用牌子寫了一個名號，安在十字架上，寫的是：猶太人的王，拿撒勒人耶穌。

**懷愛倫註釋（19–22節）**。《歷代願望》第745頁；見太27:37懷愛倫註釋。

21.zh:
猶太人的祭司長就對彼拉多說：不要寫猶太人的王，要寫他自己說：我是猶太人的王。

**不要寫。**只有約翰記錄了猶太人的這個抗議。關於它的意義，見太27:37註釋。
21.en: **Write not.** Only John records this protest. For the implications see on Matt. 27:37.

22.zh:
彼拉多說：我所寫的，我已經寫上了。

**我已經寫上了。**彼拉多非常厭惡猶太人，因此決定不再滿足他們任何得寸進尺的要求。因為這些猶太人的壓力，他不顧自己妻子的警告，拋棄自己作為法官的良知，定了一個無辜之人的死罪。他想告訴他們，如果他願意他是可以堅定的。
22.en: **I have written.** Pilate was greatly vexed with the Jews and resolved not to gratify them further. Through their pressure, against his wife’s warning and against his own better judgment, he had condemned an innocent man. He showed that he could be firm if he chose.

23.zh:
兵丁既然將耶穌釘在十字架上，就拿他的衣服分為四分，每兵一分；又拿他的裡衣，這件裡衣原來沒有縫兒，是上下一片織成的。

**分為四份。**這件衣服成了行刑者的財產。只有約翰提到了行刑士兵的人數。以下是他們分得的東西，帽子，草鞋，腰帶，披巾，帶須邊的外衣（羅泊遜）。被釘十字架的兩個強盜的衣服如何處置，經上沒有說。
**裡衣。**chitōn，貼身穿的衣服（見太5:40註釋）。
**沒有縫兒。**這件衣服的織法可能和大祭司服類似。對此約瑟弗斯描述說：“這件衣服不是由兩片布料在肩膀和兩邊的部位縫合而成的，它是一塊從上到下一體織成的布料，在脖子的部位有一個開口”（《猶太古代史》Antiquities iii. 7. 4 [161]；卷四第393頁）。
23.en:
**Made four parts.** The clothing became the property of the executioners. Only John mentions the number of the soldiers. The following division has been suggested, the headgear, the sandals, the girdle, and the tallith, the outer garment with fringes (Robertson). What was done with the clothing of the crucified robbers is not disclosed.
**Coat.** Gr. chitōn, an inner garment (see on Matt. 5:40).
**Without seam.** The garment may have been woven similarly to that of the high priest, which Josephus describes as follows, “But this tunic is not composed of two pieces, to be stitched at the shoulders and at the sides: it is one long woven cloth, with a slit for the neck” (Antiquities iii. 7. 4 [161]; Loeb ed., vol. 4, p. 393).

24.zh:
他們就彼此說：我們不要撕開，只要拈鬮，看誰得著。這要應驗經上的話說：他們分了我的外衣，為我的裡衣拈鬮。兵丁果然做了這事。

**應驗。**可譯為：“結果經文應驗了”（見太1:22；約9:3註釋；參約11:4；12:38註釋）。
**他們分了。**引用詩22:18。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第746頁。
24.en:
**Might be fulfilled.** The passage may be rendered, “as a result the Scripture was fulfilled” (see on Matt. 1:22; John 9:3; cf. on John 11:4; 12:38).
**They parted.** The quotation is from Ps. 22:18.

25.zh:
站在耶穌十字架旁邊的，有他母親與他母親的姊妹，並革羅罷的妻子馬利亞，和抹大拉的馬利亞。

**祂母親。**約翰從不在他的福音書中提耶穌母親的名字。耶穌在祂肉體和心靈雙重的痛苦中並沒有忘記自己的母親。祂看見她站在那裡，站在十字架的下面。祂瞭解她的痛苦並把她交給約翰照顧。
**與祂母親的姐妹。**我們不清楚約翰在本節中到底是提到了三個婦人，還是四個。可能“他母親的姐妹”和“革羅罷的妻子馬利亞”是指同一個人。革羅罷可能就是路24:18中的革流巴（見該處註釋）。按我們現有的信息還無法確定。
**抹大拉的馬利亞。**關於她的身份，見《路加福音》第7章補充註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第744頁；《早期著作》第176頁。
25.en:
**His mother.** John does not mention her name in his Gospel. In his bodily pain and mental suffering Jesus did not forget His mother. He saw her standing there, at the foot of the cross. He well knew her distress, and commended her to the care of John.
**And his mother’s sister.** It is not clear whether, in this verse, John mentions three or four women. It is possible that the phrases “his mother’s sister” and “Mary the wife of Cleophas” are in apposition. Cleophas may possibly be the Cleophas of Luke 24:18 (see comment there). With our present knowledge exact identity is impossible.
**Mary Magdalene.** For her identity see Additional Note on Luke 7.

26.zh:
耶穌見母親和他所愛的那門徒站在旁邊，就對他母親說：母親（原文作婦人），看，你的兒子！

**祂所愛的。**見約13:23註釋。
**母親（原文作“婦人“）。**關於這種稱呼，見約2:4註釋。
**看，你的兒子。**!約翰與耶穌的關係要比其他門徒與耶穌的關係更為親密一些（見本卷註釋第891,892頁），因此他比他們更能忠實地擔負起一個做兒子的責任。耶穌將祂的母親交託給一個門徒，人們認為這表明當時約瑟已經不在了，還有些人認為這表示馬利亞自己沒有其他的兒子了，至少沒有照顧她的兒子了。約瑟前一次婚姻所生的兒子（見太12:46註釋），即耶穌的兄長們，現在不相信耶穌，這使耶穌感到他們對待馬利亞的態度或許會像先前對待祂一樣（見約7:3-5註釋），是批評和無情的。
**懷愛倫註釋（26–27節）**。《使徒行述》第539頁；《歷代願望》第752頁；《早期著作》第177頁；《成聖的人生》第53頁。
26.en:
**Whom he loved.** See on ch. 13:23.
**Woman.** For this form of address see on ch. 2:4.
**Behold thy son!** The relationship between John and Jesus was more intimate than that between Jesus and the other disciples (see pp. 891, 892), and John could therefore carry out the duties of a son more faithfully than they. That Jesus entrusted His mother to a disciple is acknowledged as evidence that Joseph no longer lived, and is thought by some to indicate that Mary had no other sons of her own, at least in a position to care for her. Jesus’ older brothers, sons of Joseph by a former marriage (see on Matt. 12:46), did not, at this time, believe in Him, and He may have felt that their attitude toward Mary would have been critical and unsympathetic, as it had been toward Him (see on John 7:3–5).

27.zh:
又對那門徒說：看，你的母親！從此，那門徒就接他到自己家裡去了。

**懷愛倫註釋（27–28節）**。《救贖的故事》第224頁。

28.zh:
這事以後，耶穌知道各樣的事已經成了，為要使經上的話應驗，就說：我渴了。

**已經成了。**將這裡與徒13:29進行比較。
**應驗。**見詩69:20,21。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第123頁。
28.en:
**Now accomplished** Compare Acts 13:29.
**Might be fulfilled.** See Ps. 69:20, 21.

29.zh:
有一個器皿盛滿了醋，放在那裡；他們就拿海絨蘸滿了醋，綁在牛膝草上，送到他口。

**醋。**這是給耶穌提供的第二種喝的東西（見太27:34,48註釋）。
29.en: **Vinegar.** This was the second drink offered Jesus (see on Matt. 27:34, 48).

31.zh:
猶太人因這日是預備日，又因那安息日是個大日，就求彼拉多叫人打斷他們的腿，把他們拿去，免得屍首當安息日留在十字架上。

**預備日。**paraskeuē（見第14節註釋）。
**大日。**稱為“大日”無疑是因為這個安息日也是無酵節的第一日（利23:6；見《馬太福音》第26章補充註釋一）。同時代猶太的文學作品無法證實“大日”的這種用法。那些認為耶穌是在尼散月第十五日釘十字架的人主張，那個安息日之所以是大日，是因為那一週的安息日正好與初熟莊稼的搖捆日（利23:9-14）重合。然而耶穌是在初熟的果實獻上的日子復活的，準確應驗了各種預表（見《馬太福音》第26章補充註釋一；參《歷代願望》785，786頁）。
**打斷他們的腿。**這樣做是為了加速他們死亡。
**留在十字架上。**根據申21:22,23，屍體不能留在“木頭”上過夜，而要在當天埋掉。第二天作為安息日更加要求這個命令得到嚴格的執行。
31.en:
**Preparation.** Gr. paraskeuē (see on v. 14).
**Remain upon the cross.** According to Deut. 21:22, 23, bodies were not to remain upon a “tree” overnight, but were to be buried on the same day. The following day, being the Sabbath, would make even more imperative the carrying out of the command.
**High day.** Doubtless called “high day” because that Sabbath was also the first day of unleavened bread (Lev. 23:6; see Additional Notes on Matthew 26, Note 1). This use of the term “high day” cannot be demonstrated from contemporary Jewish literature. Those who hold that Jesus was crucified on Nisan 15 contend that that Sabbath was a high day because the weekly Sabbath coincided with the day of the waving of the first fruits (Lev. 23:9–14). However, Jesus rose on the day the first fruits were offered, in precise fulfillment of the types (see Additional Notes on Matthew 26, Note 1; cf. DA 785, 786).
**Legs might be broken.** That is, to hasten death.

37.zh:
經上又有一句說：他們要仰望自己所扎的人。

**他們……自己所扎的。**見亞12:10註釋。
[耶穌的安葬：約19:38-42=太27:57-61=可15:42-47=路23:50-56。註釋主要在《馬太福音》和〈馬可福音〉]。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》第197頁。

40.zh:
他們就照猶太人殯葬的規矩，把耶穌的身體用細麻布加上香料裹好了。

**懷愛倫註釋（40–42節）**。《歷代願望》第774頁。

58.en:
**Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18. The statement to follow was most solemn, and fraught with eternal significance.
**Before Abraham was.** Rather, “before Abraham came into existence.” The verb is ginomai as in ch. 1:6 and not eimi as later in this verse (see on ch. 1:1). The same combination of verbs occurs in the LXX of Ps. 90:2, “Before the mountains were brought forth [ginomai] … from everlasting to everlasting thou art [eimi] God.” See on John 1:1.
**I am.** Gr. egō eimi, here used in its absolute sense and understood by the Jews as a claim to divinity (see on v. 24). For a discussion of this title of Deity see Vol. I, pp. 170-173.
58.zh:
耶穌說：我實實在在的告訴你們，還沒有亞伯拉罕就有了我。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18節。下面的話非常神聖莊嚴，並且具有永恆的意義。
**還沒有亞伯拉罕。**“還沒有亞伯拉罕”中的動詞“有”是ginomai，它和約1:6中的“有”相同，而不是本節後半部分“就有了我”中的eimi[有]（見約1:1註釋）。動詞的同樣組合還出現在七十士譯本的詩90:2中：“諸山未曾生出[ginomai]……從亙古到永遠你是[eimi]上帝”。見約1:1註釋。
**就有了我。**egō eimi，這裡使用的是它絕對的意義，猶太人認為耶穌這是在宣佈自己的神性（見第24節註釋）。關於上帝的稱呼，見《SDA聖經註釋》卷一第170-173頁。

32.en:
**Truth.** A frequent word in John. In its basic meaning truth is that which corresponds to fact. John frequently, as here, uses the word in a wider sense to denote what is true in things pertaining to God and the duties of man, or in a more restricted sense the facts taught in the Christian religion concerning God and the execution of His purposes through Christ. This revelation had been given by Jesus (ch. 1:17). He, in fact. was “the truth” (ch. 14:6). He was “full of grace and truth” (ch. 1:14). These facts concerning the Christian religion are revealed also by the Spirit, who Himself is truth (1 John 5:6; cf. John 14:17, 26), and by the Word (John 17:17). See on ch. 1:14.
**Make you free.** The glorious truths of the gospel had been foreshadowed in the writings of Moses and the prophets. Paul describes the OT era as one of “glory,” and notes that the new era will far exceed it (2 Cor. 3:9). But many of the truths concerning the religion of Jehovah had been obscured by the inventions of the Jews. The minds of the people were blinded and a veil was over their hearts when they read the OT (2 Cor. 3:14, 15). They were bound by the burdensome traditions of the elders (Matt. 23:4; see on Mark 7:1–13) and by their sins (Rom. 2:17–24; cf. Rom. 6:14; Gal. 4:21). Jesus came to set them free. He declared that His mission was “to preach deliverance to the captives” (Luke 4:18). To those who accepted the truth He promised liberty (cf. 2 Cor. 3:17; Gal. 5:1).
32.zh:
你們必曉得真理，真理必叫你們得以自由。

**真理。**《約翰福音》中經常出現“真理”。從最基本的含義來說，真理是和事實相對應的。就像這裡，約翰經常使用這個詞的廣義來指與上帝以及人的責任有關的事，或在狹義上指基督教所教導的一些事實，而這些事實與上帝和祂通過基督所實現的旨意有關。這種啟示是通過耶穌傳給我們的（約1:17）。實際上，耶穌就是“真理”（約14:6）。在祂裡面“充充滿滿地有恩典有真理”（約1:14）。那些與基督教有關的事實同樣也是通過聖靈和道（約17:17）啟示給我們的。聖靈本身也是真理（約壹5:7；參約14:17,26）。見約1:14註釋。
**叫你們得以自由。**福音榮耀的真理已經在摩西和眾先知的著作中預言過了。保羅曾形容舊約時代有“榮光”，但他同時又指出，新約時代的榮光要遠遠超過先前的（林後3:9）。然而關於耶和華信仰的許多真理已經被猶太人的發明弄得隱晦不明瞭。當百姓讀《舊約》時他們的思想和心靈被矇蔽以至於變得昏暗了（林後3:14,15）。他們被長老們那累贅艱澀的遺傳（太23:4；見可7:1-13註釋）和自己的罪（羅2:17-24；參羅6:14；加4:21）所捆綁。耶穌來就是要釋放他們。祂宣佈自己的使命是“報告被擄的得釋放”（路4:18）。祂對那些接受真理之人的應許就是解放和自由（參林後3:17；加5:1）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第258頁；《證言》卷八第152，251頁。

44.en:
**The devil.** Literally, “the slanderer” (see on Matt. 4:1).
**Lusts.** Gr. epithumiai, “desires,” whether good (Luke 22:15; Phil. 1:23), or, more often, evil (Rom. 1:24; 6:12; 7:7, 8; etc.). Related to epithumia is the verb epithumeō, the word rendered “covet” in the tenth commandment as quoted by Paul in Rom. 7:7; 13:9. The “lusts of your father” are the evil desires that characterize him, or the desires he instills in those who do his bidding.
**Ye will do.** Literally, “you wish to do,” or “you wish to practice.”
**From the beginning.** This has often been considered an allusion to the first recorded murder, that of Abel (Gen. 4:1–8). But the spirit of murder goes back to the inception of sin. By his rebellion Lucifer brought the death sentence upon himself and upon the angels who joined him in his revolt (2 Peter 2:4). When he led our first parents into sin he brought death upon them and upon the entire human family (Rom. 5:12). Their desire to kill Jesus was evidence of the close affinity of the Jews with the archmurderer.
**Abode not.** A reference to the original fall of Lucifer (Jude 6; 2 Peter 2:4; see on Isa. 14:12–14; Eze. 28:12–14).
**In the truth.** For a definition of truth see on v. 32.
**No truth.** That is, no truthfulness. Truth and Satan have nothing in common.
**Of his own.** Literally, “out of his own [things],” that is, out of the things of his essential nature. It is his nature to lie. Jesus, on the other hand, spoke not of Himself, but spoke the truth He had heard from His Father (v. 38).
**He is a liar.** His career of falsehood began in heaven, where he first misrepresented the character and purposes of God before the angels. By his insinuations and lies in the Garden of Eden he brought about the fall of our first parents (see on Gen. 3:4).
The Talmud (Sanhedrin 89b, Soncino ed., p. 596) contains the legend that before the sacrifice of Isaac, Satan attempted to instill doubts in the mind of Abraham concerning God, and that Abraham repulsed him with the words, “‘It is the penalty of a liar, that should he even tell the truth, he is not listened to.’”
**Father of it.** According to the Greek this phrase may mean either the father of the liar or the father of the lie. Either correctly designates the great originator of falsehood. As a liar Satan was expelled from heaven and will never regain residence there. Neither will his children, for “without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie” (Rev. 22:15).
44.zh:
你們是出於你們的父魔鬼，你們父的私慾你們偏要行。他從起初是殺人的，不守真理，因他心裡沒有真理。他說謊是出於自己；因他本來是說謊的，也是說謊之人的父。

**魔鬼。**直譯是“毀謗者”（見太4:1註釋）。
**私慾。**epithumiai，“渴望”，可以是褒義（路22:15；腓1:23），但更多時候是貶義（羅1:24；6:12；7:7,8等）。和epithumia有關的動詞是epithumeō，它在十誡中譯成“貪戀”。保羅在羅7:7；13:9中也使用這個詞。“你們父的私慾”是一種惡欲，這種惡欲是魔鬼的特徵，也被他一點一點灌輸到那些遵行他命令的人心中。
**你們偏要行。**直譯是“你們想要去做”。
**從起初。**人們通常認為這裡是指世界上的第一起謀殺案──該隱殺亞伯（創4:1-8）。但是殺人的精神其實要追溯到罪開始的時候。路錫甫因為他的叛變而給自己和參加他叛亂的天使帶來死刑的判決（彼後2:4）。當他引誘我們先祖犯罪時，他就將死亡帶給他們以及全人類（羅5:12）。猶太人渴望殺害耶穌，這就是他們與撒但存在密切關係的證據。
**不守。**這裡提到了路錫甫最初的墮落（猶第6節；彼後2:4節；見賽14:12-14；結28:12-14註釋）。
**真理。**關於真理的定義，見第32節註釋。
**沒有真理。**即沒有誠實。撒但與真理和誠實之間沒有任何共同之處。
**出於自己。**或出於他自己的本性。撒但的本性就是說謊。耶穌則不說自己，而說從父那裡聽來的真理（第38節）。
**他本來是說謊的。**撒但說謊的經歷開始於天上，他最先在天使面前歪曲上帝的品格和旨意。在伊甸園中，他藉著諂媚和欺騙使我們的先祖墮落（見創3:4註釋）。
《塔木德》宋西諾版（Sanhedrin 89b，第596頁）中有這麼一段傳說：在獻以撒之前，撒但試圖將對上帝的懷疑灌輸到亞伯拉罕的心中，亞伯拉罕用以下的話將其斥退：“這是說謊之人的刑罰，他本應說真話，現在他沒人聽了。’”
**說謊之人的父。**原文既可表示說謊之人的父，也可表示謊言的父。兩者都是指那虛謊的創始者。作為一個說謊者，撒但被驅逐出天庭，並且永遠喪失了天上的居所。對於他的子民也是一樣，因為“城外有那些犬類、行邪術的、淫亂的、殺人的、拜偶像的，並一切喜好說謊言、編造虛謊的”（啟22:15）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第739頁；《佈道論》第597，598頁；《早期著作》第90，228，264頁；《善惡之爭》第502頁；《先祖與先知》第337頁；《給傳道人的證言》第365頁；《證言》卷四第623頁；《證言》卷五第137頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（44–46節）**。《歷代願望》第467頁。

28.en:
**Lifted up.** The reference here is to the crucifixion, though the word translated “lifted up” is also used of the exaltation of Christ to the right hand of the Father (Acts 2:33; see on John 3:14; cf. John 12:32). To the Jews the statement was enigmatic, though some present doubtless understood it after the crucifixion. Significantly, the shameful lifting up on the cross was the prelude to Christ’s true exaltation (Phil. 2:9).
**Son of man.** See on Matt. 1:1; Mark 2:10.
**Then shall ye know.** Events connected with the crucifixion and resurrection provided evidence that Jesus was all He claimed to be. The destruction of Jerusalem confirmed the prophecy of Jesus.
**I am he.** See on v. 24.
28.zh:
所以耶穌說：你們舉起人子以後，必知道我是基督，並且知道我沒有一件事是憑著自己做的。我說這些話乃是照著父所教訓我的。

**舉起。**這裡指的是基督釘十字架。該詞還用來指基督被高舉升到天上父的右邊（徒2:33；見約3:14節註釋；參見約12:32）。這些話在猶太人看來是深奧難懂的，但聽到的人中顯然有一部分在耶穌釘十字架之後明白了其中的含義。具有重要意義的是，被舉起掛在十字架上的羞辱成了基督真正升高的序曲（腓2:9）。
**人子。**見太1:1；可2:10註釋。
**必知道。**與釘十字架和復活有關的事件，證實了耶穌原先對自己所作的聲明都是正確的。耶路撒冷的毀滅進一步證實了耶穌的預言。
**我是基督。**見第24節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第21頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（28–29節）**。《歷代願望》第465頁；《服務真詮》第488頁。

29.en: **Not left me.** Jesus again emphasizes His union with the Father (cf. ch. 17:21). He had always cooperated with the Father in the divine purpose and plan and had always done that which was well pleasing to Him. He was never left alone. The Father had testified to His pleasure in the Son (Matt. 3:17).
29.zh:
那差我來的是與我同在；他沒有撇下我獨自在這裡，因為我常做他所喜悅的事。

**沒有撇下我。**耶穌再次強調祂與父的合一（參見約17:21）。耶穌在神聖的旨意和計劃中常與祂的父合作，祂常做使父喜悅的事。子從未被撇下，父曾親自見證祂對子的喜悅（太3:17）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第468，685頁；《善惡之爭》第469頁；《福山寶訓》第15頁；《服務真詮》第426頁；《先祖與先知》第372頁；《證言》卷八第208，289頁。

1.zh:
於是各人都回家去了；耶穌卻往橄欖山去，

**耶穌卻往……去。**惟有這一部分內容（8:1至8:11）是用早期的安色爾字母（D）寫的，但哲羅姆宣稱它在若干希臘文手稿中都有。大部分的古代拉丁語的手稿都不包含這部分。現存早期教父的著作對這部分內容也隻字未提。西方發現最早對它的評論是在哲羅姆的時代之後，而東方要遲至公元10世紀。一些手稿將這一段敘述放在路21:38後面。綜上考慮，再加上所謂寫作風格的差異，學者們下結論說這部分內容並不在約翰的原稿之中。但是他們也承認這段敘述是真實的，完全符合耶穌的作為和教訓。本註釋認為這段記敘是真實的。
**橄欖山。**見太21:1；26:30註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第86頁；《證言》卷二第508頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《歷代願望》第460頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–11節）**。《歷代願望》第460-462頁。
1.en:
**Jesus went.** [The Woman Taken in Adultery, John 7:53 to John 8:11. See Early Peraean Ministry; The Ministry of Our Lord.] This entire section (chs. 7:53 to 8:11) appears in only one of the early uncial manuscripts (D), although Jerome claims that it was present in a number of Greek manuscripts. The large majority of the Old Latin manuscripts do not have it. The passage is nowhere commented on in the extant writings of the early Church Fathers. The first comments are found following the time of Jerome, in the West, and not until the 10th century in the East. A few manuscripts place the narrative after Luke 21:38. These and certain other considerations, such as an alleged difference of style, have led scholars to the conclusion that this narrative did not appear in John’s autograph copy. However, they admit that the narrative appears to be authentic and that it is in full harmony with what Jesus did and taught. This commentary takes the position that the narrative is authentic.
**The mount of Olives.** See on Matt. 21:1; 26:30.

2.zh:
清早又回到殿裡。眾百姓都到他那裡去，他就坐下，教訓他們。

**清早。**這件事發生在次日清晨，就是住棚節的第八天（見約7:37註釋）。
**坐下。**關於耶穌教訓百姓時的姿勢，見太5:1註釋。
**教訓。**就像祂以前所做的那樣（約7:14），“開始教訓”。
2.en:
**Early in the morning.** This incident occurred the following morning, on the eighth day of the Feast of Tabernacles (see on ch. 7:37).
**Sat down.** For this posture while teaching see on Matt. 5:1.
**Taught.** Rather, “began to teach,” as He had earlier (ch. 7:14).

3.zh:
文士和法利賽人帶著一個行淫時被拿的婦人來，叫他站在當中，

這種案件應該直接帶到法庭去。文士和法利賽人陰謀策劃這個圈套是想要陷害耶穌，好定祂的罪。這些人做事的習慣絲毫沒有什麼廉恥可言。其實他們完全沒有必要在聖殿廣大百姓面前演出這一醜劇。接下來他們當眾出醜（第9節）的確是理所應當的。
3.en: **Brought unto him.** Such cases should properly be brought to the courts. The scribes and Pharisees had contrived a plot to ensnare Jesus so that they might secure His condemnation. Their procedure was contemptible. There was no need to make such a public show of the case before the multitudes assembled at the Temple. Their own public humiliation that followed (v. 9) was fully merited.

4.zh:
就對耶穌說：夫子，這婦人是正行淫之時被拿的。

**夫子。**直譯是“老師”。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–5節）**。《服務真詮》第87頁。

5.zh:
摩西在律法上吩咐我們把這樣的婦人用石頭打死。你說該把他怎麼樣呢？

**用石頭打死。**摩西的律法規定已婚的婦女行淫是要處死的，但卻沒有規定具體的行刑方式。根據《密西拿》，這種案件中的行刑方式應該是絞刑（Sanhedrin 11. 1，《塔木德》松奇諾版第558頁）。律法規定，犯這類案件的如果是一個已訂婚但尚未成親的女子，就要用石頭打死（申22:23,24）。這同樣也是《密西拿》的規定（Sanhedrin 7. 4,9，《塔木德》松奇諾版第359,451,452頁）。這樣來看，被帶來的應該是一個已經訂婚但未正式過門的女子。
你說該把她怎麼樣呢？原文的“你”是強調。耶穌被人推上了與摩西對立的位置。法利賽人對於陷害耶穌比刑罰那個女子更加關心。他們認為無論耶穌說什麼他們都能定祂的罪。他們無疑知道耶穌願意赦免人。他們希望耶穌能建議他們仁慈對待這個女子。如此，他們就可以控告祂輕視律法。如果耶穌建議對她執行死刑，那他們就能控告祂逾越了羅馬人的權柄。當時羅馬政府掌管著死刑案件的最終裁定權。
5.en:
**Stoned.** The law of Moses prescribed death for adultery when a married woman was involved, but did not specify the manner of death. According to the Mishnah death in these cases was inflicted by strangulation (Sanhedrin 11. 1, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 558). The law prescribed death by stoning when a betrothed woman was involved (Deut. 22:23, 24). This is also the rule of the Mishnah (Sanhedrin 7. 4, 9, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 359, 451, 452). It seems likely, therefore, that the case in question was one of a betrothed woman.
**What sayest thou?** In the Greek the word “thou” is in the emphatic position. Jesus is set over against Moses. The Pharisees were more concerned with entrapping Jesus than with punishing the woman. They felt that no matter what answer Jesus gave they could involve Him in condemnation. They doubtless knew of His willingness to forgive, and perhaps expected that He would recommend leniency. In this case they could charge Him with setting aside the law. If He recommended carrying out the penalty, they could charge Him with usurping the authority of Rome, which at that time reserved jurisdiction in capital cases.

6.zh:
他們說這話，乃試探耶穌，要得著告他的把柄。耶穌卻彎著腰，用指頭在地上畫字。

**試探耶穌。**見第5節註釋。
**畫。**這裡是唯一一次記載耶穌寫字。寫祂的書很多，但祂所寫的卻沒有一點保留下來。祂在道旁塵土中寫的字很快就被來往於聖殿中的人抹去了。根據傳統說法耶穌所寫的是那些控告者的罪行（參見《歷代願望》461頁）。《密西拿》也曾提到過在沙土上寫字的習慣（Shabbath 12. 5，《塔木德》松奇諾版第503頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–11節）**。《歷代願望》第461頁。
6.en:
**Tempting him.** See on v. 5.
**Wrote.** This is the only record of Jesus writing. Much indeed has been written about Him, but none of His writings have been preserved. The characters He wrote on the pavement dust were soon obliterated by the Temple traffic. According to tradition He wrote down the sins of the accusers (cf. DA 461). The practice of writing in the sand is referred to in the Mishnah (Shabbath 12. 5, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 503).

7.zh:
他們還是不住的問他，耶穌就直起腰來，對他們說：你們中間誰是沒有罪的，誰就可以先拿石頭打他。

**沒有罪的。**耶穌的話使那些執意要祂回答的控告者目瞪口呆，他們完全沒有料想到會是這樣一個結果。他們中間沒有一個人敢說自己是無罪的。或許在上天的審判臺前他們中的某些人比這個女子的罪更大（參見《歷代願望》461頁）。他們沒有一個人敢答話。
耶穌說的不是一個普遍的原則，不是說執行懲罰的人必須絕對無罪。那將使律法無法實施，因為沒有一個人適合執行刑罰。祂在這裡說到一種情況，就是人把自己立為別人的法官時，他們自己如果不是無罪的，就不可以定別人的罪。耶穌憎恨淫亂的罪（見太5:27-32註釋），但祂也憎恨自以為義的審判（見太7:1-5註釋）。
**先。**即在眾人中第一個扔石頭打她。
**拿石頭打。**根據申17:7（參見申13:9），證人要第一個拿石頭打那被定罪的人。《密西拿》這樣描述用石刑的程序：“執行石刑的地方有兩人高。證人中的一個從後身把犯人砸倒，讓他趴在地上，然後再把他翻過來。如果犯人死了，他就完成了（他的任務）；但如果犯人沒有死，第二個證人用石頭打他的前胸。如果犯人死了，那他就完成了（他的任務）；但如果還沒死，全以色列人就要拿石頭打他（罪犯），因為經上記著說：見證人要先下手，然後眾民也下手將他治死（申17:7）”（Sanhedrin 6. 4，《塔木德》松奇諾版第295頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第462頁；《服務真詮》第88，89頁；《證言》卷三第105頁；《證言》卷四第238，326頁；《證言》卷五第35，53頁；《證言》卷七第279頁。
7.en:
**Without sin.** Jesus gives the persistent inquirers an answer they are not expecting, and for which they are unprepared. None of them can lay claim to sinlessness. Perhaps before Heaven’s tribunal some of them are more guilty than the woman (cf. DA 461). None of them accepts the challenge.
Jesus is not stating a general principle, one that would make absolute sinlessness the necessary condition of fitness for taking part in the punishment of guilt. This would nullify law, for no one fitted to carry out the execution could be found. He speaks here of a case where men set themselves up as judges of others, whom they ought not to condemn unless they themselves be guiltless. Jesus abhorred adultery (see on Matt. 5:27–32), but He also abhorred self-righteous judging (see onMatt. 7:1–5).
**First.** That is, be the first of the group to cast a stone.
**Cast a stone.** According to Deut. 17:7 (cf. ch. 13:9), the witnesses were to be the first to cast a stone upon the condemned man. The procedure of stoning is described in the Mishnah as follows: “The place of stoning was twice a man’s height. One of the witnesses pushed him by the hips, [so that] he was overturned on his heart. He was then turned on his back. If that caused his death, he had fulfilled [his duty]; but if not, the second witness took the stone and threw it on his chest. If he died thereby he had done [his duty]; but if not, he [the criminal] was stoned by all Israel, for it is written: The hand of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people [Deut. 17:7]” (Sanhedrin 6. 4, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 295).

8.zh:
於是又彎著腰，用指頭在地上畫字。

**畫。**或“繼續在地上畫字”。見第6節註釋。
8.en: **Wrote.** Rather, “kept on writing.” See on v. 6.

9.zh:
他們聽見這話，就從老到少，一個一個的都出去了，只剩下耶穌一人，還有那婦人仍然站在當中。

那些人前來要定這女子的罪，他們離去是因為自己的良心定了他們的罪。毫無疑問，他們迅速離去是因為害怕自己生活中隱藏的罪惡──特別是本案中所犯的同謀罪──被暴露在光天化日之下（見《歷代願望》461頁）。他們的失敗再沒有比這更可恥的了。
9.en: **Convicted.** They had come to convict the woman. They went away convicted by their own conscience. They left the scene doubtless fearing that the guilty secrets of their lives, and particularly their own complicity in this case (see DA 461), would be revealed to the multitude. Their defeat could not have been more dramatic.

10.zh:
耶穌就直起腰來，對他說：婦人，那些人在哪裡呢？沒有人定你的罪嗎？

**婦人。**見約2:4註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（10–11節）**。《服務真詮》第88頁。
10.en: **Woman.** See on ch. 2:4.

11.zh:
他說：主啊，沒有。耶穌說：我也不定你的罪。去吧，從此不要再犯罪了！

**主。**kurios，意思可能只是“先生”（見約4:11註釋）。這個女子可能聽說過耶穌，並知道一些祂的主張。如果是這樣，她本可以用一種具有更深意義的稱呼，來表達她承認耶穌作為上帝兒子的地位。她沒有為自己辯護，也沒有祈求寬恕。
**不要再犯罪。**參約5:14。“因為上帝差祂的兒子降世，不是要定世人的罪，乃是要叫世人因祂得救”（約3:17）。耶穌的話帶著慈憐進入那女子的心中，與剛才那些控告者疾言厲色的話語形成了強烈的對比。耶穌向她指出她現在最需要的是立即離棄她的罪。悔改必須是真誠懇切的。她若不為自己的罪深深痛悔就必繼續陷於罪中。對於悔改來說，感覺、話語、聲明、意願、希望，這些在上帝眼中毫無價值。除非一個人停止作惡並離棄罪，他就不是真正悔改（見詩32:1,6；約壹1:7,9註釋）。
[世界的光：約8:12-30] 。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《服務真詮》第89頁；《醫療佈道論》第28頁；《證言》卷七第96頁；《證言》卷九第164頁。
11.en:
**Lord. Gr.** kurios, here perhaps simply “sir” (see on ch. 4:11). However, it is possible that she had earlier heard of Jesus and knew something of His claims. If so, she might have used the address with deeper significance, in acknowledgment of His position as the Son of God. There is no attempt at defense. There is no plea for forgiveness.
**Sin no more.** Compare ch. 5:14. “God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved” (ch. 3:17). Jesus’ words came to the trembling woman as words of mercy, in abrupt contrast with the angry words of her accusers. Jesus pointed her to the chief thing for which she stood in need—the immediate forsaking of her sins. Repentance must be honest and sincere. Not only must she be sorry for her sin; she must turn away from it. That repentance which consists in nothing more than feeling, talking, professing, wishing, hoping, is utterly worthless in the sight of God. Until a man ceases to do evil and turns from his sins, he does not really repent (see on Ps. 32:1, 6; 1 John 1:7, 9).

12.zh:
耶穌又對眾人說：我是世界的光。跟從我的，就不在黑暗裡走，必要得著生命的光。

**我是。**見約1:4-9；6:20註釋。
**世界的光。**就像耶穌所說的“活水”（約7:37,38）是指住棚節上的水祭的儀式，現在祂聲明自己是世界的光，無疑也和與光有關的儀式聯繫在一起。《密西拿》這樣描述：“在住棚節第一天結束的時候，他們下到曾在那裡制訂了一項重要法令的女院（一個特別的女性院落）。在那裡有四個金燈臺，上面各放著一個金碗，每個燈臺旁邊有一架梯子（根據《塔木德》，燈臺有五十肘高），四個年輕人手中捧著盛油一百二十羅革的油瓶從祭司的位置走來，將油倒進碗中。
“他們用祭司穿破的內褲和腰帶做燈芯，將燈點燃；耶路撒冷沒有一個院落不被取水之處的燈光照亮的”。
“敬虔良善的人通常會在燈臺前手裡拿著火把跳舞、歌頌、讚美。無數的利未人拿著琴、瑟、鈸、角等各種樂器聚集在從以色列院到女院的十五級臺階上，這是對應《詩篇》中的十五首上行之歌（詩120-134）。利未人就是站在這裡用他們的樂器彈奏並唱出他們的詩歌”（Sukkah 5. 2-4，《塔木德》宋西諾版第242,243頁；參《歷代願望》第五十一章）。
關於耶穌是“真光”的意義，見約1:4註釋；參《歷代願望》第五十一章。
**在黑暗裡。**在猶太人關於《出埃及記》的一部註釋中，將妥拉（律法）的話比作啟發一個人學習的明燈。關於那些不學習律法或忽視律法的人，註釋中這樣說：“他跌在石頭上，他遇見一個水溝掉在其中，他的臉摔在地上──這一切都是因為他的手上沒有拿著燈。那些心中沒有律法的人也是一樣；他遭遇罪惡，跌倒，死亡”（《米德拉西拉巴》，第439頁，出27:20註釋）。
在猶太人中間他們有一位比律法更大的，因為是祂將律法賜給他們。祂在律法中就是光的源頭（見《先祖與先知》366頁）。但是拉比們用他們的遺傳嚴重誤表那光，那些想要行在律法之光中的人被他們說成是行在黑暗之中。
**生命的光。**可以解釋為“作為生命的光”，“賜生命的光”或“源於生命的光”。耶穌不僅是光，祂還是生命（約11:25；14:6；見約1:4節註釋）。接受祂的就是接受生命：“人有了上帝的兒子就有生命”（約一5:12）。“在基督裡有生命。這生命是祂自己本來就有的，不是借來的，也不是從別處得來的”（《歷代願望》530頁）。祂來到世間是要叫人“得生命，並且得的更豐盛”（約10:10）。“上帝賜給我們永生；這永生也是在祂兒子裡面”（約壹5:11）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育之研究》第28，512頁；《安息日學訓言》第175頁；《歷代願望》第463頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第39頁；《服務真詮》第419頁；《醫療佈道論》第203頁；《給青年人的信息》第63，169頁；《先祖與先知》第367頁；《給傳道人的證言》第178，211，332頁；《證言》卷一第31，406頁；《證言》卷四第190，231頁；《證言》卷七第272頁；《證言》卷九第141頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–59節）**。《歷代願望》第463-475頁。
12.en:
**I am.** [The Light of the World, John 8:12–30.] See on chs. 1:4–9; 6:20.
**Light of the world.** As Jesus’ statement concerning the living water (ch. 7:37, 38) had reference to the water-libation ceremony of the Feast of Tabernacles, so His statement declaring Himself to be the light of the world was doubtless connected with the ceremony of lights. This ceremony is described in the Mishnah as follows: “At the conclusion of the first Festival day of Tabernacles they descended to the Court of the Women where they had made a great enactment [a special women’s gallery]. There were there golden candlesticks with four golden bowls on the top of each of them and four ladders [according to the Talmud the candlesticks were fifty cubits high] to each, and four youths drawn from the priestly stock in whose hands were held jars of oil containing one hundred and twenty log which they poured into the bowls.
“From the worn-out drawers and girdles of the priests they made wicks and with them they kindled the lamps; and there was not a courtyard in Jerusalem that was not illumined by the light of the place of the water-drawing.
“Men of piety and good deeds used to dance before them with lighted torches in their hands, and sing songs and praises. And Levites without number with harps, lyres, cymbals and trumpets and other musical instruments were there upon the fifteen steps leading down from the Court of the Israelites to the Court of the Women, corresponding to the Fifteen Songs of Ascents in the Psalms [Ps. 120–134]. It was upon these that the Levites stood with their instruments of music and sang their songs” (Sukkah 5. 2–4, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, pp. 242, 243; cf. DA 463).
For the significance of Jesus as “the true Light” see on ch. 1:4; cf. DA 464, 465.
**In darkness.** In one of their commentaries on the book of Exodus the Jews represent the words of the Torah (Law) as illuminating the one who engaged in their study. Concerning the one not engaged in their study or ignorant of them the comment says: “He stumbles against a stone; he then strikes a gutter, falls into it, and knocks his face on the ground—and all because he has no lamp in his hand. It is the same with the ordinary individual who has no Torah in him; he strikes against sin, stumbles, and dies” (Midrash Rabbah, on Ex. 27:20, Soncino ed., p. 439).
The Jews had One standing in their midst who was greater than the Torah, for He Himself had given them the Torah. He was the source of the light in the Torah (see PP 366). But the rabbis had so obscured that light with their traditions that he who attempted to walk in the light of the Torah as interpreted by the rabbis was in reality walking in darkness.
**Light of life.** This phrase may be interpreted as the light that is life, or that gives life, or that has its source in life. Not only is Jesus the light; He is also the life (chs. 11:25; 14:6; see on ch. 1:4). He that receives Him receives life: “He that hath the Son hath life” (1 John 5:12). In Jesus is “life, original, unborrowed, underived” (DA 530). He came to this earth that men “might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly” (John 10:10). “God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son” (1 John 5:11).

13.zh:
法利賽人對他說：你是為自己作見證，你的見證不真。

**你的見證不真。**耶穌在畢士大池醫病之後提出了猶太人現在所依據的原則（約5:31）。摩西的律法明確規定，在死刑案件中一個人的證言不足以採信（民35:30；申17:6）。《密西拿》中也有同樣的原則：“一個人無法為自己作證”（Kethuboth 2. 9，《塔木德》松奇諾版第151頁）。“一個人沒有權利自己（說自己是“聖潔的）”（Rosh Hashanah 3. 1，《塔木德》松奇諾版第113頁）。
13.en: **Thy record is not true.** Following the Bethesda incident Jesus Himself set forth the principle the Jews here appealed to (ch. 5:31). The Law of Moses clearly stipulated that in capital cases the witness of only one man was insufficient for conviction (Num. 35:30; Deut. 17:6). The principle appears also in the Mishnah: “No one may testify concerning himself” (Kethuboth 2. 9, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 151). “An individual is not authorized [to say “sanctified”] by himself” (Rosh Hashanah 3. 1, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 113).

14.zh:
耶穌說：我雖然為自己作見證，我的見證還是真的；因我知道我從哪裡來，往哪裡去；你們卻不知道我從哪裡來，往哪裡去。

**我的見證還是真的。**一個人為自己作的見證不一定就是假的。一個誠實之人為自己作的見證是值得信賴的。耶穌，作為上帝，從上帝而來，是不會說謊的（多1:2），祂自身的本性決定了祂的話全是真理。但是猶太人只將祂當作一個普通的人。他們既不承認祂的神格也不承認祂的使命。此外，如果真的要有一位旁證的話，耶穌有，就是差祂前來與祂同在的天父（約8:16,18；見約5:31-39註釋）。
14.en: **My record is true.** A man’s self-witness is not necessarily false. The testimony of an honest man would be reliable. Jesus, being who He was, a divine Being, and proceeding from God, who cannot lie (Titus 1:2), would naturally speak the truth. But the Jews made Him out to be an ordinary man. They acknowledged neither His divine origin nor His destiny. Furthermore, if a collateral witness was required, He had one. The Father, who sent Him, was with Him (John 8:16, 18; see on ch. 5:31–39).

15.zh:
你們是以外貌（原文是憑肉身）判斷人，我卻不判斷人。

**以外貌（原文作憑肉身）。**他們判斷的是耶穌肉身的方面，而與祂的神性無關。這個短語還出現在林前1:26；林後5:16。將這裡與約7:24節進行比較。
**我卻不判斷人。**耶穌當前的工作不是審判，而是救贖（見約3:17註釋）。非到末日祂就不“審判活人死人”（提後4:1；參徒10:42；林後5:10）。
15.en:
**After the flesh.** They judged the human side of Jesus, not discerning His divinity. The expression occurs also in 1 Cor. 1:26; 2 Cor. 5:16. Compare John 7:24.
**I judge no man.** Jesus’ present work was not that of judgment but of salvation (see on ch. 3:17). Not till the end of the age will He “judge the quick and the dead” (2 Tim. 4:1; cf. Acts 10:42; 2 Cor. 5:10).

16.zh:
就是判斷人，我的判斷也是真的；因為不是我獨自在這裡，還有差我來的父與我同在。

**我的判斷。**見第14節註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第143頁。
16.en: **My judgment.** See on v. 14.

17.zh:
你們的律法上也記著說：兩個人的見證是真的。

**你們的律法。**這個短語還出現在約10:34。約15:25中有一個類似的短語“他們律法”。這幾段話不能解釋為耶穌反對或拋棄律法。祂來不是要廢掉律法和先知（太5:17）。祂曾親自將神聖的律例交給摩西。“你們的律法”可能指猶太人聲稱他們所解釋並維護和遵守的律法，也可能是指他們傳統對律法的解釋（見可7:5-13註釋）。
**兩個人的見證。**見申17:6；19:15註釋；參民35:30。
17.en:
**Your law.** This expression occurs again in ch. 10:34; and the comparable expression “their law,” in ch. 15:25. These passages are not to be construed to mean that Jesus dissociated Himself from, or was antagonistic to, the law. He had not come to destroy the law or the prophets (Matt. 5:17). He Himself had delivered the sacred precepts to Moses. By “your law” Jesus meant either the law they claimed to expound, defend, and keep, or their traditional interpretation of it (see on Mark 7:5–13).
**Testimony of two men.** See Deut. 17:6; 19:15; cf. Num. 35:30.

18.zh:
我是為自己作見證，還有差我來的父也是為我作見證。

**作見證。**見第14節註釋。
18.en: **Beareth witness.** See on v. 14.

19.zh:
他們就問他說：你的父在哪裡？耶穌回答說：你們不認識我，也不認識我的父；若是認識我，也就認識我的父。

你的父在哪裡？這些話很可能是以一種譏誚的口氣說出來的，或許還影射著耶穌的出生。
**也不認識我的父。**耶穌揭示了猶太人對父無知的真正原因──他們忽視了父所揀選用來啟示祂的媒介。這媒介就在眼前。耶穌正在告訴他們天父的品格和特性（見約1:14註釋）。如果猶太人能正確地認識耶穌，他們就能認識祂的父。耶穌對祂的門徒說，“若不藉著我，沒有人能到父那裡去。你們若認識我，也就認識我的父”（約14:6,7）。
19.en:
**Where is thy Father?** These words are probably spoken in scorn, and with a possible allusion to the circumstances of Jesus’ birth.
**Nor my Father.** Jesus traces their ignorance of the Father to its true cause, that is, to their neglect of the means by which the Father had chosen to reveal Himself. The means was then at hand. Jesus was revealing the character and personality of the Father before them (see on ch. 1:14). Had they known Jesus aright they would have known His Father. To His disciples, Jesus said, “No man cometh unto the Father, but by me. If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also” (ch. 14:6, 7).

20.zh:
這些話是耶穌在殿裡的庫房、教訓人時所說的，也沒有人拿他，因為他的時候還沒有到。

**庫房。**耶穌在聖殿的庫房教導人，關於這個“庫房”的位置，見可12:41註釋。耶穌可能是在女院教導人，因為女性也可進到這裡來（可12:41）。見約瑟弗斯《猶太戰爭史》5. 2（200頁）。
**還沒有到。**見約7:6節註釋。
20.en:
**Treasury.** For the location of the “treasury” where Jesus taught see on Mark 12:41. Presumably He was in the Court of the Women, because women had access to it (Mark 12:41). See Josephus War v. 5. 2 (200).
**Not yet come.** See on v. 6.

21.zh:
耶穌又對他們說：我要去了，你們要找我，並且你們要死在罪中。我所去的地方，你們不能到。

**你們要找我。**見約7:34註釋。
**你們要死在罪中。**聽眾中的許多人，他們有機會的時候不接受耶穌，當他們發現祂就是彌賽亞時再想要找祂就已經太晚了。對於他們來說，恩典的門已經關閉了。他們尋找也是徒然。再沒有原諒和寬恕，他們要在自己的罪中滅亡（見耶8:20註釋）。
21.en:
**Ye shall seek me.** See on ch. 7:34.
**Die in your sins.** Many of His hearers would seek Him too late, having discovered too late that He was the Messiah whom they should have received while they had the opportunity to do so. But the door of mercy would be shut for them. They would seek in vain. The result would be that they would perish in their sins, without pardon or forgiveness (see on Jer. 8:20).

22.zh:
猶太人說：他說：我所去的地方，你們不能到，難道他要自盡嗎？

難道祂要自盡嗎？希臘原文是一個反問句，指望肯定的回答。這裡的意思和約7:35節不同。有些人推測說猶太人這裡指的是“陰間裡最黑暗的地方”，就是約瑟弗斯所說指定給自殺者的地方（《猶太戰爭史》iii. 8. 5 [375]頁）。活人是去不了這個地方的。
猶太人的疑問也並非全無道理。耶穌將要死去，祂的死要把祂和他們分開。但是耶穌將要回到天上去，猶太人若執迷不悟，將永遠到不了那裡，而不是去他們所暗示的陰間。猶太人在約7:35中的問題同樣像是含蓄的預言。耶穌死後，祂的門徒們將要在散居在外邦人中的猶太人那裡去，且要教導外邦人（徒1:8）。
22.en:
**Will he kill himself?** The form of the question in Greek shows that a negative answer is expected. The suggestion is very different from that of ch. 7:35. Some have conjectured that the Jews are making reference to “the darkest place in Hades,” to which, Josephus (War iii. 8. 5 [375]) declares, suicides are consigned. The place would be inaccessible to the living.
Their inquiry was not entirely beside the point. Jesus would die, and His death would place Him beyond their reach. But He would go to heaven, a place which, in their impenitence, they would never reach, not to Hades as they may have intended to imply. Their question in ch. 7:35 was likewise vaguely prophetic. Following His death His emissaries were to go to the Jews dispersed among the Gentiles, and also teach the Gentiles (Acts 1:8).

23.zh:
耶穌對他們說：你們是從下頭來的，我是從上頭來的；你們是屬這世界的，我不是屬這世界的。

**從下頭。**見約3:31註釋。天地之間是有差距的（參西3:1）。他們起源於這個下面的世界，因此他們的思想就是屬世界的，屬肉體的，膚淺的，短暫無常的。耶穌作為救贖主來自天上，是世人長久等待的彌賽亞。耶穌非常願意將這個偉大的真理啟示給他們，照亮他們的思想。
23.en: **From beneath.** See on ch. 3:31. The contrast is between this present world and heaven (cf. Col. 3:1). They spring from this lower world; consequently they are influenced by considerations drawn from the earthly, sensual, superficial, and transitory. Jesus came from heaven as man’s Redeemer, the long-awaited Messiah. Concerning this great fact Jesus sought to enlighten their minds.

24.zh:
所以我對你們說，你們要死在罪中。你們若不信我是基督，必要死在罪中。

**你們要死在罪中。**猶太人的得救在於他們接受上帝差來的這位拯救者。除此之外，別無他法（徒4:12）。拒絕救贖主就使他們的罪無可推諉（約15:22）。
**我是基督。**egō eimi。“基督”是後加的。這個短語還出現在第28,58節以及約13:19中。在七十士譯本中，egō eimi相當於希伯來文短語'ani hu'，直譯是“我是上帝”（申32:39；賽43:10）。顯然，正是基於這種關係，後來的譯者才在這節經文中加上了“基督”。將這裡和“我是自有永有的”（希臘文egō eimi hōon，出3:14）進行比較。這裡可能是直接引述賽43:10。那裡的措辭和這裡極其相似，“既是這樣，便可以知道，且信服我，又明白我就是耶和華。”見約6:20註釋。
24.en:
**Die in your sins.** The Jews were dependent for salvation upon acceptance of the Deliverer whom God had sent. There was salvation in none other (Acts 4:12). Their rejection of the Saviour left them without a cloak to cover their sins (John 15:22).
**I am he.** Gr. egō eimi. The “he” is supplied. The same expression occurs in vs. 28, 58, and again in ch. 13:19. In the LXX egō eimi represents the Heb. ’ani hu’, literally, “I am he” (Deut. 32:39; Isa. 43:10). It is this relationship that doubtless led translators to supply the “he” in the present passage. Compare the expression “I am that I am” (Gr. egō eimi ho ̄on) (Ex. 3:14). There may have been a direct allusion to Isa. 43:10, where the wording is strikingly similar to this present passage, “that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he.” See on John 6:20.

25.zh:
他們就問他說：你是誰？耶穌對他們說：就是我從起初所告訴你們的。

**你是誰。**耶穌剛才的話比較含蓄，猶太人現在的問題就是要讓耶穌更加清楚地說出自己的身份，好使他們對祂的控告更具操作性。但是耶穌沒有正面回答他們的問題。
**從起初。**tēn archēn。這個短語的譯法有不同的意見。但總體上來，英文KJV版、英文RSV版的翻譯似乎更加可取一些。有些人認為應譯為“從根本上”。也有人認識應譯為“全然”，並將這句改成一個問句：“我全然告訴你們又怎樣呢？”然而，從上下文的意思看，這裡還是翻譯為“從起初”比較好。實際上耶穌是在說，“這件事我早就告訴你們了。”
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第465頁。
25.en:
**Who art thou?** Literally, “Thou, who art thou?” There was a vagueness in Jesus’ statement, and so the present question was probably an attempt to draw from Him some statement that could be made the ground of a technical charge. But Jesus avoided giving a definite answer to the question.
**From the beginning.** Gr. tēn archēn. There has been much discussion over the translation of this phrase, but on the whole the translation as it appears in the KJV, RSV, etc., seems preferable and is defensible. Some suggest that the phrase should be rendered “primarily [in essence].” Others suggest the translation “at all,” and make the passage a question, “How is it that I even speak to you at all?” (RV margin). However, the context favors the rendering “from the beginning.” Jesus says, in substance, “I have been informing you about it all the time.”

26.zh:
我有許多事講論你們，判斷你們；但那差我來的是真的，我在他那裡所聽見的，我就傳給世人。

**我有許多事。**這一節的前半部分可以譯為：“我可以有許多事講論你們，判斷你們，但”等。這樣翻譯可以更好地解釋“但”這個轉折連詞。
**那差我來的。**和第16節進行比較；參約12:49；見約3:17註釋。
26.en:
**I have many things.** The first part of this verse may be translated, “I could say many things concerning you and judge, but,” etc. Such a rendering provides a better explanation for the adversative “but” than the common translation.
**Of you.** Literally, “concerning you.”
**He that sent me.** Compare v. 16; cf. ch. 12:49; see on ch. 3:17.

27.zh:
他們不明白耶穌是指著父說的。

**他們不明白。**因為他們的思想在屬靈上是黑暗的（見何4:6註釋）。
27.en: **They understood not.** Because their minds were darkened spiritually (see on Hosea 4:6).

30.zh:
耶穌說這話的時候，就有許多人信他。

**信。**譯為“開始相信”或“來相信”更合適。
[關於亞伯拉罕後裔的爭論：約8:31-59]。
30.en: **Believed.** Rather, “began to believe,” or “came to believe.”

31.zh:
耶穌對信他的猶太人說：你們若常常遵守我的道，就真是我的門徒；

**信祂。**與第30節中的“信祂”有所區別（見約1:12註釋；參約3:16）。本節只是說。相信某人所說的事是真的。若是這樣，本章餘下部分所說“信的人”改變了態度也就容易解釋了。
**常常遵守。**menō。該詞在約15:4-7中翻譯為“常在”。持守耶穌教導的原則是真誠相信祂的證據。
**真是。**alēthōs，譯為“真”或“實在”（太27:54；路9:27；太26:73；約壹2:5）。在試煉和反對面前持久忍耐是基督真門徒的標誌。耶穌勸勉相信祂的人要堅定忠貞。那些把種子撒在路邊和石頭地上的人是有危險的（見太13:4,5註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷五第433頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（31–34節）**。《歷代願望》第466頁。
31.en:
**Then said Jesus.** [The Argument About Descent From Abraham, John 8:31–59.]
**On him.** Literally, “him.” In v. 30 the phrase “on him” is a literal rendering of the Greek. It is possible that a distinction is intended between the group mentioned in v. 30 and that mentioned here. There is a difference between believing in a man and believing a man (see on ch. 1:12; cf. ch. 3:16). In the latter case one may merely believe that certain things he says are true. If the distinction is valid, the change in attitude of the “believers” that is evident in the remainder of the chapter is more easily explained.
**Continue.** Gr. menō. The same word is translated “abide” in ch. 15:4–7. Continuance in the doctrine of Jesus is evidence of the sincerity of the original profession of faith in Jesus.
**Indeed.** Gr. alēthōs, variously translated “truly” (Matt. 27:54), “of a truth” (Luke 9:27), “surely” (Matt. 26:73), “verily” (1 John 2:5). Patient continuance in the word in the face of trial and opposition is the mark of true discipleship. Jesus was exhorting those who had fixed their faith in Him to remain steadfast. There was danger that many of them would be wayside or stonyground hearers (see on Matt. 13:4, 5).

33.zh:
他們回答說：我們是亞伯拉罕的後裔，從來沒有作過誰的奴僕。你怎麼說你們必得自由呢？

**亞伯拉罕的後裔。**關於猶太人吹噓自己作為亞伯拉罕的後裔，見太3:9；約3:3,4註釋。
**從來沒有作過誰的奴僕。**從字面意義上來說，猶太人這句話是謊言。埃及就曾是他們的“為奴之家”（出20:2）。士師時代屢有外敵的奴役與壓迫。後來全國又伏在亞述人和巴比倫人的手下。因而，這裡猶太人所指的可能是屬靈上的自由，這是他們認為自己所從未丟失並值得榮耀的。這一點可以從以利亞撒的一段話中反映出來，他是耶路撒冷陷落後一群反抗羅馬之猶太人的領袖，“勇士們，長久以來，我們除了上帝之外決不侍奉羅馬和任何其他統治者，因為只有上帝是人真正公義的主”（約瑟弗斯《猶太戰爭史》vii. 8. 6 [323]；卷三第595頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第268頁。
33.en:
**Abraham’s seed.** For the boast of the Jews concerning descent from Abraham see on Matt. 3:9; John 3:3, 4.
**Never in bondage.** This was a falsehood, if literal bondage was referred to. Egypt had been to them a “house of bondage” (Ex. 20:2). The period of the judges had been punctuated by repeated foreign oppressions. Later there had been national humiliation at the hands of the Assyrians and Babylonians. However, it is possible that the Jews were referring to spiritual freedom of soul, which here they doubtless boast they had never lost. This may be reflected in a statement of Eleazar, leader of a band of Jews who held out against the Romans after the fall of Jerusalem: “Long since, my brave men, we determined neither to serve the Romans nor any other save God, for He alone is man’s true and righteous Lord” (Josephus War vii. 8. 6 [323]; Loeb ed., vol. 3, p. 595).

34.zh:
耶穌回答說：我實實在在的告訴你們，所有犯罪的就是罪的奴僕。

**實實在在地。**見太5:18；約1:51註釋。
**犯罪。**希臘原文的意思是習慣犯罪（見約壹3:9註釋）。
**奴僕。**Doulos。“一個受限制的人”，“一個奴隸”。douloi在聖經中經常與自由相對（林前12:13；加3:28；弗6:8；西3:11；啟19:18）。阿尼西母作為一個逃奴，被稱作doulos，但保羅說他應該得到比一個doulos更好的待遇（門第16節）。“作……奴僕”（約8:33）這個短語來自douleuō，它表現的是名詞doulos的動作含義。第33,34節之間的聯繫在希臘文中可以清楚的看出來。猶太人說，“我們從來沒有作過誰的奴僕”；耶穌回答說：“所有犯罪的就是罪的奴僕。”
保羅也使用過罪奴的說法（羅6:16-20）。
34.en:
**Verily.** See on Matt. 5:18; John 1:51.
**Committeth sin.** That is, according to the Greek, habitually (see on 1 John 3:9).
**Servant.** Gr. doulos, “one bound,” “a slave.” In the Bible the douloi are frequently contrasted with the free (1 Cor. 12:13; Gal. 3:28; Eph. 6:8; Col. 3:11; Rev. 19:18). Onesimus, the escaped slave, is called a doulos, and Paul recommends that he be treated above a doulos (Philemon 16). The phrase “in bondage” (John 8:33) is from douleuō, which expresses the verbal idea of the noun doulos. The connection between vs. 33, 34 is thus clearly seen in the Greek. The Jews said, “We were never in bondage”; Jesus replied, “He that committeth sin is in bondage to sin.”
The figure of slavery to sin is also employed by Paul (Rom. 6:16–20).

35.zh:
奴僕不能永遠住在家裡；兒子是永遠住在家裡。

**奴僕。**奴僕在一個家庭裡的居留權不是永久的。任何時候如果他得罪了主人就要被趕出去。但兒子卻不是這樣。他與主人是血脈相連的。他是這個家庭的子嗣，只要他還活著，就可以永遠留在家裡。猶太人誇耀他們是亞伯拉罕的後裔（見第33節註釋）。但亞伯拉罕有兩個兒子，一個是使女生的，一個是自主之婦人生的（見加第4章的比喻）。猶太人是奴僕（見34節註釋），因此有被棄絕的危險。但是聖子可以改變他們的地位使其得以自由（見約3:3,4；8:36註釋）。
35.en: **The servant.** Rather, “the slave” (see on v. 34). The slave’s tenure is not permanent. He may at any time displease his master and be expelled. Not so the son. His master’s blood courses in his veins. He is the heir and remains in the household as long as he lives. The Jews boasted of their descent from Abraham (see on v. 33). But Abraham had two sons, the one of a bondwoman and the other of the freewoman (see the allegory of Gal. 4). The Jews were slaves (see on John 8:34), and hence in danger of being rejected. But the Son could emancipate them by altering their status (see on chs. 3:3, 4; 8:36).

36.zh:
所以天父的兒子若叫你們自由，你們就真自由了。

**真自由。**猶太人認為他們是亞伯拉罕自由的兒女，並且誇耀他們的權利（見第33節註釋）。他們不願意承認自己所受的捆綁，無論是字面意義上的還是屬靈意義上的。但他們所誇耀的自由是虛假的。耶穌來就是要給他們真正的自由（羅8:2；林後3:17；加5:1）。祂是唯一一個不受罪惡捆綁的人。那些渴望這種自由的人必須向主耶穌基督懇求並且必須順從。惟獨祂有權力和職責可以使凡接受祂的人得以釋放。這個國家只有通過屬靈上的自由才能獲得他們強烈期盼的政治自由（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷四第30-32頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋（36–40節）**。《歷代願望》第466頁。
36.en: **Free indeed.** The Jews considered themselves to be the free sons of Abraham and boasted of their liberty (see on v. 33). They were unwilling to acknowledge their bondage, whether literal or spiritual. But their boasted freedom was spurious. Jesus had come to offer them genuine freedom (Rom. 8:2; 2 Cor. 3:17; Gal. 5:1). He alone is free who is free from sin. Those who desire this freedom must apply to the Lord Jesus Christ, and must comply with the conditions. It is His peculiar office and privilege to enfranchise all who accept Him. Only through spiritual freedom could the nation attain to the political freedom they so ardently desired (see Vol. IV, pp. 30-32).

37.zh:
我知道你們是亞伯拉罕的子孫，你們卻想要殺我，因為你們心裡容不下我的道。

**亞伯拉罕的子孫。**從字面上講他們確實是亞伯拉罕的子孫（參見第33節）。
**殺我。**見約7:1,19,25等。猶太人陰謀殺害耶穌的事實證明他們是罪的奴僕（見34節註釋；參羅6:16）。
**容不下我的道。**將這裡和“常常遵守我的道”（第31節）進行比較。猶太人不願接受耶穌的信息，而這正是能救他們脫離罪之奴役的信息（見第32節註釋）。
37.en:
**Abraham’s seed.** The fact of literal descent could not be disputed (cf. v. 33).
**Kill me.** See ch. 7:1, 19, 25; etc. The fact that the Jews were plotting murder was evidence that they were slaves of sin (see on John 8:34; cf. Rom. 6:16).
**My word hath no place.** Compare the phrase “continue in my word” (v. 31). The Jews were unwilling to accept the message of Jesus, a message that would have freed them from the slavery of sin (see on v. 32).

38.zh:
我所說的是在我父那裡看見的；你們所行的是在你們的父那裡聽見的。

**在我父那裡。**關於基督與父之間的親密關係，見約1:1；5:19註釋。
**行。**原文的意思是習慣上做。兒童自然會反映他們父母的特點並遵從他們的指示。
**你們的父。**耶穌後來指出他就是魔鬼（第44節），無窮慈愛之天父的對頭。
38.en:
**With my Father.** For a discussion of the close association of Christ with the Father see on chs. 1:1; 5:19.
**Do.** That is, according to the Greek, habitually. Children naturally reflect the characteristics, and obey the dictates of, their father.
**Your father.** Jesus later identifies him as the devil (v. 44), the very antithesis of the Father of infinite love.

39.zh:
他們說：我們的父就是亞伯拉罕。耶穌說：你們若是亞伯拉罕的兒子，就必行亞伯拉罕所行的事。

**我們的父就是亞伯拉罕。**這一點猶太人已經聲明過了（見第33節註釋）。也許他們意識到了第38節中耶穌所說之話的含義，就希望進行反駁。耶穌繼續說明只在肉體上做先祖的後裔沒有什麼功效。上帝看重的是品格上的特質。參保羅在羅2:28,29；9:6,7節中的論點。
**亞伯拉罕所行的事。**猶太人在肉體上的確是亞伯拉罕的後裔，但他們卻不是他屬靈的子孫。一個真兒女必然有他先祖道德上的印記。《密西拿》這樣形容亞伯拉罕的門徒：“我們祖宗亞伯拉罕的門徒，（擁有）一雙明亮的眼睛，一種順服的精神和一個謙卑的心靈”（Aboth 5. 19，《塔木德》松奇諾版，第72頁）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第154頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（39–40節）**。《基督比喻實訓》第268頁。
39.en:
**Abraham is our father.** This they had already asserted (see on v. 33). Perhaps they saw the implication of Jesus’ statement in v. 38 and hoped to counter it. Jesus proceeded to show that mere physical descent from the patriarch was no advantage. God values character qualifications. Compare the arguments of Paul in Rom. 2:28, 29; 9:6, 7.
**Works of Abraham.** The Jews were the physical seed of Abraham, but they were not his spiritual children. A true child bears the moral impress of the father. The Mishnah describes the disciples of Abraham thus: “The disciples of Abraham, our father, [possess] a good eye, an humble spirit and a lowly soul” (Aboth 5. 19, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 72).

40.zh:
我將在神那裡所聽見的真理告訴了你們，現在你們卻想要殺我，這不是亞伯拉罕所行的事。

**真理。**見第32節註釋。耶穌唯一的“罪行”就是祂來告訴世人從上帝那裡聽見的真理。
**殺我。**見第37節；參約7:1,25。
**這不是亞伯拉罕所行的事。**亞伯拉罕聽從上帝的聲音。他蒙召離開本族和父家時就“遵命出去……出去的時候，還不知往哪裡去”（來11:8；參見創12:1）。他堅定的信心為他贏得了“信之人的父”（羅4:11）的稱號。當基督在幔利的平原訪問亞伯拉罕時，亞伯拉罕沒有想要殺祂，而是將祂當作貴賓接待（創18:1-5）。
40.en:
**Kill me.** See v. 37; cf. ch. 7:1, 25.
**A man.** Gr. anthrōpos, here used in the sense of a person.
**Truth.** See on v. 32. Jesus’ only “crime” was that He had come to tell the truth, which He had received from God.
**This did not Abraham.** Abraham was responsive to the divine voice. When asked to leave his kindred and his father’s house he “obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went” (Heb. 11:8; cf. Gen. 12:1). His persistent walk of faith won for him the title, “father of all them that believe” (Rom. 4:11). When Christ visited Abraham in the plains of Mamre, Abraham did not go about to kill Him, but received Him as an honored guest (Gen. 18:1–5).

41.zh:
你們是行你們父所行的事。他們說：我們不是從淫亂生的；我們只有一位父，就是神。

**你們父。**耶穌已經告訴猶太人自己的父不是他們的父（第38節），但還沒有說他們的父就是魔鬼（見第44節）。猶太人很可能是意識到了這一點便急忙否認。
**從淫亂。**這裡顯然是在影射耶穌的出生。猶太人暗示耶穌是從淫亂生的。
**就是上帝。**如果耶穌指的是屬靈的祖先，那麼猶太人的主張和耶穌相同。上帝是以色列人的父，這不是新的觀念（見申32:6；賽64:8；等等）。
**懷愛倫註釋（41–42節）**。《歷代願望》第467頁。
41.en:
**Your father.** Jesus had already informed the Jews that His Father was not their father (v. 38), but had not yet identified their father as the devil (see v. 44). They probably saw the implication and hastened to deny it.
**Of fornication.** There is doubtless a taunt here at the supposed circumstances of Jesus’ birth, the implication being that Jesus was born of fornication.
**Even God.** If it was spiritual ancestry that Jesus was referring to, then the Jews claimed as much as did Jesus. The idea that God was the father of Israel was not new (see Deut. 32:6; Isa. 64:8; etc.).

42.zh:
耶穌說：倘若神是你們的父，你們就必愛我；因為我本是出於神，也是從神而來，並不是由著自己來，乃是他差我來。

**倘若上帝是你們的父。**猶太人顯然不是上帝的兒女。如果他們是上帝的兒女，他們就會接受上帝所差來的那位。約壹5:1,2明確了這條原則。
**由著自己。**這是《約翰福音》時常重複的主題。耶穌否認祂有任何尋求自己意思的企圖（見約7:16,18等）。
42.en:
**If God were your Father.** The Jews were clearly not the children of God. If they were, they would accept the One whom God had sent. This principle is affirmed in 1 John 5:1, 2.
**Of myself.** This is an oft-repeated theme in the Gospel of John. Jesus denies that there is any self-seeking on His part (see ch. 7:16, 18; etc.).

43.zh:
你們為什麼不明白我的話呢？無非是因你們不能聽我的道。

**因你們不能聽。**或“受不了去聽”，“不願意聽”。不聽的結果就是誤解耶穌的話。如果他們真是天父的兒女，他們一定能理解自己家中的語言。
43.en: **Because ye cannot hear.** Perhaps meaning, “because you cannot bear to hear” (RSV), or “because ye will not listen” (Robertson). The result was misunderstanding and misconstruction of the speech of Jesus. If they were the true children of the heavenly Father, they would understand the language of home.

45.zh:
我將真理告訴你們，你們就因此不信我。

**我。**“我”在原文中是強調的。耶穌通過對比表達自己。猶太人愚昧地相信魔鬼捏造的謊言。正是他將有關彌賽亞錯誤的觀念灌輸到他們的心裡（見路4:19註釋）。他們因為這種錯誤的觀念就準備接受那些諂媚他們、煽動他們個人野心的人。耶穌帶給他們的真理反而使他們那喜愛罪惡的心感到厭惡了，因此他們就拒絕了這真理。參約3:19。
45.en: **Because I.** In the Greek the “I” stands in the emphatic position. Jesus is setting Himself up by way of contrast. The Jews greedily believed the lies perpetrated by the archdeceiver. It was he who had suggested to them their false concepts of the Messiah (see on Luke 4:19). These they readily accepted for these false ideas flattered their personal ambitions. The truth that Jesus brought to them was unpalatable to their sin-loving hearts, so they rejected it. Compare John 3:19.

46.zh:
你們中間誰能指證我有罪呢？我既然將真理告訴你們，為什麼不信我呢？
